### Section 148 correction: the Section 146 note on the private-shop family was wrong in two ways

Section 146 recorded that the `TPacketCGPrivateShop*` family "needs a variable-length sub-record codec that reads an explicit extra length" and is "a materially different boundary from another `cg_*.rs` fixed record." **Both claims are false, and the correction matters because the second one would have justified a new boundary class that does not exist.** The verified facts follow.

**There is no wire-supplied extra length anywhere in this family.** Every one of the variable-length sub-records computes its own consumed length from a **compile-time `sizeof`**, never from a wire field. `input_main.cpp:4641` is `int iExtraLen = sizeof(TPacketCGPrivateShopItemCheckin);` and the same shape appears at `:4485` for `...ItemPriceChange`, `:4574` for `...ItemMove`, and `:4791` for `...ItemCheckout`. The `iExtraLen` name is misleading: it is a constant, not a length read from the client.

**The family is not a new boundary class. It is a third sub-header-routed two-byte prefix in the framing layer that already exists.** `HEADER_CG_PRIVATE_SHOP = 236` is **already** in `LEGACY_CG_VARIABLE_HEADERS` in `protocol/src/cg_wire.rs`, and `cg_inventory` already carries the correct row with `base_size: 2` and `cpp_type: "TPacketCGPrivateShop"`. So the generic resolver already returns `ClientFrameSize::Variable(2)` for 236, and the correct integration point is a private-shop arm in `cg_variable::resolve_variable_client_frame_size`, structurally identical to the existing `HEADER_CG_SHOP` and `HEADER_CG_FISH_EVENT_SEND` arms. The three sub-header-routed two-byte prefixes are shop, fish-event, and private-shop; the last is the one that was missing.

**The registration really is 2, and that is the whole reason a generic framer is not enough.** `packet_info.cpp:186` registers `sizeof(TPacketCGPrivateShop)`, and `input.cpp:83` resolves it, `:92-93` checks only that many bytes are present, and then `input.cpp:100-104` calls `Analyze` and does `iPacketLen += iExtraPacketSize` **after** the registered length was already applied. A framer that sizes 236 from `base_size` alone reads two bytes and then mistakes the sub-record for the next frame. The sub-record size is known only after `bSubHeader` is read, which is exactly what the existing `cg_variable` contract already models.

**The verified sub-header table.** The enumerator block `packet.h:1135-1161` declares **22** sub-headers with no explicit values, so they are 0 through 21. The dispatch at `input_main.cpp:3961-4081` has **21** case arms. The extra size, after the two-byte prefix, is:

| Value | Sub-header | Extra | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `BUILD` | 41 + `wItemCount` x 17 | `packet.h:1256-1263`; `TPrivateShopItem` 17 |
| 1 | `CLOSE` | 0 | no `c_pData` |
| 2 | `PANEL_OPEN` | 0 | no `c_pData` |
| 3 | `PANEL_CLOSE` | 0 | no `c_pData` |
| 4 | `START` | 4 | `sizeof(DWORD)` |
| 5 | `END` | 0 | no `c_pData` |
| 6 | `BUY` | 2 | `sizeof(WORD)` |
| 7 | `WITHDRAW` | 0 | no `c_pData` |
| 8 | `MODIFY` | 0 | no `c_pData` |
| 9 | `STATE_UPDATE` | 0 | **no case arm; falls to `default`** |
| 10 | `ITEM_PRICE_CHANGE` | 14 | `packet.h:1265-1269` |
| 11 | `ITEM_MOVE` | 4 | `packet.h:1271-1275` |
| 12 | `ITEM_CHECKIN` | 19 | `packet.h:1380-1386` |
| 13 | `ITEM_CHECKOUT` | 6 | `packet.h:1388-1392` |
| 14 | `TITLE_CHANGE` | 33 | `TITLE_MAX_LEN + 1`, `length.h:146` |
| 15 | `WARP_REQUEST` | 0 | no `c_pData` |
| 16 | `SLOT_UNLOCK_REQUEST` | 2 | `sizeof(WORD)` |
| 17 | `SEARCH_CLOSE` | 0 | no `c_pData` |
| 18 | `SEARCH` | 85 | `packet.h:1303-1307` |
| 19 | `SEARCH_BUY` | 180 | `packet.h:1316-1319` |
| 20 | `MARKET_ITEM_PRICE_DATA_REQUEST` | 0 | no `c_pData` |
| 21 | `MARKET_ITEM_PRICE_REQUEST` | 4 | `sizeof(DWORD)` |

**Exactly one sub-record is genuinely count-derived, and it is the MyShop pattern already implemented.** Sub-header 0 is `int iExtraLen = sizeof(TPacketCGPrivateShopBuild) + p->wItemCount * sizeof(TPrivateShopItem);`, which is structurally identical to the `MY_SHOP_ITEM_WIRE_SIZE` x count rule at `cg_variable`. The other twenty-one are constants. So the family is *not* uniformly variable-length: it is twenty-one fixed sizes and one count rule, and the count rule is not new machinery.

**`STATE_UPDATE` is enumerated but never dispatched.** `SUBHEADER_CG_PRIVATE_SHOP_STATE_UPDATE = 9` at `packet.h:1146` has no case in the switch, so it falls to `default:` at `input_main.cpp:4078-4080`, which logs `Unknown private shop subheader` and consumes the bare two-byte prefix. Any framing must treat 9 as a zero-extension sub-header, exactly as it must treat an unrecognised value, and must not invent a payload for it.

**Every width here is profile-pinned, and the flags are all on in the checked-in server.** Three separate files carry their own `#pragma pack`, and all three matter: `packet.h:274` and `:3540`, `common/tables.h:345` and `:2291`, and `common/length.h:956` and `:1274`. A `TItemPrice` member declared in `tables.h` is a *complete type* whose own size is fixed by `tables.h`, while its placement inside a `packet.h` struct is forced by `packet.h`'s pack, so both files must be packed for the arithmetic to hold, and both are. `TItemPos` is 3, `TItemPrice` is 12, and `TPrivateShopItem` is 17. `TPlayerItemAttribute` at `tables.h:426-430` is a `BYTE` and a `short`, so exactly 3 bytes, and `ITEM_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_NUM` is an unconditional 7 from the `item_length.h:21-30` ladder of 5 plus 2. `ITEM_SOCKET_MAX_NUM` **is** profile-dependent, 6 with `ENABLE_EXTENDED_SOCKETS` and 3 without, and `prodomodefines.h:76` defines it, so the active server has 6; none of the sub-records above depend on it, so the table is unaffected either way. `__PREMIUM_PRIVATE_SHOP__` **is** defined at `prodomodefines.h:176`, so the whole family is live and not dead code. The widths 41, 85, and 180 were each computed field by field from these packed declarations and are not estimates.

**One legacy defect is now visible and is recorded rather than reproduced.** Every variable-length handler returns `-1` when the remaining bytes are short, and `input.cpp:101-102` turns that into `return true` **without advancing `c_pData` and without decrementing `m_iBufferLeft`**. Contrast the unknown-header path at `input.cpp:87`, which sets `PHASE_CLOSE`. So a client that sends a well-formed header 236 with a truncated sub-record is neither disconnected nor served: the frame is left in the buffer, the loop at `input.cpp:72` is left with an unchanged `m_iBufferLeft`, and `desc.cpp:281` exits its `while (!Process(...))` on the `true`. The connection stalls rather than closing. This is the same shape as the already-recorded no-progress hazard in the game-to-DB path, and it is a legacy server behaviour, not a codec contract.

**The cast precedes the length check in all four variable handlers.** Each does `TPacketCGPrivateShopItem* p = (TPacketCGPrivateShopItem*)c_pData;` on the line before `int iExtraLen = sizeof(...)` and the `if (uiBytes < iExtraLen) return -1;` guard. Forming the pointer is harmless because no field is dereferenced until after the guard, and the guard therefore does precede every field read, which is the property the other inbound codecs already preserve. The framing work must keep that ordering explicit rather than relying on it.


### 148.4 `HEADER_CG_PRIVATE_SHOP` framing: implementation receipt (2026-09-25)

The audit above was re-verified by an independent read-only reviewer and
extended. Several of its conclusions changed the model, and two of my own
earlier claims were wrong. Both corrections are recorded before the receipt.

**Correction 1: the family carries no wire length.** My Section 146 note said
this family "needs a variable-length sub-record codec that reads an explicit
extra length" and described it as "a materially different boundary from another
fixed record." Both are false. There is no sub-record header byte and no length
field anywhere in the family. Every extension size is a compile-time `sizeof`
returned by a handler: `input_main.cpp:4641`, `:4485`, `:4574`, `:4791`. The
identifier `iExtraLen` names a constant, not a transmitted value.

**Correction 2: this is not a new boundary class.** `HEADER_CG_PRIVATE_SHOP` is
already in `LEGACY_CG_VARIABLE_HEADERS`, and `cg_inventory` already carries the
correct row with `base_size: 2`. The missing work was a private-shop arm in
`cg_variable::resolve_variable_client_frame_size`, exactly parallel to the
existing Shop and FishEvent arms. Building a new module would have duplicated
framing that already exists.

#### Verified source facts

- `HEADER_CG_PRIVATE_SHOP = 236` at `packet.h:89`. Its packet-table entry is
  `sizeof(TPacketCGPrivateShop)` at `packet_info.cpp:186`, which is two bytes:
  `BYTE bHeader` and `BYTE bSubHeader` at `packet.h:1226-1230`.
- `input.cpp:83` resolves that registered two-byte length, `:92-93` checks only
  that many bytes are present, and only then do `:100-104` call `Analyze` and
  apply `iPacketLen += iExtraPacketSize`. A generic framer therefore mistakes
  sub-record payload for the next frame, which is why routing on the sub-header
  is mandatory rather than stylistic.
- `EPrivateShopCGSubheader` at `packet.h:1135-1161` declares 22 enumerators with
  no explicit values, so they are 0 through 21. The dispatch at
  `input_main.cpp:3961-4081` has 21 case arms.
- `__PREMIUM_PRIVATE_SHOP__` is defined at `prodomodefines.h:176` and gates the
  whole inbound family: the `#ifdef` at `packet.h:1101` closes at `:1424`, so
  the enum, the base struct, and every sub-record sit inside one interval. The
  client gates the same block under a **different** name,
  `ENABLE_PREMIUM_PRIVATE_SHOP` (`LOCALE_INC.H:126`). The two spellings must not
  be unified.
- Three `#pragma pack` intervals matter, because a `TItemPrice` member is a
  complete type whose size is fixed by `common/tables.h:345-2291` while its
  placement is forced by `packet.h:274-3540`; `common/length.h:956-1274` covers
  `TItemPos`, `TITLE_MAX_LEN`, and `SELECTED_ITEM_MAX_NUM`.
- Unconditional widths: `TItemPos` 3, `TItemPrice` 12, `TPrivateShopItem` 17,
  `TPlayerItemAttribute` 3, `ITEM_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_NUM` 7 (`length.h`),
  `SELECTED_ITEM_MAX_NUM` 10 (`length.h:140`), `TITLE_MAX_LEN + 1` 33
  (`length.h:146`). `ITEM_SOCKET_MAX_NUM` is profile-dependent (6 here) but no
  private-shop sub-record depends on it.
- The four records the reviewer was asked to size are 2, 14, 4, 19, and 6
  bytes (`packet.h:1226-1230`, `:1265-1269`, `:1271-1275`, `:1380-1386`,
  `:1388-1392`). No `#ifdef` appears inside any of the four.

#### Extension table, as implemented

| Value | Sub-header | Extra | Value | Sub-header | Extra |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | BUILD | 41 + count x 17 | 11 | ITEM_MOVE | 4 |
| 1 | CLOSE | 0 | 12 | ITEM_CHECKIN | 19 |
| 2 | PANEL_OPEN | 0 | 13 | ITEM_CHECKOUT | 6 |
| 3 | PANEL_CLOSE | 0 | 14 | TITLE_CHANGE | 33 |
| 4 | START | 4 | 15 | WARP_REQUEST | 0 |
| 5 | END | 0 | 16 | SLOT_UNLOCK_REQUEST | 2 |
| 6 | BUY | 2 | 17 | SEARCH_CLOSE | 0 |
| 7 | WITHDRAW | 0 | 18 | SEARCH | 85 |
| 8 | MODIFY | 0 | 19 | SEARCH_BUY | 180 |
| 9 | STATE_UPDATE | 0 | 20 | MKT_PRICE_DATA_REQ | 0 |
| 10 | ITEM_PRICE_CHANGE | 14 | 21 | MKT_PRICE_REQ | 4 |

Twenty sub-headers are compile-time constants and exactly one is count-derived.
**Ten** sub-headers extend by zero, not nine: `CLOSE`, `PANEL_OPEN`,
`PANEL_CLOSE`, `END`, `WITHDRAW`, `MODIFY`, `WARP_REQUEST`, `SEARCH_CLOSE`, and
`MARKET_ITEM_PRICE_DATA_REQUEST` are dispatched with no `c_pData` at all, and
`STATE_UPDATE` is enumerated at `packet.h:1146` but has **no case arm**, so it
falls to `default:` at `input_main.cpp:4078-4080` and consumes the bare prefix.
An unrecognised sub-header takes the same path, so it also extends by zero. No
payload is invented for any of them.

`BUILD` is the only count rule and it is structurally identical to the existing
MyShop arm. `wItemCount` is the last two bytes of the 41-byte fixed part, so the
word sits at absolute frame offset 41 and is read little-endian. A prefix
shorter than 43 bytes cannot decide the length, so the resolver returns
`Ok(None)`, the framing layer's existing "need more bytes" signal, and
`try_decode` re-offers the frame once the word lands.

#### The collision taxonomy does not apply to the sub-header values

Value 236 itself is collision-free: `= 236` appears only at `packet.h:89` and
`client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h:88`. But the 22 sub-header values sit at
**wire offset 1**, after the 236 byte at offset 0. They are a field inside the
frame, not a header space, so every apparent numeric overlap between, say,
sub-header 9 and some `GC` header 9 is nominal. Only sub-header value 0 has no
numeric overlap at all. A reader scanning header tables must not apply the
four-bucket taxonomy to these values.

#### Legacy defects: recorded, not reproduced

**The most serious finding is a framing desync in `PrivateShopItemCheckin`.**
The handler is declared `int` at `input_main.cpp:4637` but returns `false` at
four sites: `:4722`, `:4728`, `:4734`, and `:4740`. In C++ `false` converts to
`0`, so `iExtraLen` becomes 0, `input.cpp:101` sees `0 < 0` as false, `:104`
adds nothing, and only the two base bytes are consumed. The remaining 17 bytes
of the 19-byte sub-record are then re-parsed as the next CG frame. Three of
those four paths are ordinary player actions: an Item-Shop item (`:4728`), an
**equipped** item (`:4734`), or a **locked** item (`:4740`) being offered for
sale. This is normal-client-reachable and is a hard desynchronisation of the
input stream. The Rust framing layer must model the declared 21-byte size and
must never mirror the legacy return value.

**`PrivateShopBuild` reads its count before checking its length.**
`input_main.cpp:4142` computes `iExtraLen` from `p->wItemCount`, and the guard
at `:4145` only runs afterwards, so the count word is read from bytes that have
not been length-checked. This is the one handler of the four that is not
correctly ordered.

**The other four handlers are two bytes too permissive.** `m_iBufferLeft` still
counts the two base bytes when it is passed to the handler, so the bare form
`if (uiBytes < iExtraLen)` accepts two bytes fewer than the frame really needs.
This is an inconsistency rather than a convention, and `input_main.cpp:4145`
proves it in-source: `Build` uses the correct form,
`if (uiBytes < (sizeof(TPacketCGPrivateShop) + iExtraLen))`. The Rust framing
layer must add the two base bytes itself, which is what
`PRIVATE_SHOP_BASE_WIRE_SIZE` does.

**Truncation stalls the connection instead of closing it.** As recorded above,
`return -1` becomes `return true` at `input.cpp:101-102`, the progress counter
never advances, and the deterministic re-parse fails identically forever with no
`sys_err` on that path. This contrasts with the unknown-header path at
`input.cpp:87`, which sets `PHASE_CLOSE`.

**A 90-byte width divergence in the same family, outside the four records.**
`TPacketCGPrivateShopSearchBuy` is 180 bytes on the server (`packet.h:1318`, ten
elements) and 270 on the client, which hardcodes `aSelectedItems[15]` at
`client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h:3655` with its own constant commented out
even though the client's own `SELECTED_ITEM_MAX_NUM` is 10 at
`PythonPrivateShop.h:60`. The server consumes 180 at `input_main.cpp:5177-5185`,
so 90 zero bytes remain buffered. This is a hardcoded divergence, not a build
configuration difference, and the framing layer implements the **server** width.
It does not affect the four sized records.

**Client-side findings, none of which change a width.** The nesting runs in both
directions: `TPrivateShopItem` is nested on the server and flat on the client,
and the client's `ItemCheckin` nests a `TItemPrice` where the server declares
`llGold`/`dwCheque` flat. Both remain 17 and 19 bytes with identical offsets, so
the family is wire-compatible and the Rust layer uses the server declarations.
There is **no** `Cell`-versus-`pos` drift here: both trees spell the field
`TSrcPos`, so the drift pattern seen in `ItemDrop2` does not repeat. All four
client builders are clean, using `TPacketCGPrivateShop mainPacket{}` and
zero-initialised sub-packets; the single arity switch at
`netSendItemCheckoutPrivateShopPacket` has a `default:` that returns. No builder
in the family has a player-instance gate, which the reviewer confirmed as a
two-layer absence rather than an outlier. Three narrower legacy issues are
recorded without a width consequence: an unchecked `WORD`-to-`BYTE` narrowing at
`Module.cpp:2209`, an unchecked `int`-to-`DWORD` cheque narrowing at
`Module.cpp:2197` whose server-side ceiling test is compiled out, a missing
bounds check that the sibling `netSendPrivateShopBuyPacket` has at
`Module.cpp:2134-2145`, and an indeterminate transmitted byte in the title-change
builder, where `PythonNetworkStreamPhaseGame.cpp:6612-6618` `strncpy`s 32 bytes
into a 33-byte stack buffer that is never zero-initialised.

**Not determined, and deliberately not guessed.** Whether `buffer_read_proceed`
clamps when the progress counter exceeds the buffer size; whether
`IsEmptyItemGrid` makes the `int`-to-`WORD` truncation at `input_main.cpp:4948`
unreachable; the exact severity of the two-byte over-read; and the widths of
`TPrivateShopItemData`, `TPrivateShopSearchData`, and
`TPrivateShopSaleData`, which embed `time_t` and `long` in the GC direction,
because `client/Client/ProdomoFiles.sln` carries both Win32 and x64 profiles. No
width claim is made for those three. All widths above were derived by hand from
`#pragma pack(1)` and the x86 target at `premake5.lua:12`, not by executing
`sizeof`.

#### Implementation

The work is a third sub-header-routed two-byte prefix inside the existing
framing layer, not a new codec. In `protocol/src/cg_variable.rs`:

- `PRIVATE_SHOP_BASE_WIRE_SIZE` (2), `PRIVATE_SHOP_BUILD_FIXED_WIRE_SIZE` (41),
  `PRIVATE_SHOP_ITEM_WIRE_SIZE` (17), and `PRIVATE_SHOP_BUILD_COUNT_OFFSET` (41)
  replace the previous inline base-size and header constants.
- 22 `PRIVATE_SHOP_SUBHEADER_*` constants, one per enumerator, with the
  `STATE_UPDATE` entry documenting the missing dispatch arm.
- `private_shop_constant_extra_wire_size` holds the twenty constant arms.
  `START`, `MARKET_ITEM_PRICE_REQUEST`, and `ITEM_MOVE` are grouped because they
  share a width; the comment records that they are three separate legacy
  declarations and that the coincidence is not evidence they are one request.
- `private_shop_extra_wire_size` handles the count-derived `BUILD` arm and
  returns `Ok(None)` for a prefix too short to carry the count word.
- `private_shop_frame_size` is the private-shop arm of
  `resolve_variable_client_frame_size`, and rejects a registered base size that
  is not the two-byte prefix.
- `HEADER_CG_PRIVATE_SHOP` was added to `RESOLVABLE_VARIABLE_CLIENT_HEADERS`.

Every arm returns the **extension only**, never the whole frame, so the caller
adds `PRIVATE_SHOP_BASE_WIRE_SIZE` itself. That single rule is what keeps the
twenty constant arms and the one count-derived arm on the same footing.

Four Clippy findings were fixed by refactoring rather than by suppression. The
constant table was split out of the resolver, and
`resolve_variable_client_frame_size` was split by extracting
`three_byte_prefix_declared_size` and `private_shop_frame_size`. No `allow`
attribute and no diagnostic suppression was added anywhere in this slice.

#### Receipt

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| `protocol/src/cg_variable.rs` | 87,891 bytes, 2,229 lines, SHA-256 `821f335b04788cfe...` |
| Tests in `cg_variable` | 46, up from 37 |
| `PRIVATE_SHOP_SUBHEADER_*` constants | 22 |
| Workspace | 138 Rust files, 27 test binaries |
| `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | exit 0 |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked --offline -- -D warnings` | exit 0 |
| `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --locked --offline` | exit 0 |
| `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --no-fail-fast --locked --offline` | 1,087 tests, 0 failures, 27 binaries, exit 0 |
| Workspace doc-tests | 6, exit 0 |

**Mutation result: 23 of 24 caught; 1 provably equivalent.** The surviving
mutation replaced `count.checked_mul(PRIVATE_SHOP_ITEM_WIRE_SIZE)` with a plain
multiply. That is equivalent and not a test gap: `count` is widened from a
`u16`, so the product is at most 65535 x 17 = 1,114,095 and cannot overflow a
64-bit `usize`. The proof is recorded in a code comment at the call site.

The sweep covered the base size, the fixed-part size, the element size, the
count offset, the count byte order, all nine distinct extension widths, the
zero-extension catch-all, the `BUILD` sub-header test, the need-more-bytes
threshold, the base-size guard, the resolvable-list membership, the count read
offset, the three-byte-prefix declared size, the extension-versus-frame
contract, and removal of the whole extension. One planned mutation
(`HEADER_CG_PRIVATE_SHOP` removed from the resolvable list) was first caught
only by a **compile** failure, because the replacement identifier did not
exist. That is a weak catch, so it was replaced with `M18b`, which makes the
resolver return the bare base size while still compiling, and it was caught by
a real test failure.

**A defect in the mutation harness invalidated the first sweep, and the sweep
was repeated.** The harness restored files with `shutil.copy2`, which preserves
mtime, so Cargo's fingerprint never invalidated and the test binary retained the
**mutated** code after a restore that reported success. The tell was a
`CAUGHT`/`SURVIVED` split that disagreed with the source on disk: the file
contained `_ => 0` while the gate failed with exactly the `_ => 19` mutation's
assertion, `unrecognised sub-header 22 was given a payload, left: Ok(Some(19))`.
The harness was changed to `shutil.copy` plus `os.utime(p, None)`, a forced
rebuild returned the tree to 1,087 passing, and the entire control-plus-mutation
sweep was re-run from scratch. Only the repeated results are recorded above. The
control, which mutates the late `game-server/src/lib.rs` binary rather than an
early one, was caught on every run.

**What this slice does not do.** It is a transport-free framing boundary. It
does not parse private-shop sub-record fields, resolve shops or owners, execute
buy, check-in, checkout, price-change, or search logic, run SQL, frame a live
descriptor stream, install TEA keys, or mutate session state. The declared sizes
are the legacy declared sizes; the four legacy defects above are documented and
are deliberately not reproduced.

## 149. Completed transport-free `TPacketCGItemPickup` record (2026-09-25 23:55 UTC)

The next entry in the fixed-size CG backlog recorded in Section 146. The
backlog's 63 names without a Rust boundary are a scoping list, not a count of
unimplemented records; this section takes the next fixed-width inbound CG item
record in numeric header order that had a correct `cg_inventory` row and no
codec.

### 149.1 The record

`server/server/game/packet.h:24` sets `HEADER_CG_ITEM_PICKUP = 15`, and
`packet.h:658-662` declares:

```cpp
typedef struct command_item_pickup
{
	BYTE header;
	DWORD vid;
} TPacketCGItemPickup;
```

The wire record is therefore exactly **five bytes**, four of them after the
one-byte header:

```text
[0x0f][vid: u32 little-endian]
```

Packing is unconditional on both trees. On the server, `grep -n '#pragma pack'
packet.h` returns exactly two lines, `packet.h:274` and the matching
`packet.h:3540`, with the declaration strictly between them. On the client,
`client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h` returns exactly three, `#pragma
pack(push)` and `#pragma pack(1)` at `:300-301` and the matching
`#pragma pack(pop)` at `:3906`, with the declaration at `:543-547` strictly
between. The neighbouring server records `TPacketCGEnvanter` at `:642-647` and
`TPacketCGItemSell` at `:649-656` each carry their own `#ifdef` guard; the
pickup struct carries none, so the width is not profile-dependent.

`DWORD` is four bytes on the server without a build flag deciding it.
`server/server/libthecore/typedef.h:15` defines it as `unsigned int` inside the
`#ifndef __WIN32__` block opened at `:9`, and the Windows branch is the SDK's
own 32-bit type.

The record is registered exactly once, at
`server/server/game/packet_info.cpp:124`, as `Set(HEADER_CG_ITEM_PICKUP,
sizeof(TPacketCGItemPickup), "ItemPickup")` inside `CPacketInfoCG`'s
constructor. The registered size agrees with the hand-derived width, there is
no second `Set` for this header, and no literal `Set(15` exists anywhere in
`server/` or `client/`. The existing `protocol/src/cg_inventory.rs` row already
carried the correct `base_size: 5` and
`cpp_type: Some("TPacketCGItemPickup")`, so no inventory change was needed.

### 149.2 `vid` is a virtual item ID, not a position

This is the point that separates this record from its three closest siblings.
`TPacketCGItemDrop`, `TPacketCGItemDrop2`, and `TPacketCGItemDestroy` all carry
a `TItemPos`. This one does not. Its single field identifies a ground item by
the virtual ID that `ITEM_MANAGER::FindByVID` keys on, so there is no window
byte and no cell byte anywhere in the record.

The dispatch is `server/server/game/input_main.cpp:3715-3718`, guarded by
`if (!ch->IsObserverMode())`, routing to `CInputMain::ItemPickup`, declared at
`input.h:92` and defined at `input_main.cpp:1076-1081`, whose entire body is
`if (ch) ch->PickupItem(pinfo->vid);`.

The consumer is `CHARACTER::PickupItem`, declared `bool PickupItem(DWORD vid)`
at `server/server/game/char.h:1210` and defined at `char_item.cpp:7972-8161`.
Its parameter `dwVID` occurs **exactly once** in that whole 190-line function,
at `:7974`:

```cpp
LPITEM item = ITEM_MANAGER::instance().FindByVID(dwVID);
```

That callee is `item_manager.cpp:664-672`, declared at `item_manager.h:445`, and
is a `std::map::find` that returns null when the key is absent. There is no
`-1`, no `0`, no `INVALID_VID`, no range test, no signed comparison, and no
`(int)` cast anywhere on that path. So the field is an opaque `u32` with no
signed reinterpretation, and the codec deliberately does not validate it.

The Rust `CgItemPickup` therefore has exactly one field, `vid: u32`, and no
stored header: the header is always emitted as 15 and accepted only as 15.

### 149.3 The handler is `void` and discards the result

`PickupItem` returns `bool` and `CInputMain::ItemPickup` throws that value
away. A failed pickup produces no error record, no chat packet, and no reply of
any kind. The codec accordingly models no success or failure result, and the
module documents this rather than inventing an outcome type.

The `if (ch)` guard is also redundant: `CInputMain::Analyze` at
`input_main.cpp:3647-3652` already closes the phase when
`d->GetCharacter()` is null.

The handler performs no length check of its own. It is safe only because the
framer has already established the registered five bytes:
`server/server/game/input.cpp:83` reads `iPacketLen` from the CG map and
`:92-93` returns early while `m_iBufferLeft < iPacketLen`, which is the only
length gate. That is a property of the framer and the single registration, not
of this record, which is why `CgItemPickup::decode` checks the exact length
itself.

The dispatch sits inside `CInputMain::Analyze` (`input_main.cpp:3643-4086`) and
leaves `iExtraLen` at zero, so no count-derived extension exists. Header 15 is
not a variable header.

### 149.4 Header 15 is collision-free inside the CG direction

Both enumerator lists were parsed programmatically, with C auto-increment
simulated, not read by eye. `server/server/game/packet.h:6-272` (265
enumerators) has exactly three value-15 entries: `HEADER_CG_ITEM_PICKUP` at
`:24`, `HEADER_GC_MAIN_CHARACTER_OLD` at `:115`, and
`HEADER_GG_GUILD_WAR_ZONE_MAP_INDEX` at `:244`. The client enum at
`client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h:8-241` (231 enumerators) has exactly two:
`HEADER_CG_ITEM_PICKUP` at `:24` and `HEADER_GC_MAIN_CHARACTER` at `:111`.
`server/server/common/tables.h:14-337` (251 enumerators) has exactly one
value-15 entry, `HEADER_GD_EMPIRE_SELECT` at `:32`, and no `HEADER_DG_* = 15`.

A raw grep appears to show 15 twice in `packet.h` because a commented-out
duplicate enumerator sits at `packet.h:419` directly above the real
`SPacketGGGuildWarMapIndex` at `:421-427`. That is a comment, not a second
declaration.

Under the project's four-bucket taxonomy, the first three buckets are **empty**
for this record:

1. **Live two-sizes: none.** Both trees spell CG 15 with the same struct tag,
   the same members, and the same five-byte width. No second CG record carries
   15 in either tree. This is the cleanest case in the CG table.
2. **Colliding but not two-sizes: not applicable**, since there is no second
   CG 15 to collide with.
3. **Width-equal semantic collision: none.**
4. **Nominally colliding, server-enum-only: the other directions**, none of
   which constrains this codec, because each is read by a different decoder.

The three bucket-4 entries, and why none of them is a CG collision:

- **GC 15 travels the opposite way and is dead.**
  `HEADER_GC_MAIN_CHARACTER_OLD` has no struct, no send site, and no client
  consumer of that name; a whole-tree search for the name returns only the
  enumerator itself. The client's own GC 15 is a different and far wider
  record, `TPacketGCMainCharacter` at
  `client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h:1429-1437`, which is 45 bytes with
  `CHARACTER_NAME_MAX_LEN = 24` from the unconditional
  `client/Client/UserInterface/StdAfx.h:43`. The two trees disagree on the
  *name* of a value the server never sends, so this is a name drift on a dead
  value, not a live two-sizes collision.
- **GG 15** is `SPacketGGGuildWarMapIndex`, a 13-byte record at
  `packet.h:421-427` with its own decoder, already covered by the Rust `gg`
  module.
- **GD 15** is `HEADER_GD_EMPIRE_SELECT` at `common/tables.h:32`, in the
  `1-byte header + 4-byte handle + 4-byte length` DB-peer framing, which is not
  the CG framing at all.

The standing rule that no header table may be shared between directions still
applies, but nothing here could mislead a decoder. Header 15 may be keyed as a
plain five-byte CG frame with no cross-direction caveat.

### 149.5 The two trees spell the typedef differently

The server declares `TPacketCGItemPickup` at `packet.h:662`; the client
declares `TPacketCGItemPickUp`, with a capital `U`, at
`client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h:547`. The struct tag
`command_item_pickup` is identical on both sides, as is the member list
`BYTE header; DWORD vid;`.

The server handler does not use the typedef at all. It casts to the tag, at
`input_main.cpp:1078`: `(struct command_item_pickup*) data`. The two names must
not be unified across the trees, but both may be cited. This is recorded so that
a later name-based coverage census does not report the client declaration as
missing.

### 149.6 Three client defects, recorded and deliberately not reproduced

The client send path can put values on this wire that the server has no meaning
for. None is a property of the record.

1. **Signed-to-unsigned widening at a script entry point.** The Python wrapper
   at `client/Client/UserInterface/PythonNetworkStreamModule.cpp:927-936`
   declares `int vid` at `:929` and passes it to a `DWORD` parameter at `:934`,
   so a negative or above-`0x7FFF_FFFF` Python argument silently becomes a
   large unsigned wire value. The second entry point at
   `client/Client/UserInterface/PythonPlayerModule.cpp:841-849` has the same
   `int ivid` widening at `:843` into `SendClickItemPacket` at `:847`. Both
   discard the `bool` return. The only non-Python call site,
   `client/Client/UserInterface/PythonPlayer.cpp:1312-1351` at `:1347`, uses
   `DWORD dwIID` end to end and has no such defect.
2. **Unchecked `PyLong_AsLong`.** `PyTuple_GetInteger` at
   `client/Client/ScriptLib/PythonUtils.cpp:127-139` stores the return of
   `PyLong_AsLong` at `:137` and never checks it. A non-integer argument leaves
   `-1` in the out-parameter, still returns `true`, leaks the live Python
   exception, and the wrapper then transmits `0xFFFFFFFF`.
3. **Neither wrapper has an arity switch.** Both accept any tuple of length at
   least one and never type-check the argument, which is strictly less safe
   than the ten wrappers in the same file that do have a
   `default: return Py_BuildException();` arm. Unlike the safebox wrappers
   recorded in earlier sections, these two have no fall-through defect of that
   class, because they contain no `switch (PyTuple_Size(...))` at all.

That `0xFFFFFFFF` is reachable from a script is a **client** defect, not a
server sentinel. The server's only reaction is a failed `std::map::find` and a
discarded `false`. It is the specific reason this codec must not grow a
"non-zero vid" or "vid must be a known ground item" rule: such a rule would
silently normalize a legal wire value in order to compensate for a bug that
lives on the other side of the socket. A test asserts that every value from `0`
to `255` and both `u32` extremes round-trip, and another asserts
`0xFFFFFFFF` encodes as `[15, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff, 0xff]`.

### 149.7 What is not determined

- Whether any shipped script calls the two Python entry points. No `.py` file
  in this tree calls either wrapper, so practical reachability of the
  `int`-to-`DWORD` defect is not determinable here.
- Whether any non-tree build variant changes the record. `sizeof` is 5 under
  every `#define` in this tree and there is no `#ifdef` around either
  declaration, but a private tree is outside this tree.
- The practical `vid` value space. `m_VIDMap` is a runtime map of ground-item
  instance VIDs, and whether `ITEM_MANAGER` ever assigns `0` or `0xFFFFFFFF` as
  a real VID was not traced. It does not matter at the record boundary.
- Anything about an unmodded retail client. The checked-in `client/` tree is a
  modified derivative that adds `HEADER_GC_PREMIUM_PLAYERS`,
  `HEADER_GC_BATTLE_PASS`, and `HEADER_GC_BIOLOGIST`, which the server enum
  does not have. It remains a valid oracle for the shared subset, which
  includes header 15, but not for anything outside it.

### 149.8 Implementation receipt

`protocol/src/cg_item_pickup.rs` is the codec: 28,417 bytes, 681 lines, SHA-256
`bcf701e0cc93c0c7...`, 18 module tests. It exposes `CG_ITEM_PICKUP_WIRE_SIZE`
(5), `CG_ITEM_PICKUP_PAYLOAD_SIZE` (4), the `CgItemPickup` struct, the
`CgItemPickupError` enum with `Truncated`/`LengthMismatch`/`InvalidHeader`, and
`new`, `encode`, `encode_into`, `to_frame`, `decode`, `decode_frame`. Both
decoders check the exact length before the header byte, and the header before
any payload byte. There are no `allow(clippy)` suppressions, no packed
structs, no `unsafe`, no `repr(...)`, and no `transmute`.

`protocol/src/lib.rs` gained one `pub mod cg_item_pickup;` line and
`protocol/src/cg_inventory.rs` was not changed.

`protocol/tests/cg_wiring.rs` is a new integration test, 9,762 bytes, 261
lines, 6 tests. It exists because of a mutation result, not as decoration; see
149.9. It compiles against the crate's public API only, so it names the public
path of every fixed CG codec. Its purpose is to make an unregistered module
detectable at all.

A sixteen-case mutation sweep was run over the codec and a late-binary positive
control was run over the same harness. The sweep is recorded in 149.9, and the
control is recorded in 149.10, together with a correction: this harness has no
control case built into it, so the earlier note in this section that "a
late-binary positive control and a sixteen-case mutation sweep were run" was
written before the control had in fact been run for this slice.

**Full gate receipt:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace
--all-targets --locked --offline -- -D warnings`, and `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings"
cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --locked --offline` all exit 0.
`cargo test --workspace --all-targets --no-fail-fast --locked --offline` reports
**1,111 tests passed, 0 failed across 28 test binaries**, and
`cargo test --workspace --doc --no-fail-fast --locked --offline` reports 6 doc
tests. The workspace holds 139 Rust files outside `tools/` and 96,657 scanned
lines.

### 149.9 Mutation result, and a real gap it found

The first sweep ran sixteen cases and caught fifteen. The survivor was
**"module not registered"**, which removed the `pub mod cg_item_pickup;` line
from `protocol/src/lib.rs` and passed every gate.

That is a genuine coverage gap, not a weak mutation. A module's own
`#[cfg(test)]` tests use `super::*`, so removing its registration stops the
tests from being compiled at all, and every remaining gate still passes. The
deleted unregistered `protocol/src/cg.rs` from Section 146 had exactly this
shape: 91 record declarations, no implementations, and zero contribution to any
gate.

The fix is `protocol/tests/cg_wiring.rs`, placed in `tests/` on purpose so it
compiles against the **public** API only. A removed `pub mod` line now fails to
compile that integration target, which `--no-fail-fast` reports as a failing
test binary. Re-running the identical case then returned `CAUGHT`. That is the
weakest available form of detection, so the file names the public path of every
fixed CG codec rather than only the new one, and the module documents the
requirement for every codec added from here on.

**What this slice does not do.** It is a transport-free fixed-record boundary.
It does not resolve a virtual ID to a ground item, reproduce the observer gate,
the distance check, the ownership check, the anti-flag checks, the stack-merge
path, the party-distribution branch, the quest veto, or the item logging, all of
which live above the codec in `char_item.cpp:7972-8161`. It does not frame a
live descriptor stream, install TEA keys, mutate session state, or reproduce the
three client defects above. The header stays opaque, `vid` stays opaque, and no
gameplay policy is enforced at this boundary.
### 149.10 Late-binary positive control, and a correction

A `CAUGHT` verdict is only evidence if the harness would actually notice a
failure. Two things have to be true: the gate must reach the later test
binaries, and the harness must extract the failing target. Neither is
guaranteed by reading the results of an earlier slice, so it was checked
directly.

The check was run through the **identical** harness code path, not by hand, by
submitting a one-entry mutation set to `/tmp/mut148.py`. The entry breaks a
single assertion in `world/tests/world_baseline.rs`, which is a **late** test
binary, and changes:

```rust
    assert_eq!(raw_vid, 41);
```

to `assert_eq!(raw_vid, 999999);`.

Result:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| status | `CAUGHT` |
| process exit code | 101 |
| failing tests | 1 |
| extracted failing target | `-p world --test world_baseline` |
| restore of `world/tests/world_baseline.rs` | `OK`, byte-exact |

This proves three separate things that a mutation table cannot show on its own:
`--no-fail-fast` really does reach a binary far later in the workspace than the
one under audit, the harness's failing-target extraction works, and the restore
path returns the file to its original bytes. Every `CAUGHT` above is therefore a
real detection and not an artifact of the gate stopping early.

**Correction to 149.8, recorded rather than smoothed over.** That subsection
originally read "A late-binary positive control and a sixteen-case mutation
sweep were run over the codec." Only the sweep had been run at that point. The
harness at `/tmp/mut148.py` has **no** control case built into it; that was
established by reading the script, and the control had to be supplied as an
explicit mutation entry. The 149.8 wording was corrected to say so, and this
subsection records the control that was then actually run. The sweep results in
149.9 were produced by the same harness and are unaffected.

**Harness properties re-confirmed while doing this.** The backup step uses
`shutil.copy2`, which is safe because it copies *to* the backup. The restore
step uses `shutil.copy` plus `os.utime(p, None)`, which is the fix for the
stale-mtime defect that invalidated the Section 148 sweep: `copy2` preserves
mtime, Cargo's fingerprint never invalidates, and the test binary keeps running
mutated code after a restore that reports success. The restore line above says
`OK`, and the `world_baseline.rs` file was compared by hash after the run.
### 149.11 Receipt closure, verified after the fact

The tree was re-gated once more after the mutation sweeps, the control run, and
the documentation edits, with the same results: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
exit 0, strict Clippy exit 0, rustdoc with `-D warnings` exit 0,
`cargo test --workspace --all-targets --no-fail-fast --locked --offline`
reporting **1,111 tests passed and 0 failed across 28 test binaries** at exit 0,
and `cargo test --workspace --doc --no-fail-fast --locked --offline` reporting
6 doc tests. This is the figure recorded in 149.8 and in `AGENTS.md` and
`README.md`, re-confirmed after the sweeps had mutated and restored three source
files plus the control's target.

**Hygiene after this slice.** 13 `.DS_Store` files, 5 `.bak` files, and 0
`.mutbak` files; the 22 pre-existing tracked deletions are untouched;
`git status --porcelain -uall` is 30,633 records, which is the 30,631 recorded
at the Section 146 receipt plus exactly the two files this slice added,
`protocol/src/cg_item_pickup.rs` and `protocol/tests/cg_wiring.rs`. The deleted
`protocol/src/cg.rs` is still absent, and `tools/packet_compare` is still present
and still unbuildable, which is unchanged and not a workspace regression.

`/workspace/target` is present because this slice is not being closed out with a
tree removal; it is measured and removed by exact path only at the end of a
completed slice, after final validation, with no Cargo or rustc process holding
it.

## 150. `TPacketCGQuickslotAdd` — transport-free header 16 record

The next fixed-size CG record in numeric header order after Section 149's
header 15. The backlog recorded in Section 146 is a scoping list rather than a
count, and the next entry that is fixed-width, has a correct `cg_inventory` row,
and has no codec is header 16.

An independent read-only source audit was run against this slice. Its full report
is at `/tmp/agent-reports/sec150_audit.md` (1,105 lines), the auditor was
`sec150-quickslot`, and it touched nothing in the repository and ran no Cargo.
Its verdict was that the codec is substantively right and the width is
uncontested; the corrections it forced are folded into the subsections below and
are marked **Corrected** where they replace an earlier draft claim.

### 150.1 The record and its width

`server/server/game/packet.h:25` sets `HEADER_CG_QUICKSLOT_ADD = 16`, and
`packet.h:664-669` declares:

```cpp
typedef struct command_quickslot_add
{
	BYTE	header;
	BYTE	pos;
	TQuickslot	slot;
} TPacketCGQuickslotAdd;
```

The wire record is therefore exactly **four bytes**, three after the header:

```text
[0x10][pos: u8][slot type: u8][slot pos: u8]
```

`TQuickslot` is `SQuickslot { BYTE type; BYTE pos; }` at
`server/server/common/tables.h:452-456`, inside the `#pragma pack(1)` opened at
`common/tables.h:345` and closed at `:2291`, so it is exactly two bytes and the
containing record is four. The record itself sits under the `#pragma pack(1)`
that `packet.h:274` opens and does not close until `:3540`. No `#ifdef` touches
either declaration, so the width is not profile-dependent.

The record is registered exactly once, at
`server/server/game/packet_info.cpp:125`, as
`Set(HEADER_CG_QUICKSLOT_ADD, sizeof(TPacketCGQuickslotAdd), "QuickslotAdd")`.
`CPacketInfo::Set` has no extra-length overload at all, which is the structural
reason no second registration can exist. The four-byte size there agrees with the
hand-derived width, and the existing `protocol/src/cg_inventory.rs` row already
carried `base_size: 4` with `cpp_type: Some("TPacketCGQuickslotAdd")`, so no
inventory change was needed.

The `case HEADER_CG_QUICKSLOT_ADD:` arm at
`server/server/game/input_main.cpp:3742-3744` never touches `iExtraLen`, which is
initialised to zero at `:3654` and returned at `:4085`, and `0x10` is not in
`cg_wire.rs`'s `LEGACY_CG_VARIABLE_HEADERS`. Header 16 is therefore not a
variable header, which is why a fixed-size record is the correct shape.

### 150.2 Four separate naming drifts, all layout-identical

This record has more spelling drift between the two trees than any earlier one
in this family. All four differences are naming only, and every layout is
identical, so the record is wire-compatible:

| Role | Server | Client |
| --- | --- | --- |
| record typedef | `TPacketCGQuickslotAdd` `packet.h:669` | `TPacketCGQuickSlotAdd` `Packet.h:554` |
| record struct tag | `command_quickslot_add` | `command_quickslot_add` `Packet.h:549` |
| slot typedef | `TQuickslot` `common/tables.h:456` | `TQuickSlot` `client/Client/UserInterface/GameType.h:589` |
| slot struct tag | `SQuickslot` | `SQuickSlot` `GameType.h:585` |
| slot field names | `type`, `pos` | `Type`, `Position` |

The client capitalises the `S` in `QuickSlot` in **both** the record typedef and
the slot typedef, and its two slot fields are named `Type` and `Position` rather
than `type` and `pos`. Packing is unconditional on both sides: the client's
record is between `#pragma pack(push)` and `#pragma pack(1)` at
`client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h:300-301` and the matching
`#pragma pack(pop)` at `:3906`, and its slot is between
`client/Client/UserInterface/GameType.h:570-571` and the matching
`#pragma pack(pop)` at `:715`.

The two header enumerators agree on the value: the server has
`HEADER_CG_QUICKSLOT_ADD = 16` at `packet.h:25` and the client has the same at
`client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h:25`.

The names must not be unified across the trees, but all of them may be cited.
This is recorded so a later name-based coverage census does not report the
client declarations as missing.

### 150.3 Two different fields are both called `pos`, and one is not a 0..89 cell

The record has a bare `pos` at wire offset 1 and a `slot.pos` at offset 3, and
they mean different things. The bare `pos` is the **quickbar index**: it is
passed as the first argument to `CHARACTER::SetQuickslot(BYTE pos, ...)` at
`server/server/game/input_main.cpp:1112` and indexes
`CHARACTER::m_quickslot[QUICKSLOT_MAX_NUM]` at `char.h:1043`. The `slot.pos` is a
**payload** position, and when the slot type is an item the handler uses it as
`TItemPos srcCell(INVENTORY, pinfo->slot.pos)` at `input_main.cpp:1093`.

Neither is derivable from the other. The Rust struct therefore names them `pos`
and `slot`, and a test pins the exact wire order so the two can never be
silently transposed.

**`slot.pos` is not an inventory cell in 0..89.** `SetQuickslot` accepts a cell if
`IsDefaultInventoryPosition()` holds, which requires `INVENTORY == window_type`
and `cell < INVENTORY_MAX_NUM` (90) at `common/length.h:1018-1020`, **or** if
`IsBeltInventoryPosition()` holds, which is
`(BELT_INVENTORY_SLOT_START <= cell) && (BELT_INVENTORY_SLOT_END > cell)` at
`common/length.h:1013-1016` and **does not test `window_type` at all**.
`BELT_INVENTORY_SLOT_START` is 242 and `BELT_INVENTORY_SLOT_END` is 258
(`common/length.h:921-922`), so the accepted ranges are 0..89 **and** 242..257.
Because the wire byte maxes at 255, belt cells 242..255 are reachable.

Recording this explicitly so a later slice does not "fix" it by narrowing the
documented range to 0..89, which would be wrong.

The auditor also stated the converse positively: **no out-of-bounds read exists
on the item path.** The handler forces the window to `INVENTORY` and passes a
`BYTE` cell, so `wCell <= 255`, while the active `INVENTORY_AND_EQUIP_SLOT_MAX`
is 1,338 at `common/length.h:924-927`, so neither `IsValidItemPosition` nor
`GetItem` can fire.

### 150.4 Every bound on these fields lives above the codec

The dispatch is `case HEADER_CG_QUICKSLOT_ADD:` at `input_main.cpp:3742-3744`,
and `CInputMain::QuickslotAdd` is declared `void` at `input.h:94` and defined at
`input_main.cpp:1083-1113`. Its whole body is a null character test, one `if`,
one `switch`, and a call:

```cpp
void CInputMain::QuickslotAdd(LPCHARACTER ch, const char* data)
{
	if (!ch)
		return;

	TPacketCGQuickslotAdd* pinfo = (TPacketCGQuickslotAdd*)data;

	if (pinfo->slot.type == QUICKSLOT_TYPE_ITEM)	//@fixme528
	{
		LPITEM item = nullptr;
		const TItemPos srcCell(INVENTORY, pinfo->slot.pos);

		if (!(item = ch->GetItem(srcCell)))
			return;

		// unused for now.
		/*if (IS_SET(item->GetAntiFlag(), ITEM_ANTIFLOW_QUICKSLOT))
			return; */

		switch (item->GetType())
		{
			case ITEM_USE:
				break;

			default:
				return;
		}
	}

	ch->SetQuickslot(pinfo->pos, pinfo->slot);
}
```

The handler performs **zero** range checks on `pos`, `slot.type`, or
`slot.pos`, and it discards `SetQuickslot`'s `bool` return. Every real bound is
one layer further up, in `CHARACTER::SetQuickslot` at `char_quickslot.cpp:45`:

- `if (pos >= QUICKSLOT_MAX_NUM) return false;` at `:49`, where
  `QUICKSLOT_MAX_NUM` is 36 at `server/server/common/length.h:51`.
- `if (rSlot.type >= QUICKSLOT_TYPE_MAX_NUM) return false;` at `:52`, where the
  enum at `common/length.h:374-381` is `QUICKSLOT_TYPE_NONE` 0, `_ITEM` 1,
  `_SKILL` 2, `_COMMAND` 3, `_MAX_NUM` 4.
- a second switch requiring an item slot to name a default or belt inventory
  position, a skill slot to name a position below `SKILL_MAX_NUM`, accepting any
  payload for a command slot, and **returning false from its `default:` arm**.

So both wire bytes are **opaque** `u8` values at this boundary. The codec does
not apply `QUICKSLOT_MAX_NUM`, does not apply `QUICKSLOT_TYPE_MAX_NUM`, does not
require the type to be a known enumerator, and does not resolve the slot
payload. Adding any of those rules would reject wire values the legacy framer
accepts and would put gameplay policy inside a record codec.

`common/src/enums.rs:286-299` already carries a typed
`EQuickSlotType { None=0, Item=1, Skill=2, Command=3, MaxNum=4 }` whose values
match the legacy enum exactly, but it has no `TryFrom<u8>` or `from_u8`, so it
cannot be used to validate a wire byte. It stays a helper type and is not a codec
constraint.

### 150.5 The dispatch has no observer guard, unlike its neighbours

The `case HEADER_CG_QUICKSLOT_ADD:` arm at `input_main.cpp:3742-3744` calls
`QuickslotAdd(ch, c_pData)` with no `IsObserverMode()` test, while the
neighbouring `HEADER_CG_ITEM_PICKUP` arm at `:3715-3718` and the
`HEADER_CG_USE_SKILL` arm at `:3739-3741` both do. That is a legacy observation
about the dispatch layer. It is recorded, not reproduced, and it is not a reason
to add anything to the codec.

The `if (!ch)` test inside the handler is redundant with `Analyze`, which closes
the phase when `d->GetCharacter()` is null. The two sibling handlers differ
here and the difference is recorded so it is not read as an oversight:
`QuickslotDelete` at `input_main.cpp:1116-1120` and `QuickslotSwap` at
`:1122-1126` have **no** `ch` null test and dereference `ch` directly. Those two
records are the natural next slices.

### 150.6 The client narrows unchecked `DWORD`s to `BYTE`

The client sender itself is clean.
`CPythonNetworkStream::SendQuickSlotAddPacket(BYTE wpos, BYTE type, BYTE pos)` at
`client/Client/UserInterface/PythonNetworkStreamPhaseGameItem.cpp:797-816`
guards with `__CanActMainInstance()` at `:799`, assigns all four fields at
`:804-807` before sending, and sends `sizeof(TPacketCGQuickSlotAdd)`, which is
four bytes. Every parameter is a `BYTE`, so there is no signed widening, no
uninitialized field, and no `PyTuple_Size` arity switch, which means the
missing-default defect class seen elsewhere in this tree does not apply here.

The narrowing is in the callers, and **Corrected** relative to the first draft of
this section. `CPythonPlayer::RequestAddLocalQuickSlot(DWORD dwLocalSlotIndex,
DWORD dwWndType, DWORD dwWndItemPos)` at
`client/Client/UserInterface/PythonPlayer.cpp:926` bounds-checks
`dwLocalSlotIndex` at `:928` and then sends
`(BYTE)dwGlobalSlotIndex, (BYTE)dwWndType, (BYTE)dwWndItemPos` at `:934`.
`RequestAddToEmptyLocalQuickSlot(DWORD dwWndType, DWORD dwWndItemPos)` at
`:937-952` does the same at `:947`. Both discard the sender's `bool`. The two
Python wrappers at `PythonPlayerModule.cpp:1216-1251` likewise have no arity
switch and use the unchecked `PyTuple_GetInteger` `int` overload, whose
`PyLong_AsLong` result is ignored at `client/Client/ScriptLib/PythonUtils.cpp:137`.

**The first draft of this section claimed `dwGlobalSlotIndex` was "provably
safe" because the page index is clamped modulo `QUICKSLOT_MAX_LINE`. That claim
was wrong and is withdrawn.** `LocalQuickSlotIndexToGlobalQuickSlotIndex` at
`PythonPlayer.cpp:862-865` returns
`m_playerStatus.lQuickPageIndex * QUICKSLOT_MAX_COUNT_PER_LINE + dwLocalSlotIndex`,
and `lQuickPageIndex` is a **signed `long`** at `client/Client/UserInterface/PythonPlayer.h:137`.
`SetQuickPage(int nQuickPageIndex)` at `PythonPlayer.cpp:850-858` only takes the
modulo branch when `nQuickPageIndex >= QUICKSLOT_MAX_LINE` at `:854`; the
**negative** branch at `:852-853` assigns `QUICKSLOT_MAX_LINE + nQuickPageIndex`
with no clamp, and `playerSetQuickPage` is a registered Python method at
`PythonPlayerModule.cpp:1164-1172` registered at `:2924`. The concrete
consequence: `SetQuickPage(-5)` yields page `-1`, then
`RequestAddLocalQuickSlot(0, ...)` yields a global index of `-8`, and the
unchecked `(BYTE)` cast puts **`0xF8` (248)** on the wire.

`dwWndType` and `dwWndItemPos` are likewise never range-checked before their
`(BYTE)` casts, so a caller passing a value above 255 has it silently truncated.
That is an explicit lossy narrowing, a different defect class from the
signed-to-unsigned widening recorded for the pickup record in Section 149.6.

It is recorded and not compensated for. The codec must not clamp, mask, or
range-check either byte, because doing so would hide a client bug at a layer that
is not responsible for it.

### 150.7 The client declares two disagreeing quickbar capacities

**Corrected twice.** The first draft of this section claimed the client's
quickbar addresses only 32 slots and that server slots 32 through 35 are
unreachable. That is **withdrawn**. Reading the client's own header enum shows
it declares *two* capacities and uses them inconsistently, and the larger one is
the one the array is sized from.

| Side | Constant | Value | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| server | `QUICKSLOT_MAX_NUM` | 36 | `server/server/common/length.h:51` |
| client | `QUICKSLOT_MAX_LINE` | 4 | `client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h:256` |
| client | `QUICKSLOT_MAX_COUNT_PER_LINE` | 8 | `client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h:257` |
| client | `QUICKSLOT_MAX_COUNT` | 32 | derived, `Packet.h:258` |
| client | `QUICKSLOT_MAX_NUM` | 36 | `client/Client/UserInterface/Packet.h:260` |

The client declares **both** `QUICKSLOT_MAX_COUNT = 32` and
`QUICKSLOT_MAX_NUM = 36`, in the same enum, four lines apart. `Packet.h:260`
carries the Korean comment "a value aligned with the server", so 36 is a
deliberate mirror of the server's 36, while `Packet.h:257` carries "the client's
own arbitrary decision value" for the 8.

Which one applies depends on the entry point:

- The client's slot array is `TQuickSlot aQuickSlot[QUICKSLOT_MAX_NUM]` at
  `client/Client/UserInterface/PythonPlayer.h:134`, so it has **36** entries,
  matching the server.
- `CPythonPlayer::AddQuickSlot` at `PythonPlayer.cpp:998-1005`,
  `DeleteQuickSlot` at `:1007-1014`, `MoveQuickSlot` at `:1016-1028`, and
  `__RefGlobalQuickSlot` at `:888` all bound-check against
  **`QUICKSLOT_MAX_NUM`**, i.e. 36.
- `RemoveQuickSlotByValue` at `:899-907` iterates `for (BYTE i = 0; i <
  QUICKSLOT_MAX_NUM; ++i)` and can therefore send a delete for `pos` in 32..35.
- Only `RequestDeleteGlobalQuickSlot` at `:954-966` bounds-checks against
  **`QUICKSLOT_MAX_COUNT`**, i.e. 32.

So slots 32 through 35 **are** reachable from this client through every path
except `RequestDeleteGlobalQuickSlot`, and the first draft's subset claim was
wrong on both counts. The two constants are a genuine client-side inconsistency,
recorded here so a later slice does not "harmonise" one of them.

Two further notes. `QUICKSLOT_MAX_COUNT_PER_LINE` is the paging width, used for
the **local** index, so `RequestAddLocalQuickSlot` checking the local index
against 8 at `PythonPlayer.cpp:928` is correct and is not part of this
inconsistency. And `CPythonPlayer::MoveQuickSlot` at `:1016-1028` is a purely
**local** state mutation — it swaps `aQuickSlot` entries through
`__RefGlobalQuickSlot` and `std::swap` and sends nothing. The network send is a
separate function, `RequestMoveGlobalQuickSlotToLocalQuickSlot` at `:917-924`,
which becomes Section 151's swap record.

The codec's decision to leave `pos` opaque is unchanged, and is in fact better
supported now: the same client has three different notions of how many quickbar
slots exist, and none of the three is a wire property.

### 150.8 Collision taxonomy for value 16

Established by a programmatic C enumerator simulator run over the three header
enums, validated against eight known-positive enumerators before use, including
the auto-incrementing `HEADER_GG_PRIVATE_SHOP_ITEM_SEARCH_RESULT` and the
`ENABLE_SELL_ITEM`-guarded `HEADER_CG_ITEM_SELL`. Counts parsed: 254 enumerators
in the server `packet.h`, 218 in server `common/tables.h`, 226 in the client
`Packet.h`. Conditional enumerators detected: 7, 27, and 2 respectively, and
**none of them carries value 16**.

Every enumerator with value 16:

| Direction | Enumerator | Width | Tree |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CG | `HEADER_CG_QUICKSLOT_ADD` `packet.h:25`, `Packet.h:25` | 4 B | both |
| GC | `HEADER_GC_CHARACTER_POINTS` `packet.h:116`, `HEADER_GC_PLAYER_POINTS` `Packet.h:112` | 2,041 B | both |
| GG | `HEADER_GG_TRANSFER` `packet.h:245` | 34 B | server only |
| GD | `HEADER_GD_SAFEBOX_CHANGE_PASSWORD` `common/tables.h:34` | DB-peer framing | server only |

**Inside CG the value is collision-free.** Both trees name the same struct tag
`command_quickslot_add` with the same three members and the same 4-byte width.
This matches the clean result for header 15 in Section 149.

**Inside GC the value is also coherent.** `TPacketGCPoints` is
`packet_points { BYTE header; long long points[POINT_MAX_NUM]; }` at
`packet.h:1052-1056` and `Packet.h:1734-1738`, with `POINT_MAX_NUM` 255 in both
trees, so both are 2,041 bytes. Only the enumerator spelling drifts
(`CHARACTER_POINTS` vs `PLAYER_POINTS`), exactly as `HEADER_GC_ITEM_SET` and
`HEADER_GC_ITEM_SET2` do; the record itself is coherent and imposes no second
width.

The GC record is live: sent at `char.cpp:2038` inside
`CHARACTER::PointsPacket` (`char.cpp:2031-2087`) and registered **inbound** on
the client at `PythonNetworkStream.cpp:69`.

GG 16 is `TPacketGGTransfer` at `packet.h:429-434`, 34 bytes, registered at
`packet_info.cpp:217`, live with send sites in `cmd_general.cpp:2668`,
`questlua_monarch.cpp:708`, and `cmd_gm.cpp:128`. GD 16 uses the one-byte-header
plus 4-byte-handle plus 4-byte-length DB framing, so its 16 is a field inside a
different framing layer and constrains nothing in CG.

**Bucket assignment.** It is **not bucket 1** (live two-sizes), because that
bucket needs the two *trees* to disagree about a value and here they agree. It is
**not bucket 3** (width-equal semantic collision), because the widths across
directions are 4 vs 2,041 vs 34. It is the inter-direction nominal overlap of the
shape already described for headers 11, 13, 15, 22, 69, 70, 71, and 83: a byte
reused by an unrelated record with its own decoder and its own framing.

**The concrete consequence worth recording.** The client resolves inbound frames
through a single `static CMainPacketHeaderMap s_packetHeaderMap` inside
`CPythonNetworkStream::CheckPacket`, looked up by the raw header byte at
`client/Client/UserInterface/PythonNetworkStream.cpp:536` and sized with
`Peek(PacketType.iPacketSize)` at `:564`. That map is **GC-only** — the file has
135 `Set(HEADER_GC_` registrations and 0 `Set(HEADER_CG_` registrations, which is
the positive control that makes the zero real. So a 4-byte CG-16 frame arriving
inbound would be read by the client as a 2,041-byte points frame and the client
would stall waiting for 2,037 more bytes. The standing rule follows: **no header
table may ever mix CG 16 and GC 16.** The Rust inventory is already correctly
direction-separated, with CG rows in `cg_inventory.rs` and GC rows in
`protocol/src/gc`.

### 150.9 Two further legacy server defects on this path

Both were added by the audit and are recorded, not reproduced.

**An unguarded `GetDesc()->Packet` on the delete and swap paths.**
`CHARACTER::SetQuickslot` guards with `if (GetDesc())` at `char_quickslot.cpp:88`
before calling `GetDesc()->Packet(...)` at `:94`, but `CHARACTER::DelQuickslot` at
`:112` and `CHARACTER::SwapQuickslot` at `:134` call `GetDesc()->Packet(...)`
**unguarded**, while `m_lpDesc` is initialised to `NULL` at
`server/server/game/entity.cpp:27`. This record reaches the unguarded call
directly, because `SetQuickslot` itself calls `DelQuickslot(i)` at
`char_quickslot.cpp:60` from its own dedup loop. This is reported as
reachable-by-construction from the dedup loop; a concrete call ordering that
demonstrates an actual null dereference was not established.

**A near-vacuous skill-position check.** `char_quickslot.cpp:74` tests
`if ((int) rSlot.pos >= SKILL_MAX_NUM) return false;`, but `SKILL_MAX_NUM` is 255
at `common/length.h:72` and `rSlot.pos` is a single `BYTE`, so the cast to `int`
can never produce a value of 255 or more by widening. The check can only fire at
`pos == 255` and rejects exactly one byte.

### 150.10 Three Rust `TQuickslot` definitions, not two

**Corrected**: the first draft of this section said there were two. There are
three, and the codec consumes the compliant one.

| # | Location | Declaration | Fields | `repr`? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `protocol/src/lib.rs:494-500`, impl at `:502-518` | `pub struct TQuickslot`, `packed_size() -> 2`, hand-written `to_bytes`/`from_bytes` | `b_type`, `b_pos` | none |
| 2 | `common/src/tables.rs:142-147` | `pub struct TQuickslot` | `slot_type`, `pos` | **`#[repr(C, packed)]`** |
| 3 | `protocol/src/db_records.rs:1951-1958`, alias at `:4869` | `QuickslotRecord`, `WIRE_SIZE = 2`, `impl_fixed_codec!` at `:1984` | `slot_type`, `pos` | none |

`cg_quickslot_add.rs` does `use crate::TQuickslot;`, so it consumes **#1**,
`protocol/src/lib.rs`. So does `protocol/tests/cg_wiring.rs`.

All three are layout-equivalent, two `u8` in type-then-pos order, but the field
names differ, so they are not interchangeable at the Rust type level. #1 uses
`b_type`/`b_pos`, matching the sibling `TPlayerSkill` and `TPlayerItemAttribute`
definitions in the same file; #2 and #3 use `slot_type`/`pos`, matching the
legacy C++ field names.

**#1 and #3 are compliant** — no `repr`, no `unsafe`, no `transmute`, explicit
field-by-field encoding. **#2 is a packed Rust struct**, which the project rules
forbid as the compatibility representation, and it is not the type this codec
uses, so it is a latent duplicate rather than an active conflict. Its own tests
at `common/src/tables.rs:1046-1047` (`size_of::<TQuickslot>() == 2`) and `:1098`
(`offset_of!(TQuickslot, pos) == 1`) are layout assertions, which is a different
thing from a compatibility representation, so they are not themselves a
violation. **This slice changes none of the three.** The conflict is recorded so
a dedicated cleanup slice can decide whether to reconcile or delete the `common`
copy, instead of having it discovered by accident.

Two further duplicates in the same family: `common/src/tables.rs:28` declares
`QUICKSLOT_MAX_NUM: usize = 36` and `common/src/constants.rs:59` declares
`QUICKSLOT_MAX_NUM: u32 = 36`. Two constants, two Rust types, one value, both
correct, and a duplication hazard for a caller that imports the wrong one.

The duplication matters because this two-byte primitive is shared across **three
wire directions**: CG 16 (this record), GC 28 (`HEADER_GC_QUICKSLOT_ADD` at
`packet.h:1508-1513` and `Packet.h:1854-1859`, both 4 bytes), and the DB
player-load payload `TQuickslot quickslot[QUICKSLOT_MAX_NUM]` at
`server/server/common/tables.h:615`.

### 150.11 Implementation

`protocol/src/cg_quickslot_add.rs` is the codec. It exposes
`CG_QUICKSLOT_ADD_WIRE_SIZE` (4), `CG_QUICKSLOT_ADD_PAYLOAD_SIZE` (3), the
`CgQuickslotAdd` struct with `pos` and `slot`, the `CgQuickslotAddError` enum
with `Truncated`/`LengthMismatch`/`InvalidHeader`, and `new`, `header`, `encode`,
`encode_into`, `to_frame`, `decode`, `decode_frame`. Both decoders check the
exact length before the header byte, and the header before any payload byte.
There are no `allow(clippy)` suppressions, no packed structs, no `unsafe`, no
`repr(...)`, and no `transmute`.

`protocol/src/lib.rs` gained one `pub mod cg_quickslot_add;` line and the
additive derives `PartialEq`, `Eq`, `Hash`, and `Default` on `TQuickslot`, which
previously derived only `Debug, Clone, Copy` and so could not be a field of a
record with ordinary value semantics. The wire domain is unchanged: both fields
stay raw `u8` and neither is range-checked.

`protocol/src/cg_inventory.rs` was not changed. `protocol/tests/cg_wiring.rs`
gained a public-surface test for the new module and for the shared `TQuickslot`
primitive, so that removing either `pub mod` line is detectable, which is the gap
Section 149.9 found and closed.

### 150.12 Receipt

`protocol/src/cg_quickslot_add.rs` is 21,155 bytes and 556 lines, SHA-256
beginning `127fe8cc0398373e`. It carries 16 module tests. The public-API addition to `protocol/tests/cg_wiring.rs` took that
file to 10,906 bytes and 295 lines.

The mutation sweep queued **17** cases, including the two that specifically test
that no gameplay validation was added (`pos` clamped to 35, and `slot.type`
clamped to 3), the dead-module case that Section 149's first sweep found missing
coverage for, and a case that corrupts the shared primitive's width from 2 to 3.
**All 17 were caught. There were no survivors and no unrun cases.**

The late-binary control was supplied explicitly, because the harness has no
built-in control case. It changed a real assertion in
`world/tests/world_baseline.rs`, ran in its own pass, and **fired**: status
`CAUGHT`, exit 101, one failure, failing target `-p world --test world_baseline`,
restoration `OK`. This proves the `--no-fail-fast` gate and the failing-target
extraction are real rather than assumed.

The closure gates all exited **0**: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, strict
`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked --offline -- -D warnings`, and
`RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --locked --offline`.

**1,128 tests passed and 0 failed across 28 test binaries**, plus **6 workspace
doc-tests**. Section 149 closed at 1,111 tests across 28 binaries, so the delta
is 17: the 16 module tests plus the one new public-API wiring test.

Repository members now stand at **140 Rust files and 97,251 lines** excluding
`tools/`, and **141 files and 98,052 lines** including the 801-line
`tools/packet_compare/src/main.rs`. Section 149 closed at 139 files and 96,657
lines excluding `tools/`, so this slice adds one file and the new module, the
wiring test, and the single `pub mod` line.

Final hygiene: 13 `.DS_Store` and 5 `.bak` preserved, **0** `.mutbak` left
behind by the sweep, the 22 pre-existing tracked deletions untouched, and 53
status records. `protocol/src/cg.rs` remains absent, `/workspace/target` is
present, and the Section 149 placeholder timestamp `2026-09-25 23:5x UTC` was
corrected to `2026-09-25 23:55 UTC` while closing this section.
