## 229g. The target: a click on a player or a monster shows its hit points, and the targeters follow each change

A client clicking any character sends `CG_TARGET` (0x3d) with its VID. Legacy answers with
`GC_TARGET` (0x3f), and from then on sends the clicker the target's hit points each time they
change. Until 229g the Rewrite had no analyzer for `CG_TARGET` in the game phase, so
`report_step` closed the connection: **a click on any player, NPC or monster disconnected the
client.** 229g ports `CInputMain::Target`, `CHARACTER::SetTarget`, `ClearTarget` and
`BroadcastTargetPacket`, and the loading phase's consume of a stray `CG_TARGET` or `CG_ITEM_USE`.
`G/` below means `server/server/game/` and `C/` means `server/server/common/`.

### 229g.1 What landed

- **The analyzer** (`prodomo/src/main.rs`):
  - `CG_TARGET` in the game phase goes to `target_step` through `world_step`, which also takes the
    three motion records. It decodes `CgTarget`, ignores a character outside the world, and hands
    the VID to the world without waiting (`GameLoopController::target`, `GameCommand::Target`);
    the descriptor waits for the command to settle before it reads the next frame, as a relay does.
  - `is_consumed` names the records an analyzer consumes with nothing done: `CG_ITEM_USE` and
    `CG_TARGET` in the login, select and loading phases (`@fixme120`,
    `G/input_login.cpp:1254-1257`), and `CG_ENTER_GAME` in the game phase, which had an arm of its
    own. Folding both into one arm keeps `analyze` under clippy's 100 lines.
- **The world** (`prodomo/src/game_state/target.rs`, new):
  - `Targets` keeps `m_pkChrTarget` and `m_set_pkChrTargetedBy` as one relation: each targeter's
    target, and each target's targeters in VID order.
  - `GameState::target` is `CInputMain::Target` and `SetTarget` (`G/input_main.cpp:2249-2269`,
    `G/char.cpp:6458-6598`). No building object has a VID (V6), so it goes straight to `SetTarget`
    with the character the VID names on the clicker's own Channel and map: a player with a body
    there or an NPC standing there, and none for anything else (VID 0 included). The same target
    returns with nothing sent. On a castle map (181 to 183) a character that is not a GM returns,
    and every character is `GM_PLAYER`. Otherwise the relation is updated and the clicker is sent
    `GC_TARGET`.
  - The record: a maximum that is not positive shows 0, 0, 0; a player shows
    `MINMAX(0, hp * 100 / max, 100)`, its hit points and its maximum; a horse (races 20101 to
    20109) with no rider, which is every horse, shows 100, 100, 100; any other NPC shows its
    percentage, hit points and maximum. A monster (`CHAR_TYPE_MONSTER`) whose race flags reach
    `RACE_FLAG_ATT_ELEC` carries `bElement`: the first of the six element flags its flags lie
    within 1024 of, 1 for `ATT_ELEC` to 6 for `ATT_DARK`, and 6 when the loop runs out
    (`G/char.cpp:6575-6592`). The alliance fields are false and 0. No target sends VID 0 and zeros.
  - `GameState::clear_target` is `ClearTarget` (`G/char.cpp:6419-6456`). `leave_world` calls it
    right after the trade's cancel, as `Destroy` calls it near its start (`G/char.cpp:654`): the
    leaver's target forgets it, and each character targeting it loses its target and is sent VID 0,
    before the view's removal.
  - `GameState::broadcast_targets` is `BroadcastTargetPacket` (`G/char.cpp:6600-6661`). It runs at
    the end of every command and every Pulse, and sends each queued hit-point change of each online
    player to the characters targeting it, oldest first.
- **The hit points** (`world/src/character/points.rs`): `PointChange`'s `POINT_HP` arm queues the
  hit points and the maximum after `SetHP`, whatever the amount, as legacy calls
  `BroadcastTargetPacket` there (`G/char.cpp:4247-4263`). `Points::take_target_broadcasts` hands the
  queue to the world.
- **A monster's hit points** (`world/src/npc.rs`): `Npc` gains `hp`, `max_hp` and `race_flag`.
  `create` sets the maximum to the proto's `dwMaxHP`, as `ComputePoints` does for a non-player
  (`G/char.cpp:3017`), fills the hit points to it, and keeps the race flags. Nothing lowers the hit
  points yet.
- **A doc correction.** `protocol::cg_pick::CgTarget`'s field doc said legacy does nothing when
  `FindObjectByVID` fails. It calls `SetTarget` with what `CHARACTER_MANAGER::Find` finds, and a VID
  that names nothing clears the target.

### 229g.2 What the client sees

- A click on a player: `GC_TARGET` with its VID, percentage, hit points and maximum, and element 0.
  A level 1 assassin stored with 325 hit points shows 50, 325 and 650.
- A click on a monster: its VID, 100 and its proto's maximum twice, and its element. The stray dog
  (vnum 101, `MAX_HP` 126, `RACE_FLAG` `ANIMAL`) shows 100, 126, 126 and element 0.
- The same click again: nothing. A click on nothing, or a VID 0: VID 0 and zeros, if there was a
  target.
- Each change of the target's hit points, a potion's tick among them: the new percentage, hit points
  and maximum.
- The target leaving the world: VID 0 and zeros, then its removal from the view.
- A client that clicks or uses an item while it loads keeps its connection.

### 229g.3 Divergences and Defects

- **V15, new** (STATUS): the characters targeting one are walked by VID (V1); `CheckTarget` waits
  for the player recovery event, so a target is kept at any distance until it leaves the world; a
  death clears no killer's target, since nothing dies; a horse has no rider and shows 100; and no
  character is a GM or polymorphed, so nobody targets on a castle map and nobody shows as a horse.
- **Four Defects not reproduced** (STATUS):
  - `CHARACTER_MANAGER::Find` finds a VID on any map, so a modified client can target, and follow
    the hit points of, a character on another map of the Core (`G/input_main.cpp:2268`). The Rewrite
    finds a target on the clicker's own Channel and map, as its click, shop and trade do.
  - `ClearTarget` and `BroadcastTargetPacket` never set `bElement`, so the byte is whatever the
    stack held. The Rewrite sends 0.
  - `SetTarget` and `BroadcastTargetPacket` multiply the hit points by 100 in an `int`
    (`G/char.cpp:6493`, `:6555`, `:6624`), which wraps past 21,474,836. The Rewrite multiplies in 64
    bits; the owner's largest maximum is 12,958,000.
  - `ComputePoints` reads a monster's `DWORD dwMaxHP` into an `int` (`G/char.cpp:3017`). The
    Rewrite holds a maximum past `i32::MAX` at `i32::MAX`; none of the owner's is.
- **No new provisional decision and no new owner question.** The element loop's fall-through
  value 6 looked like a Quirk for a monster with a flag above `ATT_DARK`. It is also `ATT_DARK`'s own
  value, and no monster of the owner's carries a flag above it with an element (229g.6), so it
  changes nothing the owner's players see.

### 229g.4 Not ported yet

- `CheckTarget`, with the rest of the player `recovery_event` (`G/char.cpp:3172-3285`): the 4800
  drop, `DistributeSP`, `UpdateKillerMode`, the poison check and the hit-point regeneration.
  `event.char.recovery_event` stays `missing`, with a 229g note.
- The killer's target clear on a death (`G/char_battle.cpp:1275-1276`): with combat.
- `G/target.cpp`'s quest target arrows (`event.target.target_event`) and `__SEND_TARGET_INFO__`'s
  drop list (`CG_TARGET_INFO_LOAD`), so `sys.combat.target` is `partial`.
- The horse's rider (`GetVictim`, `GetHorseHealth`), the polymorph and the GM levels.

### 229g.5 Correction to 229f.5

229f.5 asked "whether the owner's live server runs the OX, war and siege schedules". There is no live
server. The owner runs none: there is no `prodomo.toml` beyond the example, the test store is a fresh
database, and the owner gave only the legacy Game data. The open point is whether the OX event and
the guild, kingdom and siege wars should run once the server opens. Owner question 27 already says
so; only the 229f.5 sentence was wrong.

### 229g.7 Corrections, findings and controls

- **The session's first test runs used rustup's 1.98 `cargo`.** `~/.cargo/bin` comes first on the
  interactive shell's `PATH`, so `cargo test` built with Rust 1.98.1, which warns about a test in
  `prodomo/src/account_player.rs` that 1.85.1 does not, and `/usr/bin/cargo-clippy` then refused
  the 1.98 artifacts with `E0514`. Every later build, test, sweep and gate in 229g ran with
  `/usr/bin` first on `PATH`, so with cargo and rustc 1.85.1.
- **The test database container had stopped** (`prodomo-pg18`, exited 0 about 28 minutes before
  the first database run of the session), so the first full run failed every database test at
  `CREATE DATABASE`. It was started again with `podman start`; nothing else changed.
- **A test compared points across a command that now drains the queue.**
  `leaving_hands_back_the_points_and_ends_the_recovery` held a copy of the points with the potion's
  queued change, and the `KeptOf` command's broadcast emptied the live queue. The test now takes the
  copy's queue, and asserts it was not empty, before the comparison.
- **The first element test assumed `ATT_ELEC | TREE | ANIMAL` shows `ATT_ELEC`.** It shows
  `ATT_FIRE`: 3073 lies 1025 from 2048 and 1023 from 4096. That is legacy's arithmetic, and the test
  now pins it.
- **The analyzer passed clippy's 100-line limit** with two new arms. The consumes became one
  `is_consumed` arm and `CG_TARGET` joined the motion records under `world_step`.
- **The first gate run failed one test without the database, an old race.**
  `a_grant_sent_from_tokio_is_applied_on_the_thread_that_owns_the_world`
  (`prodomo/tests/game_loop_thread.rs`) read the Pulse counter once, right after the grant's answer.
  The loop applies a drained command and only then steps the Pulse after it (`game_loop.rs`
  `LoopRuntime::run`), so the answer can arrive while the counter is still 0. It passed in the
  database run of the same gates. The test now waits up to a second for the first Pulse before it
  asserts. Nothing in 229g touches the loop; the failing run is in `.scratch/tmp/l229g/gates-first/`.
- **The second gate run failed two chat scenarios with the database, an old harness gap.**
  `a_shout_reaches_its_empire_on_every_channel` and `a_talking_line_reaches_the_map_including_its_sender`
  each read a `GC_CHARACTER_POINT_CHANGE` of `POINT_STAMINA` to 800 (`bAmount` false, so the amount
  is 0) where they expected silence or a chat line. Yankee is stored with the column's default
  stamina of 0, so the refill of ledger 229d (`G/char_affect.cpp:219-221`) comes three seconds after
  the body stops. A run slowed by the gates' load lets those three seconds pass inside the scenario.
  These are the scenarios the 229g sweep saw fail under load (229g.8). The record is legacy's, so
  the harness now skips it: `is_stamina_refill` joins the revive timer and the monster records in
  `Keyed::read_game` and `Keyed::quiet_for`. The two scenarios about the refill read it raw and
  still assert it. The failing run is in `.scratch/tmp/l229g/gates-second/`.

## 229h. The regen event: each regen runs on its timer and stands what it lacks, and an ore vein ends

Legacy gives each timed regen entry a `regen_event` that reruns `regen_spawn(regen, false)` every
`time` seconds, and gives each ore vein a `kill_ore_load_event` that destroys it 7 to 15 minutes
after it stands. 229f stood every map's characters up once at boot and kept each regen with its
count and its first fire's draw, but nothing read them: nothing respawned and an ore vein lived for
ever. 229h ports `regen_event`, `kill_ore_load_event` and the part of `CHARACTER::Destroy` a
non-player reaches today. `G/` below means `server/server/game/`.

### 229h.1 What landed

- **The units a regen lacks** (`world/src/npc.rs`): `Regen::missing` is legacy's
  `max_count - count` (`G/regen.cpp:330`), 0 for a negative or exceeded maximum. Legacy's `num` is
  a `DWORD`, so a count above the maximum would wrap to some four billion units; the Rewrite's
  saturates. `regen_spawn` now takes the units to stand, which boot passes as `max_count` and a
  later run as `missing()`.
- **`Respawner`** (`world/src/npc.rs`, new): the spawner's tables (`Arc`s of the mob protos, the
  mob groups and the locale names, which `main.rs`'s `NpcData` now holds) and the VID counter boot
  left (`NpcSpawner::into_vids`). `respawn` runs `regen_spawn` for a regen's missing units on its
  map's region and cells, drawing from the world's dice, and answers the characters that stood and
  their count. VIDs go on from where boot stopped, so none is reused.
- **The schedule** (`prodomo/src/game_state/regen.rs`, new):
  - `Regens` keeps the respawner, the hosted cells, each map's region and the due events, a
    `BTreeSet` of (Pulse, event): `Due::Vein(vid)` or `Due::Regen { channel, map, at }`.
  - `stand_npcs` ends with `schedule_map`: each regen's first run `first_fire` seconds on (229f
    drew it as `number(0, 16)` plus its time, `G/regen.cpp:688`) and each ore vein's end at its
    drawn lifetime (`number(420, 900)` seconds, `G/char.cpp:2569`). A map stood again drops its
    old runs.
  - `process_pulse` runs `run_regens` after the warp NPCs: every event due on or before the Pulse,
    in (Pulse, event) order.
  - `fire_regen` is `regen_event` (`G/regen.cpp:582-599`): it schedules the next run `time` seconds
    on, returns when the regen lacks nothing, and otherwise respawns. `stand_more` adds what stood
    to the map's list (copy on write, `Arc::make_mut`), indexes each VID, shows each in the view,
    which sends its insert to each player that now sees it, schedules a new vein's end, starts a
    warp or goto NPC's event, and adds the count.
  - `install_respawner` hands the world the respawner and the cells; `main.rs`'s `stand_up_npcs`
    calls it after boot. Until then a run spawns nothing.
- **`Destroy` of a non-player** (`GameState::destroy_npc`), in legacy's order
  (`G/char.cpp:572-790`): a VID that names nothing is refused (`G/char_manager.cpp:131-136`); its
  regen counts one fewer (`:572-583`); each character following it follows no one, as a group
  master's party is deleted (`:661-676`); `ClearTarget` sends VID 0 to each one targeting it
  (`:654`); each viewer is sent its removal (`:786-789`); the VID index and the map's list let it
  go, the last character taking its place; and the warp list drops it. An ore vein's end calls it.
- `WarpNpc::vid` and `target::target_record` are now visible to the module.

### 229h.2 What the client sees

- Nothing new on a map whose regens are full, which is every regen boot stood completely: each
  run finds nothing missing. A unit boot could not place (236 on Channel 1, 229f) is tried again
  on each run, as legacy does, and appears in view when a try succeeds.
- An ore vein disappears 7 to 15 minutes after it stands: a player that targeted it gets
  `GC_TARGET` with VID 0, each viewer gets its `GC_CHARACTER_DEL`, and at its regen's next run a
  new vein stands in the regen's box with a new VID and its own lifetime.

### 229h.3 Divergences and Defects

- **V16 (new).** The events due on one Pulse run by Pulse, an ore vein's end before a regen, then
  by VID or by map and entry, where legacy runs its event heap's order. A map keeps its
  non-players in a list, and a destroyed one's place is taken by the last; only the Rewrite's own
  index sees the list. A run whose VIDs are exhausted logs a warning and stands nothing.
- **A legacy Defect not reproduced.** `regen_spawn`'s `num` is `DWORD` (`G/regen.cpp:326-330`),
  so a count above the maximum would make one run spawn about four billion units. Nothing in
  legacy is known to raise the count past it, but `--m_pkRegen->count` is marked "Is this really
  safe?" (`G/char.cpp:580`). The Rewrite's `missing()` saturates at 0, under the owner's standing
  decision to fix legacy bugs directly (2026-10-14).

### 229h.4 Not ported yet

- The dungeon regen (`dungeon_regen_event`, `G/regen.cpp:493`), its `IsValidRegen` check and
  `DeadCharacter`: there are no dungeons yet.
- Every other part of `Destroy`: a non-player has no shop, exchange, safebox, horse, pet, affect or
  skill event yet, and no state machine, stone or victim. A group's party is not kept, only each
  member's leader.
- Every other way a non-player ends: nothing dies yet, so only an ore vein's end makes room for a
  respawn.

### 229h.5 The owner's decision on proofs

The owner decided on 2026-10-14 that an in-memory test is enough to prove a Parity row where a
binary scenario is impractical, and that bugs and backdoors found in the original are fixed
directly. An ore vein lives 7 to 15 minutes and no config shortens it. So
`event.char.kill_ore_load_event` is `ported` on the world test
`an_ore_vein_ends_at_its_time_and_its_regen_stands_another`. `.scratch/parity/spec.md` now
allows a `path::name` scenario cell. `inventory_rows_keep_the_rules` checks the file holds

`a_scenario_cell_names_a_scenario_here_or_a_world_test_by_its_path`. The decision is also in

### 229h.7 Corrections, findings and controls

- **The draft's vein test read a stamina refill.** The world fixture entered its player at stamina
  800 against a maximum of 820, so the refill of 229d reached the inbox at Pulse 75, inside the
  vein's quiet window. The regen tests enter the player above its maximum. This is the same
  record 229g.7 found in the binary.
- **A boot-wiring mutant cannot be seen from the binary.** Without a death, a binary scenario sees
  a respawn only after a vein's 7 to 15 minutes. `boot_hands_the_regens_their_spawner_and_the_vids_it_left`
  runs `stand_up_npcs` itself and pulses its world past a vein's life.
- **229g's refill skip had a gap.** `Keyed::quiet_for` sizes each record from its header before it
  asks whether the record may arrive, and its table had no `GC_CHARACTER_POINT_CHANGE`. So a refill
  inside a quiet window still panicked with "header 17", before `is_stamina_refill` was asked. The
  sweep's baseline failed on `a_pose_reaches_the_view_including_its_sender` this way. Three parity
  suites run at once reproduced it, in that scenario and in `a_shout_reaches_its_empire_on_every_channel`.
  The table now sizes the record, and only a refill passes. The 229g gates passed because no
  refill landed in a quiet window that time.
- **The revive's end inside a move.** Under the same load, `an_armour_is_worn_swapped_and_taken_off_and_the_store_follows`
  read the revive affect's `GC_AFFECT_REMOVE`, which comes 5 seconds after entry, inside a move's

  - every scenario whose server takes too long to log "Accepting clients".

## 229i. The monster state machine: the NPCs a player stands near wait, wander, speak and run away

Legacy runs a state machine (`CFSM`) for every character in `m_set_pkChrState`. The sectrees put a
non-player in that set while a player stands near it and take it out when none does. Each Pulse,
`CHARACTER_MANAGER::Update` runs the due ones. A non-player with no victim is in Idle or Move:
- it waits;
- one time in seven it walks or runs to a random point;
- a coward runs away;
- a waiting one may say a line of `locale.monster_chat`.

Until 229i every NPC 229f stood stayed at its spawn point and never spoke. 229i ports the state set,
`CFSM`, `StateIdle`, `StateMove`, `Goto` and its `FUNC_WAIT`, `CowardEscape` and
`MonsterChat(MONSTER_CHAT_WAIT)` for a character with no victim. It also ports the sectrees' player
count, which starts and stops the machines. `G/` below means `server/server/game/`.

### 229i.1 What landed

- **The sectrees' player count** (`prodomo/src/game_state/view.rs`). `MapIndex` keeps
  `m_iPCCount` for each sectree: the players standing in its nine. The sectrees ask for each start
  and stop of the state set as a `Wake`:
  - **Arrival.** A player entering a sectree raises the count of the nine around it
    (`IncreasePC`, `G/sectree.cpp:78-86`).
  - **A move.** A player moving raises the new nine before it lowers the old (`:128-149`), so a
    sectree in both never reaches 0.
  - **Leaving.** A leaving player lowers the count (`:160-175`).
  - **A count reaching 0.** A sectree left with no player stops every NPC in it (`DecreasePC`,
    `:88-117`).
  - **An NPC entering.** An NPC entering a sectree whose count is above 0 starts (`:150-155`).
  - **A player's view.** A player's view taking an NPC in starts it, whether or not the NPC was
    seen before (`G/entity_view.cpp:110-118`).
  - **Warp and goto NPCs.** The world never starts one.
- **The state set and `CFSM`** (`prodomo/src/game_state/mob_ai.rs`, new):
  - `Minds` keeps each NPC's `Mind`, the running set and `no_wander`. A `Mind` holds:
    - the current state and the asked one (`m_pNewState`);
    - the next update's Pulse and the state's duration;
    - the rotation, the walk mode and the move (start, destination, start time and duration).
  - A new character asks for Idle and waits 1 Pulse (`G/char.cpp:263-264`). A start puts the NPC
    in the set with its next update one Pulse after the Pulse it was asked on, and an NPC already in
    the set keeps its next update (`StartStateMachine`, `:5322-5331`).
  - `process_pulse` applies the wakes first, so a wake asked between two Pulses counts from the
    earlier one, as legacy's heart pulse does. `run_minds` runs after the player moves: it applies
    the wakes again, then updates every NPC of the set whose next Pulse is due, in VID order (V1).
  - The update is `CFSM::Update` (`G/FSM.cpp`, `UpdateStateMachine`, `G/char.cpp:5338-5348`): an
    asked state becomes the state, the state runs, and the next update is its duration later.
- **Idle** (`StateIdle`, `G/char_state.cpp:362-387`):
  - **Horses.** A horse (type 8, or races 20101 to 20109) does nothing.
  - **Stones.** A stone waits 1 second.
  - **Monsters** (`__StateIdle_Monster`, `:626-736`):
    - a coward runs `CowardEscape`;
    - otherwise it waits `number(1, 3)` seconds when aggressive and `number(3, 5)` when not;
    - unless `no_wander` or `AIFLAG_NOMOVE` holds it, one time in seven (`number(0, 6) == 0`) it
      turns to a random heading and runs 300 to 700 units;
    - one that does not walk calls `MonsterChat(MONSTER_CHAT_WAIT)`.
  - **Any other non-player** (`__StateIdle_NPC`, `:507-624`):
    - it calls `MonsterChat` and waits 5 seconds;
    - unless it is a guard (11000, 11002, 11004) or `AIFLAG_NOMOVE` holds it, one time in seven it
      walks 200 to 400 units at a walk;
    - the first walk tells its view `GC_WALK_MODE` (`SetNowWalking`).
  - **The walk's point.** A walk needs both its point and its half-way point movable. The offset is
    `GetDeltaByDegree` in `f32` (`delta_by_degree`, clockwise from north).
- **`CowardEscape`** (`G/char_state.cpp:282-321`). The coward tries the reaches 3000 to 5000, then
  1000 to 3000, then 500 to 1000, with eight tries each. Each try turns to a random heading and
  draws a distance. It takes the first point whose every hundredth of the way is movable. A coward
  with no such way stays.
- **`Goto` and `SendMovePacket`** (`G/char.cpp:3471-3508`, `:3624-3636`):
  - A `Goto` to the NPC's own point or its current destination sets no new way (`:3473-3487`).
  - Otherwise it sets the way and its duration at the fall-back motion speed (V2), with the NPC's
    moving speed. The state duration becomes 4 Pulses, and the state becomes Move.
  - The view is told `GC_MOVE` with `FUNC_WAIT`, the heading as `rotation / 5`, the destination
    and the duration.
- **Move** (`StateMove`, `G/char_state.cpp:782-928`). Every 4 Pulses the NPC moves to the point the
  elapsed share of the duration reaches, turning toward it with z 0, through the view's
  `move_body`; a step off every sectree is not taken (229i.3). At the end it asks for Idle with a
  wait of `number(1, 3)` seconds. Legacy runs `UpdateSectree` in `StateMove` only for a player, so
  a non-player's view is not sampled while it walks.
- **`MonsterChat`** (`G/char.cpp:7555-7600`):
  - **Monsters.** A monster speaks one time in 61 (`number(0, 60) == 0`), the line
    `MONSTER_CHAT_WAIT * 3 + number(1, 3)` of its race.
  - **Other non-players.** A guard speaks one time in 7 and any other non-player one time in 31, a
    line `number(1, table.getn(...))`.
  - **How the line is sent.** The line is a `GC_CHAT` `CHAT_TYPE_TALKING` the speaker says to its
    view, with its VID, empire 0 and the text with its zero byte. It is a talk, not a server line,
    so it does not go through `chat_line`.
  - **Where the line comes from.** `quest::host::Host` gains `monster_chat_count` and
    `monster_chat_line`. They read `locale.monster_chat[race]` of the loaded libraries as
    `ScriptToString` returns the expression (`questlua.cpp:33`). A world with no quests says
    nothing.
- **An insert of an NPC mid-walk** (`view_encode.rs`, `loading_phase::npc_add_at`). The insert
  carries the Mind's rotation and the point the walk has reached, then the walk's `FUNC_MOVE` with
  the duration left and the NPC's walk mode, as `EncodeInsertPacket` does for a moving character.
- **The wiring.** `[game] no_wander` reaches the world (`with_no_wander`). A replaced map's NPCs and
  a destroyed NPC forget their Mind. `gamedata::mob_proto` gains `CHAR_TYPE_HORSE`,
  `AIFLAG_NOMOVE` and `AIFLAG_COWARD`.

### 229i.2 What the client sees

- **Monsters.** Each monster within a sectree of a player waits 1 to 5 seconds. One time in seven
  it runs 300 to 700 units. The client gets `GC_MOVE` (`FUNC_WAIT`, argument 0) with its heading,
  destination and duration, and draws the run.
- **Other non-players.** A non-player NPC other than a guard walks 200 to 400 units one time in
  seven. Its first walk is preceded by `GC_WALK_MODE` `WALKMODE_WALK`.
- **Chat.** Now and then a waiting NPC says a line of its race over its head.
- **Joining late.** A player entering the view of an NPC mid-walk sees it where the walk has
  reached, still walking.
- **No player near.** An NPC whose sectree no player stands near any more stops on the next Pulse
  and keeps the point it reached.
- **With `no_wander = true`.** No monster walks.

### 229i.3 Divergences and Defects

- **V1 (extended).** The NPCs of the state set update in VID order, after the Pulse's player moves.
  Legacy walks `m_set_pkChrState`, a set ordered by pointer.
- **V2 (extended).** No monster `.msa` clip is loaded, so every non-player moves at the fall-back
  300 units a second. Legacy reads the race's run or walk clip.
- **A legacy Defect not reproduced.**
  - **Legacy.** `Sync` kills a non-player whose step lands where no sectree stands (`Dead()`,
    `G/char.cpp:3403-3407`).
  - **The Rewrite.** It leaves the NPC where it stood and does not take the step.
  - **Reach.** An idle walk cannot reach this: its point and its half-way point are movable, and
    the sectrees form one rectangle.
  - It is in STATUS's Defect list, under the owner's standing decision to fix legacy bugs directly
    (2026-10-14).

### 229i.4 Not ported yet

- **The fight.** No NPC has a victim yet. `sys.combat.core` will bring:
  - `FindVictim`, `BeginFight` and the Battle state;
  - an aggressive monster's search;
  - the guard's search;
  - the return home.

  An aggressive monster near a player therefore wanders as a peaceful one does, with its own
  shorter wait. The berserk and god-speed resets of `__StateIdle_Monster` (`:643-649`) also wait
  for it: 148 protos carry `BERSERK` and 46 `GODSPEED`, but only Battle turns either on
  (`:1125-1133`).
- **The protector.** `GetProtege` and `Follow` wait for the group's party and follow.
- **The other states.** These wait for their systems:
  - a stone's spawns at each tenth of its hit points;
  - Santa;
  - the war flags;
  - `StateHorse`.
- **The monster clips and the walk-duration recomputes** (V2).
- **The `test_server` walk toggle.** Not ported: production never runs it.

## 229j. The player hits a monster: a punch or a weapon lands with legacy's damage, a lethal one stuns, and the monster dies and goes

A client hitting a character sends `CG_ATTACK`, which names the victim by VID. `CInputMain::Attack`
finds it, and `CHARACTER::Attack` goes on only while `battle_is_attackable` holds. Then:
- `battle_melee_attack` measures the reach;
- `battle_hit` computes the damage (`CalcMeleeDamage`, `CalcAttBonus`);
- `CHARACTER::Damage` draws its chances, takes the hit points and shows the hit.

A monster left with no hit points is stunned, and dies 3 seconds later (`StunEvent`, `Dead`). A
second later `dead_event` destroys it. A hit monster that lives gives its hit points back
(`recovery_event`). The attacker claims the monster (`SetSyncOwner`), and death releases the claim
(`ClearSync`).

Until 229j no NPC could be hit, and a `CG_ATTACK` closed the connection as a record no analyzer
reads. 229j ports a player's melee hit on a monster from the record to the monster's removal. `G/`
below means `server/server/game/`.

### 229j.1 What landed

- **The hit** (`world/src/character/combat/melee.rs`, new). The world crate's placeholder
  `melee_damage` and `normal_hit` are replaced by legacy's code, with every draw taken from the
  `Dice` in legacy's order:
  - **`melee_reach`** (`G/battle.cpp:172-201`). The reach is 300. For a `MELEE` monster it is the
    attack range plus 15 %, at least 350; `GetMobAttackRange` adds 300 for a ship-defence minion
    (`G/char.cpp:2656-2676`, vnums 3401 to 3605 and 3950 to 3959). A hydra is reached from 600
    further. The distance is `DISTANCE_APPROX`, and a victim exactly at the reach is hit.
  - **`calc_melee_damage`** (`CalcMeleeDamage`, `G/battle.cpp:489-666`):
    - the weapon's early returns: a worn item that is no weapon, a bow, or a sub-type the melee
      does not swing deals 0 with no draw;
    - the weapon's roll, or the bare fist's `number(0, 0)`;
    - the low roll, `number(1, 5)` below 3;
    - the hit rating (`CalcAttackRating`, `:271-297`), with the attacker's level in the evasion
      (owner question 28);
    - `CalcAttBonus`'s arms for a player on a non-player (`:299-415`) before the defence:
      the race bonuses, the monster, Metin and boss bonuses and the job resists.
  - **`strike_npc`** (`battle_hit`, `:760-817`, and the `DAMAGE_TYPE_NORMAL` branch of
    `CHARACTER::Damage`, `G/char_battle.cpp:1744-2436`):
    - the weapon resist of the victim;
    - the critical and penetrating chances, each drawn only when its point is above 0;
    - the steals of hit and spell points, the hit recovery and the mana burn;
    - the bonuses and defences, a stoneskin monster's half below its `bStoneSkinPoint`, and the
      spell points a draining monster takes;
    - `NormalAttackAffect`'s draws;
    - `MonsterChat(MONSTER_CHAT_ATTACKED)`, one time in 61.

    It returns what the hit shows as `HitEvent`s, in the order legacy sends them, and how it ended
    (`Struck`): no damage, refused on a `BANPK` cell, a stunned victim killed, an already dead one,
    or the hit points taken.
- **The monster's battle points** (`world/src/npc/fight.rs`, new). `MobFight::of` holds what
  `SetProto` and `ComputeBattlePoints` give a non-player from its proto (`G/char.cpp:2466-2500`,
  `:2849-2859`):
  - the attack grade, twice the level plus twice the strength;
  - the defence grade, the level plus the vitality plus the proto's defence;
  - the enchants and resists through `ApplyMobAttribute` (`G/char_resist.cpp:235-248`).

  `Npc` gains `fight`, `stunned` (`IsStun`) and `dead` (`IsDead`).
- **The fight in the world** (`prodomo/src/game_state/fight.rs`, new):
  - **`CInputMain::Attack`** (`G/input_main.cpp:1918-2008`) and **`CHARACTER::Attack`**
    (`G/char_battle.cpp:220-328`):
    - the victim is looked for on the attacker's own Channel and map;
    - a type other than 0 (a skill) is consumed;
    - `battle_is_attackable` (`G/battle.cpp:99-152`) refuses a dead victim, a `BANPK` cell under
      either, a fake hydra, and every kind but a monster;
    - out of reach, nothing is sent;
    - within it the attacker turns to the victim and strikes.
  - **What the hit shows**, each record to its own receivers:
    - `GC_DAMAGE_INFO` only to an attacker that targets the victim (`G/char_battle.cpp:1720-1742`),
      with the damage before it is held to the hit points;
    - the victim's hit points (`GC_TARGET`) to each character that targets it, as the hit lands;
    - `GC_SPECIAL_EFFECT` of a critical or penetrating hit to the victim's view;
    - `GC_CREATE_FLY` of a steal to the victim's view;
    - the attacker's own point records to itself;
    - the monster's chat line to its view.
  - **After the hit:**
    - a hit that took hit points starts the recovery;
    - a hit that leaves none stuns the monster: the recovery ends, `GC_STUN` goes to its view, the
      killer's PID is kept, and `StunEvent` is due 75 Pulses later;
    - a hit on a stunned monster runs `Dead` at once, with no damage shown.
  - **The claim** (`SetSyncOwner`, `G/char.cpp:5469-5555`). The attacker claims the monster:
    - only within 250 by `DISTANCE_APPROX`;
    - never for a monster `AIFLAG_NOMOVE` holds;
    - not while another attacker's claim is younger than 100 ms.

    An accepted claim sends `GC_OWNERSHIP` around every time, even for the same owner, as legacy
    does. Then `OnMove(true)` stamps the attack and ends the attacker's revive-invisible affect,
    after the claim.
  - **`Dead`** (`G/char_battle.cpp:1238-1696`):
    1. the killer is the hitter, or the player whose PID the stun kept, and the PID goes back to 0;
    2. the killer's target is cleared when it is this monster;
    3. `ClearSync` sends `GC_OWNERSHIP` with no owner;
    4. `GC_DEAD` goes to the view;
    5. `dead_event` is due 25 Pulses later.

    Then `dead_event` destroys the monster (`destroy_npc`): `ClearSync` again, the targeters'
    target cleared, its removal, and its regen's count lowered so the regen can stand another.
  - **The recovery** (`G/char.cpp:3172-3314`). Every `bRegenCycle` seconds the monster gets back
    `bRegenPercent` of its maximum, at least 1, until it is full. Each step shows its targeters
    its hit points. A stun cancels it.
  - **A leaving player** releases each monster it owns, and each one's view is told
    (`ClearSync`'s `FuncClearSync`).
  - **The events** ride the regen schedule (`Due::Stun`, `Due::Dead`, `Due::Recovery`). A
    destroyed monster cancels its own.
- **The state machine** (`mob_ai.rs`):
  - a stunned monster's Idle does nothing and draws nothing (`G/char_state.cpp:362-387`);
  - a dead monster's machine does not run (`UpdateStateMachine`, `G/char.cpp:5338-5348`);
  - a monster stunned mid-walk still arrives, since `StateMove` has no stun guard.
- **The sync** (`sync.rs`, `sync_position.rs`):
  - `CG_SYNC_POSITION` reads the same claim as the hit;
  - the owner's sync moves a monster as its own step does (`npc_move`), as legacy's `Sync` does
    (`G/input_main.cpp:2149-2152`).
- **An entrant** in the dead monster's last second is shown it with `ADD_CHARACTER_STATE_DEAD`
  (`G/char.cpp:1446-1447`).
- **The wiring:**
  - `CG_ATTACK` (2) is a world step (`attack_step`, `GameCommand::Attack`).
  - `CG_SHOOT`, `CG_FLY_TARGETING`, `CG_ADD_FLY_TARGETING` and `CG_USE_SKILL` are consumed in
    the game phase.
  - `common::cfloat` gains `f64_to_i32`, which `CalcAttBonus`'s `double` needs.
  - `gamedata::item_kind` gains `WEAPON_MOUNT_SPEAR`.

### 229j.2 What the client sees

- **A hit.** A punch or a weapon swing on a monster within reach takes legacy's damage. If the
  player targets the monster, it is shown the number, then the monster's hit points. The
  attacker's claim (`GC_OWNERSHIP`) follows.
- **Other hits:**
  - a critical or penetrating hit shows its effect;
  - a monster now and then says its "attacked" line;
  - a steal shows its orb.
- **A lethal hit.** The monster falls stunned. Three seconds later it dies: the killer's target
  clears, the monster is released and shown dead. A second later it goes, and its regen can stand
  it again on its next run.
- **A second hit on a stunned monster** kills it at once, with no number.
- **A monster that lives** gets its hit points back every few seconds until it is full.
- **Refused hits.** A hit on a player, an NPC, a stone, out of reach, or on a `BANPK` cell does
  nothing.
- **Skills.** Skills, arrows and their targets do nothing yet, and the connection stays open.

### 229j.3 Divergences and Defects

**V17, new.** A player's first fight differs from legacy in eleven ways, (a) to (k). STATUS lists
them all. The main ones:
- only a monster is hit;
- it does not fight back (229l);
- `Dead` pays no reward;
- `NormalAttackAffect` and a gold steal draw but change nothing;
- skills and the shoot and fly frames are consumed;
- the attacker's `POS_FIGHTING` is not held;
- no party revives or is told;
- a leaving player does not yet release its own ownership (229k).

**V15 and V16, reworded:**
- V15: a monster's death now clears its killer's target; a player's death waits for 229k.
- V16: the fight's three events run by due Pulse after the ore-vein ends and the regens, in the
  order stun, death, recovery.

**Defects not reproduced**, under the owner's standing decision of 2026-10-14, in STATUS's list:
- **A cross-map victim** (`G/input_main.cpp:1975`, `G/battle.cpp:172-210`).
  - **Legacy.** `CHARACTER_MANAGER::Find` searches every map, and the reach is measured by x and y
    alone. So a modified client can hit a monster at the same coordinates on another map of the
    Core.
  - **The Rewrite.** It finds the victim on the attacker's Channel and map.
- **The world boss's damage map** (`SetAccumulateDamageByVID`, `G/char_battle.cpp:2398-2405`).
  - **Legacy.** It grows for every victim a player hits, until the player leaves.
  - **The Rewrite.** It keeps no such map.
- **The recovery's `int` product** (`G/char.cpp:3191-3240`).
  - **Legacy.** The maximum times the percentage wraps past `INT_MAX`.
  - **The Rewrite.** It multiplies in 64 bits.

**Legacy kept, recorded:**
- the damage shown before it is held to the hit points (overkill is shown);
- a lethal hit only stuns;
- the penetrate draw that a later branch wastes;
- the `BLOCK` re-check on a claim (provisional; it shows only once a monster fights back);
- the attacker's level in the evasion (B5, provisional, owner question 28).

**Unreachable in 229j, noted for later:**
- `GetMaxHP() >= 0` before a division (`G/char_battle.cpp:1781`, `:2342`). The seven protos with
  `MAX_HP` 0 (9331 to 9337) are all NPCs, which are refused.
- The side effects before the `BANPK` check: `battle_is_attackable` refuses a `BANPK` cell first on
  the melee path.
- The `test_server` debug chats of `Damage` (`:1920-1921`, `:1946-1947`, `:1960-1961`,
  `:2031-2032`, `:2348`, `:2358`) are left to the `test_server` audit (owner question 5).
  `/cannot_dead` waits for the GM commands.

### 229j.5 Scenario and parity inventory

- **The parity scenarios go from 91 to 95.** Each enters Alpha with `no_wander` and ends its

  - **`a_punch_on_a_targeted_dog_stuns_it_and_it_dies_three_seconds_later_and_leaves`.** A stray
    dog (vnum 101, 126 hit points) stands where Alpha enters. Alpha targets it and punches. Alpha
    reads, in order:
    1. `GC_DAMAGE_INFO` of 322 with `DAMAGE_NORMAL`;
    2. `GC_TARGET` at 0 %;
    3. `GC_STUN`;
    4. `GC_OWNERSHIP` of the dog to Alpha.

    At least 2 seconds later: `GC_TARGET` with no VID, `GC_OWNERSHIP` with no owner, `GC_DEAD`.
    At least half a second after that: `GC_OWNERSHIP` with no owner, then the dog's removal. The
    322 is exact (`PUNCH_ON_THE_DOG`): the bare fist's only draw is `number(0, 0)`.
  - **`a_second_punch_on_a_stunned_dog_kills_it_at_once_with_no_number`.** A second punch inside

### 229j.6 Corrections, findings and controls

- **The plan left out the release on every death.**
  - **The source.** `ClearSync` calls `SetSyncOwner(NULL)`, which sends `GC_OWNERSHIP` with no
    owner around even when no owner was set (`G/char.cpp:5491-5503`, `:5549-5555`, `:5568-5575`).
    Only a `NOMOVE` character skips it (`:5472`). `Dead` runs it before `GC_DEAD`
    (`G/char_battle.cpp:1461`), and `Destroy` before `ClearTarget` and the removal
    (`G/char.cpp:653-654`).
  - **The fix.** The scenarios and the port expect the release before `GC_DEAD` and again before
    the removal, also for a dog that never had an owner. The ore veins (20047 to 20059, all
    `NOMOVE`) keep their bytes.
- **`SetSyncOwner` resends a claim.** A draft test expected nothing for the owner's own sync.
  Legacy sends `GC_OWNERSHIP` around on every accepted claim, even for the same owner
  (`G/char.cpp:5546-5555`), and the test now expects it.
- **The owner's sync did not move the monster.** Legacy's `SyncPosition` calls `victim->Sync(x, y)`
  (`G/input_main.cpp:2149-2152`). The draft stored a non-player's synced point only as a body's.
  `sync` now moves an NPC as its own step does (`npc_move`), and
  `the_owners_sync_moves_the_monster` pins it.
- **The 229i `test_server` walk toggle.**
  - **The claim.** 229i.4 said the toggle (`G/char_state.cpp:740-746`) is not ported because
    production never runs it.
  - **The facts.** Legacy's `test_server` defaults to 1 (`G/config.cpp:72`), and none of the
    owner's `CONFIG` files turns it off (STATUS, 178.5).
  - **The correction.** The `mob_ai.rs` module doc now says the toggle waits for the
    `test_server` audit (owner question 5).
- **Four research errors:**
  - **`ENABLE_EFFECT_PENETRATE`.** The damage notes said it is not defined. It is defined
    (`G/char_battle.cpp:69`) and used at `:1929` and `:2034`, so a penetrating hit sends
    `SE_PENETRATE`.
  - **A missing draw.** The AI notes' draw list (§1.13) left out `MonsterChat(ATTACKED)`
    (`G/char_battle.cpp:2245`).
  - **Alpha's point.** The restart notes (Q8) put Alpha at (607, 540). Alpha enters at (605, 540).
  - **The commands above `POS_FIGHTING`.** The research said none. There is one, `mount`, which
    legacy refuses silently in its default arm (`G/cmd.cpp:661-684`) and the Rewrite reports as
    `NotPorted`. Nothing changes until the position is held (V17g).
- **A wrong citation in a draft.** A draft of the V17 row cited `G/input_main.cpp:2949-3009` for
  `SyncPosition`. The handler is at `:2010-2160`.
- **The first gate run used the wrong cargo.**
  - **What happened.** It was started from a shell whose PATH put rustup's `~/.cargo/bin` ahead
    of `/usr/bin`. That rustup install dates from 2026-09-30, and the rewrite did not make it. So
    `cargo build` and `cargo test` ran 1.98.1. The pinned `cargo-clippy` 0.1.85 then failed with
    E0514, "found crate `tracing` compiled by an incompatible version of rustc".
  - **What counts.** That run's 3397 passes don't count. Its logs are in
    `.scratch/tmp/l229j/gates-wrong-cargo/`.
  - **The fix.** `gates.sh` now exports `PATH=/usr/bin:$PATH` itself and writes the three
    versions to `toolchain.txt`. The second run built, linted and tested with cargo 1.85.1.
  - **Earlier runs.** 229i's clippy run was clean. Since a 1.98.1 cargo under the pinned clippy
    fails the same way, its gates most likely ran with `/usr/bin` first.

Controls for the counts and the negative claims. Each search uses `grep -a` or `awk`:

- **Legacy data:**
  - `legacy/gamedata/proto/mob_proto.txt`, one line per proto;
  - the 186 spawn files (`regen.txt`, `npc.txt`, `boss.txt` and `stone.txt`) under
    `legacy/gamedata/`, race or group in column 11;
  - the quests under `legacy/gamedata/locale/europe/quest/`.

the code (`sweep229j/tree0`), one file at a time. A workflow of three agents wrote the first three
files, one per area, and each file passed the driver's `CHECK=1`:

- **`mutants229j_a.py`, 55 mutants**, all in `prodomo/src/game_state/fight.rs`.

  - 38 in `world/src/character/combat/melee.rs`;

  - 3 in `common/src/cfloat.rs` (`f64_to_i32`) and 1 in `gamedata/src/item_kind.rs`.

  - 2 each in `game_loop_messages.rs`, `game_state.rs` and `target.rs`;
  - 1 each in `sync_position.rs` and `loading_phase.rs`.

  claim's `> 250` (`sync_position.rs`) and the ATTACKED chat draw (`melee.rs`).
- **`mutants229j_e.py`, 6 mutants:** the closing pass, every survivor rerun after it was closed.

The driver's `PARITY_OK` floor went from 91 to 95 passing parity tests: the four new scenarios.

The passes:

1. **The first pass,** 142 mutants. The baseline passed, and 136 were killed, none by a compile
   error, so every kill is semantic. 11 kills came from parity scenarios, each confirmed alone:
   - the four skill and fly mutants of `main.rs` and the skill-typed attack, by
     `skill_shoot_and_fly_frames_and_refused_victims_keep_the_connection`;
   - the six that drop or misroute `CG_ATTACK` in `main.rs`, `game_loop_messages.rs` and
     `game_state.rs`, by the three punch scenarios.

2. **The closing pass,** `mutants229j_e.py`, run in the copy after a fresh tar and the clean of

## 229k. The player dies and comes back: a lethal hit stuns, `Dead` three seconds later, and the three restarts or the automatic one

A player left with no hit points is stunned, and `StunEvent` runs `Dead` three seconds later, as
a second hit on the stunned player does at once (`G/char_battle.cpp:402-459`, `:1238-1696`).
`Dead` puts the session in `PHASE_DEAD` and shows the client its restart window. The player then
comes back by a command (`do_restart_now` and `do_restart`, `G/cmd_general.cpp:471-706`) or,
three minutes after the death, by `dead_event`, which sends it to its empire's town (`:473-525`).
`DeathPenalty` takes exp from a player a monster killed (`:330-392`).

Until 229k nothing could kill a player, `/restart_here`, `/restart_town` and `/restart_now`
answered nothing, and the session had no Dead phase. 229k ports the player's side of the death,
from the lethal hit to the restart, and the player's recovery event with `CheckTarget`. No binary
path hits a player before 229l, when the monsters fight back, so world tests prove the dead arms
(owner, 2026-10-14) and a parity scenario the living one. `G/` below means
`server/server/game/`.

### 229k.1 What landed

- **The death in the world** (`prodomo/src/game_state/death.rs`, new). `PcCombat` holds what
  legacy's `CHARACTER` keeps of a player's fight beyond its points: the stun, the death, the
  killer's PID, the death penalty flag and the three events' due Pulses.
  - **`damage_pc`** (the victim side of `CHARACTER::Damage`, `G/char_battle.cpp:2248-2255`,
    `:2376-2386`, `:2425-2433`):
    - a stunned victim dies at once, and a dead one takes nothing;
    - the damage is held to the hit points, `POINT_HP` changes, and the targeters are shown the
      hit points;
    - a hit that leaves none stuns the player and keeps a player attacker's PID.

    It has no live caller until 229l's monster melee, so it and `stun_pc` are `#[cfg(test)]`, the
    repo's pattern for a test-only helper (no `allow(dead_code)` exists in the code).
  - **`stun_pc`** (`Stun`, `:422-459`): the hit point and spell point recovery pools go to 0,
    each with its own record, which ends a drinking potion; the recovery event is cancelled;
    `GC_STUN` goes to the view, self included; the points lock (below); `StunEvent` is due 75
    Pulses later.
  - **`pc_stun_event`** (`StunEvent`, `:402-420`) runs `dead_pc` with no killer.
  - **`dead_pc`** (the player arms of `Dead`):
    1. the killer is the hitter or the player whose PID the stun kept, and the PID goes back to
       0; a player killer that targets the dead player drops its target;
    2. the position is dead; the penalty flag is set for a non-player killer and cleared
       otherwise (D5: always assigned);
    3. `ClearSync`: `GC_OWNERSHIP{0, vid}` to the view, self included, the dead player's own claim
       cleared, then each NPC it owns released;
    4. the stun event is cancelled;
    5. `GC_PHASE{6}` to self, `GC_DEAD` to the view, self included, then `GC_AFFECT_ADD` to self
       for each running affect with its remaining duration;
    6. `dead_event` is due 4500 Pulses later;
    7. the trade ends for both sides (`GC_EXCHANGE END`), the shop browsing ends
       (`GC_SHOP END`), and an open safebox closes (the `CloseSafebox` command line); the mall
       stays open, as legacy closes only the safebox.
  - **`pc_dead_event`** (`dead_event`'s player branch, `:500-525`): `GC_PHASE{5}`, the player
    stands, its hit points become half its maximum (shown as an amount), the town penalty, the
    recovery starts, `CloseRestartWindow`, then the Warp to the empire's recall point.
  - **`restart`** (`do_restart_now` and `do_restart`):
    - **a living player**, stunned included, is sent `CloseRestartWindow` and its recovery
      starts, whatever the kind (`:473-477`, `:528-533`);
    - **a player with no dead event** is sent nothing (`:486-487`, `:535-536`);
    - **now** (`:478-524`): below 300000 gold the price line; `IsHack`'s line alone (B1, B20);
      else the revive where it lies at full hit points with the here penalty and the revive
      invisibility, then `GC_CHARACTER_GOLD_CHANGE{vid, 0, gold - 300000}`, and the answer
      carries the gold delta for the store;
    - **here** (`:540-558`, `:695-704`): `IsHack`'s line alone (B24); `[LS;516;n]` while more
      than 170 seconds of the dead event are left (allowed from 226 Pulses, 9.04 seconds); else
      the revive where it lies with 50 hit points, the here penalty and the revive invisibility;
    - **town** (`:560-577`, `:683-693`): the same refusals with 173 (allowed from 151 Pulses,
      6.04 seconds); else 50 hit points, the town penalty, and the Warp to the recall point.
    - Every accepted restart first sends `CloseRestartWindow` and `GC_PHASE{5}`, stands the
      player and starts its recovery (`:579-582`, `:506-509`).
  - **`stand`** (`SetPosition(POS_STANDING)`, `G/char.cpp:1436-1470`): the stun and dead events
    are cancelled, the points unlock, and the killer's PID is cleared (D6).
  - **`recall_destination`**: `GetRecallPositionByEmpire`, else the empire start
    (`G/char_battle.cpp:508-516`, `G/cmd_general.cpp:687-690`), kept only when the atlas names
    its map and the player's Channel or the Shared Channel serves it, as `WarpSet` requires.
    Otherwise the player restarts in place with the revive invisibility (B12, B13).
    `GameState::with_recall` gives the world the atlas and the Channel maps.
  - **`death_penalty`** (`DeathPenalty`, with the fixes): the arena maps 190 to 192 take nothing;
    the flag is read and cleared first (D2, owner question 32); a town restart stops there (B11);
    below level 10, or one time in three on `number(0, 2)`, the player hears `[LS;901]`;
    otherwise the loss is the level's share of the next level's exp, at most 800000, halved by a
    worn Teardrop of Goddess (70012).
  - **`revive_invisible`** (`AddAffect(215, …, true)`, `G/char_affect.cpp:668-760`): a running
    215 is ended with `GC_AFFECT_REMOVE` and reset in place, else a new one is pushed; then
    `GC_CHARACTER_UPDATE` around, self included, the affect event, and `GC_AFFECT_ADD` to self.
  - **The player's recovery** (`StartRecoveryEvent`, `recovery_event`, `G/char.cpp:3245-3314`):
    due 75 Pulses after the entry, each restart, `dead_event` and the living arm, never while
    down; each run calls `check_target` and re-arms. `check_target` (`CheckTarget`, `:6663-6670`)
    drops a target, player or NPC, 4800 or more away by `DISTANCE_APPROX`. The hit point heal and
    `DistributeSP` wait (V18b).
  - **`clear_sync` and the leave** (V17k closed): a disconnecting player's view reads its own
    release first, `GC_OWNERSHIP{0, leaver}`, then each owned NPC's, then its removal
    (`G/char.cpp:653`, `:5549-5575`). A Warp departure sends no own release, because legacy
    removes the entity first (`:6751-6752`).
  - **A disconnect while down** (B5): the leave pays the here penalty, stands the player and
    stores 50 hit points, so the relog equals `/restart_here`. Then the three events are
    cancelled, since a player's VID is reused.
  - **`block_pc_claim`**: a sync claim on a dead player, or by a stunned or dead claimer, is
    refused with `GC_DAMAGE_INFO{victim, DAMAGE_BLOCK, 0}` to both (`SetSyncOwner`'s
    `battle_is_attackable`, `G/char.cpp:5476-5483`; `G/battle.cpp:102-123`).
- **The points** (`world/src/character/points.rs`):
  - `Points` and `PointsRow` hold `exp`, which the load fills and the save already wrote;
  - `set_down` locks `POINT_HP`, `POINT_SP` and `POINT_STAMINA` while the player is down
    (`G/char.cpp:4250`, `:4268`, `:4279`), so neither a stamina refill nor anything else changes
    them; the recovery pools still change;
  - `lose_exp` is `POINT_EXP`'s negative arm (`:4078-4191`): a loss larger than the exp stops at
    0; at or above `max_level` with a quarter of the next level's exp, nothing (B18, kept);
    the level never steps down. A positive exp change is still not ported.
- **The loss table** (`world/src/character/death_penalty.rs`, new): `exp_loss_percent`
  (`aiExpLossPercents`, `G/constants.cpp:885-899`, with `__GetExpLossPerc`'s level 0 and
  above-120 arms) and `death_penalty_loss`.
- **The guards** (legacy's dead guards and the Defects):
  - a stunned or dead attacker hits nothing (`battle_is_attackable`, `G/battle.cpp:122`);
  - a stunned player's move is refused silently, as `CanMove` refuses it (D9); a dead player's
    is shown back where it lies (the ghost arm, `G/input_main.cpp:1804-1812`);
  - a stunned or dead player uses no item (D7); a dead one drops none (`G/char_item.cpp:7467`)
    and picks up none (D10);
  - a dead player starts no trade and is offered none (`G/input_main.cpp:1385`, D10), and clicks
    no NPC (D10);
  - a dead player's pose record is refused (B25, below).
- **The descriptor** (`prodomo/src/main.rs`):
  - `write_pending` turns the world's `GC_PHASE{6}` and `GC_PHASE{5}` records
    (`phase_of_record`) into `session.set_phase` at their place in the stream; every other record
    is sent as before;
  - `main_record` names the analyzer a main-input record goes to (`MainRecord`): B25's refusal
    first (`is_dead_refused` drops `CG_CHARACTER_POSITION` while the session is Dead), then the
    records the Game and Dead phases read alike (`in_main_input`), as `PHASE_DEAD` installs
    `m_inputMain` (`G/desc.cpp:526-531`); `CInputDead` is never installed;
  - `flush_turn` and `take_order` run `stand_on_phase_change`, which clears the descriptor's
    sitting pose, when a record they wrote or the order they followed changed the phase;
  - `caller_position` gives a command line `POS_DEAD` while the session is Dead, so every command
    above `POS_DEAD` answers `[LS;918]`;
  - `hold_points` keeps the exp the world left in the held row, which the save writes;
  - `restart` runs `/restart_here`, `/restart_town` and `/restart_now` in the world, and stores a
    gold answer with `db::items::apply_transfer`.
- **The command table** (`prodomo/src/command.rs`): `restart_now` matches its whole name only
  (B8); `do_restart` is `Command::Restart(RestartKind::Town)` for `restart_town` and
  `RestartKind::Here` otherwise, and `do_restart_now` is `Command::Restart(RestartKind::Now)`.
  The kind is decided once, in the table, and the descriptor passes it on.
- **The wiring:**
  - `GameCommand::Restart` and `RestartAnswer`; `GameCommand::LeaveWorld` carries a `Departure`
    (`Disconnect` or `Warp`);
  - `Due::PcStun`, `Due::PcDead` and `Due::PcRecovery` follow the NPCs' three events on the
    schedule;
  - a player inserted while dead carries `ADD_CHARACTER_STATE_DEAD` (`G/char.cpp:1095`,
    `:1446-1447`), and `GC_CHARACTER_UPDATE`'s state flag carries the dead bit
    (`G/char.cpp:1310`);
  - `affect_add_frame` moved from `loading_phase.rs` to `affect.rs`, which both use;
  - `GameState::with_max_level` reads `[game] max_level`.
- **Removed:** the world crate's placeholder `Vitality`, `DamageOutcome` and `apply_damage`, which
  nothing but their own test called.
- **The parity harness:**
  - `parity/src/server.rs`: a new server's gate gets `START_TIMEOUT`, 120 seconds, and every
    other log line keeps `PROCESS_TIMEOUT`'s 20. See 229k.7 for why.
  - `Keyed::still` and `still_for` (`prodomo/tests/parity.rs`) absorb the end of a revive timer
    the client saw start (`Keyed::timer_end`), as `quiet` already did. On the CPU-throttled host
    a neighbour's five seconds ended inside the check that follows a later login, and the talking
    line scenario failed even when run alone (229k.8). Any other record still fails the check.

### 229k.2 What the client sees

- **A living player** that types `/restart_here`, `/restart_town`, `/restart_now` or `/restart`
  gets `CloseRestartWindow` and nothing else; `/restart_n` is no command.
- **A disconnect** shows each viewer the leaver's release before its removal.
- **A target** 4800 or more away is dropped at the next recovery run, within three seconds.
- **From 229l, when a monster kills a player** (proved by world tests now):
  - the player falls stunned, its recovery pools empty, and three seconds later it is shown dead
    and released, with the restart window; a newcomer sees it lying dead;
  - it cannot move, hit, use, drop or pick up items, trade, click an NPC or sit up;
  - `/restart_here` after 9 seconds stands it where it lies with 50 hit points, `/restart_town`
    after 6 seconds sends it to its town with 50, and `/restart_now` stands it at once at full
    hit points for 300000 gold; before the wait it hears how many seconds are left;
  - three minutes later it is sent to its town with half its hit points;
  - a monster's kill costs a player of level 10 or more a share of its exp two times in three,
    and it hears `[LS;901]` otherwise.

### 229k.3 Divergences and Defects

**V18, new.** A player's death and restart differ from legacy in eleven ways, (a) to (k). STATUS
lists them all. The main ones:
- the town restart and the automatic restart write their records before the Warp's (a);
- the recovery event runs `CheckTarget` only (b);
- no pet, mount, war, dungeon, duel, arena or siege branch, and no affect 511 (c to e);
- no `ItemDropPenalty` and no quest `die` (f);
- the production arms of the restart waits and `IsHack` run (i, owner question 5);
- the automatic restart takes the town penalty (j, owner question 29);
- the penalty reads its flag before it rolls or speaks (k, owner question 32).

**Reworded:**
- V9: with no refill, a town restart's 50 hit points stay 50 after the Warp (owner question 18).
- V15: five ways became three. `CheckTarget` runs on the player recovery event every 75 Pulses.
- V16: the player's stun, death and recovery follow the NPCs' three events.
- V17: eleven ways became ten; (k), the leaving player's own release, is closed.

**Defects fixed**, under the owner's standing decision of 2026-10-14, in STATUS's list:
- **B5, a backdoor.** A disconnect while dead saved hit points of 0 or below, and the relog's
  refill stood the player up where it died at full hit points, with no penalty and no wait
  (`G/char.cpp:1779-1783`, `:4250`; `G/char_affect.cpp:660-665`). The Rewrite pays the here
  penalty, stands it and stores 50.
- **B25, a backdoor (found by the plan's critic).** `Position` has no dead guard, so a dead
  player that sits leaves `POS_DEAD` and stands up revived (`G/input_main.cpp:1530-1548`;
  `G/char.cpp:3335-3349`, `:1438-1444`; `G/char_battle.cpp:550-556`). The Rewrite refuses the
  pose while dead.
- **B8.** The prefix walk gave `restart_now` every word from `/rest` to `/restart_n`, so a typo
  paid 300000 gold (`G/cmd.cpp:298`, `:656`).
- **B1, B3, B20, B24.** `restart_now`'s refusal said "You paid" and charged nothing; it tested the
  gold before the dead event; it tested an always-true condition; and `do_restart`'s `IsHack`
  refusal was followed by an unrelated wait line.
- **B11 and D2** (provisional, owner question 32). The roll and `[LS;901]` came before the flag,
  a lucky roll kept the debt, and a town restart rolled and sent a zero exp record.
- **B12 and B13.** A failed recall Warp left the player standing where it died, unseen and with
  no revive.
- **B15 and D3** (provisional, owner question 29). The automatic restart took the here penalty.
- **D5, D6, D7, D9, D10.** A forked kill left the flag alone; standing kept the killer's PID; a
  dead player's potion was wasted; a stunned player walked for three seconds; a dead player
  picked up, traded and clicked NPCs.

**Legacy kept, recorded:**
- B9: a restart shows each viewer the player again, and the player the viewer with no removal
  first;
- B10: one record for each point change;
- B16: a recall on map 235 goes to a point of map 62, as data;
- B18: no exp loss at the top level with a quarter of the next level's exp (owner question 30);
- the level never steps down on a loss (`G/char.cpp:4155-4180`);
- D1/DE4: a death by the stun timer has no killer.

**Not reachable, noted:** the war map (B2); poison (B17); the quest `die` and sungma (D12, D13);
`pc.set_flag_kill` and `set_flag_dead`, which stay unbacked (DE1, a backdoor); the PK roll (DE7);
`CanSummon` (DE8); `/reset` under `test_server` (B23).

### 229k.4 Not ported yet

- **The monster fighting back** (229l): the monster's melee into `damage_pc`, its claim, aggro
  and damage map, `ForgetMyAttacker` and its `ReviveInvisible(5)`, and the first binary
  scenario that kills a player and reads the real `GC_PHASE{6}`.
- **The player's heal:** the recovery event's hit point heal, `DistributeSP` and `last_move`
  (owner question 18, 229l).
- **Drops and exp:** `ItemDropPenalty` and the positive exp change.
- **PvP:** the alignment, the empire points, `[LS;910]` and the killer's PK roll.
- **The group:** `dead_event`'s party reviver arm.
- **The affects:** affect 511 and the `ClearAffect` table.
- **GM commands:** `/kill`, `/stun`, `/forgetme`, `/cannot_dead`, `/can_dead`.
- **The arena revive** on the Shared Channel.

### 229k.5 Scenario and parity inventory

- **The parity scenarios go from 95 to 97:**
  - **`a_living_player_restarting_is_told_to_close_the_restart_window`.** Alpha enters with
    400000 gold. `/restart_here`, `/restart_town`, `/restart_now` and `/restart` each answer
    exactly `CloseRestartWindow`, and `/restart_n` answers that no such command exists. Nothing
    else is sent, and after the disconnect the store still holds 400000 gold.
  - **`a_target_4800_away_is_dropped_by_the_next_recovery_run`.** Yankee is stored 6000 east of
    Alpha (5765 by `DISTANCE_APPROX`), Charlie 4000 east and 600 south (4082). Alpha targets
    Yankee and reads `GC_TARGET{0}` within three seconds. Alpha then targets Charlie, which is
    kept for four seconds, and a second click on Charlie answers nothing.
- **Changed scenarios:**
  - `a_talking_line_reaches_the_map_including_its_sender`: its `/restart_here` line now answers
    `CloseRestartWindow`, and the listener hears nothing.
  - `a_leaving_player_is_removed_from_its_viewers_only` and the target scenario's disconnect read
    the leaver's release before its removal (`Keyed::sees_disconnect`).
  - `a_warp_npc_sends_its_neighbour_away_and_the_client_comes_back_at_the_target` gains a
    watcher: Yankee, on Bob's account, stands 800 north of the warp NPC. After Alpha's warp,
    Yankee reads Alpha's arrival, then its removal with no release before it, and nothing else
    (`G/char.cpp:6749-6755`). It closes `dm_warp_as_disconnect` (229k.7).
- **Unit and world tests:**

### 229k.6 Corrections, findings and controls

- **The critic's fourteen findings**, all taken before the port:
  1. `Attacker::Npc` would never be built outside the tests, which clippy refuses; `Attacker` is a
     struct with a `pc` flag.
  2. Sitting while dead is a revive backdoor in legacy (B25); the pose is refused while dead.
  3. A sync claim on a dead player, or by a down claimer, is refused with `DAMAGE_BLOCK`, as
     `SetSyncOwner`'s `battle_is_attackable` refuses it.
  4. The dead player's own claim is cleared with its release; otherwise its old owner released
     it again later.
  5. The recall fallback tests whether a Channel serves the point, not only whether the atlas
     names it, since the descriptor's `WarpSet` refuses an unserved map silently.
  6. A town restart that falls back to the spot takes the town penalty, not the here one.
  7. A stunned player's move is refused silently; showing it back would redraw it standing for
     its whole view.
  8. The descriptor's sitting pose is cleared on each phase record.
  9. The planned test did not reach the lock, since nothing heals a stunned player yet; the
     lethal-hit test now heals the stunned player directly and reads no change and no record.
  10. Dead's aura, premium shop and battle pass hooks were added to V18(d) and (e).
  11. The wait is stated one way (9.04 and 6.04 seconds); `CheckTarget` covers an NPC target.
  12. The tests assert no draw below level 10, hard-code the 1320 loss, test the living arm below
      300000 gold, read the revive's remaining duration, and check one 215 entry after the
      override.
  13. `clear_sync` replaces the leave's `release_owned` call, so the own release comes first.
  14. B16 is reachable through the recall and is recorded.
- **The restart's gold record leaves before the store's write.** Unlike an item step, whose
  descriptor stores the rows before it sends the records, `/restart_now`'s
  `GC_CHARACTER_GOLD_CHANGE` is written by the world behind the revive's records, and the
  descriptor stores the gold after. A store that refuses it closes the session the record went to,
  and the store keeps the gold, so the revive is free in that one case. The order keeps the
  record after the revive's, as legacy sends it. The doc of `restart` in `main.rs` says so.
- **A scenario point was not movable.** S2's first draft stored Charlie 4000 due east of Alpha.
  That cell is not movable, so the entry moved Charlie to the nearest movable one and the
  scenario's point check failed. Charlie is stored 4000 east and 600 south (4082 away), a
  movable cell.
- **Research corrections:**
  - the research said `input_main.cpp`'s 21 `IsDead()` lines are handler guards; 16 are, and
    `:1571` is `CheckComboHack`;
  - one research note proposed saving the town recall position at a dead disconnect and an
    admit clamp; the port keeps the position (the relog equals `/restart_here`) and adds no clamp,
    which would change every parity burst;
  - one proposed `recovery_event` as `ported`; it stays `partial`, since the heal is deferred;
  - two proposed a new outbox item or client order for the phase and the recall; the world
    writes the real `GC_PHASE` bytes, which the descriptor recognises, and resolves the recall
    itself, so it can fall back in place.

**Why the sweep was slow, and why whole parity runs failed.** Part d was the first file whose
mutants reach the parity suite. From its third mutant on, the parallel parity runs failed in bulk:
one run failed 29 of 97 scenarios. Each failing scenario passed when run alone, so the driver's
rerun (229c) counted none of them as a kill. The mutants were not the cause:
- **The host ran out of CPU credits.** It is a `t2.2xlarge` with standard credits. The balance
  reached 0 at about 11:36 and stayed there. From then on CloudWatch shows `CPUCreditBalance` 0
  and `CPUUtilization` about 21 %, so the host ran at its baseline, about a fifth of its speed.
- **Server start-up slowed past the harness's wait.** A debug server takes 4.4 seconds to open its
  gate when it starts alone. Of that, 2.5 seconds decode the hosted maps' `server_attr` (the
  gamedata LZO reader), and about 1 second stands the monsters. With eight servers starting at
  once on the throttled host, each took 19 to 25 seconds.
- **The failures cascaded.** The harness waited 20 seconds for the gate (`PROCESS_TIMEOUT`). A
  start that missed it failed its scenario. The next scenarios then started their servers
  together, so they missed it too, to the end of the run.

The fixes:
- **`parity/src/server.rs`:** the gate wait is now its own `START_TIMEOUT`, 120 seconds. Every
  other wait keeps 20 seconds. The repro (`diag229k/repro.py`) ran the same mutant on eight
  threads. Before the change it failed 29 of 97 scenarios in 200 seconds; after it, 6 of 97 in 482
  seconds.
- **`mutate_v2.py`:** `PARITY_THREADS` caps the parity suite's threads, and the resumed sweep ran
  on 4. `FLAKY_DIR` keeps each failed parallel run's output.
- **The copy only:** for part e, the copy's manifest built `gamedata` at `opt-level = 3`
  (`sweep229k/profile.toml`). That cuts the 2.5-second decode from each server's start. Overflow
  checks and debug assertions stay on.

The sweep was first stopped at 15:19, after 32 of part d's 40 mutants. The mutant then running had
changed `loading_phase.rs`; reversing its tuple restored the file, and every file's `CHECK` passed
again. The sweep resumed with the harness change in the copy (`run1b.sh`): the other 8 mutants of
part d (`rest_d.txt`, `shard_d2.log`), then part e.
