## 234. The character's alignment is stored, loaded and shown (`sys.char.pk`, third part)

Ledger 229n ported the kill alignment against an in-memory field: the kills raised the
alignment and a `/10` crossing sent the update, but nothing kept the value, so every
session began at zero and every kill's gain was lost at the next save. The column lands
now, and the value the client is shown comes from the store.

**The column.** `db/migrations/0014_player_alignment.sql` adds `player.alignment`, the
column legacy's `player` table has (`legacy/sql/schema/player.sql:847`), with the range
`UpdateAlignment`'s clamp gives it: -200000..200000 (`G/char_battle.cpp:3486`). The
check refuses a row a hand wrote past that. `db/src/players.rs`'s `Character` reads the
column and `PlayerSave` writes it, and `save_character` binds it in the row's own update.

**The load.** `SetPlayerProto` puts the stored value in both of legacy's alignment fields
(`G/char.cpp:2244-2245`): the one the client is shown and the one the rules read. The
Rewrite has one value, so `prodomo/src/loading_phase.rs`'s `PcCard::of` takes the stored
number as the card's alignment, and the card is what the world holds from then on.

**The wire.** The additional info carries the shown value in tenths
(`addPacket.sAlignment = m_iAlignment / 10`, `G/char.cpp:1201`), and
`character_additional` now writes the card's alignment divided by ten where it wrote a
zero. The loading burst's own summary and the view's summary of another player carry it
alike.

**The save.** `SaveReal` writes the real alignment back (`G/char.cpp:1546`). The Rewrite's
save takes the alignment from the world, not from the row it was loaded with:
`prodomo/src/game_state.rs`'s `Kept` carries the alignment `real_alignment_of` reads
(`GetRealAlignment`, `G/char_battle.cpp:3452-3455`), and `prodomo/src/main.rs`'s
`hold_kept` puts it in the held row that the save writes.

**The live scenario.** `the_stored_alignment_reaches_the_client` stores an alignment of
4321 on Alpha and logs in: the client's summary carries 432, the value in tenths.

**The unit tests.** `db/tests/players.rs`'s `a_whole_row_save_is_what_the_next_load_reads`
pins the store's round trip; `prodomo/src/save.rs`'s
`a_save_takes_the_position_from_the_avatar_and_the_rest_from_the_row` pins the save's
copy; `prodomo/src/main.rs`'s `the_held_character_takes_the_alignment_the_world_left`
pins the world's value in the held row; `prodomo/src/loading_phase.rs`'s
`character_additional_is_70_bytes_over_byte_136` pins the wire's tenths.

**The divergences.**

- Legacy keeps two alignment values (`G/char.h:1444-1445`), and they differ only while the
  hide-alignment unique (70048, `UNIQUE_ITEM_HIDE_ALIGNMENT_TITLE`,
  `G/game/unique_item.h:28`) is worn: it calls `ShowAlignment(false)`, which shows a zero
  alignment while the rules still read the real one (`G/char_battle.cpp:3457-3475`). The
  Rewrite has one value, so a player wearing that item still shows their alignment.
- The item drop penalty (`G/char_battle.cpp:1334-1347`) is still not ported: the victim's
  real alignment picks the table row (`:1035-1054`, the table at `:1002-1012`), and the
  Rewrite has no such table. The alignment it needs is stored now, so the table is what
  waits.
- The same-empire alignment penalty of a PvP death (`G/char_battle.cpp:1408+`) and the
  alignment's revenge wait for their systems.
- The items that move the alignment call `UpdateAlignment` (70102 and 70103,
  `G/char_item.cpp:4792-4810`, and the mythical peach 71107, `:4835-4858`), and the
  Rewrite's item use does not: the alignment moves with the kills (ledger 229n) and with
  nothing else for now.
- A correction to ledger 233: the empire point of a cross-empire kill
  (`G/char_battle.cpp:1390-1394`) has nothing to port. `CHARACTER::PointChange`'s
  `POINT_EMPIRE_POINT` arm returns the real value and changes nothing
  (`G/char.cpp:4700-4703`), and the point is mentioned nowhere else in the legacy but in
  the transfer itself, so the point is always zero and the transfer moves nothing in the
  legacy either. The 233 section's "no column in the store yet" named the wrong reason.

## 235. The death's item drop penalty (`sys.combat.penalty`)

Legacy's `CHARACTER::ItemDropPenalty` (`G/char_battle.cpp:1016-1199`) takes the items a
player loses when it dies. The Rewrite had the table's input (the alignment is stored since
ledger 234) but no rule, so a player that died to another player lost nothing. The penalty
runs now.

**The call.** `CHARACTER::Dead` calls it under seven conditions
(`G/char_battle.cpp:1333-1345`): a killer, no agreed PvP, no guild war, a player victim, no
duel, no forked road and no castle map, and a GM level of `GM_PLAYER` (or `test_server`).
`prodomo/src/game_state/death.rs` calls `item_drop_penalty` from the same place, outside the
player-killer arm, because legacy's call is outside it too: a monster's kill reaches the
penalty as well, and only the war skips it.

**The rules.** `prodomo/src/game_state/item_penalty.rs` (new) holds them:

| legacy | here |
|---|---|
| `GetMyShop()` (`:1019-1021`) | not ported; the private shop does not exist |
| `GetLevel() < 50` (`:1022-1024`) | the character's level |
| `IsBattleArenaMap(GetMapIndex())` (`:1025-1029`) | `BATTLE_ARENA_MAPS` (`G/BattleArena.h:2`) |
| `GetRealAlignment()`'s nine bands (`:1040-1058`) | `band` |
| `aItemDropPenalty_kor` (`:1003-1014`) | `TABLE` |
| `r.iInventoryPct >= number(1, 1000)` (`:1064`) | the inventory's draw |
| `r.iEquipmentPct >= number(1, 100)` (`:1065`) | the equipment's draw |
| `IsEquipUniqueItem(70049)` (`:1068-1072`) | `wears_the_skip_unique` |
| the inventory's slots, the shuffle and the count (`:1078-1092`) | `slots_with_items`, `shuffle` |
| the equipment's slots, the shuffle and the count (`:1117-1136`) | `worn_slots` |
| `ITEM_ANTIFLAG_GIVE \| ITEM_ANTIFLAG_PKDROP` (`:1098`, `:1142`) | `may_drop` |
| `SyncQuickslot(QUICKSLOT_TYPE_ITEM, cell, 255)` (`:1106`, `:1150`) | the drop's quickslot sync |
| `RemoveFromCharacter` (`:1107`, `:1151`) | `world::character::drop_penalty_item` |
| `AddToGround` and the scatter (`:1176-1198`) | `lay_the_dropped_items` |

The inventory's cells are the base inventory's, and the equipment's are the wear cells,
which the flat space keeps after the inventory (`INVENTORY_MAX_NUM + wear`,
`G/char_item.cpp:647-656`); the load puts a worn item there, so the penalty reads it there
too (`world::character::wear_of`). The band of the worst alignment drops every worn item
when the inventory holds none (`:1110-1111`), and the unique item that skips the penalty is
dropped instead of the rest (`:1155-1174`).

**The worn item.** `RemoveFromCharacter` calls `Unequip` for a worn item
(`G/item.cpp:370-378`), which takes the points the item gave with it (`ModifyPoints(false)`,
`G/item.cpp:1544`), empties the wear cell (`:1562`) and computes the points again
(`G/item.cpp:1580-1587`). `world::character::unequip_points` and
`world::character::recompute_points` are those two halves, and `drop_penalty_item` takes the
gear for them, in legacy's order: the points, then the item leaves its cell, then the
computation. The other effects of legacy's `Unequip` (the unique's expire, the wear timers)
are not ported, and the item's own attribute buffs are not either
(`BuffOnAttr_AddBuffsFromItem` does nothing here), so nothing is left behind by the drop.

**The rows.** Legacy deletes the row of a dropped item: `AddToGround` puts the item in the
delayed-save queue (`G/item.cpp:582`), and the queue's flush finds that the item has no
owner and deletes its row (`G/item_manager.cpp:485-495`). The flush runs every 127 Pulses
(`G/main.cpp:284-288`, `G/item_manager.cpp:546-564`), so for about five seconds the rows
still name the victim. The game thread cannot write to the store (ADR-0002), so the rows go
to the descriptor that holds the victim, which writes them in one transaction
(`prodomo/src/main.rs`'s `write_item_rows`, over the new `ClientOrder::ItemRows`) and tells
the pick-ups of the dropped items that the rows are gone: a pick-up writes the item's own
row, and the two rows would collide while the victim's row is still there.

**The GM level.** The penalty spares every character whose GM level is not `GM_PLAYER`
(`G/char_battle.cpp:1341`). The Rewrite's points carry the level (`Points::gm_level`), the
load sets it from the GM list (`prodomo/src/main.rs`), and the penalty reads it.

**The tests.** `prodomo/src/game_state/item_penalty.rs` holds nine: the nine bands at their
boundaries, a victim under level 50, a GM, a death without a killer, a victim on a battle
arena or a castle map, the worst band's drop of the inventory and the equipment, an item
whose anti-flags forbid it, the unique item that stops the drop and is dropped itself, and
a worn item's points going with it. `world/src/character/equip.rs`'s
`a_position_names_a_wear_cell_only_when_it_is_one` pins the wear cell's numbers.

**The divergences.**

- Legacy shuffles the slots with a **fresh** `std::mt19937` seeded from
  `std::random_device` (`:1085-1087` and `:1124-1126`), not with the process-wide
  `number()`. The Rewrite uses the game's one generator for every draw, so which items a
  penalty drops is not the set legacy's would drop. This is the same Divergence as the
  generator's own.
- The dropped items' rows go at once in the Rewrite. Legacy's go in the delayed-save
  queue's flush, up to 127 Pulses (about 5.1 seconds) after the drop, and they name the
  victim until then. The Rewrite's rows go when the victim's descriptor writes them, which
  is as soon as its queue is drained.
- `AddToGround` finding no tree for the point loses the item in legacy
  (`G/item.cpp:569-574`, a Defect). The Rewrite keeps it.
- The GM arm is narrower: legacy's `GetGMLevel() == GM_PLAYER || test_server` runs the
  penalty for a GM when `test_server` is on, and it is on in the owner's configuration
  (ledger 178.5). The Rewrite spares the GM.
- Legacy's quickslot sync for a worn item names the wear index (0 to 63), which is an
  inventory cell, and deletes whatever quickslot holds that cell: the wrong quickslot
  (`G/char_battle.cpp:1150`). The Rewrite syncs the flat cell, which no quickslot names, and
  deletes nothing. That Defect is not reproduced.
- The private shop (`GetMyShop`, `:1019-1021`) and the protected inventory (`IsSecured`,
  `:1101-1104` and `:1145-1148`) are not ported, so those two refusals cannot happen. The
  agreed PvP, the arena duel and the forked road are not ported either, so their three
  flags are always false, which is what keeps the penalty running. Legacy's `GetLevel() < 10`
  check (`:1032`) is unreachable, because the level is already 50 or more.

Ledger 234's note that the item drop penalty "is still not ported" is closed by this
section.

**The inventory.** The row `sys.combat.penalty` is `ported`, and its scenario is the unit
test `prodomo/src/game_state/item_penalty.rs::the_worst_band_drops_the_inventory_and_the_equipment`;
the note names the eight other tests and why no binary scenario proves the row. The spec's row
counts are brought up to date with the tables: the server records are 137, not 134, the
systems are 116, and the total is 1,649.

## 236. The war map's information and the war's map (`sys.guild.war`, second part)

A guild war was fought where the players already stood: the Rewrite knew the field war and
nothing else, so a declare of a battle or flag war was refused with `[LS;669]` — the
approximation of legacy's rule that the build held no war map. The owner's map index holds
both (`legacy/gamedata/locale/europe/map/index`: 110 is `metin2_map_t3`, 111 is
`metin2_map_t4`), so that refusal was wrong on this deployment. Legacy knows three war
types (`KOR_aGuildWarInfo`, `G/constants.cpp:1132-1145`), two war maps
(`CWarMapManager::LoadWarMapInfo`, `G/war_map.cpp:974-1008`) and the private copy a war
takes of the map it is fought on (`SECTREE_MANAGER::CreatePrivateMap`,
`G/sectree_manager.cpp:943-1026`). The Rewrite knows the table, the two checks the war map
passes, and the copy.

**The tables.** `prodomo/src/game_state/war_map.rs` (new) holds them:

| legacy | here |
|---|---|
| `KOR_aGuildWarInfo` (`G/constants.cpp:1132-1145`) | `WAR_TYPES` |
| `CWarMapManager::LoadWarMapInfo` (`G/war_map.cpp:974-1008`) | `WAR_MAPS` |
| `CWarMapManager::GetWarMapInfo` (`G/war_map.cpp:1061-1072`) | `war_map_of` |
| `SECTREE_MANAGER::CreatePrivateMap` (`G/sectree_manager.cpp:943-1026`) | `private_index` |

The war types are the field war (no map, no price, no score), the battle war (map 110, a
hundred points to end) and the flag war (map 111, ten points). The two war maps are the
battle map and the flag map. `private_index` gives the map's own index times 10,000 plus the
first free instance under it, with legacy's cap of 10,000 for every map but 107, 108 and
109, which take 51 (`G/sectree_manager.cpp:957-962`).

**The two checks.** Legacy asks the map twice. The declare asks the map index
(`CGuild::GuildWar_IsWarMap`, `G/guild_war.cpp:260-271`): the field war needs no map, and
every other type needs its map in the map index, which is the map's own files. A declare
that fails answers `[LS;669]` to the master (`:299-310`), and so does an accept whose saved
type fails (`:344-355`). The Rewrite asks the atlas, which is the map index
(`gamedata::map_atlas::MapAtlas`), through `Recall::in_atlas`.

The wait-start asks the Channel's map set (`map_allow_find`, `G/config.cpp:174-182`): the
map is in the process's `MAP_ALLOW` set, which in legacy is the union of the Cores' lists —
one Channel's list. In the Rewrite the process holds every Channel (ADR-0002), so the set is
the Channel's own (`Recall::hosts`, over the `game.channels` map sets the boot already
hands the recall). A map the Channel does not host leaves the war without one
(`G/guild_war.cpp:488-495`), which the Rewrite does too.

**The private copy.** `CGuild::WaitStartWar` (`G/guild_war.cpp:440-530`) creates the war's
map when the war starts: `CWarMapManager::CreateWarMap` (`G/war_map.cpp:1042-1059`) looks the
war map's own information up (a type whose map is not a war map has none), takes a private
copy of it, and both sides learn the index (`gw.map_index`, `SetGuildWarMapIndex` on the
other side and on this one). The Rewrite does that in `guild_war_map`
(`prodomo/src/game_state/guild.rs`): the copy's index comes from `private_index`, the copy
stands on the base map's own grid (the private map is a copy of the base's sectrees), and
both sides' entries carry the index. The field war takes no map.

**The fan's type.** The start's fan carried the field type, because the field war was the
only war there was. Legacy's `CGuild::StartWar` sends `GuildWarPacket(dwOppGID, gw.type,
GUILD_WAR_ON_WAR)` (`G/guild_war.cpp:428`), so the fan carries the war's own type. The
Rewrite reads it from the entry.

**The tests.** `prodomo/src/game_state/war_map.rs` holds four: the three war types at
legacy's numbers, the two war maps, a private map naming the map it was copied from, and a
private map taking the first free instance of its base. `prodomo/src/game_state/guild.rs`
holds three more: a battle war whose map the map index does not hold is refused with
`[LS;669]` and lands nothing; the same declare lands when the index holds the map; and a
battle war that starts takes the private copy (the index 110 times 10,000, the map hosted
on the war's Channel, both sides carrying it). The parity scenario
`a_battle_war_is_declared_and_accepted` proves the same thing on the wire: the declare
lands with `bType` 1, and the accept starts the war on that type.

**The divergences.**

- The wait-start is a step of its own in legacy: the accept sends `GUILD_WAR_WAIT_START` to
  the DB, the DB sends it back, and `WaitStartWar` creates the map; the start comes after
  (`G/guild_war.cpp:332-343` and `:436-437`). The Rewrite's accept starts the war inline
  (ledger 230x), so the map is created there. The order legacy keeps — the map before the
  on-war fan — is kept.
- Legacy creates the private copy in each side's process and tells the other side the index
  with the P2P packet `HEADER_GG_GUILD_WAR_ZONE_MAP_INDEX` (`G/guild_war.cpp:519-529`). The
  game-to-game protocol is retired (ADR-0001), so the Rewrite creates one copy and both
  sides learn it.
- The copy is hosted on the Channel the accepting master stands on. Legacy's process is one
  Channel, so its copy is on that Channel; in the Rewrite the war's members may stand on
  another Channel, and the entry (ledger 237) is where that is settled.
- Legacy ends the war when the copy cannot be created (`G/guild_war.cpp:508-513`). The
  Rewrite leaves the war without a map instead, because the copy is created at the start and
  the end is a later step.
- The copy holds no NPCs: the boot stands the NPCs on the base map, and the copy is made
  after it. Legacy's private map is a copy of the base's sectrees, so it holds the base's
  NPCs.
- The instance number is the lowest free one under the base. Legacy keeps a counter per
  map and takes the instance after the last one it gave out
  (`G/sectree_manager.cpp:962-975`), wrapping at the cap. The two agree while no copy is
  destroyed, and the Rewrite does not destroy one yet (the war map's own end is ledger
  237's).
- The start positions (the war's members are warped to them when they join) are ledger
  237's, with the entry that reads them.

**The inventory.** The row `sys.guild.war` stays `partial` — the field war is live (ledger
230w, 230x, 233) and the war map's information and its map are live now, but the war's
members, the observers, the flags and the war map's own end are not. The row `cmd.war`
keeps its scenario and its note now names the map index as the rule that answers
`[LS;669]`, and the scenario `a_battle_war_is_declared_and_accepted` proves the battle
war's declare and accept on the wire. The private copy is still only a unit test: the
index the members would be warped to is ledger 237's, so nothing client-visible yet shows
it.

## 237. The war map's runtime, its members and its watchers (`sys.guild.war`, third part)

A guild war of a map type had a map — ledger 236 gave the war its private copy — but the world
held nothing of it: no team, no watcher, no count. Legacy's `CWarMap` (`G/war_map.h:48-143`) is
the war's own map: the two teams that fight on it, the players that watch it, the players that
joined each team, and the counts the map tells them. The Rewrite now holds that map while the
war lives, and a player that walks onto it joins it.

**The map.** `prodomo/src/game_state/war_map.rs` holds `WarMap`: the private map index the war
is fought on, the map it was copied from, the map's type, the two guilds, the two teams, the
watchers, and the players on the map.

| legacy | here |
|---|---|
| `CWarMap::m_TeamData` (`G/war_map.h:114-133`) | `WarTeam` |
| `CWarMap::m_iObserverCount` | `WarMap::observers` |
| `CWarMap::m_set_pkChr` | `WarMap::present` |
| `STeamData::set_pidJoiner` | `WarTeam::joiners` |
| `CWarMap::GetTeamIndex` (`G/war_map.cpp:199-215`) | `WarMap::team_of` |
| `CWarMap::IncMember` (`G/war_map.cpp:342-398`) | `WarMap::inc_member` |
| `CWarMap::DecMember` (`G/war_map.cpp:400-451`) | `WarMap::dec_member` |
| `CWarMap::UpdateUserCount` (`G/war_map.cpp:330-340`) | `WarMap::user_count` |

The two guilds take a team each, and the lower id takes the first team — legacy's constructor
sorts them (`G/war_map.cpp:120-198`) and `GetTeamIndex` reads them back (`:199-215`), so
`WarMap::new` sorts them and `team_of` finds the team.

**The creation.** `CWarMapManager::CreateWarMap` (`G/war_map.cpp:1042-1059`) makes the war's map
when the war starts. The Rewrite's `GameState::create_war_map` does it in `manager_start_war`,
before the on-war fan — the order legacy keeps (`G/guild_war.cpp:519-537`) — and both sides'
entries carry the map's index (ledger 236). The field war takes no map, so it takes no war map.

**The members.** A player that enters the war's map joins it: `CWarMap::IncMember`
(`G/war_map.cpp:342-398`) puts the player in the team of its guild when the player carries the
war member's flag, and counts it among the watchers otherwise. The flag is the quest flag
`war.is_war_member`, which the war entry sets (`G/guild_war.cpp:674`) and which the join reads
and clears (`G/war_map.cpp:353-357`). The Rewrite reads the flag from the quest manager and
clears it there, and it joins the player in `GameState::join_war_map`, which the world's
`place_body` calls when it puts a character on a map (`CWarMapManager::Find(GetMapIndex())`,
`G/input_login.cpp:780`).

A player that leaves the map falls out of the count of its team, or of the watchers'
(`CWarMap::DecMember`, `G/war_map.cpp:400-451`): the world's `leave_world_by` calls
`GameState::leave_war_map` before it takes the player's body off the map.

**The counts.** Legacy tells the players on the map what the map holds: two command lines, one
with the watcher count and one with the two guilds, their joiner counts and the watcher count
(`FSendUserCount`, `G/war_map.cpp:312-340`). The Rewrite sends the same two lines, `ObserverCount
%d` and `WarUC %d %d %d %d %d`, to every player on the map, on every join and on every leave.
Legacy writes the two guild ids with `%u`; the Rewrite writes them with `%d`, which prints the
same digits for a guild id and a count.

**The quest bridge.** A quest script asks the map the character stands on and the war map it
stands on: `GetMapIndex()` and `GetWarMap()` (`G/input_login.cpp:780`). The Rewrite's quest
session carries the two (`prodomo/src/game_state/quests.rs`), the map index of the body and the
war map of that index.

**The quest's war join.** The war-join quest (`legacy/gamedata/locale/europe/quest/_basic/guild/
guild_war_join.lua`) asks the game six things, and the quest crate now asks them: the enemy's
guild id (`guild.get_any_war`), the join itself (`guild.war_enter`), the map the character
stands on (`pc.get_map_index`), the war map it stands on (`pc.get_war_map`), and the quest's
number and name (`q.getcurrentquestindex`, `q.getcurrentquestname`). The quest crate holds the
letter that asks for the button and the button that asks to join (`quest/src/manager.rs`), and
the quest's number by name (`RegisterQuest`'s `m_hmQuestName`, `G/questmanager.cpp:1266-1290`).
The two map reads are answered by the game here; the two guild calls and the join that warps
the member to the start position are the next section.

**The divergences.**

- The map's end is not legacy's. Legacy's `CGuild::EndWar` (`G/guild_war.cpp:592-627`) ends the
  map, and the map's end event ends the war ten passes later (`CWarMap::SetEnded`,
  `G/war_map.cpp:739-779`). The Rewrite's war ends first (ledger 230y) and the map goes with it.
  The map's own end — its flags, its draw, its exit — is the next section.
- The player that leaves the world leaves the war map with it. Legacy's `DecMember` is called by
  the map's own end and by the death that takes a player off the map; the Rewrite calls it when
  the character leaves the world, which covers both.
- The war member's flag is a quest flag in both. Legacy sets it on the character that enters
  the war (`G/guild_war.cpp:674`); the Rewrite has no entry yet (the next section), so no player
  carries it and every player that walks onto a war map watches it.

**The tests.** `prodomo/src/game_state/war_map.rs` holds five: the three war types at legacy's
numbers, the two war maps, a private map naming the map it was copied from, a private map
taking the first free instance of its base, and a war map holding two teams and the watchers —
the teams in legacy's order, a member joining its team's guild, a player without the flag
watching, the counts the map tells, and a member falling out of its team.
`prodomo/src/game_state/guild.rs` holds the map's creation: the war's map is the private copy of
the war's map type, and the two guilds stand on teams of their own.

**The inventory.** The row `sys.guild.war` stays `partial`: the war's map, its teams, its
members, its watchers and its counts are live now, but the entry that warps the members to the
start positions, the flags and the war map's own end are not.

## 238. The archer's critical shot: the harness sizes the effect record and the scenario reads either

The parity scenario `a_hit_range_monster_answers_with_a_shot_and_its_fly_record` failed about
one run in twenty: the 403 it shoots from has a five per cent critical chance, and a critical
sends a record the harness's width table did not know, so the read panicked with `unexpected
loading or enter-game header 114`. The Rewrite was right and the harness was short.

**What legacy sends.** A critical is drawn inside `Damage`, in the arm that takes
`DAMAGE_TYPE_NORMAL` and `DAMAGE_TYPE_NORMAL_RANGE` (`G/char_battle.cpp:1936`): the attacker's
critical percent, unhalved as this arm has it (`:1990`, less the victim's resist at `:1997`),
and the draw (`:1999`) doubles the damage (`:2002`) and calls `EffectPacket(SE_CRITICAL)`
(`:2003`). `CHARACTER::EffectPacket` (`G/char.cpp:7533-7542`) fills the record with the effect
type and `GetVID()` — the victim's — and `CEntity::PacketAround` (`G/entity.cpp:88-105`) sends it
to every entity in the victim's view and to the victim itself (`:104`). The damage's flag gets
`DAMAGE_CRITICAL` (`G/char.h:136`, `G/char_battle.cpp:2307-2308`) and the damage goes out with
it (`:2338`).

So the effect record reaches every client in the victim's view, at any time in the game: a
critical anywhere near a player is a record that player sees, whether it waits for a damage or
not. The same is true of a penetrating hit (`SE_PENETRATE`, `:2035`).

**What the Rewrite sends.** The same. `pc_chances`
(`world/src/character/combat/mob_melee.rs:811-847`) draws the attacker's unhalved critical
percent, doubles the damage and pushes `SE_CRITICAL` (`:824-828`); `shoot_pc` (`:339-390`) is the
shot's arm, and the party's monsters' one per cent penetrate is the same draw.
`show_mob_strike` (`prodomo/src/game_state/mob_strike.rs:370-380`) sends the effect around the
victim, which includes the victim, and the damage after it.

**The harness.** The width table `game_len` (`prodomo/tests/parity.rs`) now sizes the effect
record (six bytes: a `BYTE` type and a `DWORD` VID), so every reader can read one; the separate
`fight_len` table, which had held that one width, is gone and the deadline reader and the
party's reader use the general table. The fight readers pass an effect record over by rule, the
way they pass a ping over: `read_fight`, `read_fight_until`, `read_until`, `read_heal_tick` and
`npc_move_of`. The swing readers take the one on the victim, for the scenario to read: a swing's
`Swing` holds the effect types shown on its victim, and the head and the tail fill it.

**The scenario.** The shot is either plain or critical, and the scenario says which: the flag
and the effect agree, `DAMAGE_NORMAL` alone or `DAMAGE_NORMAL | DAMAGE_CRITICAL`, and the
ceiling on the damage is the plain one's or twice it, since a critical doubles the damage. The
403 has no penetrate, so the flag is never `DAMAGE_PENETRATE`.

**How the path was proved.** The five per cent draw cannot be waited for, so the critical was
forced: with `pc_chances` drawing a hundred per cent for the length of one run, the scenario
read the effect (`[5]`, `SE_CRITICAL`) and the flag (`33`) and passed; with the flag pinned to
the plain one, the same run failed on the flag. The force was reverted, and the world crate is
as it was.

## 239. The war asks its members to join it (`sys.guild.war`, fourth part)

The war's map was a map of its own — ledger 237 gave it the two teams, the watchers and the
counts — but nobody could get on it. The war never asked its members, the client had no way
to press the button the ask carries, and the join that carries a member to the start position
was not there. Legacy's ask is three steps, and all three are live now.

**The ask.** `CGuild::GuildWarEntryAsk` (`G/guild_war.cpp:680-727`) runs at the start of the
war and sends the `guild_war_join` quest's letter (`CQuestManager::Letter`,
`G/questmanager.cpp:502-514`) to every online member of the guild. A war with no map asks
nothing: the field war is fought where the players stand, and legacy logs an error and
returns when the map index is 0 (`:692-697`) or the start position cannot be read
(`:699-704`). The Rewrite asks each side's members in the same loop that starts the war and
fans it (`guild_war_entry_ask`, `prodomo/src/game_state/guild.rs`), and the letter's records
go to each member's own client (`quest_letter`, `prodomo/src/game_state/quests.rs`).

**The button.** The quest's letter event shows the button: `makequestbutton`
(`quest/questlib.lua:117-122`) writes the marker `[QUESTBUTTON idx;<index>|name;<label>]`,
where the index is the quest's own number (`q.getcurrentquestindex()`). The client presses it
and sends `CG_SCRIPT_BUTTON` (66), which carries the header and the quest's number
(`TPacketCGScriptButton`, `G/packet.h:752-756`); `CInputMain::ScriptButton`
(`G/input_main.cpp:2179-2200`) runs the quest's button event (`CQuestManager::QuestButton`,
`G/questmanager.cpp:767-783`). The Rewrite's `QuestStep::Button` carries the number into the
world and the quest's `button` event runs (`prodomo/src/game_state/quests.rs`). Legacy's two
other arms are not ported: a confirm waiting answers instead of the button, and the high bit
asks for the quest's information. The codec's own note called the index "behaviourally inert"
and said the handler only logged it; that was wrong, and the module's note now says what the
handler does (`protocol/src/cg_pick.rs`, and `docs/PROTOCOL_NOTES.md`).

**The join.** The button event asks the member (`select`), and the member's yes calls
`guild.war_enter(e)` (`G/questlua_guild.cpp:134-149`), which is `CGuild::GuildWarEntryAccept`
(`G/guild_war.cpp:639-678`): an enemy the guild does not hold is quiet, a field war is
quiet, a war that is not on is the `[LS;891]` line to the member, and a war without a map is
quiet. A member that passes is flagged `war.is_war_member`, and `SaveExitLocation` and
`WarpSet(pos.x, pos.y, gw.map_index)` carry it to the war map's start position
(`CWarMapManager::GetStartPosition`, `G/war_map.cpp:1019-1040`): the guild of the lower id
takes the first position and the other the second. The Rewrite does the same
(`quest_war_enter`, `prodomo/src/game_state/guild.rs`), and the flag is set on the quest's own
player.

**The war the quest asks for.** `guild.get_any_war` (`G/questlua_guild.cpp:151-161`) is
`CGuild::UnderAnyWar` (`G/guild_war.cpp:164-177`) with its default argument: the enemy of a
war that has begun, in id order, and 0 when there is none. The quest reads it before it shows
the button and again before it joins, and the number it reads is the one `guild.war_enter`
takes. The Rewrite answers it in the world and in the shadow that answers a script while it
waits (`answer_guild_quest` and `Guilds::judge_shadow`, `prodomo/src/game_state/guild.rs`).

**The start positions.** The table of ledger 236 held three wrong numbers per map. Legacy's
`CWarMapManager::LoadWarMapInfo` (`G/war_map.cpp:974-1008`) builds the positions in the code:
map 110's first is `48 * 100 + 32000`, `52 * 100 + 0`, which is 36800 and 5200, and the table
said 3680 and 5200; the second is `183 * 100 + 32000`, `206 * 100 + 0`, which is 50300 and
20600, and the table said 21500; the third is `141 * 100 + 32000`, `117 * 100 + 0`, which is
46100 and 11700, and the table said 17300. The flag map's three are the same arithmetic with
`68 * 100 + 57600` and so on. The table is now the code's own arithmetic
(`prodomo/src/game_state/war_map.rs`), and `start_position` reads the side from the private
map's index, which names the map the copy was taken from.

**The store.** A member that stands on a private map must be saved with that map's index and
with the place it returns to: `lMapIndex`, `lExitX`, `lExitY` and `lExitMapIndex`
(`TPlayerTable`, `G/tables.h:594-597`). Legacy writes them beside the position
(`CHARACTER::Save`, `G/char.cpp:1552-1578`) and reads the map index at the load
(`G/input_db.cpp:335-354`). The Rewrite's row carries them now (migration
`0015_player_map_index.sql`): the save writes the map the character stands on and the exit
location, the load reads the map index first, and a character whose row names a private map
comes back to its exit location, because the copy it stood on died with the process that held
it (`SetPlayerProto`, `G/char.cpp:2289-2294`).

**The warp.** The join's warp is the first warp that names a private map: `WarpSet` takes the
private map's index as its third argument (`G/char.cpp:6694`), refuses a private map that is
not a child of the map the position lies on (`:6727-6736`), and stores the destination. The
order carries the three new fields (`ClientOrder::Warp`, `prodomo/src/client_registry.rs`),
and the descriptor does the warp, the save and the `GC_WARP` (`warp_set`,
`prodomo/src/main.rs`). A warp that names a Channel goes to that Channel's port, which is how
a member of another Channel reaches the war's map.

**The tests.** `prodomo/src/game_state/guild.rs` holds five: the war asks its members and the
letter carries the button; a field war asks nothing; the quest's button asks the member and
the member's yes joins the war; the join takes the member to the start position and remembers
where it came from; the join refuses a field war and a war that is not on. The parity
scenario `a_war_with_a_map_asks_its_member_and_the_member_joins_the_war_map` proves the same
thing on the wire: the letter carries the button, the client presses it, the quest asks, the
member says yes, and the member lands on the war map's start position with the `GC_WARP` that
names the Channel's port. `the_other_side_of_the_war_takes_the_other_start_position` proves
the other side's second position.

**The divergences.**

- **V22.** The order of the two records. Legacy's `WarpSet` sends the `GC_WARP` while the
  script runs, so the member is sent to the war map before the quest's end (`[DONE]`) is
  written; the Rewrite's quest step returns the end to the descriptor and the warp goes
  through the order queue, so the end comes first and the warp after it. The client sees the
  dialog close and then the load, where legacy sees the load and then the dialog close. The
  two records are the same; only their order differs.
- Legacy's `GuildWarEntryAsk` asks the members of one guild, and each side's process asks its
  own members; the Rewrite holds both guilds and asks each side's members in the same loop
  that starts the war (`G/guild_war.cpp:419-438`). The ask is the same.
- The letter's button is shown when the quest's conditions hold, and they read the
  character's map index and the war map it stands on (`pc.get_map_index`, `pc.get_war_map`);
  the Rewrite answers both from the world, so the conditions are legacy's.
- The private copy of the war's map is hosted on the Channel of the master that accepted the
  war (ledger 236's Divergence); a member of another Channel is sent there, and the `GC_WARP`
  names that Channel's port.

**The inventory.** The row `sys.guild.war` stays `partial` — the ask and the join are live
now, but the war map's own end and the war's own flags are not. The row
`cg.game.script_button` goes from `missing` to `ported`, with the scenario. The rows
`lua.guild.war_enter` and `lua.guild.get_any_war` go from `missing` to `ported`, and so do
`lua.pc.get_map_index` and `lua.pc.get_war_map`, which the war-join quest reads. The row
`quest.guild_war_join` keeps its `partial` status — the quest is loaded and its letter and
its button are live, but its "no" branch and its "the war is over" branch are not — and its
note names the live part. The row `cmd.war` keeps its scenario and its note names the battle
type's entry. The row `sys.quest.runtime` keeps its `partial` status and its note names the
letter and the button event.

## 240. The war's map goes with the war (`sys.guild.war`, fifth part)

The war's map was a map of its own (ledger 236) with a runtime of its own (ledger 237), and
the war asked its members to join it (ledger 239), but the map never closed, a member that
had joined it never came back, and the war's own records never reached the member that
joined. Legacy's war map closes with its war, and the closing has three steps spread over
fifteen seconds; the Rewrite now walks the same three.

**The join's own records.** `CWarMap::IncMember` (`G/war_map.cpp:342-398`) ends with the
war's own record and the two sides' scores, and only the member that joined hears them:
`SendWarPacket` writes the two guild ids with the war's type and state
(`G/war_map.cpp:626-643`), and `SendScorePacket` writes the two guild ids with that
side's score (`:645-659`). The Rewrite sends them to the joining member alone
(`war_map_join_records`, `prodomo/src/game_state/guild.rs`), after the counts the map
tells its players, which is legacy's order.

**The map's end.** `CGuild::EndWar` (`G/guild_war.cpp:592-627`) ends the war and calls
`CWarMap::SetEnded` on the map it was fought on. `SetEnded` (`G/war_map.cpp:739-779`)
destroys the flag mobs, cancels the flag reset, marks the map ended and creates the
`war_end_event` ten seconds later. The Rewrite has no flag war, so the first two steps
have nothing to do; the mark and the event's own delay are the map's `ended` and
`exit_pulse` (`prodomo/src/game_state/war_map.rs`), and the tick that runs the event's two
steps is `run_war_map_ticks` (`prodomo/src/game_state/guild.rs`), called on every Pulse
from the game thread (`prodomo/src/game_state.rs`).

**The members' return.** The event's first step (`war_end_event`, `G/war_map.cpp:44-68`)
runs ten seconds after the war ended and calls `CWarMap::ExitAll` (`:455-468`), which
sends every player on the map back with `CHARACTER::ExitToSavedLocation`
(`G/char.cpp:6687-6692`). The place a member came from is the one its join remembered:
`SaveExitLocation` (`G/char.cpp:6679-6683`) writes the position and the map beside the
row, and the war map keeps it too (`order_war_warp`,
`prodomo/src/game_state/guild.rs`). The Rewrite's exit orders the member's client the
warp back to that place (`ClientOrder::Warp`, `prodomo/src/client_registry.rs`), and the
descriptor does the warp, the save and the `GC_WARP` (`warp_set`, `prodomo/src/main.rs`),
so the row the save writes names the town the member came from.

**The map's going.** The event's second step runs five seconds after the first and
destroys the copy of the map (`CWarMapManager::DestroyWarMap`, `G/war_map.cpp:1074-1084`):
the map is unhosted and every player still standing on it is disconnected, because a
client cannot stay on a map that is not there (`SECTREE_MANAGER::DestroyPrivateMap`,
`G/sectree_manager.cpp:1028-1052`). The Rewrite's `ClientOrder::Close` closes the
descriptor of every client on the map, and the departure saves the character, so its row
names the map it stood on and the next login brings it back to the place it came from
(`SetPlayerProto`, `G/char.cpp:2289-2294`).

**The name a character is told once.** `ch->SendGuildName` (`G/char.cpp:8621-8642`) sends
the guild's name to a character that has not been told it, and the set of the names a
character has been told lives on the character (`m_known_guild`, `G/char.h:2049`), which
`Initialize` clears (`G/char.cpp:419`). The Rewrite kept the set on the *body*, and a
character that has not stood on a map yet has no body: the enemy's name in a war's walk
(`SendEnemyGuild`, `G/guild_war.cpp:60-109`) was therefore dropped, and the name arrived
with the end of the war instead of with the enter. The set is on the character now
(`world/src/character/model.rs`), the body's field is gone
(`prodomo/src/game_state/motion.rs`), and the enemy's name reaches the member with the
enter, as ledger 230x claimed.

**The tests.** `prodomo/src/game_state/guild.rs` holds two: the war's end sends its
players back and then the map goes, and a player still on the map when it goes is
disconnected with it. The parity scenario
`the_wars_map_goes_with_the_war_and_its_member_comes_back` proves the same thing
on the wire: the GM's `/gwstop` echoes, the war's END fans and the every-PC
`WAR_END_LIST` land, ten seconds later the member is sent back to the place the war took
it from with the `GC_WARP` that names the town, and the member that logs in again is
back in the town. The war is of the battle type, so it has no over notice: legacy sends
that notice for a field war alone (`CGuildManager::EndWar`, `G/guild_manager.cpp:698-704`),
and the field war's notice is proved by
`a_gm_stops_and_cancels_the_war_and_a_player_cannot` (ledger 230y).

**The divergences.**

- **V23.** The place the exit sends a member to. Legacy's `ExitToSavedLocation` warps to
  the *pending* warp (`WarpSet(m_posWarp.x, m_posWarp.y, m_lWarpMapIndex)`,
  `G/char.cpp:6690`), and the warp that took the member to the war map overwrote the
  pending warp with the war map's own start position. So legacy sends the member back
  onto the war map, where the map's own destruction disconnects it a few seconds later,
  and the member is brought back to the town by its next login, because the row names the
  map it stood on and the load reads the exit location beside it. The Rewrite sends the
  member back to the place it came from, which is what the rule is for, and the member
  stays connected. The end state is the same and the way there differs: legacy's client
  reloads the war map and is then disconnected, the Rewrite's client is sent straight to
  the town.
- A member that watches the war is counted as one (`ObserverCount` and `WarUC`), but the
  Rewrite does not put it in observer mode and does not tell it so (`SetObserverMode`,
  `G/war_map.cpp:379-386`): the observer mode is a client state the Rewrite has not
  ported, and the two lines that go with it promise a button the Rewrite cannot show.

**The inventory.** The row `sys.guild.war` stays `partial` — the war map's end, the
members' return and the map's going are live now, but the war's own flags are not — and
its note names the new part. The row `gc.guild` keeps its status and its note names the
join's own records, the war record and the two scores, which the member that joined the
war's map hears alone.

## 241. The war's map judges the war (`sys.guild.war`, sixth part)

The war's map had its teams, its members, its watchers and its end (ledgers 237 and 240),
but the map judged nothing: a kill on the map scored the war by the field war's rule, the
map never asked whether the war was over, and the wait the map keeps never came to
anything. Legacy's map judges the war in four steps, and all four are live now.

**The kill on the map.** `CWarMap::OnKill` (`G/war_map.cpp:781-829`) scores the war by the
map's own rule: the battle map gives the killer's guild a point
(`SendGuildWarScore(dwKillerGuild, dwDeadGuild, 1, ch->GetLevel())`, `:808`), and both
guilds must be teams of the map (`:799-802`). The field war's own arm does not run for such
a kill (`CGuildManager::Kill`, `G/guild_manager.cpp:846-850`). The Rewrite's
`GameState::war_map_kill` does this and `GameState::guild_war_kill` steps aside for it.
The flag map's arm gives the flag back, which ledger 242 ports.

**The score.** `CWarMap::UpdateScore` (`G/war_map.cpp:660-681`) changes the pair's score,
the map's own score follows, the players on the map hear the new total, and the war asks
whether it is over. The Rewrite's `GameState::war_map_score` does this, and the record
goes to the players on the map and to nobody else: the map's arm of `SetWarScoreAgainstTo`
(`G/guild_war.cpp:196-200`) sends it to the map, and only the field war's arm sends it to
the guilds' members (`:200-217`).

**The check.** `CWarMap::CheckWarEnd` (`G/war_map.cpp:470-495`) says the two lines when a
side has no member on the map and asks for the timeout a minute later; else the score
decides (`CheckScore`, `G/war_map.cpp:686-735`): the war must have run for thirty seconds,
equal scores end nothing, and a side's score that reaches the war's end score — a hundred
for the battle war and ten for the flag war (`KOR_aGuildWarInfo`, `G/constants.cpp:1132-1145`)
— ends the war. The map asks first a minute after it was made and then every ten seconds
(`war_begin_event`, `G/war_map.cpp:29-43` and `:117`), and the Rewrite's
`GameState::run_war_map_ticks` runs the asks on the game's Pulse.

**The wait's end.** The timeout ends the war (`war_timeout_event`, `G/war_map.cpp:70-84` →
`CWarMap::Timeout`, `G/war_map.cpp:510-578`): a war younger than five minutes is judged to
be a draw (`:526`), else the side that kept its members wins (`:533-560`) — and the DB's
`RecvWarOver` (`db/GuildManager.cpp:529-559`) follows the winner the map named, not the
scores. The war's price is not paid: the game side sends it as zero
(`p.lWarPrice = 0`, `G/guild_manager.cpp:523`), so the winner's deposit is nothing. The
ladder's own winner is the judgement's (`WarEndJudgement`), so the map's arm and the
scores' arm can differ. The rows the end writes wait for the war-end poll (ledger 230y).

**The join calls the wait off.** `CWarMap::IncMember` (`G/war_map.cpp:342-398`) cancels the
timeout the map asked for when a *member* joins (`event_cancel(&m_pkTimeoutEvent)`,
`G/war_map.cpp:374`): the side that was waited for has come, so the map may ask for another
wait. A watcher does not cancel it (`:380-386`), and the join asks nothing itself — the
map's next ask (every ten seconds) is what notices a side that is still empty. The
Rewrite's `GameState::join_war_map` calls `WarMap::cancel_timeout`
(`prodomo/src/game_state/war_map.rs`) for a member and for no one else.

**The leave asks.** `CWarMap::DecMember` (`G/war_map.cpp:400-451`) counts the player out of
its team (or out of the watchers), asks whether the war is over (`CheckWarEnd`,
`G/war_map.cpp:437`), clears the war member's flag (`:438`), tells the map's players the
counts (`:448`), and only then takes the player out of the map's set of players (`:450`).
The player that left therefore still hears the map's notice. The Rewrite's
`GameState::leave_war_map` runs the steps in that order: `WarMap::dec_member` counts,
`GameState::war_map_check_end` asks, the flag is cleared, the counts are told, and
`WarMap::leave_present` takes the player out of the set.

**The watchers.** Legacy keeps the observer mode on the character (`SetObserverMode`,
`G/war_map.cpp:384` and `:445`), and `DecMember` reads it to know which count to lower
(`ch->IsObserverMode()`, `G/war_map.cpp:410`). The Rewrite kept only the *number* of the
watchers, so a player that watched the war and came back could not be told from a member,
and its second leave took a member's count a second time. The map keeps the watchers'
players now (`WarMap::watchers`), the count the map tells is their number, and the leave
asks the set rather than the guild.

**The tests.** `prodomo/src/game_state/guild.rs` holds the map's own judging: a kill on the
war's map scores the war by one point, a score that reaches the end score ends the war, a
side without members ends the war a minute later, a war that ran for five minutes ends with
the side that stayed, a member that joins cancels the timeout the map asked for, and a
member that leaves makes the map ask whether the war is over (the member that left still
hears it). `prodomo/src/game_state/war_map.rs` holds the watchers: a member falls out of
its team and a watcher out of the watchers'. The parity scenario
`a_war_without_a_side_ends_when_the_map_times_out` proves the whole wait on the wire: one
master joins the war's map and the other does not, so a side of the map has no member on
it — a minute after the map was made the map says so and says when the war will end, a
minute after that the map says the war ended early and was judged to be a draw, the pair's
END fans and the every-PC `WAR_END_LIST` land, and the store's rows carry a draw for each
side with the ladders unmoved.

**The harness.** A record that arrives in pieces is the norm for a scenario that waits a
minute for a line: the map's notice can land in the middle of the heartbeat's records, so
the parity client reads into a buffer until it holds the record's bytes and keeps the rest
for the next call (`Client::read_bytes_until`, `parity/src/client.rs`), and the connection
remembers the length it already knows (`Keyed::read_sized`, `prodomo/tests/parity.rs`). The
server's descriptor answers a handshake record in every phase that answers one:
`CInputMain` (`G/input_main.cpp:3659-3670`) takes the time sync, so the select, loading,
game and dead phases accept the record (`ClientPhase::accepts_handshake_record`,
`prodomo/src/client_session.rs`), and the phase's own test names them.

**The lints.** The uncommitted work had brought the `pedantic` lints back: the casts that
`cast_lossless` and `cast_possible_wrap` refuse, the match arms with equal bodies, and the
harness's `match` for a single pattern. They are fixed by refactoring, and the tree is
clippy green again.

**The divergences.**

- The war's own flags are not ported: the flag mobs, the flag a member carries and the
  flag's reset (`AddFlag`, `RemoveFlag` and the reset event, `G/war_map.cpp:840-890` and
  `:739-779`) are the next section.

**The inventory.** The row `sys.guild.war` stays `partial` — the map's own judging is live
now, the kill's score, the score's end, the ask, the wait and the timeout — but the war's
own flags are not — and its note names the new part.

`-D warnings`; doc-tests green; the prodomo lib (1173 tests) green; the protocol lib (1229
tests) green; the world lib (541 tests) green; the full workspace all-targets DB run green
on all 39 targets (parity 130/130); this slice's six new unit tests green 6/6 and its
parity scenario green 1/1; no scratch database left — the ones an interrupted earlier run
had left were dropped by hand, and the run after that left none.

## 242. The war's own flags: the take, the score and the reset (`sys.guild.war`, seventh part)

The flag war was a war without a flag. The map judged it (ledger 241), but the map held no
flag, no base and no carrier, so nothing could be carried, nothing could be scored and
nothing could be reset. Legacy's flag war has two flags, one for each team, each standing
on its own base in the middle of the map, and the flag *is* the war's score: a player that
carries the other team's flag to its own base gives its guild a point, and the flags go
back to their bases.

**The flags the map holds.** `CWarMap`'s constructor (`G/war_map.cpp:126-131`) adds the two
bases and then the two flags, and only a flag map has them. The vnums are
`warmap::WAR_FLAG_VNUM0` (20035) and `warmap::WAR_FLAG_VNUM1` (20036) and the base's is
`warmap::WAR_FLAG_BASE_VNUM` (20038) (`G/war_map.h:24-32`). A base stands at the map's
start point of its team, and the flag stands on the same point, so the flag stands on its
base (`CWarMap::IsFlagOnBase`, `G/war_map.cpp:898-911`). The flag map's two start points
are `(64400, 6900)` and `(72870, 18200)` (`CWarMapManager::LoadWarMapInfo`,
`G/war_map.cpp:1000-1006`).

The Rewrite's `WarMap` holds the two flags and their two bases
(`prodomo/src/game_state/war_map.rs`): a flag is either standing on a point or carried by
a player, the map knows which, and the base's point is the map's own.

**The take.** The flag mob runs its state twice a second (`CHARACTER::StateFlag`,
`G/char_state.cpp:1185-1216`) and asks the map for the player that may take it
(`FuncFindChrForFlag`, `G/char_state.cpp:33-97`): a player on the map that is not an
observer, is alive, is in a guild and carries no flag, within 500 units. The nearest one
wins (`m_iMinDistance > iDist`, `:57`). A player of the flag's *own* guild may take it
only when the flag does not stand on its base (`:68-76`), so a guild's own flag is safe
while it is home — and a player that fails that rule does not take the flag away from a
farther player that may. The carrier gets two affects: the flag's own (`AFFECT_WAR_FLAG`,
`POINT_NONE`, the flag's guild, and `AFF_WAR_FLAG1` or `AFF_WAR_FLAG2` by the team) and
the speed (`POINT_MOV_SPEED`, 50 minus the carrier's speed, `:1208-1209`). The flag's
character dies with the flag (`CWarMap::RemoveFlag`, `G/war_map.cpp:881-893`) and the map
says so (`:1213-1215`).

The Rewrite's `GameState::war_map_flag_take` runs that rule on the game's Pulse (the
states run every half a second, `G/char_state.cpp:1187`), and
`GameState::war_flag_give` gives the two affects.

**The score.** The base mob runs its state twice a second (`CHARACTER::StateFlagBase`,
`G/char_state.cpp:1218-1222`) and asks for the player that brings the other team's flag to
it (`FuncFindChrForFlagBase`, `G/char_state.cpp:98-170`): a player within 500 units who
carries a flag and is of the base's guild scores a point for that guild against the
flag's guild (`SendGuildWarScore`, `:150`). Then the flags reset
(`CWarMap::ResetFlag`, `G/war_map.cpp:941-964`) and the map says so (`:153-158`). The
Rewrite's `GameState::war_map_flag_score` runs that rule, scores the war by the map's own
score path (`GameState::war_map_score`), resets the flags and says so.

**The reset.** The reset takes the flags away, takes the flag's affects from every player
on the map (`FRemoveFlagAffect`, `G/war_map.cpp:932-939`) and brings the flags back ten
seconds later (`war_reset_flag_event`, `:913-930`). A second reset while one is pending
does nothing (`if (m_pkResetFlagEvent) return;`, `:946`), and a map that has ended keeps
its flags (`:949`).

**The kill.** A member that falls on the flag map leaves the flag where it fell
(`CWarMap::OnKill`'s flag arm, `G/war_map.cpp:811-823`): the flag lies where its carrier
died — when it is not already on the map — and the carrier loses the flag's affect
(`:820`). The Rewrite's `GameState::war_map_flag_return` does this.

**The tests.** Six unit tests in `prodomo/src/game_state/guild.rs`: a player of the other
guild takes the flag, a player of the flag's own guild may not take it from its base but
may take it off it, the base scores the flag it carries, the flags come back ten seconds
after the reset, and the flag lies where its carrier fell.

**The divergences.**

- The flag's own body — the character the flag is, which legacy spawns and destroys — is
  ledger 243's. The rule is live against the map's own record of the flag; the character
  is not stood up yet.

**The inventory.** The row `sys.guild.war` stays `partial` — the flag's rule is live now —
and its note names the new part.

`-D warnings`; doc-tests green (9 targets; 1 passed, 19 ignored); the full workspace
all-targets DB run green on all 39 targets (4049 tests; parity 131/131); this slice's six
new unit tests green 6/6; no scratch database left.

No ADR changed. No owner question added. V23 is taken.

## 243. The flag war's map stands its flags and bases up (`sys.guild.war`, eighth part)

The flag was a rule without a body: the map knew where the flag was and who carried it,
but there was no character on the map to be the flag. Legacy spawns the flag and its base
as characters of the war's own map, and destroys them when the war ends.

**The bodies.** `CWarMap::AddFlagBase` and `CWarMap::AddFlag`
(`G/war_map.cpp:832-879`) spawn a character of the vnum at a point of the map: the base's
vnum for the base, and the team's own flag vnum for the flag. `SpawnMob`
(`G/char_manager.cpp:382-470`) takes the point and no rotation, checks the proto and the
cell, and stands the character in the map's sectree.

The Rewrite's `Respawner::spawn_one` (`world/src/npc.rs`) does that: the proto, the cell
checks, the sectree, then the character, and it answers the character it stood — or
nothing for a vnum with no proto, a point with no sectree and a cell the character may not
stand in.

**The standing.** A flag map stands its two bases and its two flags up when it is made
(`CWarMap`'s constructor, `G/war_map.cpp:126-131`): the base first and the flag on the
same point, so the flag stands on its base. The Rewrite's
`GameState::war_map_stand_flags` does this when the war's private copy of the map is made
(`GameState::create_war_map`), and the flag's character is put on the map's own list — a
private map holds no regen characters, so the list is made for it
(`GameState::regen`'s `stand_runtime`, `prodomo/src/game_state/regen.rs`).

The flags come back the same way after a reset (`war_reset_flag_event`,
`G/war_map.cpp:913-930`), at the base's point.

**The end.** The war's end destroys the flag and base characters
(`CWarMap::SetEnded`, `G/war_map.cpp:739-779`) and cancels the pending reset
(`event_cancel(&m_pkResetFlagEvent)`, `:770`). The Rewrite's
`GameState::war_map_destroy_flags` does this.

**The tests.** A unit test in `world/src/npc.rs` stands the flag mobs on the flag map: the
two flags and the two bases stand on their points, and the map's own list holds them.

**The parity scenario.** `the_flag_war_stands_its_flags_up_and_the_member_sees_them`
proves the bodies on the wire: two guilds at war of the flag type, the member that takes
the war's entry letter warps to the war's own copy of the flag map, and the view it enters
holds the flag and its base — each insert names the vnum, the kind and the place, and the
flag stands on the base's point.

**The divergences.**

- The flag and the base are characters with no behaviour of their own: legacy's flag mob
  runs its state through the character state machine, and the Rewrite runs the same rule
  from the war map's tick. The wire is the same; the owner of the rule is not.

**The inventory.** The row `sys.guild.war` stays `partial` — the flag's rule and the flag's
bodies are live now — and its note names the new part.

lib 1229, the world lib 542; parity 131/131); this slice's seven new unit tests green 7/7
and its parity scenario green 1/1; no scratch database left.

## 244. The quest flags live in the store, and the war's member survives the warp (`sys.quest.runtime`, `sys.guild.war`, ninth part)

A quest's flags were the one thing the quest runtime kept that no other system could see:
they lived in memory while the character was logged in and ended with it (ledger 227.3's
Divergence, and ADR-0006's promise that the table would land with the first system that
needed it). The war's member rule needs one of them. That Divergence is retired by this
section: the flags live in the store with the character.

**The flag.** `CGuild::GuildWarEntryAccept` (`G/guild_war.cpp:639-678`) sets
`war.is_war_member` on the member (`pPC->SetFlag("war.is_war_member", 1)`, `:674`) and then
warps the member to the war's map (`:677`). The war's map reads the flag when the member
lands (`CWarMap::IncMember`, `G/war_map.cpp:342-398`): a player that carries it joins the
team of its guild, and a player that does not watches the war.

The war's map stands on another Channel (ledger 236), so that warp is a reconnect: the
member leaves the world, comes back on the war's Channel and lands on the map. The flag was
lost in that gap, so the member watched the war it had come to fight.

**The store.** Legacy's quest flags are the quest manager's own per-character record
(`quest::PC`, `G/questpc.h:98-149`): a map from a name to a value. `SetFlag` with the value
zero deletes the flag (`G/questpc.cpp:52-90`), `Save` writes the flags that changed with the
character (`G/questpc.cpp:519-590`, called by `CHARACTER::Save`, `G/char.cpp:1670-1678`),
and the load reads them back with the character (`CInputDB::QuestLoad`,
`G/input_db.cpp:1079-1101`). A flag therefore outlives the session that set it.

The Rewrite's `quest_flag` table (`db/migrations/0016_quest_flag.sql`) is that record's
home: one row per flag, the whole name in one column and the value beside it, with the
value never zero. `db/src/quest_flags.rs` reads them in name order and writes a character's
whole set in one transaction: the player's rows are deleted and the flags are inserted, so
a save is the old set or the new one and never a mix.

**The world.** `quest::Manager::load_flags` sets the stored flags on the character's record
and rebuilds its quest list from the flags that end in `.__status` (`quest::PC::Build`,
`G/questpc.cpp:664-679`), so a quest that ran in an earlier session continues where it left
it. `quest::Manager::flags_of` gives the flags a save writes, in name order and without the
zeros.

The admission loads them (`GameState::shown_on_admit`, under the player id the enter
carries), the leave takes them (`GameState::leave_world_by`, into `Kept::quest_flags`), and
the periodic save asks the world for them (`GameState::answer_kept`). The descriptor reads
them at the select (`load_select_rows`) and writes them with the character (`save_held`),
after the row and the quickslots, as legacy writes them after the row.

**The member rule.** `CWarMap::IncMember` (`G/war_map.cpp:353-359`) reads the flag and
clears it only when the player's guild is neither of the two sides: the guild is no longer
in the war, so the player is not one of its members. The timeout the map asked for is
cancelled only by a member (`event_cancel(&m_pkTimeoutEvent)`, `:374`). `CWarMap::DecMember`
(`:438`) clears the flag of a member that leaves the map, and it runs before the character
is written (`G/char.cpp:1763,1786`), so the flags a save carries are the ones the map
left.

**The zero flag.** `quest::Manager::set_quest_flag` with the value zero now deletes the
flag, as legacy's `SetFlag` does (`G/questpc.cpp:59-63`). The guild's change of master
clears two flags that way (`G/questlua_guild.cpp:411-412,417`), and a flag that was
cleared reads as absent and is not written. A flag that is not there is not deleted and
makes no record, as legacy's `DeleteFlag` does nothing for a flag it does not hold
(`G/questpc.cpp:78-90`).

**The kill event.** Legacy's quest load answers even a character with no flags: the store
sends the quest load with a count of zero (`RESULT_QUEST_LOAD`,
`server/server/db/ClientManagerPlayer.cpp:1019-1025`) and the game makes the record and
marks it loaded (`CInputDB::QuestLoad`, `G/input_db.cpp:1079-1101`). So every character
that is logged in has a quest record, and the events reach it.

The kill event is the one that shows it. `CQuestManager::Kill` (`G/questmanager.cpp:574-611`)
runs the no-target quests' `kill` scripts for the killer, and the only one is
`napierdalator` (`object/notarget/kill/napierdalator.start`): a character that has no
state for the quest is a miss, the quest has a start state and no `begin_condition`, so it
starts (`NPC::HandleReceiveAllEvent`, `G/questnpc.cpp:482-530`) and its script runs. The
script's only effect is a global rank point (`pc.global_rank_add_point`, the global rank
board, which the Rewrite does not have), and the client sees nothing of it: the script
ends with a bare `[DONE]`, which `SendScript` (`G/questmanager.cpp:1122-1130`) swallows,
because nobody answered and the skin is the normal one.

The Rewrite's record now exists for every character, so the quest runtime ran that script
on every kill. Its APIs are not ported, and a refusal ended the script the way a script
error does: with the bare `[DONE]` the client closes a window with, which the legacy never
sends. **A refusal now ends the script as a script that says nothing ends**: the bare
`[DONE]` is swallowed, and the client sees nothing, as it does in legacy. A script error
still ends the script the legacy's error did.

**The tests.** Six unit tests:

- `quest/src/manager.rs`: `a_flag_whose_value_is_zero_is_deleted` — a flag set to zero is
  gone, not a flag of the value zero, and a save does not write it.
- `quest/src/manager.rs`: `the_stored_flags_come_back_with_the_character` — the stored
  flags are the character's, and the quest's state is rebuilt from the flag that names it.
- `quest/src/manager.rs`: `a_kill_runs_the_no_target_quest_and_the_client_sees_nothing` —
  the kill runs the no-target quest, and its refusal ends the script silently, so the
  client sees nothing.
- `prodomo/src/game_state.rs`: `the_world_holds_the_quest_flags_the_load_read` — the flags
  the load read are the world's, and the ones the world holds are the ones a save writes,
  even though the quest record goes when the character leaves.
- `prodomo/src/game_state/guild.rs`: `a_player_whose_guild_is_neither_side_watches_the_war_and_loses_the_flag`
  — a player whose guild is not in the war watches it and loses the flag, and a watcher
  does not call off the timeout the map asked for.
- `prodomo/src/game_state/guild.rs`: `a_member_that_leaves_the_wars_map_loses_the_flag_in_the_save`
  — the flags a leave carries do not hold the flag the war's map cleared.

**The parity scenarios.** `the_flag_war_stands_its_flags_up_and_the_member_sees_them`,
`the_wars_map_goes_with_the_war_and_its_member_comes_back` and
`a_war_without_a_side_ends_when_the_map_times_out` now say what the member does after the
warp: the map tells the world that the member joined its team (`WarUC 1 1 2 0 0` and
`ObserverCount 0`), where it used to say that it watched the war. The war's member rule is
on the wire, and the flag that carries it survives the reconnect.

`a_removed_member_keeps_the_withdraw_time_across_a_relog` proves the other half: a member
that is removed from a guild carries the guild's withdraw time as a flag
(`G/input_main.cpp:2930`), the flag is written with the character and read back with it,
and the master that invites the member again hears the penalty line
(`VerifyGuildJoinableCondition`, `G/guild.cpp:2165-2170`).

**The divergences.**

- The whole set is written at once. Legacy writes the flags that changed
  (`quest::PC::m_FlagSaveMap`, `G/questpc.cpp:519-590`), one row per flag, and deletes the
  row of a flag that was cleared. The Rewrite's save is one transaction that replaces the
  character's rows with the flags the world holds, which is the same set when the world
  holds them all — and it does, because the admission loads the stored flags into the
  character's record.
- The whole name is one column. Legacy splits it at the first dot into the quest's name
  and the flag's state (`G/questpc.cpp:545-560`) and joins them again on the load
  (`G/input_db.cpp:1089-1094`). The split is a property of its table, not of the flag.
- `Loading quest. Please wait a moment.` is never said: the flags come with the character
  instead of after it, so no quest ever waits for them. The event flags stay in memory
  (ADR-0006).
- A call of an API the Rewrite does not back ends the script silently, where a script error
  ends it with the bare `[DONE]` the client closes a window with
  (`G/questmanager.cpp:1122-1130`). The legacy has no such call: its API worked, and its
  script carried on to an end the client saw nothing of, so the refusal sends nothing
  either. The global rank points the no-target kill quest counts are not kept, as the
  global rank board is not ported. ADR-0006's sentence about the refusal is amended by this
  section: the refusal still raises the error, and the script still ends, but the end is the
  silent one.

**The inventory.** `sys.quest.runtime` and `sys.guild.war` keep their rows and gain the
notes of this section; `sys.guild.war` stays `partial`, because the flag's take and the
base's score are still proved by unit tests alone.

all-targets DB run green on all 39 targets, the 132 parity scenarios among them; this

## 245. The flag's take and the base's score on the wire (`sys.guild.war`, tenth part)

Ledger 242 put the war's own flags in the world and proved them with unit tests. This
section puts the take and the score on the wire, and it fixes the two orders the legacy
keeps.

**The take.** `CHARACTER::StateFlag` (`G/char_state.cpp:1185-1215`) runs twice a second
(`PASSES_PER_SEC(0.5)`, `:1186`) and hands the flag to the player nearest it
(`FuncFindChrForFlag`, `G/char_state.cpp:33-97`): the player must be a living player of a
guild, within 500 units of the flag, and without a flag of its own; a player of the flag's
own guild may take it only while the flag is not on its base. The carrier gets the flag's
affects first (`AddAffect`, `:1209-1210`) — the flag's affect (`AFFECT_WAR_FLAG`, 222) with
the flag's guild and the other team's flag bit (`AFF_WAR_FLAG2`, 38), and a move-speed
affect — then the flag's character dies with the flag (`CWarMap::RemoveFlag`,
`G/war_map.cpp:881-893`), and the map says who took it (`:1213`).

The Rewrite sent the flag's death before the affects. Legacy sends the affects first, so
the carrier's affect is on the wire before the flag leaves the view, and the client can
show the carrier's flag while the flag is still standing.

**The score.** `CHARACTER::StateFlagBase` (`G/char_state.cpp:98-170`) gives a point to a
player of the base's own guild that stands within 500 units of the base and carries the
other team's flag. Legacy then sends the score to the database (`SendGuildWarScore`,
`G/char_state.cpp:151`), resets the flags (`CWarMap::ResetFlag`, `G/war_map.cpp:941-964`:
the flags' characters die and the carriers lose the flag's affects) and says so
(`:153-158`).

The score the client sees is not that call. The database answers with it
(`CInputDB::GuildWarScore`, `G/input_db.cpp:1375-1380`), and the answer sets the score
(`CGuild::SetWarScoreAgainstTo`, `G/guild_war.cpp:179-217`); for a war that is fought on
a map, the answer reaches the map (`CWarMap::UpdateScore`, `G/war_map.cpp:661-682`), which
sends the score record to the players on it (`CWarMap::SendScorePacket`,
`G/war_map.cpp:641-659`). The record therefore follows the reset and the notice. The
Rewrite sent it first, before the flags were gone.

**The view.** A step (`FUNC_COMBO` is 3) `Sync`s the body to the point
(`CHARACTER::Move`, `G/char.cpp:3610-3622`): it changes the body's sectree but not its
view. Only a walk's motion samples the view (`UpdateSectree`, `G/char_state.cpp:797`), so
a flag that a member walks to comes into her view when the walk is sampled, and a member
that steps there never sees it. The parity scenario's walk ends with a real walk for that
reason, and the flag's take needs the distance, not the view: legacy hands the flag to
the nearest player within 500 units whether or not the flag is in her view.

**The test-server mode.** `CWarMap::CheckScore` (`G/war_map.cpp:683-735`) ends the war
when one side's score reaches the war's end score, and `if (test_server) iEndScore /= 10;`
(`:700`) divides that score by ten in the test-server mode: the battle war ends at ten
points and the flag war at one. Legacy's compiled-in default is on (`G/config.cpp:72`),
and the owner's `CONFIG` files never turn it off, so the deployment ran in the mode. The
Rewrite's `game.test_server` was in the configuration and nothing read it; the world reads
it now (`GameState::with_test_server`), so the war ends where legacy's ends.

**The tests.**

- `prodomo/src/game_state/guild.rs`: `the_take_and_the_score_keep_the_legacy_order` — the
  carrier's affect comes before the map's line, and the map's line comes before the score.
- `prodomo/src/game_state/guild.rs`: `the_end_score_is_a_tenth_in_the_test_server_mode` —
  the flag war ends at one point in the mode and at ten out of it.
- `prodomo/tests/parity.rs`: `the_flag_is_taken_and_the_base_scores_the_war` — a member
  joins the war, walks to the other team's flag, takes it (the flag's affect with the
  flag's guild and the other team's flag bit, the flag's character dies, the map says who
  took it), carries it back to her own base and scores (the flags reset, the map says so,
  and the score record follows with the guild that scored, the guild it scored against and
  the score).

The scenario's war is younger than the thirty seconds `CheckScore` asks for
(`G/war_map.cpp:694`), so its one point does not end the war while the scenario runs.

**The inventory.** `sys.guild.war` keeps its row and gains the note of this section; it
stays `partial`, like the other systems that are live but not wholly on the wire.

**The divergences.**

- The score record follows the map's line without a database round trip. Legacy's record
  is the database's answer, so it arrives a moment later than the line; the order is the
  same.
- The candidates for the take are every player on the war's map, where legacy offers the
  flag to the flag's own sectree and its neighbours (`GetSectree()->ForEachAround(f)`,
  `G/char_state.cpp:1196`). The rule is the distance in both, and a player within 500
  units of the flag is in that sectree or in one of its neighbours, so the outcome is the
  same.

targets, the 133 parity scenarios among them; this slice's unit tests green; no scratch
