## 246. The whisper reaches the character it names (`sys.char.chat`, second part)

Ledger 188 made the `Chat` handler live for the talking, party, guild and shout arms and
left the `Whisper` arm out. This section ports it: the whole of `CInputMain::Whisper`
(`G/input_main.cpp:340-649`), from the record the client sends to the line that lands, and
the line that waits for a character that is not there.

**The record.** `TPacketCGWhisper` (`G/packet.h:587-592`) is the header, the size word, a
25-byte name field and the text. The codec (`protocol/src/cg_whisper.rs`) and the record
the client receives (`protocol/src/gc_whisper.rs`) are new; the handler was not. The name
is a C string, so it ends at the first NUL, and the size is a floor rather than an
equality (`uiBytes < pinfo->wSize` is the only refused relation,
`G/input_main.cpp:344-345`). A size under the fixed part is the legacy's close case
(`iExtraLen < 0`, `:349-353`), and the Rewrite closes there too. The fixed parts are
measured, not summed: 28 bytes for the request and 30 for the answer, from a 32-bit
compile of the verbatim struct bodies under `#pragma pack(1)` with the repository's
known-width controls (a packed two-`long` struct is 8 bytes).

**Where the target is.** The legacy looks in two places: its own character manager
(`CHARACTER_MANAGER::FindPC`, `G/char_manager.cpp:244-260`), which matches the name
without regard to the case, and its P2P manager (`P2P_MANAGER::Find`,
`G/input_main.cpp:403`), which knows the characters of the other cores. The Rewrite runs
every Channel in one process (ADR-0002), so the first lookup is the world's character
manager and the second is the process-wide client registry
(`ChannelClients::outbox_of`). The registry's match ignores the case, as `FindPC` does.

**What the line says.** The record the target receives is the sender's name and the text
(`G/input_main.cpp:624-641`). The type is `WHISPER_TYPE_NORMAL`, or `WHISPER_TYPE_GM` when
the sender is a game master (`G/input_main.cpp:619-620`). The game master is
`CHARACTER::IsGM` (`G/char.cpp:6373-6380`), which is true when the sender's GM level is not
`GM_PLAYER` **or** the test-server mode is on, and the mode is on by default
(`G/config.cpp:72`, and the owner's `CONFIG` files never turn it off). So the Rewrite's
type is the game master's in the default deployment, and the descriptor builds the record
because it holds the sender's GM level and the mode.

The type's high nibble carries an empire when the target is on another Channel
(`G/input_main.cpp:556-566`), and the Channel that receives the line strips it again
(`G/input_p2p.cpp:80-83`). The text conversion that nibble is for is `ConvertEmpireText`,
whose body is empty in this tree (`G/empire_text_convert.cpp:47-55`), so the nibble changes
nothing the client sees. The Rewrite sends the plain type, which is the byte the client
sees in the legacy too.

**The three drops.** The sender's own name drops the line (`if (pkChr == ch) return
(iExtraLen);`, `G/input_main.cpp:372`), an empty line sends nothing (`if (buflen > 0)`,
`:622`), and the sender is told nothing when the line lands. The Rewrite drops the same
three, and the order is the legacy's: the target is found first, the emptiness is checked
in the delivery branch, and the self-check comes before both.

**A character that is not there.** The legacy leaves the line for the target when no
character answers to the name (`G/input_main.cpp:404-505`). The line waits in the DB
server's memory (`CClientManager::m_OfflineMessage`,
`server/server/db/ClientManager.cpp:4631`) and is read back when the target next enters
the game (`CHARACTER::ReadOfflineMessages`, `G/char.cpp:11438-11446`). The DB server is
retired (ADR-0001), so the waiting lines live in the world's memory, which is the same
store in one process. The sender is told with a `WHISPER_TYPE_SYSTEM` record
(`G/input_main.cpp:482-493`): either that the line was left for the target, or that the
sender has to wait, which is ten seconds per sender (`bDelay`,
`G/input_main.cpp:426-428`). The waiting lines are dropped after five hours
(`CClientManager::OfflineMessageGarbage`,
`server/server/db/ClientManager.cpp:4637-4654`), once an hour.

**The tests.**

- `protocol/src/cg_whisper.rs`: the fixed part is 28 packed bytes, the header is 19, the
  record decodes from golden bytes, the size word is little-endian, trailing bytes past the
  declared size are ignored, a short declared size is its own refusal, a truncated prefix is
  reported, the text and the name stop at the first NUL, and every name byte survives.
- `protocol/src/gc_whisper.rs`: the fixed part is 30 packed bytes, the header is 34, a line
  without text is 30 bytes, the record decodes from golden bytes, the size word is
  little-endian, every type byte survives, the `bCanFormat` byte is the legacy's `bool`,
  and a short size, a foreign header and a truncated record are refused.
- `prodomo/src/game_state/whisper.rs`: `the_line_reaches_the_target_and_not_the_sender`,
  `the_sender_hears_nothing_when_it_names_itself`,
  `a_line_for_an_absent_name_waits_and_the_sender_is_told`,
  `a_second_line_within_ten_seconds_is_refused`,
  `an_empty_line_leaves_nothing_and_says_nothing`,
  `the_lines_waiting_for_a_character_are_read_when_it_enters`,
  `a_name_finds_its_character_whatever_the_case` and
  `an_unknown_name_has_no_target`.
- `prodomo/tests/parity.rs`: `a_whisper_reaches_the_character_it_names` — the line reaches
  the character it names, the name is matched without regard to the case, the line crosses
  a Channel, the sender's own name drops it, and an empty line sends nothing.
- `prodomo/tests/parity.rs`: `a_whisper_for_a_character_that_is_not_there_is_left_for_it` —
  the sender is told with the system's notice, and the target reads the waiting line when
  it enters.

The scenario's server has to be ten seconds old before the first line may be left, because
the legacy's wait is measured from the sender's last line, and the sender's clock starts
at zero when its character is created (`dwLastOfflinePMTime`, `G/char.cpp:271`) while
`get_dword_time()` counts the process's uptime. The scenario reads the server's clock from
a handshake and waits for it.

**The inventory.** `cg.game.whisper` and `gc.whisper` are `ported`, with the first
scenario. `sys.char.chat` keeps its `partial` row and gains this section's note: the
banword conversion, `SpamBlockCheck`, the prism check and the whisper-block modes are
absent. `sys.bus` moves from `missing` to `partial`: the whisper crosses Channels through
the client registry, as the shout does, so the notices, find, warp, guild and messenger are
what is left of the bus. The game-to-client coverage moves from 108 implemented rows to 109
and from 26 missing ones to 25, and `AGENTS.md`'s table says so.

**The divergences.**

- The whisper-block modes (`BLOCK_WHISPER`) have no port, so the sender-blocked and
  target-blocked answers are unreachable. The Rewrite has no block mode at all yet.
- The prism's text tag (`ProcessTextTag`, `G/input_main.cpp:574-618`) and `SpamBlockCheck`
  (`:540-553`) are absent, so a line that legacy would refuse or convert goes as it is.
- The banword conversion is not a divergence: the legacy's own call to
  `CBanwordManager::ConvertString` is commented out (`G/input_main.cpp:434`, `:554`), so no
  legacy line is converted either.

## 247. The flag carrier sees the flag before the take (`sys.guild.war`, a follow-up)

Ledger 245's scenario walked straight to the other team's flag and then read until the
affect arrived, taking the flag's insert from the records it had already passed. That read
is a race. The take is the distance alone (`FuncFindChrForFlag`,
`G/char_state.cpp:33-97`); the flag comes into a walking player's view only when the walk's
motion is sampled, which is every sixteenth Pulse (`UpdateSectree`,
`G/char_state.cpp:795`). A walk whose last leg lands within the take can take the flag
before a sample runs, and the flag's character dies with the flag, so the insert never
reaches the carrier at all — on the legacy as on the Rewrite.

The scenario now stages its walk a take short of the flag: a point 1200 units from it,
beyond the take's 500 and inside the view's `VIEW_RANGE + VIEW_BONUS_RANGE`
(`G/entity_view.cpp:94`). The walk there ends in a real walk (`FUNC_MOVE` is 1), whose
motion samples the view, so the flag's insert does arrive, and the scenario reads until it
does before it walks the rest. The take keeps its own place in the wire record: the
affects, the flag's character's removal, the map's line, and the base's score. A failed run
of the scenario before this section showed the race (`the other team's flag came into her
view`, on a run whose `walk_to` landed within the take without a sample).

Two comments in the scenario's helpers were corrected with it. `walk_to`'s refused move is
750 units of `MOVE_DISTANCE_DIVISOR` (`G/input_main.cpp:1757-1891`), that is 75 000 map
units, not 750; and the sampled view's citation is `G/char_state.cpp:795`, where the
sixteenth-Pulse condition stands.

**The test.** `prodomo/tests/parity.rs`:
`the_flag_is_taken_and_the_base_scores_the_war` keeps every assertion it had and gains the
staging walk, the read that waits for the flag's insert, and the take that no longer
carries the insert's race. The scenario ran five times in a row without a variance
besides the full run's green record below.

No product code changed. `sys.guild.war` keeps its `partial` row and gains the note of
this section.

## 248. The friend add, its yes and its remove are live (`sys.messenger`, first part)

The messenger is the friend list: `MessengerManager` (`G/messenger_manager.cpp`) keeps
the relations (`m_Relation`/`m_InverseRelation`, `G/messenger_manager.h:79`), the GM
team list (`ENABLE_MESSENGER_TEAM`, `common/prodomodefines.h:155`), the online set and
the pending requests as CRC pairs (`m_set_requestToAdd`, `:302`). The list rides the
store: `Login` (`:46-60`) asks the DB for the account's rows, and the answer loads the
relations, sends the list, tells every holder of this name of its login, and stands the
GM team list up the same way (`LoadList` `:159-194`, `LoadTeamList` `:24-52`). A player
that leaves loses its rows the same way: `CHARACTER::Disconnect` calls `Logout`
(`G/char.cpp:1817`), which fans the logout to every holder and erases the rows from
memory (`:196-271`).

The wire is two records. `protocol::cg_messenger` is `HEADER_CG_MESSENGER` (67):
the 2-byte base (`TPacketCGMessenger`, `packet.h:1944-1977`), 4 more VID bytes for
`ADD_BY_VID` (0) and a raw 24-byte name field (`CHARACTER_NAME_MAX_LEN`,
`common/length.h:15`) for `ADD_BY_NAME` (1) and `REMOVE` (2). `INVITE_ANSWER` (3)
and every unknown subheader consume the base alone, the analyzer's own default arm
(`G/input_main.cpp:1225-1228`). `protocol::gc_messenger` is `HEADER_GC_MESSENGER`
(74): the 4-byte envelope whose `size` word counts it (`TPacketGCMessenger`,
`packet.h:1877-1906`), one `connected + length + name` entry per companion with no
terminator (`SendList`, `G/messenger_manager.cpp:481-513`), and the login, logout and
`REMOVE_FRIEND` records as an envelope with a length byte and the name. The `INVITE`
subheader (6) is never sent, so the codec declares the byte and produces no record of
it. `protocol::gc_inventory` marks the row implemented: 110 of 134 game-to-client
bytes now, 24 missing (12 fixed-size, 12 dynamic); `AGENTS.md` carries the same
counts.

The store is one table, `db/migrations/0017_messenger_list.sql`: `messenger_list`
holds one row per direction of a friendship, keyed by the `(account, companion)` pair,
because `AuthToAdd` calls `AddToList` twice (`:330-332`) and each call inserts its own
row (`:348-350`). The same pair of inserts with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` is the same
stored fact as legacy's insert-after-freshness-check (`:337-339`). The remove deletes
both legs in either key order, the way `__FIX_DELETE_FRIEND_REFRESH__`'s own DELETE
does (`:447-448`), and `wipe_name` deletes every row either side names, the way the
character deletion does (`server/server/db/ClientManagerPlayer.cpp:1541`). Every
value is a bound parameter: legacy interpolated the names into the SQL
(`:58,349,447-449,474-475`), which the `EscapeString` gate before them (`:51-55`,
`:341-345`) tried to make safe. That gate is a Defect this crate does not reproduce.
The account and companion columns are the ported Name shape, 2 to 24 ASCII letters
and digits.

The world is `prodomo/src/game_state/messenger.rs`, one `Relations` beside the
whisper's own state: the relation and its inverse, keyed by the character Name's
bytes in byte order as legacy's `std::set<std::string>` is. `login` is `LoadList`
and `LoadTeamList`: it loads the rows the caller read, fans `SendLogin`'s LOGIN to
every holder past its GM gate, sends the LIST (none when the list is empty, because
`LoadList` early-returns on `uiNumRows == 0`), and stands the GM team list up from
the grants other than the entrant's own name. `logout` is `MessengerManager::Logout`:
the LOGOUT fans first, then the erase of every map the name is in. `request_to_add`
is `RequestToAdd` (`:273-324`): it refuses a target the relation already holds or a
request already pending, else computes the CRC pair of the two names in the request's
own order (`GetCRC32` at `:294-304`, the byte-at-a-time CRC-32
`game_state::guild_mark` carries for the marks) and sends the target the
`messenger_auth %s` command line, whose answer is the `do_messenger_auth` command.
`auth_to_add` is `AuthToAdd` (`:326-363`): it recomputes the pair with the same two
names in the same order and consumes it, sends the added line (`:346`) and both
LOGIN records to both sides, and answers whether the rows need writing. A deny sends
`[LS;548;%s]` and consumes the pair with no rows (`G/cmd_general.cpp:2288-2291`).
`remove_from_list` is `RemoveFromList` (`:365-451`): it refuses a target the
relation does not hold, else sends `REMOVE_FRIEND` (`:431-451`) and the deleted
line (`:399`) to the two sides legacy does and erases both directions. The GM gate
is `gm_get_level`'s (`G/gm.cpp:12-14`): the record's owner is a player and the
companion is a grant, which legacy answers with no record (`:554-566`). The
test-server mode silences the gate in it, because `gm_new_get_level` answers
`GM_IMPLEMENTOR` before the map is asked (`G/gm.cpp:12-14`).

The descriptor (`prodomo/src/main.rs`) runs the record's own gates before the world
runs `RequestToAdd` past them. The `ADD_BY_VID` arm is `CInputMain::Messenger`'s
(`G/input_main.cpp:1140-1178`): quiet for a VID nobody holds, quiet for a companion
with no outbox, `[LS;659]` when a player adds a GM (in or past the mode), quiet when
the caller names itself; the observer and block-mode gates pass because this build
has no observer mode and block modes are unported. The `ADD_BY_NAME` arm
(`:1180-1214`) reads the target with `FindPC` past its own self and block gates and
answers a name that is not there with `[LS;660;%s]` (`:1196-1198`); the caller's own
level is the points', the name's is the grant the store holds, matched on the account
and the name regardless of the case the way `gm_get_level` reads it
(`G/input_db.cpp:1806-1830`). The remove answers with nothing; the descriptor writes
both rows' delete after the world runs, and a refused delete closes the way a refused
load does. Login reads the rows and the GM names before the world runs, the same
admission the enter's load already is. The answer is `do_messenger_auth`
(`G/cmd_general.cpp:2272-2296`): the second word names the requester and every word
but `y` (first byte) is a deny; the world runs the answer and the descriptor writes
both rows' insert only when the answer became a friendship.

**The test.** `prodomo/tests/parity.rs`:
`a_friend_request_answered_yes_lists_both_directions_and_relogin_keeps_it` proves
the round trip: Alice's `ADD_BY_NAME Yankee` reaches Bob as the `messenger_auth
Alpha` line, Bob's `/messenger_auth y Alpha` lists both directions (each side hears
the added line and the other's LOGIN, and the pair's rows land in the store), the
rows survive the relogin (Alice's next enter carries the LIST with Yankee), and the
remove takes both rows back (the remover hears the `REMOVE_FRIEND` record, the
removed side hears who left the list). The GM `TEAM_LIST` rides behind the enter in
every existing enter helper that grants it, and the login's own LOGOUT and logout
fans prove the leave path. `cg.game.messenger`, `cmd.messenger_auth` and
`gc.messenger` are ported; `sys.messenger` is `partial` (block modes, the invite
answer and the offline rework are not ported). No ADR changed. No owner question
added. V26 is taken.

## 249. The block byte refuses the line it names (`sys.char.chat`, `sys.messenger`, second part)

The block mode is one byte on the character (`m_pointsInstant.bBlockMode`,
`G/char.h:471`) with the seven `EBlockAction` bits (`G/char.h:370-379`):
exchange, party invite, guild invite, whisper, messenger invite, party request,
and view equipment. `CHARACTER::SetBlockMode` (`G/char.cpp:7643-7656`) writes the
byte, chats `setblockmode %d` to the character's own client, and writes the seven
`game_option.block_*` quest flags beside it; `CHARACTER::SetBlockModeForce`
(`:7658-7661`) writes the byte and chats the same line, and no quest flag moves.
`CHARACTER::IsBlockMode` (`G/char.h:899`) tests one bit. The login restores the
byte from the flags: `quest game_option`
(`legacy/gamedata/locale/europe/quest/_basic/game_option.lua`) sums the seven
flag bits into `val` and calls `pc.send_block_mode(val)`, which is
`ch->SetBlockModeForce((BYTE)lua_tonumber(L, 1))`
(`G/questlua_pc.cpp:2190-2197`; a non-number is zero, and only the low byte
survives the cast).

The Rewrite keeps the byte in `GameState::block_modes`, keyed by VID; the store
keeps the seven flags in the character's quest-flag rows, which the descriptor
already loads and saves. `/setblockmode` is `do_setblockmode`
(`G/cmd_general.cpp:2300-2309`): an empty line is quiet (`if (*arg1)`), otherwise
the word reads as a number (`str_to_number`: a non-numeric word is zero, and only
the low byte survives) and becomes the character's own block mode. The world's
answer carries the `setblockmode %d` command line for the client's own queue and
the seven flag writes for the store; the descriptor merges the flags into its
held record (zero flags dropped) and saves the record. `pc.send_block_mode` runs
through the quest bridge: the session chats the same `setblockmode %d` line in
the step's own records, no flag moves, and the last byte the scripts set rides
the session and lands on the world after the step, next to where the world's own
flag writes would have landed.

The two gates that read a bit are live. `CInputMain::Whisper`
(`G/input_main.cpp:340-649`) drops the sender's own name before any block check
(`:372`); a sender who blocks whispers hears the sender-blocked record with the
target's name (`:387-400`, repeated at `:508-517` once the target's descriptor is
known); otherwise the target who blocks whispers answers the target-blocked
record with the target's name (`:518-529`). The legacy writes the name twice
(`strlcpy` into `szNameFrom` both times, `:392-393`) and sends the fixed 30-byte
record with no payload, so the name the client shows is the target's in both
answers (`common/length.h:424-426`: 2 is target-blocked, 3 is sender-blocked).
`CInputMain::Messenger` answers `[LS;657]` when the companion blocks friend
requests, both for the `ADD_BY_VID` arm (`:1154-1160`, past the observer arm and
before the no-desc, GM and self gates) and for the `ADD_BY_NAME` arm
(`:1202-1206`, past the self gate), and the request never runs. The exchange,
party, guild, request and equipment bits ride along unwatched: their use sites
(`G/exchange.cpp:135`, `G/char.cpp:5673`, `:5846`, `:2412`, `G/guild.cpp:2046`)
are unported systems.

**The test.** `prodomo/tests/parity.rs`:
`a_block_byte_refuses_the_line_it_names` proves all five legs: Alice's
`/setblockmode 8` lands her whisper block and she hears the `setblockmode 8`
command line; her whisper to Yankee answers the sender-blocked record naming
Yankee and Bob hears nothing; with her own block cleared and Yankee's block set,
her whisper answers the target-blocked record naming Yankee and he hears
nothing; Yankee's `/setblockmode 16` lands his friend-request block, so Alice's
add answers `[LS;657]`, Yankee hears nothing, and the store holds no
`messenger_list` row. The sender check runs before the target check, so her own
block answers first when both are set. Unit tests pin the parser (digits only,
low byte only, a non-numeric word is zero), the seven flags beside the byte, the
self-name drop before any block check, the blocked records' type and target
name, the messenger `[LS;657]` answers for both arms with no pair waiting, the
bridge's number dwording and low-byte truncation (a non-number is zero, nothing
pushed), and the session's line plus last-wins pending byte.
`cmd.setblockmode` and `lua.pc.send_block_mode` are ported;
`sys.char.chat`, `sys.messenger` and `quest.game_option` stay `partial` (the
unported bits' use sites, INVITE_ANSWER, the offline rework). No ADR changed. No
owner question added. V26 stays open.

## 250. The other block bits refuse at their own gates (`sys.messenger`, third part)

The four use sites the ledger 249 close left unwatched are live. `CExchange::Start`
(`G/exchange.cpp:120-150`): the self trade, the non-player trade, the victim's open
shop or safebox (the busy line), the distance, the victim's live trade (`ALREADY`),
then the victim's `BLOCK_EXCHANGE` bit, which chats the rejecting line. The port
keeps that order: the busy arm before the distance, the `ALREADY` arm before the
block arm, and the block arm chats `The other player is rejecting the exchange.`
to the starter while the victim hears nothing and no trade opens.
`CHARACTER::PartyInvite` (`G/char.cpp:5839-5908`): the non-leader line (`[LS;832]`)
before the guest's `BLOCK_PARTY_INVITE` bit, which answers `[LS;833;%s]` naming
the guest to the inviter while the guest hears nothing and no invite waits.
`CHARACTER::RequestToParty` (`G/char.cpp:5651-5676`): the no-leader line, the live
request, the PC pair, then the leader's `BLOCK_PARTY_REQUEST` bit, which refuses
quietly — the caller answers `PartyRequestDenied`, the leader hears nothing, and
no request waits. `CGuild::Invite` (`G/guild.cpp:2027-2055`): the quest-running
arms before the invitee's `BLOCK_GUILD_INVITE` bit, which answers `[LS;940]` to
the inviter while the invitee hears nothing and no invite waits, before the auth
(`[LS;941]`) and empire (`[LS;942]`) gates.

The offline rework's first gate is live too. `CInputDB::ReadOfflineMessages`
(`G/input_db.cpp:2455-2476`) refuses a character that blocks whispers (`:2460`):
no record is written and the rows stay waiting. The port's
`deliver_offline_messages` returns before taking any row when the entering
character's bit is set, at the same call site the enter answer already held
(`G/input_login.cpp:728-729`).

`MESSENGER_SUBHEADER_CG_INVITE_ANSWER` has no handler arm in the checked-in
server: `protocol/src/cg_messenger.rs:77-78` already records that no arm reads
it, so there is nothing to port.

**The test.** `prodomo/tests/parity.rs`: a new
`a_block_byte_refuses_at_the_exchange_party_and_guild_gates` proves the four legs
(the 100-line lint keeps them out of `a_block_byte_refuses_the_line_it_names`).
Yankee spawns beside Alpha (the trade's distance arm runs before the block arm),
and the purse rides in before the enter (the founding judge reads the world's
in-memory gold): his exchange bit answers the rejecting line to Alice and he
hears nothing; his party-invite bit answers `[LS;833;Yankee]` to her and he hears
nothing; Alice's request bit then refuses Yankee's `/party_request` quietly (he
hears `PartyRequestDenied`, she hears nothing); then she founds `MyGuild` and her
guild-invite answers `[LS;940]` to her while Yankee hears nothing. A
`set_block_mode` helper sends each `/setblockmode` line and drains its command
line, skipping the peer's arrival chats on a fresh enter. Unit tests pin each
gate's line, silence, and waiting-row absence, plus the offline-message drop with
the rows left waiting. `sys.messenger` stays `partial` (the team list beyond the
GMs, INVITE_ANSWER's absent arm, the offline rework's remainder). No ADR changed.
No owner question added. V26 stays open.

## 251. The deleted character's friends forget it (`sys.messenger`, `sys.login.character`)

The character deletion wiped every messenger row the name was in, either as the
account or as the companion
(`snprintf(queryStr, ..., "DELETE FROM messenger_list%s WHERE account='%s' OR \
companion='%s'", ..., szName, szName)`, `D/ClientManagerPlayer.cpp:1541`), so no
row names a character that is gone. The port's `db::players::delete_player` did
not, so a deleted character's friendships survived as rows a `pc.change_name`
rename never touches (`pc_change_name`'s wipe is `MessengerManager::RemoveAllList`,
`G/questlua_pc.cpp:2291-2292`, and that bridge is not ported; the select-phase
`CHANGE_NAME` that is ported only clears the flag). A recreated character with
the same Name would inherit a live friend list it never made.

The fix reads the name before the archiving delete and wipes its rows in the same
transaction, and only when the delete takes the row: a refused delete (wrong
code, a level outside the limits, an empty slot) leaves the lists alone. The
delete parity scenario seeds both legs of an Alpha-Beta friendship before the
delete and asserts afterwards that no row names Alpha, and the `db` unit test
asserts the wipe beside the archived row.

`sys.login.character` stays `ported` (its scenario now names the wipe) and
`sys.messenger` stays `partial` (the team list beyond the GMs, INVITE_ANSWER's
absent arm, the offline rework's remainder). No ADR changed. No owner question
added. V26 stays open.

## 252. The tenth whisper in a run closes the connection (`sys.char.chat`)

The whisper's chat-counter gate is live. `CInputMain::Whisper`
(`G/input_main.cpp:352-362`, behind `#ifdef ENABLE_WHISPER_CHAT_SPAMLIMIT`):
the counter increments on the reset of a new window first, ahead of the
block-chat affect and the rest of the handler; at 10 and above the line is
consumed with no record and a disconnect is scheduled (`DelayedDisconnect(0)`),
while below 10 the line proceeds through the rest of the handler. The port's
`ChatState::judge_whisper_counter` runs that gate at the same call site — the
top of the whisper handler, before the character lookup — on the same counter
the chat lines share (`held.chat`), with the same window reset
(`CHAT_COUNTER_WINDOW_PULSES`, five seconds) and the same disconnect refusal.
A whisper has no interpreter arm, so unlike a chat line no `/`-prefixed text
escapes the counter.

**The test.** `prodomo/tests/parity.rs`: a new
`a_tenth_whisper_in_a_run_closes_the_connection` sends ten lines back to back
(the burst leaves no room for a five-second window reset between sends) and
proves the nine reach the character they name while the tenth is consumed, the
target hears nothing of it, and the connection closes. The sends carry no reads
between them, so the delivery loop skips only the ambient strays (a stamina
refill, the walk's own look update, an ownership clear, a view removal) with a
deadline drain, and the sender's own walk strays are read only until the close
or the first quiet beat. Unit tests pin the gate: nine pass, the tenth refuses,
and a later window passes again.

`sys.char.chat` stays `partial` (`SpamBlockCheck`, the prism check). No ADR
changed. No owner question added. V26 stays open.

## 253. A player lists a grant but hears logout for the name (`sys.messenger`, fourth part)

`MessengerManager::SendLogin` answers nothing when the record's owner is a player
and the companion is a grant (`ch->GetGMLevel() == GM_PLAYER &&
gm_get_level(companion.c_str()) != GM_PLAYER`, `G/messenger_manager.cpp:554-556`),
while `SendLogout` has no such gate (`G/messenger_manager.cpp:571-593`). The
relation still lands both directions: `AuthToAdd` inserts both legs whatever the
gate says (`G/messenger_manager.cpp:328-332`), and `__AddToList` answers the
offline leg through the ungated `SendLogout` (`G/messenger_manager.cpp:336-355`).
The port's `Relations::auth_to_add` answered the online leg with LOGIN whenever
the companion stood in the game, so a player listing a grant heard LOGIN for a
name legacy never logs in. The port now answers through the same gate: LOGIN
only when the companion is online and neither the owner-player/grant-companion
pair holds, else LOGOUT. The companion's level is the points' own when the
companion is online (`gm_get_level`, `G/gm.cpp:110-113`, resolved at admission
from the store's grant) and the player's when nobody answers to the name, which
is legacy's list's own answer since its list holds nothing. The gate reads
`state.test_server` for both sides (`G/gm.cpp:53`: the mode makes every level
`GM_IMPLEMENTOR`), so the mode keeps answering LOGIN everywhere, and the
scenario runs with `test_server = false` to prove the live gate. The load path
that fans a login to every holder of the name (`G/messenger_manager.cpp:190-193`)
already ran through the same gate; `companion_level_of` now serves both call
sites. The `CG_MESSENGER` add arm's own GM gate (`G/input_main.cpp:1186-1190`,
`[LS;659]`) is untouched: the scenario's asker is the grant, so its ask passes.

**The test.** `prodomo/tests/parity.rs`: a new
`a_player_lists_a_gm_but_hears_logout_for_the_name` grants Alpha `HIGH_WIZARD`
to Alice's account, enters Alice (no team record: the grant names her own
character) and Yankee (the grant's `TEAM_LIST` trails his burst, which
`enter_world_on_with_team` drains), and proves Alice's `ADD_BY_NAME Yankee`
reaches Yankee as the `messenger_auth Alpha` ask, his yes lists both directions
in the store, and the answers split: Alice hears Yankee as LOGIN while Yankee
hears Alpha as LOGOUT, never LOGIN. Yankee walks (his fixture row sets no
stamina, and the schema default is 0) and already saw Alice inside his own
enter burst, so only `alice.sees_arrive(..., true, ...)` follows the enters.
Unit tests pin both legs: a player companion answers LOGIN to the owner's
registry outbox, while a grant companion answers LOGOUT with the pair still
holding.

`sys.messenger` stays `partial` (the team list beyond the GMs, INVITE_ANSWER's
absent arm, the offline rework's remainder). No ADR changed. No owner question
added. V26 stays open.

## 254. The team's login and logout fans are proved (`sys.messenger`, fifth part)

The port carried the team's login and logout fans since 248, but nothing proved
them. The sweep is closed at the negative control: `RemoveAllList` appears only
in `G/messenger_manager.cpp` (its sole caller is the unported `pc_change_name`
quest bridge, ledger 251), `P2PLogin`/`P2PLogout` are retired with the DB-peer
protocol (ADR-0002), and `GC_INVITE` has no send site (`INvite` lives only in the
packet enum). What is live is `LoadTeamList`'s own fans
(`G/messenger_manager.cpp:48-52`), `SendTeamList` with its online/offline split
(`:99-136`), `SendTeamLogin` with no GM gate (`:145-176`), `SendTeamLogout`
(`:178-208`), and the two fan loops of `Logout` (`:241-246`).

The port already stood all of it up 1:1 except one deliberate absence: legacy's
`Logout` returns early for a name the login set never held (`:243-244`), while
the port fans unconditionally. The set exists only to suppress the DB round trip
`Login` runs; the fans and the erase are pure memory work the port's `Logout`
repeats exactly, and the port has no DB trip to suppress, so there is nothing
to skip. Three new unit tests pin the delivery split the sweep turned up: the
entrant's own TEAM_LIST rides the world's own outbox
(`write_to_client(vid)`), while the holders' TEAM_LOGIN and TEAM_LOGOUT ride
the registry (`deliver`, by name) — `a_login_sends_the_team_list_to_the_entrant`,
`a_login_fans_the_team_login_to_every_holder`,
`a_logout_fans_the_team_logout_to_every_holder`. Parity extends the 253
scenario's drop: Yankee holds both a friend row and a team row for Alpha, so
Alice's disconnect answers the release, the LOGOUT, the TEAM_LOGOUT, and the
removal, in `Logout`'s own fan order (`:203-208` before `:241-246`).

`sys.messenger` stays `partial` (the team list beyond the GMs, INVITE_ANSWER's
absent arm, the offline rework's remainder). No ADR changed. No owner question
added. V26 stays open.

## 255. A GM silences a character for a parsed time (`cmd.block_chat`, `cmd.jy`, `sys.char.chat`)

The lay is `do_block_chat` (`G/cmd_gm.cpp:3364-3433`) with the retirement ledger
it forced. The gate runs before the split (`:3366-3370`): `answer_block_chat`
asks `block_chat_allowed` first, so a player that sends an empty line hears the
refusal, never the usage — the upgraded gate test runs the whole dispatch for
that reason. The split is `one_argument`, the time is `parse_time_str`
(`G/utils.cpp:236-287`), and the port matches it byte for byte: a bare number
adds when the back ends with no unit, an empty back is 0, and a byte outside
the digits and `s`/`m`/`h`/`d` refuses the line. The refusal is the two format
lines, never the usage. A space refuses the line, so the usage example's own
`1m 30s` never lays; the scenario pins that the example spells a lay legacy
refuses.

The rework the slice turned up is that `do_block_chat` has no unsilence arm.
Its last lines (`:3429-3430`) are a bare `AddAffect` for every lay, 0 included:
a 0 (and a bare name, which parses to 0) is the same `AddAffect(223,
POINT_NONE, 0, 0, 0, 0, true)` a 90-second lay is, and `AddAffect` stands a 0
duration up to 1 (`G/char_affect.cpp:676-680`). The `[LS;988]` release belongs
to `RemoveAffect(AFFECT_BLOCK_CHAT)` (`:863-868`), which no command, whisper
arm, or talk arm calls — the sweep of `AFFECT_BLOCK_CHAT` outside
`char_affect.cpp` finds only the two command lays, the whisper gate, the talk
gate, the GG arm, and the enum. So the port lays the 0, chats no release, and
the lay's own 1-to-0 tick lifts it: that tick is the slice's recorded
Divergence, because legacy's silence never ticks (the tick loop
`ProcessAffect` decrements every row, `:424-442`, but the silence's own event
never runs — legacy's `StartAffectEvent` cadence is the unported `passes_per_sec`
event wheel). The quiet-0-lift the tree carried was a fiction; the scenario's
tail now retires the old row, lands the 0-add, and reads the tick's own
remove within the second, with the store row still standing.

The rest is 1:1. A lay over one tick chats `[LS;852]` before the add
(`AddAffect`, `:670-674`); the override retires the old row first, then the
add lands. The talk gate answers `SendBlockChatInfo` (`G/input_main.cpp:126-155`)
with the full ladder — `[LS;652]` at 0, 1028 for hours and minutes, 1029 for
hours alone, 1030 for minutes alone, 1042 for seconds alone — carried by a new
`BlockChatInfo` effect, never the old flat key. The whisper gate answers the
`[LS;652]` info line (`:364-368`), after the spam counter (`:355-362`) the
port keeps in 252's stead. A live lay writes its row, as `AddAffect` writes
`QUERY_ADD_AFFECT` for a PC (`:756-765`); an offline name's row is written by
the name (`CClientManager::BlockChat`, `db/ClientManager.cpp:2159-2186`),
quiet when no row carries it, and the caller hears the requested line either
way. The silence rides the load (`LoadAffect`, `:573-666`): a restored row's
add rides the enter-game burst behind the update, and only the silence is
saved, because only it is ported.

`cmd.block_chat` and `cmd.jy` go `ported` on
`a_gm_silences_a_character_and_the_silence_answers_its_chat`, which lays
`1m30s`, reads the notice and the add, hears `[LS;1030;1;30]` on a talking
line, the `[LS;652]` info line on a whisper, the usage on an empty line, the
format pair on a spaced time, quiet on the caller's own name, and the 0 lay's
retire-add-tick tail. `cmd.vote_block_chat` stays `missing`: its body returns
before its first split. `cmd.block_chat_list` stays `missing`: its answer is
the unported `QID_BLOCK_CHAT_LIST` return query.

Gates: fmt clean; build with no warnings; clippy green with `-D warnings` on
the workspace all-targets run; doc green with `-D warnings`; doc-tests green
(1 passed, 25 ignored); the full workspace all-targets DB run green on all 40
targets (prodomo lib 1238, parity 141 of 141, protocol 1267), with the new
silence scenario among the passes; no scratch database left. `rustfmt` and

## 256. A new session forgets the last one's block byte and offline clock (`sys.messenger`, sixth part)

The offline rework's remainder turned out to be state that outlived its session. Every
enter in legacy is a new `CHARACTER`, and `CHARACTER::Initialize` zeroes the block mode
with the rest of `m_pointsInstant` (`memset(&m_pointsInstant, 0, ...)`, `G/char.cpp:252`)
and the offline-line clock (`dwLastOfflinePMTime = 0`, `:270-271`). The port keeps both
in the world, keyed by VID (`GameState::block_modes`, `GameState::last_offline_pm`), and
a player's VID is its player id (`character_vid`, `prodomo/src/main.rs`), so the next
session of the same character found the last one's values under the same key. The leave
cleaned every other VID-keyed map (the outbox, the affect event, the browse, the trade,
the storage, the portal times and the body) and missed these two. Three things followed
from it. A sender that came back inside ten seconds was told to wait, where legacy lets
the first line of the new session through. A character that blocked whispers kept the
block across a relog in this run, while its client was never sent the `setblockmode`
line that shows it, and lost it at a restart. And the offline read at the enter gated on
the last session's byte, so the lines that waited for a character that had once blocked
whispers stayed unread. `GameState::forget_whisper_session` now drops both values when a
character leaves, for every departure, beside `forget_portal_times`.

The sweep for writers of the byte is closed at both controls: `bBlockMode` is written only
by `SetBlockMode` (`do_setblockmode`, `G/cmd_general.cpp:2309`) and `SetBlockModeForce`
(`pc_send_block_mode`, `G/questlua_pc.cpp:2194`). Ledger 249 said the login restores the
byte through `quest game_option`, and that holds for legacy only. The bridge is live, but
nothing runs the quest `login` event: `CQuestManager::Login` (`G/questmanager.cpp:541-556`,
called from `QuestLoad` or `quest_login_event`, `G/input_db.cpp:1005-1048` and
`:1104-1115`) has no counterpart in `quest::Manager`, while `levelup` and `kill`, the
positive controls, are dispatched from `game_state/quests.rs`. So until
`event.input_db.quest_login_event` is ported a session starts with the byte at zero, as
legacy's does for the moment before its login event. Twenty-seven quests have login
scripts, which is why that event is a slice of its own. `game_option`'s own script adds 6,
not 64, for `block_view_equipment`; the quest source is never edited (ADR-0004), so the
event will reproduce it when it lands.

The read is in the order legacy runs it. `CClientManager::RequestReadOfflineMessages`
answers every waiting line and erases them (`server/server/db/ClientManager.cpp:4613-4629`,
the erase at `:4628`), and only then does `CInputDB::ReadOfflineMessages` refuse a
character that blocks whispers (`G/input_db.cpp:2460`). The refused lines are gone.
Ledger 250 said they stay waiting, which misread where the erase is. The port now takes
the lines before its gate. With the byte at zero at every enter the gate cannot fire at
the enter today, which is also legacy's usual case: the read's answer is one DB round
trip, while the login event that restores the byte waits for the next tick of a
one-second event. The garbage sweep drops a line at five hours to the millisecond:
`duration_cast<hours>(age).count() >= iHour` truncates (`:4648`), and the port kept a line
that was exactly five hours old.

Nothing else of the messenger is left. Ledger 248 recorded "the team list beyond the
GMs". Legacy's team query is `SELECT '%s',mName FROM common.gmlist WHERE mName!='%s'`
(`G/messenger_manager.cpp:61-62`), every row of the table whatever its `mAuthority` or
`mServerIP`, less the entrant's own name under MySQL's case-insensitive comparison. The
descriptor lists every grant but the entrant's own, compared without regard to the case
(`messenger_load`, `prodomo/src/main.rs`). The only rows legacy would list beyond that are
`PLAYER` rows, which `gm_grant` refuses by its `CHECK` (migration 0001: "a player needs no
grant"). `MESSENGER_SUBHEADER_CG_INVITE_ANSWER` has no handler arm (ledger 250). Two
legacy details of the offline path were checked and need nothing: the text the port
stores already stops at its first NUL and at `CHAT_MAX_LEN` (`CgWhisper::decode`), as
`strlcpy` into `buf` does (`G/input_main.cpp:430-432`), and `bCanFormat` stays true on the
delivered line, because its only `false` is behind `__BL_CLIENT_LOCALE_STRING__`
(`G/input_main.cpp:630`), which nothing defines (the same sweep finds
`LOCALE_STRING_RENEWAL` defined at `common/prodomodefines.h:32`).

**The test.** `prodomo/tests/parity.rs`: a new
`a_new_session_forgets_the_last_ones_block_byte_and_offline_clock`. Yankee blocks
whispers and leaves. Alice blocks whispers and comes back, so her line to the absent
Yankee is left for him (the system's sent notice), not refused as the sender's block. Her
second line is told to wait. She comes back again and her third line is left at once, and
the scenario asserts that the relog fit inside the ten seconds, or the line would not tell
the two clocks apart. Yankee comes back and reads the first and the third line as
`WHISPER_TYPE_OFFLINE` records from Alpha, because his block went with his last session.
Unit tests in `game_state/whisper.rs`: `a_new_session_may_leave_a_line_at_once`,
`a_new_session_starts_with_no_block_byte`, `a_line_is_dropped_at_five_hours_and_not_before`,
and `a_character_who_blocks_whispers_loses_the_lines_that_waited` (renamed from 250's
`a_character_who_blocks_whispers_reads_no_waiting_line`, whose assertion now holds that the
line is gone). Mutation sweep, each mutant applied to the fixed file and restored by
checksum, all semantic kills and none a compile error: dropping the leave's call fails both
session unit tests and the scenario (at Alice's first line, the sender-blocked record);
dropping only the clock's removal fails the scenario at the third line; `<=` for `<` in the
sweep fails the five-hour test; and gating before the take fails the blocking-reader test.

`sys.messenger` goes `ported` on
`a_friend_request_answered_yes_lists_both_directions_and_relogin_keeps_it`, with the note
naming the scenarios of 249 to 256. `lua.pc.send_block_mode` stays `ported`, but its
scenario is now the unit test that runs it
(`prodomo/src/game_state/quests.rs::send_block_mode_lands_the_line_and_the_last_byte_wins`):
the scenario 249 named never reaches the bridge, and no binary scenario can until the login
event is ported. `quest.game_option`, `event.input_db.quest_login_event` and
`cg.game.messenger` have new notes. The 249 scenario's doc no longer says the next enter
still refuses.

Gates: fmt clean; build with no warnings; clippy green with `-D warnings`; doc green with
`RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings"`; doc-tests green (1 passed, 25 ignored); the full workspace
all-targets DB run green on all 40 targets (prodomo lib 1241, parity 142 of 142, protocol
1267) against `postgres:18` in Podman; no scratch database left. `rustfmt` and
`cargo-clippy` are the `/usr/bin` pair.

No ADR changed. No owner question added. V26 stays open.

## 257. The quest login event (`event.input_db.quest_login_event`, `quest.game_option`)

A character now runs its quest `login` event when it enters the game. `quest::Manager::login`
is `CQuestManager::Login` (`G/questmanager.cpp:541-556`) with `NPC::OnLogin`
(`G/questnpc.cpp:353-397`). It needs a character the manager has seen, which the load makes,
as `CheckQuestLoaded` needs `IsLoaded`. One pass runs every no-NPC `login` script in quest
order, at the character's state of each quest, or at the start state when the character
never ran the quest and may start it (`MatchingQuest`, `G/questnpc.h:112-139`). This is
`HandleReceiveAllNoWaitEvent`, so a script still waiting for its client is closed with
legacy's `QUEST NOT END RUNNING on Login/Logout` warning. A second pass runs every `letter`
script the same way (`HandleReceiveAllEvent`), and there a waiting script is kept
(`G/questnpc.cpp:621-758`). The pass is the new `Run::handle_receive_all`. `levelup` moves
onto it as well, because `NPC::OnLevelUp` is `HandleReceiveAllEvent` too (`:348-351`), so it
runs matches and starts in one quest-order pass instead of `handle_event`'s order, which ran
every match before every start.

`GameState::quest_login` runs in `answer_enter_world` after `shown_on_admit`. That puts it
behind the messenger login and `deliver_offline_messages`, and its records ride the outbox
that `main.rs` drains after the burst. So the client gets them behind the burst, the war
list, the team list, the friend LIST and the offline lines, which is legacy's order: the
offline read is synchronous in `Entergame` (`G/input_login.cpp:728-729`), and the login
waits for the quest load. A Warp re-enters through `answer_enter_world`, so the login runs on
every Warp, as legacy's reconnect does. A Divergence on timing: the login runs at once. When
legacy's quest load lands before the game phase, `quest_login_event` runs the login at the
first one-second tick that finds the character in the game (`G/input_db.cpp:1005-1048`,
`:1104-1115`).

Two API names join `BRIDGED`, which goes from 60 to 62.

- `pc.getqf` (`pc_get_quest_flag`, `G/questlua_pc.cpp:1180-1197`) reads the running quest's
  flag `QUEST.NAME`, 0 when unset. An argument that is not a string is warned
  `QUEST wrong get flag` and answers nothing.
- `pc.send_block_mode`. Its dispatch arm has existed since ledger 249, but the name was never
  bridged, so a Lua call to it was refused. Ledger 256's unit test reached the arm directly
  and could not see this.

What a login sends. For a character on a map no zone script names, every enter hears:

- `dungeoninfo`'s `dungeon_info_qid 1`, because it is the first quest of `quest_list`;
- `event_info`'s `event_info 0 0 0`, because no ported system sets an event flag;
- `game_option`'s `syschat`, which names what the stored `block_*` flags block, but only
  when the byte is not 0, then its `setblockmode N`.

`game_option` adds 6 for `block_view_equipment`, as its source says (ADR-0004). From level 30,
`item_attr67add`'s `send_letter` sends `[QUESTBUTTON idx;40|name;Sixth and Seventh Bonus][DONE]`
in skin 0. These are the bytes legacy's `SendScript` sends. Legacy then sends a
`GC_QUEST_INFO` that titles the button (`q.set_title`, `q.start`, then `SendQuestInfoPakcet`
from `EndRunning`, `G/questpc.cpp:231-308`, `:343-346`). The port's `q.set_title` refuses, so
that record is missing. This is the next slice. Four more login scripts are worth noting:

- `sash_mission`, for a non-GM from level 40, moves to `information`.
- `yohara_system`, from level 120, moves to `information_new`.
- The letters of both states end at `find_npc_by_vnum`, a refusal, so nothing reaches the
  client.
- `costume_option` and `ds_give_qualification` refuse silently.

**Not ported.** `EndRunning` runs the old state's `leave`, the new state's `enter` and its
`letter` when a script changes its state (`G/questpc.cpp:352-371`), and the port runs none of
them. So legacy sends a level-40 character the sash letter twice at login: once from the state
change and once from the letter pass. The port sends it neither time.

**A port Defect, fixed.** A `set_state` was lost whenever the script did not end in its first
step:

- One called before a `wait`, `select` or `input` was carried on the `Pc`, but nothing applied
  it when the answer ended the script.
- One called after a resume was dropped outright.

The cause: `execute` applied the pending state only when the first step ended, and the
refusal and error paths threw it away. Now `Run::end_running` applies it at every end of a
script, whether the script finished, refused or failed, because legacy's `EndRunning` follows
every `RunState` that returns false. `Running` carries its quest's number for this. A
Divergence remains: `quest_setstate` writes the state and its flag at once
(`G/questlua_quest.cpp:112-146`), but the port moves the quest only when the script ends. So
a character that leaves while the script waits keeps the old state.

**The tests.** `prodomo/tests/parity.rs`. The harness reads the login on every enter path:

- `Keyed::level` comes from the loading burst's `POINT_LEVEL` (slot 1).
- `read_login_event` and `read_login_event_blocking` read the four lines and, from level 30,
  the letter.
- `read_enter_tail` is the hand-read enter tail of five scenarios.
- `enter_world_blocking` enters a character whose flags block something.

With the login wired and the harness unchanged, 119 of the 142 scenarios failed on records
nobody accounted for. That is the positive control that every enter runs it.

## 258. The quest window's info (`lua.q.set_title`, `lua.q.start`, `gc.quest_info`)

The level-30 login letter now titles its quest in the client's quest window, and the window's
entry runs the quest's `info` page. Ledger 257 sent `item_attr67add`'s button and stopped at
`q.set_title`, a refusal; legacy follows the button with a `GC_QUEST_INFO`.

**The record.** `protocol::gc_quest_info` is `HEADER_GC_QUEST_INFO` (81), byte 81 of
`gc_inventory`, now implemented. `packet_quest_info` (`G/packet.h:1868-1877`) is header,
`WORD size`, `WORD index`, `WORD c_index` (`__QUEST_RENEWAL__`, `prodomodefines.h:18`) and
`flag`: 8 bytes. The i686 cross compiler is not installed on this machine, so the width was
measured with `clang++-19 -target i686-linux-gnu -fsyntax-only` and `static_assert`:
`packet_script` 6, a packed two-`long` struct 8 and `sizeof(long)` 4 as controls, an assertion
of 7 failing as the negative control, and the x86-64 target failing the `long` controls. Each
`flag` bit appends one part in bit order (`quest::PC::SendQuestInfoPakcet`,
`G/questpc.cpp:231-308`): the begin byte, the 31-byte title, the 17-byte clock name, the
clock's `int`, the 17-byte counter name, the counter's `int`, the 25-byte icon file. The
decoder refuses bit 7, a begin byte other than 0 or 1, and a size that is not 8 plus the parts.

Three legacy Defects in it are not reproduced (`docs/STATUS.md`, PROTOCOL_NOTES):

- The size word is always 8: the struct is copied into the buffer before each part adds its
  length to `qi.size`. The client reads the parts by `flag`, but a record whose parts arrive
  after its first 8 bytes would be framed wrong. The encoder writes the whole record's size.
- A name is written as `N` bytes from `c_str()`, so the bytes past its terminating zero are
  whatever the string's buffer held. The encoder writes zeros there.
- A name of `N` bytes or more is sent with no terminator. The encoder keeps `N - 1` bytes.

**The runtime.** `q.set_title`, `q.start` and `q.done` join `BRIDGED`, 62 to 65, in a new
`window_api` beside `pc_api` and `guild_api`:

- `q.set_title` takes the last argument, text or a number (`lua_tostring`), and sets the
  title bit (`quest_set_title`, `G/questlua_quest.cpp:36-45`; `SetCurrentQuestTitle`,
  `G/questpc.cpp:458-462`). Anything else changes nothing.
- `q.start` begins a quest only when its `iIndex` is 0 (`SetCurrentQuestStartFlag`,
  `G/questpc.cpp:215-221`, `:441-450`), and `PC::SetQuest` gives every numbered quest its
  number. So `send_letter`'s `q.start` changes nothing, and the letter's record carries the
  title alone: flag 2, index 40, category 0.
- `q.done` ends a numbered quest: the begin byte goes to 0 and its bit is set
  (`SetCurrentQuestDoneFlag`, `:223-229`, `:433-439`). Of the owner's quests only
  `clear_letter` reaches it, on `event_end`, which waits for `cmd.eventflag`; `questlib.lua`'s
  `restart_quest`, `complete_quest`, `giveup_quest` and `complete_quest_state` call it too, and
  no quest calls them (`restart_quest` is found inside `giveup_quest_menu`, the positive
  control). The row stays partial with a unit test.

Each running script carries a `Window` (index, begin flag, title and the two send bits) that
starts empty with the quest's number, moves into the call context while a step runs and back
before any end reads it. `Run::end_running` sends it through the new `Game::quest_info` when a
bit is set, before the script's `set_state` lands, which is `EndRunning`'s order
(`G/questpc.cpp:342-346`, then `:352-371`). The prodomo `Session` encodes it into the step's
records, so the record follows the button's `GC_SCRIPT`.

`c_index` is `GetQuestCategoryByQuestIndex(qi.index)` (`G/questmanager.cpp:312-318`), keyed by
the `WORD` index. `Manager::load` now reads `quest/questcategory.txt` as
`ReadQuestCategoryToDict` does under `_QR_MS_` (`:320-365`): the first word is `atoi`'s
category, the second the quest's name, and an unknown name is warned with legacy's line. A
line of fewer than two words is warned and skipped, where legacy indexes past its vector (a
Defect, `docs/STATUS.md`). A missing file is logged and every category is 0. The owner's file
is empty, so every category is 0.

**The window's entry.** `CG_SCRIPT_BUTTON` with the high bit is the quest window's
`__SelectQuest` (`CInputMain::ScriptButton`, `G/input_main.cpp:2189-2193`). `GameState::quest`
routes it to the new `Manager::info`, which is `CQuestManager::QuestInfo`
(`G/questmanager.cpp:739-765`) and `NPC::OnInfo` (`G/questnpc.cpp:761-808`): nothing while a
script runs, nothing for a quest the character has no state of (`QUEST no quest by`), and
otherwise the quest's `info` script at that state, or a `QUEST no info script by state`
warning. Unlike the button, it never starts a quest. `m_bQuestInfoFlag` is written and never
read, so it has no port. A confirm waiting would take the press first in legacy; `confirm`
is still refused, so no script waits on one.

For `item_attr67add` the `info` page is its `when button or info` text in skin 1, then
`set_state(talk)`. `talk` has no `info` and no `login`, so a second press answers nothing and
the next login sends no letter.

**The tests.** `prodomo/tests/parity.rs`:

- `GC_QUEST_INFO` joins `dynamic_len`, `word_sized` and `game_len`, sized by its own word.
- `read_login_event_blocking` reads, from level 30, the golden record `server_quest_title(40,
  "Sixth and Seventh Bonus")` after the button, built in `packet_quest_info` field order. Every
  scenario that enters a character at level 30 or above reads it: all 143 pass.
- New scenario `the_quest_window_runs_the_letters_info_and_the_quest_moves_on`: Alpha
  (level 154) enters, presses the window's entry for quest 40 and gets the page in skin 1 with
  `[DONE]`. A second press, a press for quest 999 and one for `dungeoninfo` (quest 1, a
  `button` with no `info`) are unanswered. After the disconnect,
  `item_attr67add.__status` is stored as -1624975941, the CRC32 of `talk` (0x9f24d5bb) as a
  signed `long`. The next login sends the three lines and no letter.

Unit tests:

- `protocol`: six in `gc_quest_info`: the letter's golden bytes, every part in bit order (107
  bytes), the done byte and the bare 8-byte record, `c_field`'s cut, the decoder's refusals
  (legacy's size 8 among them) and each bit's part size.
- `quest`: `questcategory_txt_reads_as_the_word_split_did`,
  `the_quest_window_names_follow_legacys_argument_rules`,
  `the_letter_titles_its_quest_and_the_window_runs_its_info` (with a press while the OX
  manager's menu waits and one for `dungeoninfo`) and
  `the_window_sends_the_parts_its_bits_name_under_the_words_index`.
- `prodomo`: `the_letter_titles_its_quest_and_the_window_runs_its_info` (a press before the
  login is quiet, the golden record follows the button, the page runs) and
  `the_quest_window_goes_out_as_one_quest_info_record` (golden bytes with category 0x0203 and
  the begin byte).

**Mutation sweep.** Fifteen mutants, each applied to the pristine file, checked to change
executable code by line position, and restored by checksum. All fifteen are semantic kills,
none by compile error:

- `quest`: the window not moved back after a resume; `end_running` not sending; `q.start`'s
  and `q.done`'s conditions inverted; `q.set_title` setting no bit; `info` starting a quest
  with no state; `info` running the `button` event; the category looked up by a fixed index;
  the begin byte on every record; `info` running while a script waits. The last survived the
  first pass, which is why the OX-menu press was added to the manager test. The `q.start`,
  `q.done` and `q.set_title` mutants were re-run after the Clippy refactor moved them into
  `window_api`.
- `prodomo`: the high bit pressing the button; the record not queued; the category dropped;
  the high bit kept on the index. The category mutant is invisible with the owner's empty
  `questcategory.txt`, which is why the session golden test carries category 0x0203.
- `protocol`: legacy's size word of 8.

The sweep's first pass compared line sets and reported three mutants as "not code" because
the mutated line also appears elsewhere in the file; the comparison is now positional.

`info` running the `button` event was first set aside as equivalent, on a search of the
`.quest` files alone, where all 14 triggers are `when button or info`. The search widened to
`.lua` (`when (.* or )?(info|button)\b` over `legacy/gamedata/locale/europe/quest`; 25
triggers in 19 files; `game_option.lua` as the negative control with 0 hits, and a lone
`when info begin` line as the positive control) finds two `button` triggers with no `info`:
`dungeoninfo` and `guild_war_join`. `dungeoninfo` runs at every login, so the manager test
and the scenario now press its window entry and expect nothing, which kills the mutant.

## 259. The sash and Yohara letters (`lua.find_npc_by_vnum`, `lua.target.vid`, `lua.pc.setqf`, `gc.target_create_new`)

A script's state change now runs the scripts legacy's `EndRunning` runs, so the sash letter
reaches the client and marks Theowahdan. Ledger 257 moved the sash and Yohara quests on at the
login and stored their states, but ran no `leave`, `enter` or `letter` script on the change,
and the letter pass ended both letters at `find_npc_by_vnum`, a refusal.

**The state change.** `Run::end_running` hands the state the script's last `set_state` named
to the new `Run::goto_state`, with the state the script started in. That is
`quest::PC::EndRunning` (`G/questpc.cpp:310-374`, the change at `:352-371`):

1. The quest and its `__status` flag move to the new state. When it is the old one, nothing
   else runs.
2. The old state's `leave` script runs at the old state; running it puts the flag back, as
   `PC::SetQuest` does.
3. The quest and the flag move to the new state, and its `enter` script runs.
4. The new state's `letter` script runs when the flag still names the new state. An `enter`
   that moved the quest on again has changed it, so its letter does not run.

Each script runs as `NPC::ExecuteEventScript` runs it (`G/questnpc.cpp:966-988`, through
`CQuestManager::EnterState`, `LeaveState` and `Letter`, `G/questmanager.cpp:474-514`): the
quest's own no-NPC script for that event and state, nested inside the end that started it, so
a script that ends runs its own `EndRunning` first. `Run` carries the no-NPC scripts
(`no_npc`) and the nesting depth (`changes`). A change past 16 deep logs an error and moves
the quest without running its scripts; legacy recurses until its stack runs out. That is a
Divergence (`STATE_CHANGE_DEPTH`, `docs/STATUS.md`). The status flag is written only in
`goto_state` and `execute`, both into `pc.flags`; the bridge's half of the flags never holds
it, so the `letter` check reads the flag the nested `enter` left.

Still partial: legacy's `quest_setstate` writes the flag at once
(`SetCurrentQuestStateName`, `G/questpc.cpp:115-118`), and the Rewrite writes it when the
script ends. No loaded script reads its own status after `set_state`.

**The API.** Eight names join `BRIDGED`, 65 to 73:

- `pc.setqf` is `pc_set_quest_flag` (`G/questlua_pc.cpp:1215-1229`). Text or a number names
  a flag of the running quest, and a number, `int(rint(...))` (rounded half to even), is its
  value. A zero deletes the flag (`quest::PC::SetFlag`, `G/questpc.cpp:52-76`). Anything else
  logs `QUEST wrong set flag` and changes nothing.
- `find_npc_by_vnum` is `_find_npc_by_vnum` (`G/questlua_global.cpp:792-822`). A number names
  a race, and the answer is the VID of an NPC of that race on the character's map, or 0. A
  non-number logs and answers 0.
- `target.vid`, `target.npc` and `target.pc` are one function, `target_vid`
  (`G/questlua_target.cpp:47-70`). Text or a number names the mark and a number is its VID;
  without both the call logs and does nothing. The third argument is the name the client
  shows, and a numeric fourth of 0 keeps the record from the client. The VID is read as a
  `DWORD`: legacy's `(int)` cast would clip the Rewrite's NPC VIDs, which start at
  0x8000_0000. That is a Divergence.
- `target.delete` ends the running quest's mark of that name, `target.clear` all of its
  marks, and `target.id` answers the VID of the mark of that name, or 0
  (`G/questlua_target.cpp:72-134`).

The marks belong to the quest's number (`GetCurrentQuestIndex`). Four new `Game` methods carry
them to the world: `find_npc`, `create_target`, `delete_target` and `target_vid`, with the new
`quest::manager::Target`.

**The world.** `prodomo/src/game_state/quest_target.rs` is `CTargetManager` for
`TARGET_TYPE_VID` (`G/target.cpp`), one `QuestTargets` per process:

- `create` takes the next ID of the one counter (`++m_iID`). A mark of the same quest and
  name is replaced in place: its `GC_TARGET_DELETE` first when the client heard of it, then
  the new `GC_TARGET_CREATE` (`CreateTarget`, `:134-238`). Otherwise the mark is added.
- `delete` ends the quest's marks of that name, or all of them, in the order they were made
  (`DeleteTarget`, `:240-282`).
- `vid` answers `target.id` (`GetTargetEvent`, `:284-315`).
- `logout` forgets a character's marks with no record (`CTargetManager::Logout`, `:350-363`,
  which `CHARACTER::Disconnect` calls, `G/char.cpp:1815`). `GameState::end_quests` calls it
  beside the manager's logout.

The create record is `GcTargetCreateNew` (`TPacketGCTargetCreate`, `G/packet.h:2523-2530`):
the header 125, `lID`, the 33-byte `szName`, `dwVID` and `bType` `TARGET_TYPE_VID` (2,
`G/target.h:7`). The delete is the 5-byte `GcHeaderAndDword` with header 124 and the `lID`.
Both codecs existed; the coverage counts do not move. `protocol/src/gc_vid.rs`'s row for 124
now says the field is the target's ID, not a VID.

`find_npc` answers the first NPC of the race on the character's map whose race is
registered. Legacy keeps a set per race only for the races `RegisterRaceNum` registers: a
proto of type NPC, WARP or GOTO (`G/mob_manager.cpp:83-84`) and the three Christmas races
(20031, 20032 and 9004, `G/char_manager.cpp:47-49`, `G/xmas_event.h:8-10`). Any other race
answers 0. Legacy walks an `unordered_set` (`G/typedef.h:33`) in no defined order; the
Rewrite answers the first spawned. That is a Divergence.

Two legacy Defects are not reproduced (`docs/STATUS.md`):

- `CreateTarget` compares the stored name, cut to 32 bytes, with the whole name the script
  passed (`strcmp`), so a mark named with 33 bytes or more never replaces its own earlier
  mark. The Rewrite compares both names cut to 32 bytes.
- `SendTargetCreatePacket` builds the record on the stack and `strlcpy`s the name into it, so
  the bytes of `szName` past the terminator are stack bytes. The Rewrite zero-fills them.

**What the login now sends.** The quest login event runs the `login` scripts in quest order
(`item_attr67add` is 40, `sash_mission` 44, `yohara_system` 49). From level 30
`item_attr67add` sends its letter. From level 40 a non-GM's `sash_mission` moves to
`information`: the `enter` deletes `time_to_wait` and `collect_count`, and the `letter`
finds Theowahdan (60003, who stands on maps 1, 21, 41 and 373), marks him, and sends `A
special cloth`. From level 120 `yohara_system` moves to `information_new`, and its letter
looks for the statue (20433, whose only `npc.txt` is `metin2_map_defensewave_port`'s), finds
none, and sends `Statuia Razboinicului`. Then the letter pass runs both letters
again: the sash's new mark replaces the login's, `GC_TARGET_DELETE` before the new create. A
character whose stored states already moved gets only the letter pass.

**The tests.** `prodomo/tests/parity.rs`:

- The login reader is now `read_login_lines` (the three command and info lines) and
  `read_login_letters`: `item_attr67add`'s letter, then one pass of the marking letters
  (`read_marking_letters`: a mark when it comes, then the letter), then a second pass when
  one follows within the quiet window. The second pass expects each first-pass mark replaced.
  A login pass that moved nothing sends one pass, and a login pass that moved a quest sends
  two; the records of one step go out together, so the wait only runs out on a login with
  one pass.
- Every scenario that enters a character at level 40 or more on map 1 reads the mark and the
  letters. All 144 scenarios pass.
- `the_quest_window_runs_the_letters_info_and_the_quest_moves_on`: the relog now reads the
  letter pass's sash mark, with ID 3, and both letters.
- New scenario `the_sash_letter_marks_theowahdan_and_the_letter_pass_marks_him_again`: Alpha
  (level 154) enters 1000 from Theowahdan with three stored flags of the sash quest. The
  scenario reads Theowahdan's VID from the view's insert of race 60003, then the golden
  `GC_TARGET_CREATE` of ID 1 on that VID, the sash and Yohara letters, `GC_TARGET_DELETE` of
  ID 1, the create of ID 2, and both letters again. After the disconnect the quest's stored
  flags are `__status` 695801987 (the CRC32 of `information`) and `kept` 9: the `enter`
  deleted the two counters. The relog sees Theowahdan at the same VID and gets the letter
  pass alone: the create of ID 3, no delete, and both letters.

Unit tests:

- `quest`: `a_state_change_runs_the_new_states_enter_and_letter` (the `enter`'s deletions,
  the target, and a relog's letter pass replacing the target),
  `a_state_change_leaves_enters_and_letters_in_legacys_nesting` (a synthetic quest whose
  states move each other: the chat order of `leave`, `enter` and `letter`, the skipped letter,
  and the 16-deep guard), `setqf_rounds_to_even_and_a_zero_deletes`, and three for the
  arguments: `find_npc_by_vnum_dwords_the_race_and_misses_as_zero`,
  `the_target_names_follow_legacys_argument_rules` (`target.vid`, `npc` and `pc`) and
  `the_target_id_delete_and_clear_find_the_quests_targets`. The level-up test now expects the
  sash letter at 40 and the sash and Yohara letters at 120.
- `prodomo`: `find_npc_by_vnum_answers_only_registered_races`,
  `a_letter_marks_the_npc_it_finds_until_the_character_leaves` (the golden 125 record behind
  a level-up, then `leave_world` clearing the mark), and four in `quest_target` with golden
  bytes: `a_target_of_the_same_quest_and_name_is_replaced`,
  `names_keep_32_bytes_and_long_names_match`, `a_delete_ends_the_quests_targets_in_order` and
  `the_id_wraps_at_the_top_of_int`.

The first parity run after the change failed 114 scenarios. The reader expected
`item_attr67add`'s letter in the letter pass, but its letter is a `login` script, so it comes
first. The trace seemed to show its button five times: each peek prints the record it puts
back. With the order fixed, 12 relog scenarios still failed. Their quests had moved on an
earlier login, and the reader took the letter pass's mark for a login-pass mark. The reader
now reads one pass and looks for a second.

**Searches.** No loaded quest calls `target.npc`, `target.pc`, `target.clear` or `target.id`:

**Mutation sweep.** Twenty-seven mutants, each applied to the pristine file, checked to change
executable code by line position, and restored by checksum. The first pass killed 24, all
semantic, none by compile error:

- `quest`: `leave` run at the new state; `enter` never run; the letter always run, and never

  sending no delete, a replace adding a mark, a replace ignoring the quest, the store's logout
  keeping the marks, `kept` not cutting at 32 and not stopping at a zero, the ID never

Three survived:

- The flag put to the new state, not the old, before the `leave` (Q6) is equivalent. `execute`
  writes the flag for the script it runs, as legacy's `PC::SetQuest` does

- A `set_state` to the script's own state running the change scripts (Q7) survived because no
  test named its own state. The flip quest's `d` now has a `kill` script that calls

  still registers 20031, because 20032 is a Christmas race too. The stronger mutant
  (`&& race == 0`, so only the proto type registers) is killed by
  `find_npc_by_vnum_answers_only_registered_races`.

So 26 of 27 are killed, all semantic, and the equivalent one's line is gone. The parity

## 260. The mark's click and its event (`event.target.target_event`, `gc.target_update`, `lua.item_name`, `lua.target.delete`)

A click on Theowahdan, marked by the sash letter since ledger 259, now runs the sash quest's
`theowahdan.target.click`. Each mark's event tells the client where the marked character
stands, and `item_name` answers, so the answer to the click's first page moves the quest to
`go_to_disciple`, whose letter marks the captain.

**The click.** `Manager::click` first asks the new `Game::target_at` for the quest and kept
name of the clicker's first mark on the clicked character (`GetTargetInfo(pid,
TARGET_TYPE_VID, vid)`, `G/target.cpp:317-348`). When there is one, the new `Run::on_target`
runs `NPC::OnTarget` (`G/questnpc.cpp:206-264`) on the no-NPC scripts, at the character's state
of that quest. That is `CQuestManager::Click`'s target arm (`G/questmanager.cpp:934-945`):

1. The `target` entries run in order. An entry matches when its argument begins with the mark's
   name. This is `strncmp` over the name's length, so `boss` also answers `bossy.click`.
2. The verb after the argument's first dot must be `click`, and the entry's condition must
   hold.
3. The first match runs and takes the click, and the NPC's own scripts do not run. With no
   match the click goes on to the NPC as before.

The argument is the first line of the entry's `.arg` file, read as the C string `OnTarget`
compares (`NPC::LoadStateScript`, `G/questnpc.cpp:171-180`). A character that never ran the
quest matches nothing.

The new `Manager::target` is `CQuestManager::Target` (`G/questmanager.cpp:723-736`): the
mark's event reports `arrive` and `die` through it, and a character the manager never saw
misses, as legacy's `GetPC` returns NULL. No loaded quest has an `arrive` or `die` script (see
Searches), so both answer that nothing ran.

While another script waits for its client, a matching mark takes the click and runs nothing,
and the waiting script keeps its place. Legacy runs the target script through
`ExecuteQuestScript`, and its `PC::SetQuest` puts the new state in place of the waiting one
without closing it (`G/questpc.cpp:140-164`). The waiting dialog's answer then reaches the
wrong script. That is a Defect, not reproduced, and the Rewrite's behaviour is a Divergence
(`docs/STATUS.md`).

**The event.** `prodomo/src/game_state/quest_target.rs` now runs `target_event`
(`G/target.cpp:57-132`). Each mark carries its event number, the map it was made on, the
Pulse its next check is due, and the spot the client last heard (`old`). `process_pulse` calls
`run_quest_targets`, which runs every due event, character by character in the order the
marks were made:

- The first check comes a second after the mark (`PASSES_PER_SEC(1)`).
- When the character stands on another map, the next check comes in `MINMAX(12, 5000 / 60,
  125)` = 83 Pulses and nothing else happens.
- When no character holds the marked VID, the quest's `die` script runs and the mark ends
  with its `GC_TARGET_DELETE` (`DeleteTarget`).
- Otherwise, within 500 (`DISTANCE_APPROX`) the quest's `arrive` script runs. When the marked
  spot differs from `old`, the client hears `GC_TARGET_UPDATE` and `old` moves to it. That
  record is header 123, 13 bytes: `lID`, `lX`, `lY` (`TPacketGCTargetUpdate`,
  `G/packet.h:2532-2537`, whose `long`s are 4 bytes on the 32-bit target). A mark the script
  made silent sends nothing.
- The next check is `MINMAX(12, iDist / 60, 125)` Pulses later, or a second later when an
  `arrive` found no script (`G/target.cpp:78,128-131`).

A replaced mark (`CreateTarget` on the same quest and name) keeps its event, its map and its
due Pulse, and its `old` goes back to (0, 0), so the client hears the spot again at the next
check. The codec `GcTargetUpdate` existed, so the coverage counts do not move.

Two differences from legacy:

- Legacy's `CHARACTER_MANAGER::Find` looks for the marked VID across the process. The Rewrite
  looks in the character's own Channel, whose worlds hold the only characters a mark can name.
  That is a Divergence (`docs/STATUS.md`).
- Legacy's `FindByPID` miss ends the event and leaves the mark listed. A character's marks end
  when it leaves the world (ledger 259), so no event outlives its character.

**`item_name`.** The sash click's second page names the item it asks for with
`item_name(85000)`. `_item_name` (`G/questlua_global.cpp:649-671`) works in two steps:

1. It answers "" unless `ITEM_MANAGER::GetTable` finds the vnum, either as an exact row or
   strictly inside a range row.
2. Otherwise it answers `LC_LOCALE_ITEM_TEXT(vnum, language)`, which is `locale_item_find`:
   the name from the language's `item_names.txt`, or `NoName`.

`locale_item_init` (`G/locale.cpp:167-185`) reads the file as `locale_mob_init` reads
`mob_names.txt`, and `LocaleService_LoadItemNameFile` (`G/locale_service.cpp:480-500`) loads
one per language.

The Rewrite reuses the monster-name reader:

- `MobLocaleNames::load_language_file` and `MobNamesByLanguage::load_file` take the file name.
- `ItemNamesByLanguage` is `MobNamesByLanguage` over `ITEM_NAMES_FILE`.
- The boot loads every language's `item_names.txt` beside the quests and refuses to start with
  "Item names are unusable" when one cannot be read.
- `Session::item_name` asks `ItemProtos::get`, which handles the range rows, and then the
  character's language.

The Lua name shares `mob_name`'s argument rules: a number or numeric text names the vnum,
anything else answers "". `BRIDGED` goes from 73 names to 74. 85000 is in no proto row, so the
sash page reads `x40 .` with nothing between, as legacy's does.

**The tests.** `prodomo/tests/parity.rs`. Every map-1 login from level 40 marks Theowahdan
(ledger 259), so a second after the mark every such scenario now hears his spot. The harness
reads around it:

- `is_mark_update` names the record.
- `read_game_raw` and `read_game_raw_until` skip it.
- `drain_game` sizes it and filters it out.
- `quiet_for`, `closes_within`, and the readers that size records themselves (the chat counter,
  `wire_for`, the revive reader, the swing and move loops, and the party swing) accept it.
- `read_game_marked` and `still_marked_for` are the readers that keep it. Under them an
  unexpected update is a finding.

New scenario `a_click_on_marked_theowahdan_runs_the_sash_quests_target_script`:

1. Setup: Alpha enters 1000 from Theowahdan along y (960 by `DISTANCE_APPROX`), with the sash
   quest stored at `information` and the Yohara quest at `information_new`.
2. The login reads its lines, `item_attr67add`'s letter, the letter pass's mark of Theowahdan
   (ID 1) and the sash and Yohara letters.
3. At least 600 ms after the mark, `GC_TARGET_UPDATE` (1, 482800, 943900) arrives. Then 1.5
   seconds pass with no record: he stands still, so the checks every 16 Pulses send nothing.
4. The click on him brings `GC_TARGET_DELETE` of ID 1, then the first page (12 lines, skin 1,
   titled `teowahdan`, the `mob_name` of 60003) ending `[NEXT]`, and nothing else in the quiet
   window. The NPC's own scripts do not run.
5. The answer 254 brings the second page (13 lines) ending `[DONE]`, the captain's mark
   (`GC_TARGET_CREATE` of ID 2 named `Captain`, on another VID), the letter `Increase your
   power`, and a second later the update (2, 466900, 949100). Then 1.5 seconds pass with no
   record.
6. After the disconnect the stored `sash_mission.__status` is 1675612723, the CRC32 of
   `go_to_disciple`.

All 145 scenarios pass. Ledger 259's sash scenario is unchanged: its `still` readers skip the
update.

  The API probe gains `item_name`: a number and numeric text name 11901, and an unknown vnum,

- `prodomo`, in `quests`:
