**A flaky fixture.** The first mutation sweep counted kills from
`the_marks_event_follows_the_npc_and_ends_with_it`. Fifteen runs of the unchanged code then
failed it four times. The test moves Theowahdan by hand, and his own idle wander
(`__StateIdle_NPC`: one draw in 7, a move timed on the clock) sometimes walked him back
between two checks. The trace showed `npc_move` taking him from (500, 1021) back to (600,
600).

The owner's protos give both 60003 and 20355 `NOMOVE` (`AI_FLAG`), so on the server neither
ever wanders, and the scenario was never exposed. The `marked_theowahdan` fixture now gives him
`AIFLAG_NOMOVE` as the proto does, and 30 runs of the quest tests pass 30 times. The sweep was
run again in full after the fix.

**Searches.**

- 85000 has no name. `item_proto.txt` has no row for it: a scan of the vnum column read 7123
  exact rows and 180 range rows, and none covers 85000. As controls, 11901 is an exact row and
  110050 falls inside `110000~110099`. The English `item_names.txt` has no row for 85000 and
  names 11901 `Smoking` at line 1938.
- No loaded quest has a target `arrive` or `die` script. `target\.(arrive|die)` over every
  file of `legacy/gamedata/locale/europe/quest` finds none. `target\.click` finds the two
  callers, `_basic/sash_mission.lua` and `_basic/yohara_system.lua` (the positive control).
  `target\.zzz` finds none (the negative control).
- `item_name[[:space:]]*\(` matches nine files of the quest tree. One hit, in `locale.lua`, is
  `c_item_name`, a `questlib.lua` helper that writes an `[ITEM value;N]` tag and never calls
  `item_name`. The other eight call it:
  - The sash quest is the one this slice reaches. It also names its reward, 85005 (`Esarfa
    Master (normala)`, in the protos), in `__complete`.
  - `questlib.lua` calls it only inside `say_item_vnum`, `say_item_vnum_inline` and
    `show_horse_menu`.
  - The rest belong to systems not ported: the 7th and 8th skills, the battle pass, the
    enchanted forest, the guild melt, the teleport ring and the dungeon library.
- The language files: `country/*/item_names.txt` has eleven files, and ten are byte-identical
  (one SHA-256). `es` names vnums 10 to 19 `Espada+N` where the others say `Sabie+N`, and adds
  three rows at its end (30400 to 30402). The eleven `mob_names.txt` are identical.

**Mutation sweep.** Thirty-six mutants, each applied to the pristine file, checked to change
executable code by line position, and restored by checksum.

- **The event** (`quest_target`):
  - the next check's ceiling raised and its floor lowered;
  - the distance step made 61;
  - the pace without an `arrive` script ignored;
  - a replace forgetting the pace or the event, or keeping the last spot;
  - the first check made at once;
  - an unchanged spot sent again, and the last spot not kept;
  - `die` not ending the mark;
  - `arrive` needing less than 500;
  - the check after another map coming the next Pulse;
  - a mark answering any VID;
  - the update naming the next ID;
  - an NPC or a character on another map found as gone, an NPC or a character of another
    Channel found, and another map ending the mark (T16 to T20, added with the `Marked`
    refactor below).
- **The click** (`quest`):
  - the target arm asking another verb;
  - the name matched whole, not as a prefix;
  - any verb matching;
  - the condition ignored;
  - a waiting script not holding the target, or the match not taken while it waits;
  - the argument not cut at its line end;
  - `item_name` reading the monster names.
- **The names** (`prodomo` and `gamedata`):
  - the session's `item_name` skipping the proto, reading the monster names, or reading the
    first language;
  - the session's `target_at` asking another VID;
  - the item names file being the monsters', and `load_file` reading the monster file;
  - the boot dropping the item names.

The first pass left four survivors, and each now has the witness named under Tests:

- T12, `arrive` at less than 500. No step stood at exactly 500. Now Theowahdan stands 500 and
  501 away.
- M6, the argument not cut at its line end. No quest named a target with a newline. A `when`
  name may be a string, so `"two\nlines".target.click` compiles to the argument
  `two\nlines.click`, which `getline` cuts to `two`.
- G3, `item_name` reading the first language. The test had one language.
- B1, the boot dropping the item names. Nothing read them past the boot: the sash page's 85000
  has no proto, so it answers "" either way. Now the boot test reads them.

That pass also counted T13, the check after another map coming the next Pulse, as killed by
the flaky test. Run again with the fixture fixed, it survived. Its witness is the new
another-map test.

**The potion windows.** Two of the three full runs before the last one failed

tick: 599 from 500". The scenario passed eight runs alone. The affect event writes a step's HP
point and its recovery point as two frames (`run_affect_event`,
`prodomo/src/game_state/affect.rs`), so on a loaded host the drink's quiet window, 300 ms in
that scenario, can close between them. The three scenarios that fold heal ticks now read their

no heal step from the pool the rest of it folds to, the helper reads the next record and
requires it to be the recovery point for the same VID. The server is unchanged.

The control was a temporary 450 ms pause between a step's frames, reverted by checksum. The
old harness then failed all three scenarios with the gate's message, and the new one passed all
three. The first draft of the helper folded the window's head before it checked that the last
record was an HP point, and it failed all three on a whole pair; the check now comes first.

## 261. The captain's "Yes" and the play time (`lua.pc.get_playtime`, `lua.pc.getplaytime`)

The sash quest's captain now answers his click. His `select("Yes", "No")` answered 1 stores
`time_to_wait` at `60 * 3 + pc.get_playtime()` and moves the quest to `time_to_wait`, and that
state's window counts the wait down in minutes played.

**The play time in the world.** `PointsRow` gains `playtime`, and `Points::load` puts it in the
real `POINT_PLAYTIME` only, as `SetPlayerProto` does (`SetRealPoint(POINT_PLAYTIME,
t->playtime)`, `G/char.cpp:2296`). Nothing sets the instant slot, so the points record still
sends 0 there (`PointsPacket` sends `GetPoint`, `G/char.cpp:2056-2057`). `load_points` passes the
row's `playtime_minutes`. The new `Points::set_playtime` is `SetRealPoint(POINT_PLAYTIME, ...)`.
Every full `PointsRow` literal in `world` and `prodomo` names the field; 14 were found by a
script rather than by line number.

**The bank.** `CreatePlayerProto` banks the minutes played into the real point before it reads
the points (`G/char.cpp:1519-1545`). The save cycle now computes the bank once, at one instant,
through the new `played(held, at)` in `prodomo/src/main.rs`. `GameCommand::KeptOf` carries it as
`playtime: Option<i32>`, `answer_kept` sets it on the character's points before it reads them,
and `save_held` writes the same minutes. The descriptor's row keeps the minutes it loaded:
`hold_points` does not copy the bank back, because `played` adds the session's whole minutes to
the loaded ones each time, which is what legacy's remainder carry amounts to. A Warp and the
logout bank too, but the character leaves the world, and the next session loads the row.

**The quest call.** `Game::playtime` is `GetRealPoint(POINT_PLAYTIME)`, and the `pc_api` arm
answers it under both registered names, `pc.getplaytime` and `pc.get_playtime`
(`pc_get_playtime`, `G/questlua_pc.cpp:874-878`, `:3841-3842`). `BRIDGED` has 76 names, in
`api::NAMES` order. The session reads its points, and 0 without them.

**Divergence.** Legacy banks at every `SaveReal`, which the delayed-save queue runs within 29
Pulses of each `CHARACTER::Save()` (`G/char.cpp:1472-1476`): a level step (`:4001`, `:4241`), a
quest reward (`G/questpc.cpp:332-337`), a skill change (`G/char_skill.cpp:716`, `:902`), a trade,
a shop and more. The Rewrite's world sees only the save cycle's bank, so `pc.get_playtime` can be
up to one cycle (120 seconds by default) late. Recorded in STATUS.

**Not ported.** Each bank's alignment: 5 a minute, or 60 or 120 for a negative alignment, outside
a `BANPK` cell (`UpdateAlignment`, `G/char.cpp:1529-1539`). It is noted in `sys.char.save` and in
the STATUS Divergence row. The captain's click after the wait calls `pc.give_item2`, a refused
name, and `__complete` needs `pc.count_item`, `pc.remove_item`, `pc.give_item2_select` and
`item.set_socket`.

**The tests.**

- `world`: `the_playtime_is_a_real_point_the_bank_replaces`.
- `prodomo` lib: `the_playtime_loads_as_a_real_point_the_points_record_does_not_send`
  (`loading_phase`), and `the_sash_wait_counts_down_the_minutes_a_save_banks`
  (`game_state::quests`). The second runs the owner's `sash_mission` at `time_to_wait` with a
  wait ending at 480 and 300 minutes played: the window says 180, a `KeptOf` banking 302 says 178,
  and a `KeptOf` with no bank leaves 302.
- `prodomo` bin: `a_save_banks_the_loaded_minutes_and_the_whole_session`. No play clock means
  no bank; 60 000 ms banks nothing and 60 001 banks a minute; a held row that took back points
  holding 301 still banks 302 at 150 seconds, not 303.
- `quest`: `the_pc_names_answer_and_count_the_reads` reads a negative play time under both
  names.
- Parity, `prodomo/tests/parity.rs`:
  - `a_yes_to_the_captain_waits_three_hours_of_playtime`. Alpha has 300 minutes and stands
    1000 from the captain at `go_to_disciple`. The login marks him with ID 1, and the update
    follows. The click deletes the mark and says the first page up to its `wait()`. The answer
    says the second page, ending in `[QUESTION 1;Yes|2;No]`. Answer 0 gets `[DONE]` with skin
    0 (`Select` set the done flag, `G/questmanager.cpp:1113-1130`). Then the new state's letter
    marks him with ID 2, and its update follows. The quest window says 180 minutes. The logout
    stores the state's CRC32 (3464966988 as the `int` -830000308), the flag 480, and 300
    minutes, since less than a minute was played.
  - `a_save_past_a_minute_of_play_counts_the_captains_wait_down`. The save cycle is 1 second
    and the ping cycle 600. The window says 180 minutes, then 179 at 62 seconds after the
    entry. The logout stores 301. This scenario takes about 65 seconds.
  - `enter_beside_theowahdan` became `enter_beside(keyed, vnum)` for both NPCs.

**Rows.**

- `lua.pc.get_playtime` is `ported`, with `a_yes_to_the_captain_waits_three_hours_of_playtime`.
- `lua.pc.getplaytime` is `partial`: it is backed with unit tests only, and no quest calls it.

- Notes were added to `quest.sash_mission` and to `sys.char.save`. `sys.char.save` notes the

## 262. The quest's give (`lua.pc.give_item2`)

`pc.give_item2` now gives. `guild_create`'s reward page hands over its book, and every
other quest that calls it on a dialog step or a click gets `AutoGiveItem`.

**The bridge.** `pc_give_or_drop_item` (`G/questlua_pc.cpp:540-587`) is `give_item2` in
`quest/src/manager.rs`. A number, or text that reads as one, is the vnum, as `(int)` then
`DWORD`. Other text is a locale name's case-insensitive prefix (`ITEM_MANAGER::GetVnum`,
`G/item_manager.cpp:722-738`, through the existing `ItemProtos::vnum_by_locale_name`). Anything
else, or a name no proto has, gives nothing and answers 0. A positive second number is the
count, rounded to even (`rint`), and one that rounds to 0 gives nothing. Otherwise the count is
1. The `Game` trait gains `item_vnum` and `give_item`, and `BRIDGED` has 77 names, in
`api::NAMES` order.

**The give.** `world::character::auto_give_item`, in `ground.rs`, is `AutoGiveItem(vnum, count)`
with `bMsg` set (`G/char_item.cpp:9081-9223`):

- No proto answers `NoProto`, and nothing changes.
- An item flagged `STACKABLE` that is neither `ITEM_BLEND` nor `ITEM_TOGGLE` first tops up
  every stack of its vnum whose sockets are the proto's (`FN_check_item_socket`, `:172-181`),
  in cell order (the base cells, then the bank cells, as the pick-up's `merge_cells`), up to
  the stack limit. `MAKECOUNT` raises the count to `value1` at each such stack. There is no
  `ANTI_STACK` check, unlike the pick-up. Taken whole, legacy's `[LS;444;%s]` line ends it.
- Otherwise `make` is asked for what is left. A placed item sends the line, then the item set
  with its cell highlighted, then a potion's quickslot (`:9175-9200`). With no free cell the
  item is answered `Unplaced`, for the ground.
- `ENABLE_SPECIAL_DROP_CHAT_RENEWAL` is not defined, so the line is the `ChatPacket` arm.
  Search: no `#define` of it under `server/server` or `legacy/config`. Positive control:
  `#define ENABLE_CUSTOM_INVENTORY` is found at `prodomodefines.h:202` by the same search.
- The text protos' sockets are all 0 (`ItemProto::sockets`), so a stack matches when its
  sockets are all 0.
- The blend merge after `CreateItem` (`:9145-9171`) is unreachable: `make_drop_item` refuses
  `ITEM_BLEND`, as it refuses `ITEM_QUEST` and `ITEM_RING`, so such a give makes nothing.

`MoveKind::Given` names the outcome, and `ITEM_FLAG_MAKECOUNT` is now `pub(crate)`.

**The session.** `Session::give_item` makes the item with the drop's `make_drop_item`, using
the proto's magic percent (`CreateItem(vnum, count, 0, true)`). It encodes the records
through `MovedItems::new`, in the script's records at once, so they reach the client ahead of
the page the script sends when it ends. The rows go to `item_rows`, and an unplaced item goes
to `laid`.

- `GameState::run_quests_giving` arms the new `Giver` (the character's items and quickslots
  through the new `Character::items_points_and_quickslots_mut`, the unlocked cells, the IDs,
  the Gaussian, the attributes and the masks). It answers the rows, and it lays each unplaced
  item at the character's feet (`lay_given`): the 300-second destroy event, then ownership
  for 300 seconds for an `ANTI_DROP` item and 60 otherwise (`:9203-9218`). Such an item has no
  row until it is picked up, as a monster's drop has none.
- `run_quests` keeps its signature and gives nothing. Only `quest` (a dialog step) and
  `quest_click` give.
- `QuestStepOutcome` and `ShopAnswer::Quest` carry the rows. A click with rows returns as a
  quest even when no script took it.
- The descriptor stores them with `store_quest_items` (`db::items::apply_row_changes`, one
  transaction) before the climbs, the guild stores and the records. A failure closes the
  connection.

**Divergences and Defects** (one new STATUS row):

- A letter, the login, a level, a kill or a target's event gives nothing and answers 0. No
  descriptor stores their rows, and an item the store never sees would be lost.
- The count reaches `AutoGiveItem` as a `WORD`, which legacy wraps. The Rewrite stops it at
  65535, and the stack limit then bounds it.
- The quickslot names the cell as a `BYTE`, so legacy's potion in a bank cell past 255 names
  the wrong base cell. The Rewrite fills no slot then.
- For 80003 to 80007 legacy's gold-bar log reads the item before its `NULL` check
  (`G/questlua_pc.cpp:584-589`). Neither the log nor the rewards log is written.
- The base search stops at the unlocked cells, as the pick-up's does (ledger 198.3).

**The owner's data.** The sash captain gives 85000, which has no row in `item_proto.txt`, and
no range row covers it. Search: the 180 range rows, and `^85000\t`. Positive control:
85001-85008 are found by the same search. So on the owner's data the captain's material never
arrives, `pc.count_item(85000) < 40` always holds, and `__complete` cannot be reached.
`guild_create` gives 70101 (`ITEM_SPECIAL`), `cards_event` 79506 and `fishing_event` 50033.
`guild_create`'s `run` state is set by no quest and no C++ source (a search of the quest folder
and `server/server/game/*.cpp` finds only its own file, `guild_manage.lua`'s unrelated local and
`locale.lua`), so the scenario seeds `reward`.

**The tests.**

- `world` (ground):
  - `a_give_without_a_proto_changes_nothing_and_makes_nothing`
  - `a_stackable_give_tops_up_the_stacks_in_cell_order`
  - `what_the_stacks_leave_is_made_into_the_first_free_cell`
  - `a_makecount_stack_takes_the_protos_count`
  - `a_full_inventory_answers_the_made_item_for_the_ground`
  - `a_refused_make_gives_nothing_more`
  - `a_placed_potion_fills_the_first_empty_quickslot`
- `quest`: `the_pc_names_answer_and_count_the_reads` gives:
  - by vnum, by numeric text and by name;
  - rounds 2.5 to 2 and 3.5 to 4;
  - refuses a count of 0.4, an unknown name and a table;
  - takes 1 for a negative count;
  - stops 70000 at 65535.
- `prodomo` lib: `a_give_names_sets_and_stores_the_item_or_lays_it`. 85000 gives nothing. Two
  swords take IDs 1000 and 1001, each a line and a set, with a `Created` row owned by the
  reader. A third, with both unlocked cells taken, is laid with no record and no row. With no
  giver the answer is 0. `a_laid_undroppable_give_stays_its_takers_five_minutes` pins the
  lay's ownership.
- Parity: `guild_creates_reward_page_gives_the_book_into_the_first_free_cell`. Alpha's
  `guild_create` stands at `reward` (CRC32 1322349139), and the login sends its letter. The
  window's entry sends `[LS;444;Cartea Intelepciunii]`, then the item set of 70101 at cell 0,
  then the page. The row is in the store before the page is read. At the logout
  `set_state(start)`, the state 0, has deleted the flag.

**Rows.**

- `lua.pc.give_item2` is `ported`, with the scenario.
- A note was added to `quest.guild_create`.

**STATUS.** The header names 262 and the next slice: `pc.count_item` and `pc.remove_item`, then
`pc.give_item2_select` and `item.set_socket`. It has 77 backed names and the new row.

**Mutation sweep.** 15 mutants (G1-G15) were applied to the pristine files, and each changed
executable code. Every file was restored by checksum. In the first run 13 were killed, all
semantic, with no compile-error kills:

- G4 (the placement sends no name) was not applied: its text is also a substring of the

- G15 (the lay's ownership is always 60) survived: no test reached the ground lay's

So all 15 were killed, semantically.

## 263. The quest's count and removal (`lua.pc.count_item`, `lua.pc.remove_item`)

`pc.count_item` and `pc.countitem` now answer `CountSpecifyItem`. `pc.remove_item` and
`pc.removeitem` now run `RemoveSpecifyItem`. A seeded `__complete` of the sash quest counts
the material, finds none, and sends the player back to the captain.

**The world.** The new `world/src/character/specify_item.rs` holds both
(`G/char_item.cpp:8791-8940`):

- **The scan.** Both read the base inventory up to `Inventory_Size()`, the unlocked cells
  (`ENABLE_EXTEND_INVEN_SYSTEM`, `prodomodefines.h:60`), then the custom banks
  (`ENABLE_CUSTOM_INVENTORY`, `:202`), in cell order. Legacy skips an item its owner sells
  in a personal shop or a premium private shop (`__PREMIUM_PRIVATE_SHOP__`, `:176`). The
  Rewrite has neither, so nothing is skipped.
- **`count_specify_item(items, usable_cells, vnum)`** sums the counts.
- **`remove_specify_item(items, slots, protos, usable_cells, (vnum, count))`** takes stacks
  in order:
  - A count of 0 takes nothing.
  - Each stack the rest covers is `SetCount(0)`.
  - The first stack the rest does not cover is updated (`UpdatePacket`).
  - A count past what is held takes everything.
- **A used-up stack** syncs its slots as `SetCount(0)` does (`G/item.cpp:303-330`):
  - One that chains (`chains_when_used_up`) is cleared first, and its slots then follow the
    next item of its vnum.
  - Any other has its slots deleted before the clear.
  - The chain's `FindSpecifyItem` runs at once, before the next stack is taken. So a slot
    that follows a stack the same removal then uses up is deleted in its turn.
- `MoveKind::Removed` names the outcome. The gold-bar log is not written.

**The bridge** (`quest/src/manager.rs`):

- `count_item` is `pc_count_item` (`G/questlua_pc.cpp:777-799`):
  - A number-like last argument is the vnum, dworded.
  - Text there makes the first argument a locale name's prefix (`GetVnum`), as legacy reads
    index -1 for the test and index 1 for the name.
  - A name no proto has counts 0, and so does anything else.
  - A first argument that is not text counts 0, where legacy hands `GetVnum` a null name (a
    Defect).
- `remove_item` is `pc_remove_item` (`:801-860`):
  - It acts on one argument or two, and on any other count it takes nothing.
  - The first argument, number-like, is the vnum, dworded. Text is a name's prefix. A name no
    proto has, or anything else, logs and takes nothing.
  - With one argument the count is 1. With two, the second is dworded, and one that is not a
    number is 0.
  - It pushes nothing.
- The `Game` trait gains `count_item` and `remove_item`. `BRIDGED` has 81 names, in
  `api::NAMES` order.

**The session.**

- `run_quests_giving` now arms the `Giver` on every step whose character is in the world.
  The new `Giver::stores` says whether the step's descriptor stores the rows (a dialog step
  or a click, as in ledger 262).
- `pc.count_item` counts on every step.
- `pc.give_item2` and `pc.remove_item` change the items only where `stores` is set.
- A removal's records reach the client at once, as `SetCount` sends them. Its rows go out
  with the step's, and the descriptor stores them before it sends (ledger 262's
  `store_quest_items`).
- Quickslot changes reach the store through the save cycle's `KeptOf`, as every other
  item step's do.

**Two callers now share the world's functions:**

- `GameState::count_specify_item` (the `new_xmas_event` carry check, `reward.rs`) read all
  180 base cells and no bank. Its doc said `ENABLE_CUSTOM_INVENTORY` was undefined; it is
  defined (`prodomodefines.h:202`). It now calls `count_specify_item` with the unlocked
  cells. No test observes the change: the check matters only while `new_xmas_event` is set,
  and nothing sets it. The function is pinned by the world's tests.
- The guild's `remove_create_item` now calls `remove_specify_item` for one 70101 and keeps
  `MoveKind::GuildMade`. Its records are unchanged: no slot can name a 70101 cell, since
  `QuickslotAdd` takes only `ITEM_USE` items.

**The callers on the owner's data.** The sweep of the quest folder for the four names found
51 calls in 18 files. An earlier listing of it stopped at 40 lines, so the sweep was run
again whole. The control: 10 files call `pc.get_level`. The reachable ones:

- `sash_mission`'s `__complete` click counts 85000. The scenario takes the `< 40` branch.
  That is the only branch the owner's data allows: 85000 has no proto (ledger 262).
- `cards_event`'s "Card set" (count, remove, give) belongs to NPC 20417, which stands in no
  `npc.txt`. Search: `20417` under `legacy/gamedata` finds only the protos and the name
  files. Control: 20011 is found in three `npc.txt`.
- The fishing and Tanaka events need an event flag nothing sets.
- The forest and the ship defense need a party or a dungeon.
- The teleport ring needs `select_table` and `pc.warp`.
- The skill books and `item_attr67add` need an item's `use` and `item.get_vnum`.
- `change_empire` needs `pc.change_empire`, and the altar of power needs guild land.
- `guild_manage.lua:128` is short-circuited by `guild_create_item = false` (`:98`).
- `questlib.lua:439-440` is the horse menu, which waits for `horse.*`.

So `pc.remove_item`, `pc.countitem` and `pc.removeitem` stay `partial`, with unit tests.

**The tests.**

- `world` (`specify_item`):
  - `the_count_sums_the_unlocked_cells_and_the_banks`
  - `a_removal_uses_up_stacks_in_cell_order_and_trims_the_last`
  - `a_removal_past_what_is_held_takes_everything_and_zero_takes_nothing`
  - `a_removal_skips_the_locked_cells`
  - `a_used_up_stack_deletes_its_slot_before_the_clear`
  - `a_used_up_potion_chains_its_slot_to_the_next_then_deletes_it`
- `quest`: `the_pc_item_names_give_count_and_remove` takes ledger 262's give checks and
  covers both counting names:
  - by name, numeric text and a dworded number;
  - the last argument's number against the first's name;
  - a table, an unknown name and no argument count 0.

  `the_pc_removal_names_take_one_or_the_count` covers both removing names:
  - one argument takes 1, and a second is dworded (-1 is `u32::MAX`, text is 0);
  - an unknown name, a table, no argument and three arguments take nothing.
- `prodomo` lib: `a_give_names_sets_and_stores_the_item_or_lays_it` now also counts the two
  held swords. A removal takes one with its clear and its `Destroyed` row. With `stores`
  unset the session counts but neither gives nor removes, and with no character it counts 0.
- Parity: `a_complete_sash_quest_without_the_material_goes_back_to_the_captain`.
  - Alpha logs in 1000 from Theowahdan at `__complete` (CRC32 557528158). The letter pass
    marks him as `theowahdan_reward` with ID 1, and his spot follows.
  - The click deletes the mark and says the first page up to its `wait()`.
  - The answer says the material is short, ending in `[DONE]`.
  - `go_to_disciple`'s letter marks the captain with ID 2, and his spot follows.
  - The logout stores `go_to_disciple`.

**Rows.**

- `lua.pc.count_item` is `ported`, with the scenario.
- `lua.pc.remove_item`, `lua.pc.countitem` and `lua.pc.removeitem` are `partial`, with
  their callers in the notes.
- A note was added to `quest.sash_mission`.

**STATUS.**

- The header names 263. The next slice is `pc.give_item2_select` and `item.set_socket`,
  then the names the removal's callers wait for.
- It has 81 backed names.
- The give's Divergence row now covers the removal: legacy runs both on every event.

**Mutation sweep.** 15 mutants (S1-S15) were applied to the pristine files, and each changed
executable code. Every file was restored by checksum. All 15 were killed, semantically, with no
compile-error kills:

- S1-S7 (the world's scan, the boundary of a used-up stack, the chain, the delete sync, and a

- S8-S10 (the count's argument, one argument's count of 1, and the argument count) were

- S11-S12 (a removal where nothing is stored, and the session's count) were killed by the
  session test.
- S13 (the count answers 40 more) was killed by the parity scenario alone. That is the

## 264. An item's quest `use` event (`item.get_vnum`, `lua.pc.get_skill_group`)

A used `ITEM_QUEST` now runs its own `use` scripts and becomes the quest item. The boost and
ward reset book (71000) answers its early pages over the wire.

**Legacy** (`G/char_item.cpp:2842-2888`, `G/questmanager.cpp:819-860`, `G/questnpc.cpp:283-289`):

- `UseItemEx`'s `case ITEM_QUEST` runs after `UseItem`'s checks and the limit loop.
- An item with neither `ITEM_FLAG_QUEST_USE` (`1 << 10`) nor `ITEM_FLAG_QUEST_USE_MULTIPLE`
  (`1 << 11`, `common/item_length.h:369-370`) calls `CQuestManager::UseItem`, or `SIGUse` when
  `GetSIGVnum() != 0`. The arm returns true and consumes nothing.
- `UseItem` makes the quest item `SetCurrentItem(item)`, then runs
  `m_mapNPC[vnum].OnUseItem`, which is `HandleEvent(pc, QUEST_ITEM_USE_EVENT)`.
- The text protos' `QUEST_USE` name sets bit 9, not 10 (`ProtoReader.cpp:398-400`). Legacy
  tests the bits, and so does the Rewrite. No `ITEM_QUEST` row on the owner's data names
  `QUEST_USE_MULTIPLE` or `QUEST_GIVE`, the two names that set those bits.

**The world** (`world/src/character/equip.rs`):

- `use_item` lets an `ITEM_QUEST` through the same checks as the other uses, in the same order:
  - the job and sex flags;
  - the running script (`@fixme150`);
  - the level and champion limits;
  - the belt cell;
  - the timer refusal.
- It then answers the new `MoveKind::QuestUsed` with no record and no change.
- 70002 is refused as not ported: `RENEWAL_PICKUP_AFFECT` (`prodomodefines.h:151`) gives it an
  affect arm (`:2852-2872`).
- The arena check of 50051-50053 waits for the arena.

**The bridge** (`quest/src/manager.rs`):

- `Manager::use_item(pid, (item, vnum), game)`:
  - It records the item's ID as the character's quest item (`Pc::item`, `m_pQuestItem`).
  - It runs the vnum's `use` scripts through `handle_event`.
  - A character the manager never saw gets a record, as a click does (`GetPC`).
- `Cx::item` carries the quest item into the bridge.
- `item.get_vnum` (`G/questlua_item.cpp:138-149`) answers the vnum of the item the character
  still holds under that ID, or 0.
- `pc.get_skill_group` (`G/questlua_pc.cpp:1339-1343`) answers `GetSkillGroup()`.
- The `Game` trait gains `skill_group` and `held_vnum`. `BRIDGED` has 83 names, in
  `api::NAMES` order.
- `pc.give_item2` is `pc_give_or_drop_item`, which never sets the quest item
  (`G/questlua_pc.cpp:540-590`). Only the `use` event sets it.

**A Defect not reproduced.** `m_pQuestItem` is a raw pointer that nothing clears when the item
is destroyed (`G/char.cpp:7620-7633`; the only `ClearQuestItemPtr` caller is
`ClearCurrentItem`). An `item.get_vnum` after the item is used up, sold or removed reads freed
memory. The Rewrite keeps the ID and answers 0 once the character no longer holds it. It is
recorded among the Defects in STATUS.

**The session** (`prodomo/src/game_state/quests.rs`):

- `GameState::use_item` calls `use_quest_item` when the world answers `QuestUsed`.
- It skips an item whose proto carries a quest-use bit.
- It runs the manager on a storing step (`run_quests_giving` with `stores_items`), so a `use`
  script may give and remove.
- Its records join the step's records, and its item rows join the step's row changes, stored in
  the step's one transaction before the client hears them.
- Its `guild.*` calls are answered as a click's are.
- The quickslots are taken again after the scripts, since a removal may have synced them.
- `MovedItems::quest` carries the GRAND climbs and the guild stores. The descriptor's
  `use_an_item` stores them before `finish_item_step`, with the click's `store_quest_climbs`
  and `store_quest_guild_stores`.
- `skill_group` reads the card's group, and `held_vnum` reads the character's items by ID.

**`SIGUse`.** `GetSIGVnum()` is set for an `ITEM_QUEST` only by a special item group of type
`quest` (`G/item_manager.cpp:412-420`). The owner's `special_item_group.txt` holds one group
(`Cufar_Lumina_Lunii`, vnum 50011) with no `type` line, so it is not quest-typed.

- Search: `quest` (case-insensitive) in that file finds nothing.
- Control: `Group` finds the one group.

`SIGUse` never runs, and it is not ported.

**The callers on the owner's data.** The `use` triggers (search `when [0-9]+\.use|\.use or`
under the quest folder) are:

- the four skill books of `7and8th_skills.lua`;
- `TeleportRing.lua` (70058);
- `item_attr67add.quest` (72347-72350);
- `change_empire.lua` (71054);
- `battle_pass.lua` (25150-25162, whose vnums have no proto).

The reachable path is 71000's early answers.

- A character with no skill group hears that it has no apprenticeship.
- One with a group and no boost or ward skill hears that it learned none.
- One with a learned skill reaches the confirmation, whose "Yes" calls `pc.set_skill_level`
  before `pc.remove_item(item.get_vnum(), 1)`.

The other scripts wait for other names:

- The boost books need `pc.get_job` and `select_table`.
- The teleport ring needs `TeleportRing.MainWindow`.
- `item_attr67add` needs `pc.getf`.
- `change_empire` needs `get_time`'s flag and `pc.change_empire`.

So `item.get_vnum` stays `partial`, with unit tests.

**The tests.**

- `world`: `a_quest_item_passes_the_checks_and_changes_nothing`. The use answers `QuestUsed`
  and changes nothing. A waiting script refuses it, and so does a level limit. 70002 is refused
  as not ported.
- `quest`:
  - `a_used_quest_item_runs_its_use_script` runs the real 71000 script. With no group it gives
    the apprenticeship answer. With a group it gives the no-skill answer. With a learned skill
    it reaches the waiting confirmation, and a second use then runs nothing. A vnum with no
    script runs nothing.
  - `the_quest_item_is_the_used_one_while_it_is_held`: `item.get_vnum` answers 0 before any
    use, the held item's vnum after one, and 0 once the item is gone.
- `prodomo` lib:
  - `a_give_names_sets_and_stores_the_item_or_lays_it` also reads `held_vnum` for the given
    sword.
  - The new `the_session_reads_the_group_and_holds_no_item_without_a_character` reads
    `skill_group` from the card, and `held_vnum` with no character.
- Parity: `a_used_reset_book_runs_its_quest_and_stays`.
  - Alpha (skill group set, no boost or ward skill) is given 71000 by the console and uses it.
  - The script titles the page "Rolle des Lehrwandels", says no skill is learned, and ends in
    `[DONE]`.
  - The book stays in its row, and a second use runs the script again.
  - An earlier draft expected the apprenticeship answer. It failed because `add_characters`
    seeds Alpha with a group, which is why the scenario now asserts the richer branch, through
    `pc.get_skill_group` and 18 `pc.get_skill_level` reads.

**Rows.**

- `lua.pc.get_skill_group` is `ported`, with the scenario.
- `lua.item.get_vnum` is `partial`, with its callers in the note.
- Notes were added to `cg.game.item_use`, `quest.7and8th_skills` and `sys.quest.runtime`.

## 265. The skill books' choice (`pc.get_job`, `pc.set_skill_level`, `select_table`)

The boost and ward books now teach the skill a player picks, and the reset book forgets it, over
the wire.

**Legacy** (`G/questlua_pc.cpp:915-919`, `:2112-2123`; `G/char_skill.cpp:183-258`, `:907-1110`):

- `pc_get_job` pushes `GetJob()`.
- `pc_set_skill_level` reads `(DWORD)lua_tonumber(L, 1)` and `(BYTE)lua_tonumber(L, 2)`, calls
  `SetSkillLevel`, then `SkillLevelPacket()` whatever `SetSkillLevel` did, and pushes nothing.
- `SetSkillLevel`:
  - a vnum at or past `SKILL_MAX_NUM` (255, `common/length.h:72`) logs and returns;
  - under `__7AND8TH_SKILLS__` (`prodomodefines.h:165`), a vnum in 221..=243 with a level above 0
    returns when `SkillCanUp` refuses it;
  - the slot takes `MIN(40, bLev)`, and the master type follows the ladder (40, 30, 20);
  - the `ENABLE_REWARD_SYSTEM` tail then runs the reward missions.
- `SkillCanUp`: a ward skill (221-228) rises only while every other ward skill is at 0, and a
  boost skill (236-243) only while every other boost skill is. Any other vnum is refused, but
  only 221..=243 ever asks. The extra `SKILL_HELP_SALPOONG` term of 239 sits behind
  `__WOLFMAN_CHARACTER__`, which nothing defines.
  - Search: `WOLFMAN_CHARACTER` under `server/server/common` and `premake5.lua` finds nothing.
  - Control: `define __7AND8TH` finds `prodomodefines.h:165`.
  - `SKILL_HELP_SALPOONG` itself has no definition anywhere in `server/` (control:
    `SKILL_HELP_BYEURAK` is defined at `G/skill.h:197`), so the gated term could not compile.
- `select_table(t)` is `questlib.lua`'s `q.yield('select', t)`, the same wait as `select(...)`.
  The Rewrite already read its table through `host::getn`, so it needed nothing new.

**The bridge** (`quest/src/manager.rs`, `quest/src/host.rs`):

- `pc.get_job` answers `Game::job`.
- `pc.set_skill_level` reads both numbers through `coerce_number` and `dword`, so a missing or
  non-number argument is 0, and passes the level's low byte, as the block mode's byte is read.
  It pushes nothing.
- The `Game` trait gains `job` and `set_skill_level`. `BRIDGED` has 85 names, in `api::NAMES`
  order.

**The session** (`prodomo/src/game_state/quests.rs`):

- `job` reads the card's job.
- `set_skill_level`:
  - a vnum past the 255 slots logs `vnum overflow` and sets nothing;
  - a 7/8th skill above 0 obeys `skill_can_up`, the family exclusion;
  - otherwise the slot takes the level up to 40, and the slot, level and read stamp join the
    step's `climbs`, which the descriptor stores with `store_skill` as it stores a GRAND climb
    (a 0 deletes the row);
  - byte 76 is sent either way.
- No point is recomputed, as legacy recomputes none here. No owner script sets 141, the one
  passive skill the Rewrite caches.
- The reward missions' tail waits for `sys.custom.reward`.

**The callers on the owner's data.** `pc.set_skill_level` and `pc.get_job` are called only by
`_basic/7and8th_skills.lua` (search of the quest folder; control: the same search finds the
`select_table` callers in the guild quests and the teleport ring).

- 50514 (boost) and 50515 (ward) run to the end: the offer, the choice, the confirmation, and
  `pc.remove_item(item.get_vnum(), 1)` then `pc.set_skill_level(vnum, 1)`.
- 71000 (reset) runs to the end: each learned skill back to 0, then the removal.
- 50525 (GRAND) still needs `pc.is_skill_book_no_delay`, `pc.get_real_alignment`,
  `pc.remove_skill_book_no_delay` and `pc.change_alignment`.
- Alpha's seeded skill group is 49, which indexes nothing in 50514's table, so its script would
  end in a Lua error, as legacy's would. The scenario sets the group to 2.

**The tests.**

- `quest`:
  - `the_boost_book_teaches_the_chosen_skill_and_the_reset_book_forgets_it` runs the real
    50514 and 71000 scripts against the fake: a shaman of group 2 is offered 243 and a cancel,
    the two "Yes" answers remove the book and set 243 to 1, and 71000 sets it back to 0 and
    removes itself.
  - `the_job_reads_and_the_skill_level_sets_its_numbers`: the job; a text vnum and a level of
    300 (low byte 44); no arguments (0, 0); a fraction and a text level (4, 0); 40.7 (40); and
    `pcall(type, ...)` proves the call pushes nothing.
- `prodomo` lib:
  - `the_session_reads_the_group_and_holds_no_item_without_a_character` also reads the job
    (`with_session`'s card is now (3, 1), so the job and the group differ).
  - The new `a_set_skill_level_lands_within_the_slots_and_the_exclusions`: the family
    exclusion both ways, a re-raise of a learned ward skill, 0 always landing, 244 with no
    family, the cap at 40 with the read stamp, slot 254, a refused 255, and byte 76 on every call.
- Parity: `the_boost_book_teaches_a_skill_and_the_reset_book_forgets_it`.
  - Alpha (job 3, group 2) is given 50514 by the console and uses it.
  - `select_table` offers "Summon Lightning Boost" and "Cancel"; the first answer brings the
    confirmation; "Yes" clears the cell, sends byte 76 with slot 243 at level 1 and master type
    0, and ends with `[DONE]`.
  - The store holds no item and one `player_skill` row (243, 1, 0).
  - The console gives 71000 into the freed cell. Its use asks; "Yes" sends byte 76 with slot 243
    at 0, clears the cell and ends. The store holds no item and no skill row.

**Rows.**

- `lua.pc.get_job` and `lua.pc.set_skill_level` are `ported`, with the scenario.
- `lua.item.get_vnum` is `ported`: the books reach it over the wire.
- `lua.pc.remove_item` stays `partial` (a step that stores no rows still takes nothing); it names
  the scenario.
- `quest.7and8th_skills` stays `partial`, for 50525.

**STATUS.** The header names 265, with 85 backed names. The next slice is `pc.give_item2_select`
and `item.set_socket`, then the GRAND book's alignment names.

## 266. The selected give and its socket (`pc.give_item2_select`, `item.set_socket`)

A quest can now give an item, make it the quest item, and write one of its sockets. The one caller
on the owner's data, the sash quest's reward, stays unreachable, so both names are `partial`
with unit tests.

**Legacy** (`G/questlua_pc.cpp:679-729`, `G/questlua_item.cpp:125-136`, `G/item.cpp:1643-1656`):

- `pc.give_item2_select` is registered as `pc_give_or_drop_item_and_select`
  (`G/questlua_pc.cpp:3888`). It reads the vnum and the count as `pc_give_or_drop_item` does and
  runs `AutoGiveItem`, but every path pushes nothing, and a given item becomes the quest item
  (`SetCurrentItem`).
  - Search: `give_item2_select` over `server/server` finds only the registration line.
  - Control: `"give_item2"` finds its own registration at `:3862`.
- Its gold-bar log runs `item->GetID()` for 80003-80007 even when `AutoGiveItem` gave nothing:
  a null dereference, a Defect. The Rewrite writes no gold-bar log, so it has no counterpart.
- `item_set_socket` needs the quest item and two `lua_isnumber` arguments. It takes `(int)` of
  each, and an index of 0 to `ITEM_SOCKET_MAX_NUM - 1` calls `SetSocket`.
  `ITEM_SOCKET_MAX_NUM` is 6 under `ENABLE_EXTENDED_SOCKETS` (`common/item_length.h:13-18`,
  `prodomodefines.h:76`), as `common::constants` already holds.
- `CItem::SetSocket` writes the socket, then `UpdatePacket` (the owner's `GC_ITEM_UPDATE`; none
  for an item with no owner) and `Save`. Its item log runs only with `bLog`, which this call
  leaves false.

**The world** (`world/src/character/specify_item.rs`, `items.rs`, `item_move.rs`):

- `CharacterItems::set_socket(id, index, value)` writes one socket of a stored item and answers
  its sockets, or `SocketRefused` (`NotHeld`, `Index`).
- `set_item_socket(items, id, (index, value))` answers a `MoveDone` of the new kind
  `MoveKind::Socketed`. It holds the item's `GC_ITEM_UPDATE` and `ItemChange::Sockets`, or
  nothing for an item not held or an index past the sockets.

**The bridge** (`quest/src/manager.rs`, `quest/src/host.rs`):

- `pc.give_item2_select` runs `give_item2`'s reads and give, pushes nothing, and sets `Cx::item`
  to a non-zero ID. A give of nothing keeps the old quest item.
- `operate` now writes `Cx::item` back to `Pc::item` after every run, so a later run (and its
  `item.get_vnum`) sees the item a run selected.
- `item.set_socket` (the helper `set_socket`) needs a quest item and two number-like arguments,
  takes `c_int` of each (so -0.5 is index 0 and an out-of-range value is `INT_MIN`), and passes
  an index of 0 to 5 to `Game::set_socket`.
- `BRIDGED` has 87 names, in `api::NAMES` order.

**The session** (`prodomo/src/game_state/quests.rs`):

- `set_socket` finds a laid item first: a give no cell took lies in `laid` until after the step,
  and a socket written there sends nothing, as a ground item has no owner.
- Otherwise, on a step whose descriptor stores item rows, `set_item_socket` runs on the held
  items. Its record joins the step's records and its `RowChange::Sockets` joins the step's rows,
  which are stored in the step's one transaction before the client hears them.
- A step that stores no rows writes nothing and logs, as the give and the removal do.

**The caller.** `sash_mission.lua:204-215`: `__complete`'s click calls
`pc.give_item2_select(85005, 1)` and `item.set_socket(1, 1)` only after
`pc.count_item(85000) >= 40`.

- Search: `^85000` in `legacy/gamedata/proto/item_proto.txt` finds nothing.
- Control: the same search for `^85005` finds the sash's row (`ITEM_COSTUME`, `COSTUME_SASH`).

85000 has no proto, so no character holds it and the branch never runs. The other `use`,
click and dialog scripts call neither name (search of the quest folder, beside the library
files: one hit each, both in `sash_mission.lua`).

**The tests.**

- `world`: `a_socket_write_updates_the_held_item_and_nothing_else`. The write lands with its
  update record and its sockets change, the last socket takes a negative value, and an ID not
  held or an index of 6 changes and sends nothing.
- `quest`: `the_selected_give_becomes_the_quest_item_whose_socket_is_set`.
  - A socket before any give writes nothing.
  - The select pushes nothing (`pcall(type, ...)`), gives through `give_item`, and makes item 77
    the quest item, which `item.get_vnum` reads.
  - The four writes that land: `(1, 1)`, `('2', 3.9)` as (2, 3), `(-0.5, 8)` as (0, 8), and
    `(5, -2147483649)` as (5, `INT_MIN`).
  - The writes refused: index 6, index -1, one argument, and a text value.
  - A second run with a give of nothing still writes to item 77.
- `prodomo` lib:
  - The setup of `a_give_names_sets_and_stores_the_item_or_lays_it` moved into
    `with_giving_session`, so the new test shares it.
  - The new `a_socket_lands_on_the_held_or_laid_item_and_is_stored`: a held sword's socket sends
    0x19 and answers `RowChange::Sockets`; a laid sword takes its socket and sends nothing; an

## 267. The GRAND book's alignment names (`pc.get_real_alignment`, `pc.change_alignment`, the no-delay pair)

A quest can now read the real alignment, move it, and read and remove the no-delay book
affect. All five names run through the GRAND book 50525's live `use` script, which is the
only caller on the owner's data, so all five rows are `partial` with a unit scenario.

**Legacy** (`G/questlua_pc.cpp:106-119,1081-1100`, `G/char_battle.cpp:3477-3565`):

- `pc_get_real_alignment` pushes `GetRealAlignment()/10`, an `int` division truncating
  toward zero (`:1081-1085`), registered as `get_real_alignment` (`:3824`).
- `pc_change_alignment` takes `(int)(lua_tonumber(L,1)*10)` and runs `UpdateAlignment`
  (`:1093-1100`), registered under both `changealignment` (`:3834`) and `change_alignment`
  (`:3837`). `lua_tonumber` answers 0 for a non-number, so a non-number moves nothing.
- `pc_is_skill_book_no_delay` pushes whether `FindAffect(513)` finds a row (`:113-119`);
  `pc_remove_skill_book_no_delay` runs `RemoveAffect(513)` and pushes nothing (`:106-111`).
  `AFFECT_SKILL_NO_BOOK_DELAY` is 513 (`G/affect.h:76`), beside the book bonus 512.
  A sweep of `server/server` for an `AddAffect` of 513 finds no grant: no legacy path
  grants the affect, only `ShamanSystem.cpp:258-261`, `char_item.cpp:4746-4751`,
  `char_skill.cpp:361-366,510-516` and the quest remove find or take it.
  - Control: the same sweep for 512 finds its grants.
- `UpdateAlignment` compares shown with real (`bShow`), takes the shown /10, clamps the
  real value to ±200000, copies it to the shown one and sends `UpdatePacket` when the /10
  moved — then tests the eight bonus affects in its own order (570, 573, 572, 571, 574,
  575, 576, 577) and adds the band's two affects with `bOverride`: band 1
  (10000-39999) gives 570 `POINT_ATTBONUS_HUMAN` +3 and 572 `POINT_MAX_HP` +500, band 2
  (40000-79999) 571 +6 and 573 +1000, band 3 (80000-119999) 574 +9 and 575 +1500, band 4
  (120000 and up) 576 +12 and 577 +2000, each for `ALIGNMENT_TIME` (one year in ticks).
- The removal tests are exact equalities against the real value: 570 and 572 stay only
  at exactly 10000, 571 and 573 only at 40000, 574 and 575 only at 80000, 576 and 577
  while at least 120000. Any other value in a band removes and re-adds its pair on every
  update — a Quirk, reproduced.
- The shown value leaves the real one only while the hide-alignment unique (70048) holds
  it at 0 through `ShowAlignment(false)` (`G/char_battle.cpp:3457-3475`,
  `G/char_item.cpp:8287-8288,8556-8557`, `G/item.cpp:2177-2178,2236-2237`,
  `G/unique_item.h:28`). No ported path grants that unique, so the Rewrite keeps one
  value: documented in `alignment.rs`, not a Divergence.

**The caller.** The only caller on the owner's data is the GRAND book 50525's `use` script
(`7and8th_skills.lua:161-298`): line 252 reads `pc.get_real_alignment()` for the
`-19000+need_alignment` gate, lines 170 and 264 read `pc.is_skill_book_no_delay()` at the
two rest gates, line 265 removes it, and line 290 moves the alignment on a failed read.
  - Search: the five names over `legacy/gamedata/locale/europe/quest` (`*.lua`,
    `*.quest`) finds only `7and8th_skills.lua`.
  - Control: the same search for `pc.set_skill_level` finds the boost, ward and reset
    books' lines beside the GRAND book's.

**The bridge** (`quest/src/manager.rs`, `quest/src/host.rs`):

- `pc.get_real_alignment` answers `real_alignment()/10` (`i32`, truncating toward zero).
- `pc.changealignment` and `pc.change_alignment` share the helper `change_alignment`:
  `(int)(number * 10)` through `host::c_int`, 0 for a non-number, and nothing pushed.
- `pc.is_skill_book_no_delay` answers `has_skill_book_no_delay()`;
  `pc.remove_skill_book_no_delay` runs `remove_skill_book_no_delay()` and pushes nothing.
- `BRIDGED` has 92 names, in `api::NAMES` order.

**The world** (`prodomo/src/game_state/alignment.rs`):

- `GameState::update_alignment` is `UpdateAlignment`: clamp in `i64` (an amount that
  would overflow an `int` clamps; the x86 result there is undefined), the crossing
  update before the band changes, the eight removals in legacy's order, then the band's
  two adds with `bOverride`. The removals take back the one point slot each, as every
  other affect removal does; legacy recomputes every point, which agrees for these
  point-only affects.
- `clamped_alignment`, `stale_alignment_bonus`, `alignment_bonuses` and `alignment_bonus`
  are pure and shared with the session.
- The kill's `raise_alignment` (`G/char_battle.cpp:794-807`) now routes through it: by 2,
  or by 7 (14 with the unique 70051) while negative. Its old inline clamp and update are
  gone.

**The session** (`prodomo/src/game_state/quests.rs`):

- `Session` carries the script's alignment and its recorded amounts. `change_alignment`
  clamps and records; a later read in the same script sees the earlier change.
- The amounts settle after the step, in order, through `update_alignment` — once per
  call, as legacy runs them, each clamped on the value the one before it left.
- `has_skill_book_no_delay` reads the borrowed affects; `remove_skill_book_no_delay`
  takes every row of the kind with its remove frame, as `RemoveAffect(DWORD)` takes all
  rows (`G/char_affect.cpp:864-879`).
- The settle writes through the outbox queue while the step's own records travel the
  direct answer, so on a quest step the band frames land before the step's dialog. The
  50525 script ends its alignment step with `say` lines, so on the wire the crossing
  update precedes the failure text where legacy sends it after. Recorded here; the
  scripted-client scenario will pin the order.

**The tests.**

- `quest`: `the_alignment_and_no_delay_book_names_follow_legacy`. The /10 truncates

  - `the_bands_are_the_four_legacy_windows`, `each_bonus_stays_only_at_the_value_legacy_names`,

## 268. The GRAND book over the wire (the five alignment rows to `ported`)

The scripted-client scenario for the whole GRAND book flow, which 267 left waiting. No
production code changed: the bridge, the world update and the settle all held over the
wire as the unit scenario pinned them. The five quest-api rows are `ported`.

**The scenario** (`prodomo/tests/parity.rs::the_grand_book_reads_the_alignment_and_moves_it_on_a_failed_read`):

- Alpha, a shaman of the second group whose `next_time` is an hour out, uses 50525 with
  no no-delay affect and is refused at the first rest gate (`[DONE]`, the book stays on
  its row). This pins `pc.is_skill_book_no_delay`'s false arm over the wire.
- Zulu, with no rest stamp at all, uses the book, says yes to the warning, picks ward
  221 from the `select_table` offer, passes the `-19000+need_alignment` gate (0 is above
  -18000) through `pc.get_real_alignment`, and confirms. No skill row is hosted for the
  ward, so the read fails silently and the failure text ends the script — and the failed
  read moves the alignment through `pc.change_alignment`, which the disconnect banks
  between -5000 and -3330 (`-number(333, 500)` times legacy's ×10), beside the
  `next_time` flag the confirm set.
- The removal's `ITEM_SET` clear lands before the failure dialog: the give/take records
  precede the script's own in the step's answer.

**What the wire taught.** Three scenario bugs, all in the test, none in the server:

- Zulu at level 1 died mid-script: a monster aggroed it past the 5-second revive cloak
  at Alpha's spawn. Zulu is level 154 now, which no map-1 monster touches.
- The alignment check first read `BETWEEN -500 AND -333`, forgetting legacy's ×10
  (`G/questlua_pc.cpp:1096`); the bridge multiplies, so the range is -5000 to -3330.
- The `next_time` check first counted unscoped rows and expected a
  `training_grandmaster_skill.skill221` flag the script never sets. Only the confirm's
  `setqf("next_time")` exists, and Alpha's seed row shares the name, so Zulu's flag is
  scoped to its player row.

Clippy `too_many_lines` on the scenario (149/100): it split into the test plus the two
helpers `grand_book_refuses_alpha_at_the_rest_gate` and
`grand_book_fails_zulu_and_moves_its_alignment`, fixed by refactoring with no `#[allow]`.

**Parity.**

- `lua.pc.get_real_alignment`, `lua.pc.changealignment`, `lua.pc.change_alignment`,

  with the scenario.
- `quest.7and8th_skills` has a note.

## 269. The guild man's questions (41 reader and guild names, `game.request_make_guild`)

The character readers and the guild triad a quest asks about its reader: gold under its
four spellings, empire, HP/SP and their maxima, exp and next exp, race, name, VID,
leadership, the global and local positions, the weapon/armor/`get_wear` vnums, the shown
alignment, `pc.has_guild`/`pc.get_guild`/`pc.is_guild_master` under both spellings each,
`npc.get_empire`, and `game.request_make_guild` (42 names, 41 rows: `pc.get_alignment`
shares its row with `pc.get_real_alignment`, which 267 ported). Six rows are `ported`
through the guild man's founding chat; the other 35 are `partial` with unit coverage.

**Legacy** (`G/questlua_pc.cpp`, `G/questlua_npc.cpp:43-52`, `G/questlua_game.cpp:51-62`):

- `pc_get_money` pushes `GetGold()` (`unsigned long long`, `:1073-1077`) through
  `lua_pushnumber` (`double`); gold above 2^53 rounds there, so the bridge's `as f64`
  keeps the rounding behind a documented `#[allow]`. Registered under four names
  (`:3822-3823`, `:3830-3831`).
- `pc_get_hp/max_hp/sp/max_sp` (`:921-979`), `pc_get_exp/next_exp` (`:891-901`),
  `pc_get_race` (`:903-907`), `pc_get_name` (`:885-889`), `pc_get_vid` (`:880-884`),
  `pc_get_leadership` (`:862-866`), `pc_get_empire` (`:1304-1308`), each pushing its
  getter, most under two spellings.
- `pc_get_x/y` push `GetX()/100` and `GetY()/100` (`:737-749`); `pc_get_local_x/y` push
  the position minus the map base, over 100 (`:751-775`).
- `pc_get_weapon/armor` push the worn vnum, 0 when the cell is empty (`:1028-1050`);
  `pc_get_wear` pushes nil when the cell is out of range or empty, and a non-number
  argument logs `QUEST wrong set flag` and pushes nothing (`:1052-1071`).
- `pc_get_real_alignment` and `pc_get_alignment` push the real and the shown value,
  each /10 (`:1081-1091`); this build keeps one value (267), so one arm answers both.
- `pc_hasguild` pushes whether a guild id is held (`:325-330`), `pc_getguild` the id
  (`:332-337`), `pc_isguildmaster` the master flag (`:339-350`), each under two names.
- `npc_get_empire` pushes the NPC's empire, 0 with no NPC (`G/questlua_npc.cpp:43-52`).
- `game_request_make_guild` sends the bare `HEADER_GC_REQUEST_MAKE_GUILD` byte and
  pushes nothing (`G/questlua_game.cpp:51-62`).

**The caller.** The guild man's founding chat (`guild_manage.lua:93-144`): its menu
with-clause reads `pc.hasguild()`, the yes-branch gates on `pc.level >= 40` (154 passes)
and `pc.gold >= 200000` (ported already and the money family), and `guild_create_item`
is false, so the script ends with `game.request_make_guild()`.

**The bridge** (`quest/src/manager.rs`, `quest/src/host.rs`):

- `pc_api` dispatches the read-only names to `pc_readers` first, and the flag pair to
  `pc_flags`; both return the miss/push-nothing distinction the families need.
  `pc_get_wear` stays in `pc_api` (a non-number pushes nothing, which `pc_readers`'
  `None` cannot say), reading `(BYTE)` as the low byte of `dword`, as
  `pc_send_block_mode` does.
- New `Game` readers: `gold`, `empire`, `hp`, `max_hp`, `sp`, `max_sp`, `exp`,
  `next_exp`, `race`, `char_name`, `char_vid`, `leadership`, `position` (the four),
  `worn_vnum`, `guild_id`, `is_guild_master`, and `request_make_guild`. The `Fake`
  answers from fields; the `Session` from the reader context and the points.
- `MapIndex::base` answers the grid's first sectree times 6400 through saturating
  `i32::try_from` (a map base fits; map 1's columns are 64 and 140).
- `BRIDGED` grows to 134 names in `api::NAMES` order.

**The session** (`prodomo/src/game_state/quests.rs`):

- `reader_context` threads the guilds through `GameState::guild_pair` (the id and the
  master flag, 0 and false with none) beside gold, empire, name, position, leadership,

  `ArmedSession` borrow (the line lint), and `request_make_guild` pushes the one-byte

**The scenario** (`prodomo/tests/parity.rs::the_guild_chat_reads_the_level_and_gold_gates`):

## 270. The fortieth material (the flag family, the money writer)

Seven names: `pc.getf`/`pc.setf` (another quest's flags), `pc.delqf` (the flag delete),
and `pc.change_money` under its four spellings (`changegold`, `changemoney`,
`change_gold`, `change_money`). One row is `ported` through the sash quest's `__complete`
over the wire; the other six are `partial` with unit coverage.

**Legacy** (`G/questlua_pc.cpp:1102-1165,1231-1243`, `G/char.cpp:3823-3850`):

- `pc_get_another_quest_flag` pushes `GetFlag(sz.sz2)`, 0 when unset (`:1141-1165`);
  `pc_set_another_quest_flag` writes `int(rint(...))` there, 0 deleting (`:1123-1139`,
  `G/questpc.cpp:52-76`). `lua_isstring` accepts text and numbers, as `getqf`/`setqf` do.
- `pc_del_quest_flag` deletes `GetCurrentQuestName().sz` whether or not it was set
  (`:1231-1243`, `G/questpc.cpp:78-90`); a non-string logs `argument error`.
- `pc_change_money` moves `(long long)lua_tonumber(L, -1)` — the *last* argument
  (`:1102-1121`). Below 0 logs `QUEST wrong ChangeGold` and moves nothing; `ChangeGold`
  refuses a total reaching `GOLD_MAX_MAX` (`common/length.h:100`, 1.2e18) with
  `[OVERFLOW_GOLD]` and moves nothing; otherwise the gold moves and the client hears
  `TPacketGCGoldChange` with the amount clamped to 0 for a loss.

**The caller.** The sash quest's `__complete.enter` deletes `time_to_wait` and

## 271. The hidden costume (`pc.hide_costume`, `/hide_costume`, `quest.costume_option`)

One quest name, one chat command, one quest script, and the enter-game restore that
precedes them both. All three rows are `ported` through one wire scenario.

**Legacy** (`G/questlua_pc.cpp:3553-3600`, `G/cmd_general.cpp:3934-3979`,

- `pc_hide_costume` takes `(BYTE)` of the first argument as the part (1-5: body, hair,
  sash, aura, weapon) and a boolean hide; a non-number part, a non-boolean hide, or a
  part outside 1-5 logs and changes nothing. The matching setter lands the mask bit,
  chats `SetXCostumeHidden %d`, writes the `costume_option.hide_*` quest flag (0

  part outside 1-5 is quiet, and a hide runs the setter plus `UpdatePacket`.

  armor's look (through its transmutation; `__CHANGE_LOOK_SYSTEM__` is off, but the
  `#else` arm reads the same vnum path the Rewrite's `look_of` takes), the weapon the
  weapon's look, and hair, sash and aura 0.

Eight quest names: the quest item's socket, proto value, count and type pair, the
room check, and the GM gate with its level. One row is `ported` through the wire
scenario; the other seven are `partial` with unit pins. The slice takes V26.

**Legacy** (`G/questlua_item.cpp:107-123,175-202,259-301`, `G/questlua_pc.cpp:478-499`,

`G/char.cpp:6353-6358`):

- `item_get_socket` pushes the quest item's socket at `(int)` of the first argument,
  0 with no quest item, a non-number argument or an index outside `ITEM_SOCKET_MAX_NUM`
  (6, under `ENABLE_EXTENDED_SOCKETS`).
- `item_get_value` pushes `GetProto()->alValues[index]` (`G/item.cpp:1598-1602`), 0 with
  no quest item, no proto, a non-number argument or an index outside
  `ITEM_VALUES_MAX_NUM` (6). The owner's 72347 row carries its 10 in `VALUE3`, which is
  what the spiral's script reads.
- `item_get_count`, `item_get_type` and `item_get_sub_type` push the quest item's count
  and its proto's type pair, 0 with no quest item; the type pair is 0 with no proto.
- `pc_enough_inventory` pushes false for a non-number vnum or a vnum with no proto,
  else whether `GetEmptyInventory(size)` finds a base cell below `Inventory_Size()`.
- `pc_is_gm` pushes `GetGMLevel() >= GM_HIGH_WIZARD` (3); `pc_get_gm_level` pushes the
  level. In the test-server mode `GetGMLevel` answers `GM_IMPLEMENTOR` whatever the

  character was a GM and the sash quest's `not pc.is_gm()` gate never opened.

  the old `pc_api` stub that answered false is gone. `pc.enough_inventory` answers the
  room by `(DWORD)` of its first argument, false for a non-number.

  under the giver's unlocked count. `held_socket` reads the held item's socket,
  `held_value` its proto's value, `held_shape` its count with the proto type pair (0

## 274. The temple guardian's warp (`pc.warp`, `game.drop_item_with_ownership`, `pc.get_conqueror_level`)
Three quest names: the warp, the owned drop and the conqueror reader. One row is
`ported` through the wire scenario; the other two are `partial` with unit pins. The slice
takes no Divergence.

**Legacy** (`G/questlua_pc.cpp:209-240,3632-3637`, `G/questlua_game.cpp:168-213`,
`G/char.cpp:6694-6792`, `G/item.cpp:1733-1775`):

- `pc_warp` needs two numbers and answers false without them; `IsHack` refuses the
  rest, and the test server chats the point. Past the gates it runs `WarpSet(x, y,
  map)`: the third argument is a private index (at or above 10000, of the resolved
  map), and the call answers true whatever the warp does.
- `game_drop_item_with_ownership` makes `count` of the vnum on one to three arguments
  (1 with one, the seconds are read only when number-like) at the character's feet
  (`number(-200, 200)` each way), owned by it (`SetOwnership(ch[, secs])`, 30 at 10
  and below, 30 with no stamp). No proto makes nothing; it pushes nothing.
- `WarpSet` resolves the map by position, refuses a private index of another map and
  a sorted inventory (`__SORT_INVENTORY_ITEMS__`, `prodomodefines.h:143`), then
  saves, leaves the sectree and sends the own removal and `GC_WARP`.
- `pc_get_conqueror_level` pushes the character's conqueror level.

**The bridge** (`quest/src/manager.rs`, `quest/src/host.rs`):

- Three `Game` methods: `warp`, `drop_with_ownership` and `conqueror_level`.
  `BRIDGED` grows to 157 names in `api::NAMES` order.
- `pc_warp` and `drop_with_ownership` are helpers (`pc_api` and `api` would trip the
  line lint): the warp answers false without two numbers, the drop runs on one to
  three arguments. The conqueror level joins `pc_readers`. The test-server line stays
  with the audit, as the anywhere spawn's does.

**The world and session** (`prodomo/src/game_state/quests.rs`,
`prodomo/src/game_state/reward.rs`, `parity/src/server.rs`):

- The session carries the `IsHack` snapshot and the armed conqueror level, so the
  warp answers what the world would judge and the reader reads its own level. Both
  calls record their ops; the world judges them after the step, the drops before the
  warps (a script could drop and leave).
- `lay_drop_owned` makes the item through the kill drops' `CreateItem` (`rare_pct`
  -1), lays it at the feet and owns it by the reader for the stamped seconds. A vnum
  with no proto lays nothing, as legacy's `NULL` does.
- `order_quest_warp` finds the target map in the atlas and orders the reader's client
  the warp on the Channel hosting it; the descriptor runs `WarpSet` (the private
  index, the sort gate, the save, `GC_WARP`). A target no Channel hosts orders
  nowhere, as the failed `CMapLocation::Get` does, while the call still answers true.
  The sort gate needs no state: the Rewrite never sorts, as the warp NPC's notes say
  of its unported arms.
- `make_drop_hit` is shared with the quest judge. `parity` gains
  `start_with_npcs_channels` (the NPC lines plus a chosen topology).

**The scenario**
(`prodomo/tests/parity.rs::a_yes_to_the_temple_guardian_warps_to_the_ochao_temple`):

  letter, the sash's change mark, the letter pass's replacement, the letters, the

  past `IsHack`, the dialog ends with `[DONE]`, and the client hears its own removal
  and the `GC_WARP` naming the temple point and Channel 1. The row holds the target.

**Mutation sweep.** Skipped, as in 269, 271, 272 and 273: the bridge pins every value
(the warp's gates, the truncation, the private index, the hack both ways, the drop's
counts and silences, the conqueror read), the session pins the recording and the
answer, the world pins the ownership stamps and the feet, and the scenario pins the
wire order (the menu, the page, the removal, the warp, the row).

**The gate runs failed thirteen times.**

- Three `Session` literal sites missed the new fields (then four, then the last).
- `pc_readers` has no `number` closure; the conqueror arm builds its own value.
- `ClientOrder` was unimported and `make_drop_hit` private to its module.

- The click offers a menu before the dialog; the scenario answered none.

## 275. The statue's return (`warp_to_village`, `pc.can_warp`, `pc.set_conqueror`)
Four quest names: the village warp, the warp gate, and the conqueror reader and setter.
All four rows are `ported` through the wire scenario. The slice takes no Divergence.

**Legacy** (`G/questlua_global.cpp:1060-1071`, `G/questlua_pc.cpp:2723-2735,3632-3647`,
`G/char.cpp:11659-11700`):

- `_warp_to_village` runs `WarpSet(g_start_position[empire])` on the current character
  and pushes nothing. `pc_can_warp` answers `CanWarp()`, false with no character.
  `pc_get_conqueror_level` answers `GetConquerorLevel()`, 0 with no character.
- `pc_set_conqueror` runs `SetConqueror()` with no arguments read: `SetConqueror(true)`
  chats "You have already reached the Champion Level." for a conqueror, and "You must
  fill up at least 1 EXP Marble at level 120 to reach Champion Level." below the
  level-120 filled marble (`GetLevel() < gPlayerMaxLevel`, or at it with `GetExp() <
  GetNextExp() / 4`). Else the conqueror level becomes 1, the step, point and sungma
  slots reset in both arrays, the conqueror exp clears, and the points recompute
  (`ComputePoints`, `PointsPacket`, the `POINT_CONQUEROR_EXP` update).

**Rewrite** (`quest/src/manager.rs`, `quest/src/host.rs`, `prodomo/src/game_state/quests.rs`,
`world/src/character/points.rs`, `prodomo/tests/parity.rs`):

- The bridge takes `warp_to_village` (pushes nothing), `pc.can_warp` (the armed gate)
  and `pc.set_conqueror` (recorded, pushes nothing); `pc.get_conqueror_level` stays on
  the armed level. `BRIDGED` keeps `NAMES` order, which the host test pins.
- The session holds a `WarpGates` byte (hack refusal, warp pass) instead of two bools,
  the armed gates and the conqueror level, plus the village and conqueror call counts.
  `ReaderContext` carries the gates and the level; a hacked reader disarms the pass.
  `arm_quest_session` packs its borrows into `SessionInputs` and builds the session in
  `build_session`, splitting the `Quests` borrow (manager vs protos/names) so the armed
  session's manager borrow does not collide. `api`'s `number` and `item_name`/`mob_name`
  arms are `drawn_number` and `named_thing`.
- `order_village_warp` runs the quest warp to the reader's empire start (`EMPIRE_START`,
  so Shinsoo's (469300, 964200)); `make_conqueror` chats the two legacy lines through
  `CHAT_TYPE_INFO` and changes nothing, or transitions via `Points::become_conqueror`
  (level 1, the step, point, exp and sungma slots cleared in both arrays) with
  `compute_points` after. The conqueror point and exp packets wait for their system.
- The scenario stands the warrior statue (20433) on map 1 with Alpha level 154 and
  `yohara_system` at `killReward_new` (seeded CRC32): the reward state's letter deletes
  its stale Overseer mark first, so the letter pass marks Theowahdan again (ID 2)
  before the letters. The click offers the ship's Return and the Yohara trip plus the
  close (three entries, since `ship_defense` and `yohara_manager` both chat on the
  statue and `yohara_system`'s reward state has no click); "Da" to the Return runs the
  village warp with the remove packet, the warp record and the stored position.
  The congratulations chat and `set_conqueror`'s transition wait for the Hydra kill.

Parity rows: `lua.warp_to_village`, `lua.pc.can_warp`, `lua.pc.get_conqueror_level` and
`lua.pc.set_conqueror` are `ported` (`a_yes_to_the_statues_return_warps_to_the_village`).
`quest.ship_defense` and `quest.yohara_system` stay `partial`: the defence event, the
rankings, the statue's mark and click, and the Hydra kill wait for their systems.

## 276. Theowahdan's Combination (`pc.open_sash`, `pc.open_changelook`)
Two quest names: the sash open and the changelook open. `open_sash` is `ported`
through the wire scenario; `open_changelook` is `partial` (bridged, the window waits).
The slice takes no Divergence.

**Legacy** (`G/questlua_pc.cpp:3523-3549`, `G/char.cpp:9888-9936`,
`G/packet.h:2795-2818`):

- `pc_open_sash` runs `OpenSash(lua_toboolean(L, 1))` on the current character when
  the first argument is a boolean, else `sys_err("Invalid argument: arg1 must be
  boolean")`; it pushes nothing. `pc_open_changelook` runs
  `ChangeLookWindow(true)` with no argument read; it pushes nothing.
- `OpenSash(combination)` chats `SASH_OPEN` when that side stands, `SASH_CLOSE`
  when the absorption side blocks a combination, and `COMBINE_CLOSE` when the
  combination side blocks an absorption; else the side stands and the open record
  goes out (subheader `OPEN`, the combination flag, every number 0,
  `tPos = { INVENTORY, 0 }`).
- `TPacketSash` is 23 bytes: header 0xe7, subheader, `bool bWindow`, two `DWORD`s,
  `TItemPos` (window byte, cell word), `DWORD dwVnum`, and the two long absorb
  numbers.

**Rewrite** (`protocol/src/gc_sash.rs`, `protocol/src/gc_inventory.rs`,
`quest/src/manager.rs`, `quest/src/host.rs`, `prodomo/src/game_state/quests.rs`,
`prodomo/tests/parity.rs`):

- The codec pins the 23-byte record with golden bytes; the inventory row flips to
  implemented (112 of 134, 22 missing) and the coverage table in `AGENTS.md` follows.
- The bridge takes `pc.open_sash` (only a `Value::Boolean` opens; anything else
  logs and changes nothing) and `pc.open_changelook` (no argument read); both push
  nothing. The four window names live in `pc_windows` so `pc_api` stays under the
  line limit. `BRIDGED` keeps `NAMES` order, which the host test pins.
- The session holds a sash bitset (combination, absorption) and the changelook
  call count; `open_sash_window` chats the three legacy keys through
  `CHAT_TYPE_INFO` or stands the side and queues the open record.
- The scenario replays the reward state's click first (the short-material page, the
  captain's mark and letter, so the menu has eight chats with Transmutation fifth),
  then opens Combination over the quest window, answers "Yes", and reads `[DONE]`
  before the 23-byte open record with the combination flag.

Parity rows: `lua.pc.open_sash` and `gc.sash` are `ported`
(`a_yes_to_theowahdans_combination_opens_the_sash_window`). `lua.pc.open_changelook`
is `partial`: bridged, the window waits. `quest.sash` and `quest.changelook` stay
`partial`: the sash's add, remove and refine, and the changelook's window, wait for
their systems.

Tests:

- `quest` lib: `the_sash_opens_for_a_boolean_and_the_changelook_opens_always` (a
  boolean opens, nil/number/text change nothing, the changelook opens and pushes
  nothing).
- `prodomo` lib: `the_session_opens_the_sash_or_chats_its_keys` (the open stands
  and sends, the three key chats, the push-nothing).
- `prodomo/tests/parity.rs`: `a_yes_to_theowahdans_combination_opens_the_sash_window`.

## 280. The forest room's ticket check (`party.get_member_pids`, `q.begin_other_pc_block`, `q.end_other_pc_block`)

Three quest names: the on-map member PIDs and the other-PC stack. All three are
`ported` through the wire scenario. The slice takes no Divergence: the refusal page
names nobody because legacy's own loop walks the level list, not the ticket list
(`enchanted_forest_zone.lua:169`), and the page is what the Reference client shows
against legacy too.

**Legacy** (`G/questlua_party.cpp:413-442`, `G/questlua_quest.cpp:204-217`,
`G/questmanager.cpp:1087-1099,2051-2093`, `G/char_item.cpp:8791-8940`):

- `party_get_member_pids` pushes one Lua number per on-map member PID and returns
  the count; with no party it pushes nothing and returns 0.
- `quest_begin_other_pc_block` takes `lua_tonumber` of the last argument, grows the
  PC stack even for an offline PID, and switches the current PC and character when
  `GetPC` finds one (`FindByPID`); an unknown PID keeps the old one.
- `quest_end_other_pc_block` pops the stack and runs for the pushed PID again; with
  no open block it logs and stays quiet.
- Inside a block the `pc.*` readers and `RemoveSpecifyItem` run against the blocked
  character, as `GetCurrentCharacterPtr` answers it.

**Rewrite** (`quest/src/manager.rs`, `quest/src/host.rs`,
`prodomo/src/game_state/quests.rs`, `prodomo/tests/parity.rs`):

- The bridge pushes the member PIDs in `party_api` (one value per PID, its own
  arity) and runs the stack in a new `quest_api` family, which also holds the
  index and name readers: `begin` pushes `cx.current`, asks the game, and switches
  only when the game switched; `end` pops and asks. `BRIDGED` keeps `NAMES` order
  (174 names), which the host test pins.
- The session snapshots every online PC (VID, level, name, points, items, cells)
  at the step's start. `begin_other_pc` clones from it (`None` for an offline PID,
  the stack still growing); the level, name, VID, points, count and removal arms
  answer the innermost switched frame. A block's removals land on the snapshot and
  record their takes, which run against the world after the step with their records
  to their owner's client and their rows for the store.
- The scenario forms Alice's party with Yankee over the wire, seeds Alice's ticket,
  and Alice says "Da": the ticket loop runs the block over both members and the
  refusal page follows.

Parity rows: `lua.party.get_member_pids`, `lua.q.begin_other_pc_block` and
`lua.q.end_other_pc_block` are `ported`
(`the_leaders_click_on_the_forest_room_is_refused_for_want_of_a_ticket`).
`lua.pc.get_level` was already `ported`; `lua.pc.getname` and `lua.pc.get_name`
stay `partial` (the script fills a list it never prints, so no scenario hears a
blocked name yet). `quest.enchanted_forest_zone` stays `partial` for the dungeon
manager names past the ticket check.

Tests:

- `quest` lib: `the_member_pids_and_the_block` inside
  `the_reader_names_answer_what_the_game_holds` (the pushed PIDs, the switched
  write, the offline stack growth, the end's restore).
- `prodomo` lib: `a_block_runs_for_the_blocked_pc_and_its_end_restores_the_reader`
  (the blocked level/name/VID/count, the snapshot removal, the end's restore, the
  unswitched frame).
- `prodomo/tests/parity.rs`:
  `the_leaders_click_on_the_forest_room_is_refused_for_want_of_a_ticket`.

## 281. The alchemist's dragon-soul windows (`ds.give_qualification`, `ds.is_qualified`, the two opens)

Four quest names: the qualification grant and read, and the refine and
attr-change opens. All four are `ported` through the wire scenario, with the three
quest scripts and the two window records. The slice takes no Divergence.

**Legacy** (`G/questlua_dragonsoul.cpp:14-70`, `G/char_dragonsoul.cpp:70-158`,
`G/char_affect.cpp:668-760`):

- `ds_give_qualification` runs `DragonSoul_GiveQualification()`, which is
  `AddAffect(540, APPLY_NONE, 0, AFF_NONE, INFINITE_AFFECT_DURATION, 0, false,
  false)`: the infinite row appends (no override, no dedupe), the zero apply
  computes nothing, and the add packet goes to the player at once, in the call.
- `ds_is_qualified` answers a Lua number, 1 or 0.
- `ds_open_refine_window` opens only with the qualification: the reader hears
  `HEADER_GC_DRAGON_SOUL_REFINE` with `DS_SUB_HEADER_OPEN` (0) and a default
  `TItemPos` (`SItemPos()`: `INVENTORY` (1), `WORD_MAX`).
- `ds_open_attr_change_window` opens unconditionally: the one-byte
  `HEADER_GC_DS_PLUS_CHANGE_ATTR_OPEN`.
- Quest order is the ADR-0006 order (`quest_list`, then the other scripts by
  path): `dragon_soul.lua` sorts between `costume_option.quest` and
  `event_info.lua`, so the grant's add rides between the hides and
  `event_info`'s line.
- 540 sits in the 500-600 no-clear band (`IS_NO_CLEAR_ON_DEATH_AFFECT`,
  `G/char_affect.cpp:57-60`), so the death keeps it and re-sends it with every
  held affect (`G/char_battle.cpp:1561-1569`).

**Rewrite** (`quest/src/manager.rs`, `quest/src/host.rs`,
`prodomo/src/game_state/quests.rs`, `prodomo/src/game_state/death.rs`):

- The four names join `BRIDGED` in `NAMES` order and land in `dungeon_api`
  (folded into the `d.*` family: a standalone `ds_api` trips
  `clippy::unnecessary_wraps`, as nothing it calls can fail).
- The grant lands in the call: the infinite row pushes into the session's live
  affect event and its add packet joins the step's records beside the script's
  own lines, in call order — so a later `ds.is_qualified` in the same step
  answers true, and the login event carries the add between the hides and
  `event_info`. The counter stays only as the "ran" witness. The two opens
  queue for the apply pass, as the windows' sends need the world.
- `WorldMoves` bundles the step's world-visible queues (laid, warps, drops, the
  counts, the sash and changelook opens, the `ds.*` opens, the party sets) so
  `run_quests_giving_raw` stays under the line lint.
- `clear_affects_on_death` keeps the 500-600 band, so 540 survives and the
  death re-sends it.

**Parity** (`.scratch/parity/`):

- `quest-api.md`: `lua.ds.open_refine_window`, `lua.ds.open_attr_change_window`,
  `lua.ds.give_qualification`, `lua.ds.is_qualified` to `ported`.
- `server-records.md`: `gc.dragon_soul_refine`, `gc.ds_plus_change_attr_open`
  to `ported`.
- `quests.md`: `quest.dragon_soul`, `quest.dragon_soul_plus_attr_change`,
  `quest.dragon_soul_refine` to `ported`.

**Tests**:

- `prodomo` lib: `the_session_grants_the_ds_qualification_in_its_call_and_queues_the_opens`
  (the infinite row and its add packet land in the call; the opens queue);
  `death_clears_the_hit_affects_and_ends_the_poison` also seeds 540 and asserts
  it survives with no remove.
- `prodomo` parity: `the_alchemists_chats_open_the_dragon_soul_windows_once_qualified`
  (the alchemist on map 1; the login grants; the refine chat opens 209/sub 0
  with `INVENTORY`/`WORD_MAX`; the gated attr chat opens 211 on "Da").
- `prodomo` parity helpers: `read_login_lines_hiding` reads the infinite add
  between the hides and `event_info`; `read_script_past_ticks` reads a dialog
  past the affect event's tick records; `is_ds_qualification_add` filters the
  death's re-sent grant; the 209/211 headers join `game_len`.

Fixes while green:

- The grant first queued for the apply pass, so every login carried it ahead of
  `dungeoninfo`'s line; legacy's `AddAffect` sends in the call. Moving the push
  and the add packet into the bridge call put it in quest order.
- The death cleared 540 and the failure tail showed its remove; legacy's
  no-clear band keeps it. Keeping 500-600 made the death re-send it, as legacy

- Clippy `too_many_lines` on `run_quests_giving_raw` (the `WorldMoves` bundle),
  on the new lib test (the grant asserts extract), on the scenario (the tick
  reader extracts), `match_same_arms` on the one-byte router arm (folded), and

`ACMD(do_priv_empire)` (`G/cmd_gm.cpp:3107-3167`) and the game side of
