## 383. The whisper partner's details (`CG_WHISPER_DETAILS`, `GC_WHISPER_DETAILS`)

`CInputMain::WhisperDetails` (`G/input_main.cpp:3603-3638`, dispatched at `:3938-3940`)
answers a whisper window's question about its partner: the client sends a 25-byte name, and
the server answers `GC_WHISPER_DETAILS` (246) with that name and the language of the character
holding it, found on this core (`FindPC`) or another (`P2P_MANAGER::Find`), else
`LOCALE_DEFAULT` (`LOCALE_EN`, 1, `C/length.h:1215`). An empty name is not answered (`:3607`).

- `protocol/src/gc_whisper.rs` gains `GcWhisperDetails` (`name: [u8; 25]`, `language: u8`),
  27 bytes, with golden bytes, a decode, every language byte, and the short and foreign
  refusals. The width was measured with `g++ -m32 -fsyntax-only` `static_assert`s over the
  verbatim struct bodies under `#pragma pack(1)` (`i686-linux-gnu-g++-12` is not installed,
  and `-m32` cannot link here): `TPacketGCWhisperDetails` 27 with `bLanguage` at offset 26,
  `TPacketCGWhisperDetails` 26, and the packed two-`long` control 8. `GcWhisperError` now
  names its fields (`Truncated { needed, actual }`, `Header { expected, actual }`). The GC
  inventory row is implemented: 115 implemented, 19 missing (8 fixed-size, 11 dynamic), in
  `gc_inventory.rs`, the four pinned counts of `protocol/tests/cg_wiring.rs`, and the
  `AGENTS.md` coverage table.
- `prodomo`: `MainRecord::WhisperDetails`, `whisper_details_step`, and the pure
  `whisper_details_answer`. The partner is looked up in the process-wide client registry
  (`entry_of`, every Channel, case-insensitive), which stands in for `FindPC` and
  `P2P_MANAGER::Find`; a name nobody online holds, or one that is not UTF-8, is answered
  with 1. The echo is at most 24 bytes with the 25th byte 0.
- Fix to ledger 379: a language switch updated only the account, so the client registry's
  entry kept the login language, and every line read through it (the shout, the notices,
  the warp NPC, the empire privilege lines) stayed in the old language. `Lease::set_language`
  (`DESC::SetLanguage`, `G/char.cpp:11641`) now runs in `change_language_step`.
- Defects not reproduced: legacy reads the asked name as a C string that may run past its

## 384. The target window's drop list (`CG_TARGET_INFO_LOAD`, `GC_TARGET_INFO`)

`CInputMain::TargetInfoLoad` (`G/input_main.cpp:66-123`, `__SEND_TARGET_INFO__` and
`ENABLE_SEND_TARGET_INFO_EXTENDED` on, `C/prodomodefines.h:142,146`) answers the target
window's question with what the target may drop, built by
`ITEM_MANAGER::CreateDropItemVector` (`G/item_manager.cpp:915-1095`).

- `prodomo/src/game_state/target_info.rs` (new): `GameState::target_info`, the pure
  `drop_list`, `Makers::listed` and `info_records`. The target is found as `CG_TARGET` finds
  it (on the asker's Channel and map; `targeted` is now `pub(super)`); a player lists
  nothing. The list runs legacy's arms in order: the common loop adds nothing (its `item` is
  still `NULL`, `:944`), every `drop` group row, one `kill` row drawn as `GetOne` draws
  (`number(1, total)` against the running part percents, with no kill-per-drop gate), the
  `limit` rows when the level limit read as a `DWORD` is at most the asker's level, every
  `thiefgloves` row, and the proto's `DROP_ITEM` when the etc table names it. The stone arm
  is dead (`ENABLE_STONE_DROP_ON_METIN` is undefined, C15). Only a monster or a stone is
  answered, checked after the list (and its draw), as legacy does. One entry is sent as it is,
  a stone included; several are sorted by `CustomSort` and sub-type with the stones skipped.
- Each entry is what `CreateItem(vnum, count, 0, true, pct)` would show: the mask's vnum;
  the count (gold keeps the row's up to `INT_MAX`, a stackable item is held between 1 and the
  stack limit on the `DWORD` count, a `MAKECOUNT` item asking for 1 takes `VALUE1`, anything
  else is 1), cut to the record's `WORD`; and the rarity, the percent ×10000 (a `kill` row's
  rare percent), with the etc drop's default -1 sent as `0xFFFFFFFF`.
- `gamedata::item_kind` gains `ITEM_MATERIAL` (5) and `ITEM_SKILLFORGET` (22), pinned to
  their name indices; `world::character::ITEM_FLAG_MAKECOUNT` is now public.
- The descriptor takes 0x3b as a world step (`target_info_step`, `GameCommand::TargetInfo`,
  `GameHandle::target_info`); a malformed record closes the connection.
- Defects not reproduced: legacy makes a real item per entry, with a new ID and, for a timed
  item, a running expiry event, and never destroys it (a leak per click); a row with percent
  0 sends the item's uninitialised `dwRarity`. The Rewrite makes no item and sends 0.
- Divergence: ties of kind and sub-type keep the table's order (a stable sort);
  `std::sort` orders them as libstdc++'s introsort happens to once there are more than 16.

Scenario `the_target_window_lists_what_a_monster_may_drop`: test drop tables give the dog
`drop`, `kill` and `limit` rows (the limit at level 200, above Alpha's 154), a stone 8001 a
`thiefgloves` stone, and shopkeeper 9001 a `thiefgloves` potion. The dog answers the sword
(count 2 held at 1, rarity 20000), then the two potions in table order (3 at 5000, then the
kill row's 4 at 7); the stone answers its one stone; the shopkeeper, Alpha herself and an
unknown VID are unanswered. Passed 8/8; the mutant that skips stones in a single list failed
it. Unit tests `a_count_is_what_create_item_would_hold` and
`the_list_runs_the_groups_in_order_and_sorts_several_without_stones`. Rows:
`cg.game.target_info_load` and `gc.target_info` are `ported`.

Also: `assert_mesh_wire` (`prodomo/tests/parity.rs`) now lets a nearby NPC's chatter
(`is_npc_chatter`) ride after the mesh, as the other wire helpers do. The first suite run
failed `a_set_moves_a_named_characters_race_sex_job_alignment_and_gaya` on such a line from
VID 0x80000bff; it passed 8/8 alone before the change.

## 385. The smith refine (`CG_REFINE`, `GC_REFINE_INFORMATION`)

A refinable item given to a smith opens the refine window (`CHARACTER::RefineInformation`,
`G/char_item.cpp:1865-1968`, reached from `ReceiveItem`'s smith arms, `:9452-9481`), and
`CInputMain::Refine` (`G/input_main.cpp:3316-3391`) runs `DoRefine` (`G/char_item.cpp:
1421-1585`) on the answer.

- `protocol/src/gc_refine.rs` (new): `GcRefineInformation`, the server's 60-byte
  `TPacketGCRefineInformation` under `HEADER_GC_REFINE_INFORMATION` = 119 (0x77,
  `G/packet.h:192`), which the client registers as `_NEW`. The 0x5f `_OLD` byte is only an
  enumerator (`packet.h:179`) and is never sent, so row `gc.refine_information` is `unused`
  (positive control: `HEADER_GC_TARGET_INFO` shows its enumerator and its send site). Golden
  bytes and refusal tests; the 0x77 inventory row is implemented (116 of 134, 18 missing:
  7 fixed-size, 11 dynamic), and the pins in `gc_inventory.rs`, `protocol/tests/cg_wiring.rs`
  and `AGENTS.md` follow.
- `gamedata::refine`: `RefineRecipes::from_dump` reads `refine_proto` from the owner's
  `player.sql` (579 recipes; the first row of an id is kept); the server loads it at boot and
  refuses to start on a dump that does not parse. `gamedata::item_kind` gains `USE_TUNING`.
- `world::character::smith_refine` (new): `refined_item` is `CreateItem` plus
  `CopyAllAttrTo` (`G/item_manager.cpp:1965-2013`): an accessory's sockets are copied;
  otherwise the stones of the first three sockets are packed from socket 0 behind the
  created sockets, and the refine element and attributes are copied. `swap_refined` sends
  the quickslot delete, the clear and, on a success, the new item's set.
  `drop_item::stamp_created_sockets` is now shared with the drop path.
- `prodomo::game_state::smith_refine` (new): the window (`refine_information`, which marks
  the character as refining), and `refine`: the busy line `[LS;1014]` (trade, safebox, shop),
  the cancel (255), the refine time that `IsHack` refuses a warp for (`[LS;437;%d]`,
  `G/char.cpp:8283-8288`), the normal refine, and the money-only arm with
  `deviltower_zone.can_refine` and its hack log for a set of 500 and up; then `DoRefine`'s
  gates in legacy's order (`[LS;1002]`, `[LS;1077]`, `[LS;1003]`, `[LS;991]`, `[LS;67]`,
  `[LS;1035]`), the materials, the draw (10 off for money-only), the swap, and the fee
  (`ChangeGold`'s record with amount 0). The give arms now open the window, and the destroy
  and give steps refuse while it is open. The window closes on every answer and on a
  departure.
- The descriptor takes 0x60 as a belongings step (`refine_an_item`, `GameCommand::Refine`);
  no observer check guards it, as in legacy. A malformed record closes the connection.
- Not ported (hooks): the scroll types 2, 3, 5 and 6 return where `DoRefineWithScroll`
  returns while `m_iRefineAdditionalCell < 0`, since only the unported `CG_ITEM_USE_TO_ITEM`
  sets it; guild smiths (fee, draw and deposit); `IsSecured`; the cube, aura and dragon
  soul refine windows; the refine, item and money logs; the `ApplyAddon` roll, which
  `CopyAttributeTo` overwrites in any case.
- Divergences: a gift from a custom bank cell (290 and up) or another window opens no
  window, where legacy writes the cell into the window's one-byte `pos` and the client's
  refine names a different cell; a refined item that would not fit its cell is refused
  before anything changes, where legacy's `AddToCharacter` overlaps the cells below. Both
  are in `docs/STATUS.md`'s defects list.

Scenario `a_smith_refines_a_sword_for_its_fee`: a smith 20016 beside Alpha (50000 gold).

## 386. An item used on an item (CG_ITEM_USE_TO_ITEM: stones and tuning scrolls)

`CInputMain::ItemToItem` (`G/input_main.cpp:1006-1022`) is routed in the game and dead phases
behind the observer gate (`:3719-3722`), which `is_observer_refused` now names. It runs
`CHARACTER::UseItem`'s gates for the used item (`G/char_item.cpp:7168-7400`): the dead check,
`CanHandleItem` (the sash and changelook windows and an open refine), the job, sex, level,
champion and quest checks of `world::character::use_checks`, shared with `CG_ITEM_USE` through
the new `use_source`. Two `UseItemEx` arms are ported:

- **The stone** (`ITEM_METIN`, `:6965-7034`, `world::character::put_stone`): a pick or rod
  target is silent; a stone of a kind the item already holds answers `[LS;426]`; a body stone
  on an item that is not body armour `[LS;427]`, a weapon stone on a non-weapon `[LS;428]`, any
  other target `[LS;431]`. The first socket whose value is 1 or 2 and at least the stone's grade
  takes the stone's vnum with `[LS;1613]` and the item's update record, and one stone is spent;
  no such socket answers `[LS;431]`. `ENABLE_ADDSTONE_FAILURE` is not defined, so no draw.
- **The tuning scroll** (`USE_TUNING`, `:5959-6013`): the +3 and +4 stone lines, the scroll's
  type from `value0` (set 702 needs the dragon scroll, set 501 refuses the others), both cells in
  the base inventory, then `RefineItem` opens the window of that type with the scroll's cell
  kept (`m_iRefineAdditionalCell`). `CG_REFINE` with types 2, 3, 5 and 6 then runs
  `DoRefineWithScroll` (`:1595-1862`): the scroll must still be the one used and differ from the
  item; the war god's and memo scrolls refuse an item at +4 or more with `[LS;1056]`, the
  yagong scrolls one below level 40 with `[LS;162]`, `IsRefineThroughGuild` aside; the odds are
  the recipe's, the yongsin and yagong tables, 100 for the war god's and memo scrolls and 80
  for the dragon's. A success swaps to the refined item; a failure swaps to the item it was
  refined from (`GetRefineFromVnum`, the first proto in vnum order), or keeps the item when
  there is none or the scroll is a magic iron, whose failure takes legacy's last arm. The
  scroll, the materials and the fee are spent either way. The plan code is shared with the
  smith's (`RefinePlan` gained the fail outcome and the scroll).

The other target arms (the detachment, the attribute and socket scrolls, costumes, talismans,
hair, the sash and changelook cleaners) fall to the plain use, which refuses them as not
ported.

Defect not reproduced: `m_iRefineAdditionalCell` is never initialised and `ClearRefineMode`
does not reset it. The Rewrite starts with no scroll cell, keeps the last one as legacy does,
and forgets it when the character leaves. The window's one-byte `pos` limits the scroll refine
to the base inventory, as in ledger 385.

Scenario `a_stone_and_a_blessing_are_used_on_a_sword`: a stone sits in the sword's empty socket
and a second is refused with `[LS;426]`; the war god's blessing opens the type-5 window on a +6
sword whose refine `[LS;1056]` refuses, and refines the +0 sword at 100 percent, spending the
scroll and the fee and keeping the stone. Eight concurrent runs passed. A mutant dropping the
same-kind check was killed; the file was restored by checksum. Unit tests in
`game_state::use_to_item`: `a_failed_scroll_refine_steps_the_item_back`,
`a_failed_magic_iron_keeps_the_item`, `the_refine_level_is_the_number_after_the_last_plus`.

Inventory: `cg.game.item_use_to_item` and `sys.item.sockets` are `partial` (scenario in the
note), and the `cg.game.refine` and `sys.item.refine` notes name the scroll refine. Counts:
client-packets 73 ported / 10 partial / 23 missing / 5 unused; others unchanged.

## 387. The event board (CG_REQUEST_EVENT_DATA, GC_EVENT_INFO)

Legacy's `event` table (`legacy/sql/schema/player.sql:120-129`) is stored in migration 0023
with a CHECK behind every rule (`EVENT_TYPE_NONE` refused, both times within the first second
after the epoch and 2038-01-19, the 32-bit range `TEventTable` carries). `db::events::load_all`
reads every row in id order (`m_mapEvent`'s order) with `EEventTypes` members from
`BuildEventNameMap`'s order, and `serve` installs them into the world once after migration, as
the guilds are installed: a world opened without its calendar answers every board empty.
`CInputMain::RequestEventData` (`G/input_main.cpp:5466-5475`) is routed in the game and dead
phases with no observer gate (`:3920-3921`), and the world answers with one `GC_EVENT_INFO`
(`CEventManager::SendEventInfo`, `G/event_manager.cpp:613-646`), listing the events that start
in the asked month and the uncompleted ones that start in an earlier month. The month is UTC;
legacy's is `localtime`'s. The codec is `protocol::gc_event`: the 3-byte header with its size
word and one 22-byte `TPacketEventData` per listed event, measured by compiling the verbatim
bodies under `#pragma pack(1)` with `g++ -m32 -fsyntax-only` `static_assert`s (linking fails:
the 32-bit runtime libraries are missing), with a packed two-`long` control of 8; a 30-byte
assertion failed as it should, and the same file under `-m64` failed the entry and the
control.

Defects not reproduced: a calendar past 2978 entries truncates `wSize`, so the Rewrite refuses
one that does not fit; the year is never compared, so a same-month event of another year is
listed and a December one is never a "previous month" in January, and the Rewrite lists the
same months, both recorded in STATUS.

Scenario `the_event_board_lists_its_month_and_the_earlier_open_ones`: three stored rows, then
March's board (its own OX row and the earlier open fishing row, in id order with every field),
February's (its own two), and January's empty record. The first boot migrates, the rows are
seeded, and the reboot installs the calendar, as the guild's reboot scenario does. Eight
concurrent runs passed. A mutant dropping the earlier-month arm was killed; the file was
restored by checksum. Unit tests: the month filter and the UTC month boundary in
`game_state::event_calendar`, the id order and the refused rows in `db/tests/events.rs`, the
type names in `db::events`, and the golden bytes and the too-long calendar in
`protocol::gc_event`. The third settled pick arm pushed `apply_pick` past Clippy's line limit,
so the three settled arms now share `apply_settled_pick`.

`sys.event.manager` is `partial` (scenario in the note). Counts: client-packets 74 ported /

## 388. The melt's stone pick and the quest confirm (CG_SCRIPT_SELECT_ITEM, CG_QUEST_CONFIRM, GC_QUEST_CONFIRM)

A script's `select_item` and `confirm` now wait for the client. `CG_SCRIPT_SELECT_ITEM`
resumes a script suspended in `select_item` with the picked cell (`CQuestManager::SelectItem`,
`G/questmanager.cpp:179-194`); with none waiting it answers nothing. `CG_QUEST_CONFIRM`
(`CInputMain::QuestConfirm`, `G/input_main.cpp:2236-2248`) folds any nonzero answer to
`CONFIRM_YES`, and the world finds the waiter by its PID itself, which retires the
`PidOnline` round trip. `Manager::confirm` runs the answer as the waiter's own event, as
legacy's `GetPC(waiter)` does: only the asked character is heard, `[END_CONFIRM_WAIT]`
(`QUEST_SKIN_NOWINDOW`) ends the wait, and the script resumes with the answer. The asked
character's `GC_QUEST_CONFIRM` (74 bytes, `ConfirmWithMsg`, `G/char.cpp:8076-8088`) goes to
its client, or straight into the step's records when a script asks its own character.
`confirm_timeout_event` answers `CONFIRM_TIMEOUT` (2) after `timeout` seconds of Pulses.

The guild alchemists' melts run over the wire. `pc.ore_refine` and `pc.diamond_refine` spend
in `OreRefine`'s order (`G/mining.cpp:421-464`): the 100 ore, then the fee's
`GC_CHARACTER_GOLD_CHANGE`, which `pc.change_money` now sends when it is called, as
`ChangeGold` does, then the stone, then the draw. The quest item bridge gains `item.get_id`,
`item.get_cell`, `item.select` and `item.select_cell`.

Divergence: `item.select` finds only an item the character holds; legacy's
`ITEM_MANAGER::Find` takes any item of the server by id. Defects not reproduced, recorded in
STATUS: legacy never cancels `confirm_timeout_event`, so a stale timer answers a later confirm
early, and the Rewrite disarms the timer when an answer is heard (a new confirm replaces it);
`OreRefine` takes the ore before it checks the gold, and the Rewrite checks the gold first.

Two fixes outside the slice. `quest::sources::scripts` walked only real folders
(`DirEntry::file_type` does not follow links), so a linked quest folder was skipped; it now
follows links (`a_linked_folder_holds_scripts_like_a_real_one`). The harness's `link_all_but`
wrote a scenario's file through a folder an earlier file had linked, into `legacy/`; it now
replaces such a link with a made folder and accepts a folder the owner's data lacks. The
stray probe file this left in `legacy/gamedata/locale/europe/quest/` during one run was
removed, and `git status legacy/` is clean. The `pc.destroy_guild` and `pc.remove_from_guild`
bridge arms were missing from `pc_api` (`the_guild_manage_names_answer` and
`the_guild_man_parts_and_disbands` failed); they are restored. `host::BRIDGED` now lists the
two refine names in the order of the API table.

Scenarios. `an_ore_melt_asks_for_a_stone_and_melts_with_the_one_picked` (amber alchemist 20061):
a pick with nothing waiting is silent; the question page with the 2700 that
`GetOreRefineCost` shows, then `[SELECT_ITEM]`; the closed window's 0 and a pick that is not a
stone are each told so and spend nothing; the stone's pick clears the ore cell, sends the
3000 fee, clears the stone cell and then shows the win (the refined amber in the freed cell)
or the loss. `a_confirm_asks_another_character_and_hears_its_answer_or_the_timeout` adds a
probe quest on 20025, a talking NPC that no owner quest or shop names, because no owner quest
calls `confirm`. Zulu's 7 is heard as 1 and no timeout follows 2.5 s later; Alpha cannot answer
for Zulu; Zulu's no is heard as 0; unanswered, the timeout answers 2 after at least 1.9 s, and a
late answer is silent. The diamond scenarios now pass the race to `melt_refiner`. Eight runs
of both new scenarios passed. Four mutants were applied to pristine files and restored by
checksum, and all four were semantic kills: dropping `end_confirm_wait`, passing no replier,
passing the answer byte unfolded, and shifting the selection by one. Disarming on a heard
answer is an equivalent mutant at the wire, because a new confirm replaces the arm and a
stale arm meets no waiting script.

Inventory: `cg.game.script_select_item`, `cg.game.quest_confirm`, `gc.quest_confirm`,
`event.questlua.confirm_timeout_event`, `lua.item.get_id`, `lua.item.select`,
`lua.item.select_cell`, `lua.pc.ore_refine` and `lua.pc.diamond_refine` are `ported`.
`lua.item.get_cell` is `partial` (unit test only). `quest.guild_building_melt` stays `partial`:
the master's rebuild click waits on `building.reconstruct` and `npc.get_guild`. Counts:
client-packets 76 ported / 10 partial / 20 missing / 5 unused; server-records 77 ported / 15
missing / 3 partial / 38 codec / 1 unused; quest-api 108 ported / 83 partial / 508 missing;
timed-events 11 ported / 4 partial / 84 missing.

- `gamedata::item_kind::USE_BAIT` (6). `world::character::bait` holds `use_bait`: the use
  checks, socket 2 of the rod in the weapon cell set to the bait's value 0, and one bait spent.
  The line is `[LS;418]` while fishing (and nothing changes), `[LS;419]` with the name when the
  rod already had bait, and `[LS;420]` when it had none; without a rod nothing happens.
  `GameState::use_item` routes a bait there before the generic step, because the line needs the
  fishing state.
- `prodomo::game_state::fishing`: `fish` sets the rotation to `dir * 5`, then casts or takes.
  The cast refuses a blocked cell `[LS;1051]`, no rod `[LS;817]` and an empty bait socket
  `[LS;818]`, else sends `START` around and arms the event `number(10, 40)` seconds of Pulses
  ahead. The event's first firing is the bite: it draws the fish (`DetermineFish` with the
  `manwoo_event`/`fish_miss_pct` flags and the never-fished vnums) and sends `REACT` around, and
  `FISH` to a fisher with the fish mind affect or a unique item of group 10009. Six seconds later
  the fish gets away: `FAIL` around and the rod's bait emptied. A take before the bite sends
  `STOP`; after it, `Compute` on the milliseconds since the bite lands the fish (`SUCCESS`
  around, the fish event boxes, `FISH`, and the fish with its length in socket 0) or misses
  (`FAIL`); then the rod trains on a 1 in 5 and its bait is spent. `fish_simul` shares
  `compute`. A disconnect or a Warp ends the event. The descriptor decodes `CG_FISHING`, closes
  on a malformed record, and stores the answered rows.
- Not ported: the multi-farm gate (`sys.custom.multi_farm`; every character fishes), the
  `fishevent` highscore (`lua.highscore.register`), the premium fish mind and `FishLog`.
- Defects not reproduced (`docs/STATUS.md`): the uninitialised `dir` of every sub-header but
  `START` is sent as 0; the unchecked sectree in the block check; `lower_bound` past the end in
  `DetermineFish` reads as the empty catch.

Scenarios: `a_rod_takes_its_bait_and_a_cast_taken_before_the_bite_stops`,
`a_bite_left_on_the_line_gets_away_and_a_take_after_one_lands_or_misses` (the second take
waits 3 s after the bite so both the catch and the miss are reached; eight runs reached each
four times) and `a_cast_on_a_block_or_without_a_rod_is_refused`. Eight runs of each passed. Four
mutants were applied to pristine files and restored by checksum, and all four were semantic

lines swapped.

  names).

## 392. The horse's state

The horse without a summon: `CHorseRider`'s level, health, stamina and drop time
(`G/horse_rider.cpp`), `CHARACTER::SetHorseLevel` (`G/char_horse.cpp:396-400`), `EnterHorse`
and the `__FIX_NIVEL_CAL__` refresh in `CInputLogin::Entergame` (`G/input_login.cpp:647-650`,
`:887-897`), the stamina regeneration event (`G/horse_rider.cpp:254-283`), the GM lines
`/horse_state`, `/horse_level` and `/horse_set_stat` (`G/cmd_gm.cpp:3745-3833`), and the quest
names that need no summoned horse (`G/questlua_horse.cpp`, `G/questlua_pc.cpp:1491-1525`).

- `world::character::horse`: `Horse` holds `HorseInfo` and the full `c_aHorseStat` table
  (`HORSE_STATS`, 31 rows). `set_level` clamps to 0..30, refills both pools and moves the drop
  time three days on; `enter` starts the regeneration of a living horse and takes the drops that
  came due; `catch_up_logoff` is `UpdateHorseDataByLogoff`; `feed`, `revive`, `set_stat`, the
  riding pair and the two event steps follow legacy, a health of 0 killing the horse and
  emptying its stamina. The horse records which event runs and whether it was created afresh;
  the world owns the schedule. `send_info` queues `horse_state %d %d %d` only while summoned or
  ridden, and only on a change, so no line goes out yet. `Points` carries the horse.
- Store: migration `0024_player_horse.sql` adds `horse_level` (CHECK 0..30), `horse_riding`,
  `horse_hp`, `horse_hp_droptime` (CHECK 0..4294967295), `horse_stamina`, `horse_skill_point`
  and `last_play_at` to `player`. `PlayerSave` writes the horse and stamps `last_play_at`; the
  load answers the horse and the seconds since that stamp (0 for a NULL stamp, which is
  unobservable: the horse is level 0 or refilled at entry).
- `prodomo::game_state::horse`: `enter_horse` runs after the enter-game burst and before the
  quest login: `EnterHorse`, then, for a level above 0, `SetHorseLevel(GetHorseLevel())` with
  byte 76. The refresh plants skill 130 in memory only; every login plants it again from the
  stored level (owner question 35 asks whether the refill is a Quirk). A row stored while ridden
  enters unridden until the riding slice. `horse_timers` holds each horse's due Pulse
  (period × 25), runs on `run_horse_timers` and is dropped on leave. `/horse_level` tells the
  caller, then plants the level on the named character with `ComputePoints` and byte 76, and the
  descriptor stores the planted skill through the shared `store_other_skill` (also used by
  `/setskillother`). `/all_skill_master` now runs `SetHorseLevel(40)` first, so the horse stands
  at 30.
- `quest`: the `Game` trait gains `horse()` (a `HorseView`), `set_horse_level` and
  `feed_horse`; the new `horse_api` family bridges `horse.is_riding`, `advance`, `get_level`,
  `set_level` (a number only, `(int)` then clamped), `get_health`, `get_health_pct`,
  `get_stamina`, `get_stamina_pct` (0 without a horse, `MINMAX(0, x * 100 / max, 100)`),
  `get_grade`, `is_dead`, `feed`, `pc.get_horse_level` and `pc.is_horse_alive` (`BRIDGED` is
  203 names, in the inventory's order). The session's `set_horse_level` lands the skill as a
  climb, so the store keeps it.

Scenario: `a_horse_levels_feeds_and_dies_by_gm_lines_and_quests` (the usage and missing-name
lines; `/horse_level Alpha 25` with one byte 76 at 25; `/horse_set_stat 10 30` read as 25% and
21%; a probe quest's readers, a feed, an advance to 26 that refills, a word that sets nothing
and 99 clamped to 30; `/horse_set_stat 0 5` kills the horse before the 5 lands; the dead horse

`a_master_line_plants_every_usable_skill` now reads the horse at 30. Eight runs passed. Three

## 393. The summoned horse

The horse leaves the character's sheet and stands in the world: `CHARACTER::HorseSummon`
(`G/char_horse.cpp:122-260`), `StateHorse` (`G/char_state.cpp`), `horse_dead_event`
(`G/char_horse.cpp:111`), `ReviveHorse` (`G/horse_rider.cpp`) and the horse arm of
`CanReceiveItem`/`ReceiveItem` (`G/char_item.cpp:9483-9520`).

- `world`: `HorseRider` keeps the summoned horse's VID; `summon` speaks the state, `unsummon`
  hides it from a rider not riding, a death is taken once by the world, and the lines the rider
  hears are `HorseLine::State` or `HorseLine::Hide`. `GiveUnported::Horse` is gone: the herb and
  the feed reach the horse arm.
- `prodomo`: the new `game_state::horse_summon` module.
  - The summon: a horse of level 1 or more, none summoned, no mount ridden and not on the OX
    map, stands 2000 to 2500 away on each axis with a random sign (the draws left to right,
    `[INFERENCE]`: C++ leaves the operand order open), or within 100 when called near or dead;
    its race is the level's horse plus the guild and master steps, it faces its rider's
    rotation plus 180, and it is named `<rider>'s `. A dead horse lies with `GC_DEAD` and
    `horse_dead_event` sends it back 60 seconds later. A failed spawn says `[LS;887]`.
  - The unsummon: a dead horse, or one not sent off from far, is destroyed at once; a living one
    runs 3500 straight away from its rider and goes at its next Idle (`StateHorse` with no rider).
  - `StateHorse` every 12 Pulses: no rider destroys; at 400 or more it follows, running past 700;
    otherwise it wanders 200 to 400 every 5 to 12 seconds, unless `no_wander` holds (the test
    switch; its doc now says so).
  - `/horse_summon`, `/horse_unsummon` and `/user_horse_back` (`[LS;501]`, `[LS;502]`,
    `[LS;504]`); the horse's death unsummons it; leaving the world unsummons it; a purge spares a
    horse with a rider; a destroyed horse forgets its rider and its dead event.
  - The gift: a herb of the horse's grade revives the giver's horse, spends one and says
    `[LS;452]`; feed of the grade feeds it, spends one, says `[LS;453]` and shows `SE_HPUP_RED` on
    the horse; a dead horse refuses feed. `IsDead()` now reads the NPC's dead flag, not its hit
    points. Owner question 36 asks whether a herb spent on another rider's horse is a Quirk.
- `quest`: the `Game` trait gains `summon_horse`, `unsummon_horse` and `revive_horse`;
  `HorseView` gains `summoned`. `horse.is_summon`, `horse.is_mine`, `horse.summon`,
  `horse.unsummon`, `horse.revive` and `pc.revive_horse` are bridged (`BRIDGED` is 209 names). The
  summon, unsummon and revive are queued as `HorseOp`s and run in the world after the step, since
  the horse belongs to the world, so `horse.is_summon` read in the same step sees the horse as it
  was.
- Two unit tests were rewritten for `StateHorse`: `each_kind_of_npc_waits_its_own_idle_time` now
  reads a horse with no rider gone at its first Idle, and `only_a_monster_is_hit` refuses a hit
  on a horse that has its rider. Two test session builders were tightened by one line each to
  stay under Clippy's `too_many_lines`.

  `set_mount_vnum` takes the state the caller saw. The recompute floored each attribute below

  at twice strength (`G/char.cpp:3067-3071`, jobs and guild war read through the existing

  of the bare stats (`G/char.cpp:3123-3130`) are the recompute's own records. `recompute`'s
  pool clamp is now `clamp_pools`, so both Clippy's `too_many_lines` and the unit test's mount
  floor case fit. A costume mount applies no floor and no bonus (`G/char.cpp:3026`,
  `G/MountSystem.cpp`).

  or more, a level 2 rider carrying no normal mount, alive, still, unmounted, outside the guild
  war and untouched by polymorph (`IsRiding` in the same file), unsummons its horse from near,
  and rides: the mount shows in the re-show's `dwMountVnum` and the look update, and the
  compute's records carry the changes. `StopRiding` dismounts (the member and `GetMountVnum`
  disagree past the end, legacy's shape), recomputes with the old floor, sends the four zero
  changes, and summons the horse back near with the old VNUM. Death, damage-polymorph and the
  stamina finish stop the ride; enter-game remounts the saved rider that still looks mounted.
  `/horse_ride`, `/user_horse_ride` (with the state line's flush) and the death and polymorph
  arms say `horse_state`; the consume event's own stamina half is unchanged.
- `quest`: `horse.ride` and `horse.unride` call the rider's start and stop through the move
  queue with `is_mine`-style truth; `horse.is_riding` and `pc.is_mount` answer the VNUM
  (`BRIDGED` is 211 names).

  `lua.horse.is_riding`, `lua.pc.is_mount` and `event.horse_rider.horse_stamina_consume_event`

## 395. The horse's names

`horse.set_name` and `horse.get_name` are ported (`G/questlua_horse.cpp:231-283`), with the
name manager (`CHorseNameManager`, `G/horsename_manager.cpp`) as the world's
`horse_names` map keyed on the player id.

- `set_name` answers 0 without a horse and 1 for a name the europe rules refuse: two to 24
  bytes, ASCII letters and digits, and the banword and mob-name judge the guild name uses.
  Otherwise it answers 2 and queues `HorseOp::SetName`, which the world runs after the step.
  The world sets the `horse_name.valid_till` flag a month on (five minutes on a test server),
  adds `AFFECT_HORSE_NAME` (531) with the Pulse count legacy passes as its duration, and
  rewrites the name. It then syncs the named flag and runs the compute. The unsummon and the
  far summon back follow, and the summon back never computes, so only this compute prices
  the name. A number argument pushes nothing, as `lua_isstring` fails it.
- `get_name` pushes the manager's name, empty with none.
- The summoned horse carries the manager's name when it is not empty, otherwise
  `"<rider>'s "` (`G/char_horse.cpp:206-216`).
- `ComputeBattlePoints` floors the rider's armour to the horse row's `iArmor` and adds 20
  for a named horse before the grade bonuses (`G/char.cpp:2822-2838`). `Horse::named` is
  the manager's answer, which the world sets before each compute. The item-shop defence
  bonus still scales the sum. A draft of this slice dropped that term, which the
  `points` unit test `the_armour_and_the_item_shop_defence_bonus_raise_every_defence`
  caught in the full suite, and the term is back in place.
- `Validate` (`G/horsename_manager.cpp:58-75`) runs on each affect tick, ahead of the
  countdown. While the flag is current, the affect lives one tick more. Once the flag is
  stale, it removes the affect, empties the name, and unsummons and re-summons the horse.
- The store keeps the name in `player.horse_name`, a `bytea` of at most 24 bytes, empty for
  none (migration `0025_player_horse_name.sql`; legacy keeps the `horse_name` table). It is
  read at load and written on every save from the manager.
- Refactor: `Horse`'s one-shot reports (died, stopped, new timer) moved into
  `HorseReports`, to keep the struct under Clippy's bool limit.

Scenario `a_horse_is_named_bad_names_refused_and_the_mount_pays`:
- The naming answers 2, the month's add (300 seconds as Pulses on the test server) leads 12
  point changes, and the defence grade carries the 54 floor plus 20.
- The ride's stop summons the horse back as `Shadowfax`.
- A bad name and a one-letter name answer 1, and a number answers nil, each with the name
  kept.
- Once the probe stales the flag with `pc.setf`, the next tick removes affect 531 and
  summons the horse back as `Alpha's `, and the store ends with an empty name.

Eight runs passed. Five mutants were applied to pristine files and restored by checksum; all
five are semantic kills: the 20 bonus to 0, the inverted `Validate` comparison, the dropped
emptying, the inverted summon-name filter, and the naming without the manager rewrite. The
inverted comparison at first survived, because the scenario never staled the flag. The stale
step was added for it, and the mutant now fails.

## 396. The rider's feed line

`/user_horse_feed` is ported (`do_user_horse_feed`, `G/cmd_general.cpp:105-133`) as the
player line `GmLine::UserHorseFeed`, run by `GameState::user_horse_feed`
(`prodomo/src/game_state/horse_summon.rs`). Its answer carries the item rows, which the
descriptor stores, as `/sort_inventory`'s does.

- With no horse summoned (`GetHorse() == NULL`), the caller hears `[LS;501]`, or
  `[LS;505]` while riding, since the ride unsummons the horse.
- With a horse summoned, the food is `50054 + grade - 1`, which is 50056 at grade 3. If the
  caller holds none (`CountSpecifyItem`), it hears `[LS;507;%s]` with the proto's locale
  name.
- Otherwise `RemoveSpecifyItem(food, 1)` takes one and its records go out first.
  `FeedHorse` runs next: a living horse gains a point of health and its drop time moves on,
  while a dead horse eats nothing although the food is spent, as legacy does. The horse
  then settles, so a crossed grade sends its state line, and the caller hears
  `[LS;506;%s;%s]` with the name and an empty second argument.
- The private-shop gate (`GetMyShop`) is not ported (`sort_inventory.rs` records the same
  gap), so it never refuses.

Scenario `a_summoned_horse_is_fed_by_its_rider_until_the_food_runs_out`:
- Without a horse the line hears `[LS;501]`.
- At level 25 the far summon stands the horse, and `/horse_set_stat 20 140` says
  `horse_state 25 2 3`.
- Two lines eat the stack of two 50056: first the stack's update to 1, then its clearing
  set, each followed by `[LS;506;Ginseng rosu;]`. The health stays in grade 2, so no state
  line goes.
- The third line hears `[LS;507;Ginseng rosu]`.
- `/user_horse_ride` deletes the standing horse, and the line then hears `[LS;505]`.
- The store ends without item 61 and with `horse_hp` 22.

Eight runs passed. Four mutants were applied to the pristine file and restored by
checksum; all four are semantic kills: the 501 and 505 swap, the food without its `- 1`,
the dropped `FeedHorse`, and the count gate at `< 0`.

- `is_horse_riding` is `IsHorseRiding`.
- `can_use_horse_skill` is `CanUseHorseSkill`, which reduces to riding on a grade-3 horse.

The sites that read them:
- **Emotions** (`emotion.rs` `run_emotion`, `G/cmd_emotion.cpp:158-216`): a rider hears
  `[LS;1043]` before any other gate. A victim who rides gives `[LS;1044]`, checked after the
  player and self checks.

  still send the emotion with victim 0. It now returns, as legacy's `return` at `:200-207`
  does.

  `false`.

## 399. `RefreshAffect` and the quest mount

`CHARACTER::RefreshAffect` (`G/char_affect.cpp:769-778`) now ends `ComputePoints`, as at
`G/char.cpp:3150`: after the pool clamp and before the `@fixme118` restore, every held affect's
point is laid again. Before this, a recomputation (an equip, a level, a ride) dropped every
buff's point until the buff ended, which then took back a value it no longer held.

- `Points` (`world/src/character/points.rs`) keeps `affect_points`, the `(apply_on, value)` of
  each held affect, through `affect_point_added` (point 0 is skipped) and `affect_point_removed`
  (the first equal entry goes). `recompute` runs the list through `nested`.
- `GameState::compute_affect` (`prodomo/src/game_state/affect.rs`) is `ComputeAffect`: it updates
  the list, then changes the point. The twelve `change_pc_point(±affect.value)` sites in
  `alignment.rs`, `dragon_soul.rs`, `guild.rs`, `horse_summon.rs`, `death.rs`, `affect.rs` and
  `pc_skill.rs` call it. The quest host's `take_affect` removes the entry before its own point
  change.
- `POINT_MOUNT` (109) moves from `NOT_PORTED` to `PLAIN`. `change_pc_point` runs its arm
  (`G/char.cpp:4711-4715`): after the records it calls `mount_vnum` with the new total.
- A login's restore (`GameState::load_affects`, split out of the admission) pushes each restored
  row into the list without applying its point, so the point lands at the next computation. A
  saved `AFFECT_MOUNT` or `AFFECT_MOUNT_BONUS` row (the mount is saved: `IS_NO_SAVE_AFFECT` names
  neither) sends its add in load order and its remove after every add, the mounts' first, and is
  not restored (`ENABLE_MOUNT_COSTUME_SYSTEM`'s `RemoveAffect` pair, `G/char_affect.cpp:644-645`).
  The skipped load-time `ComputeAffect` and the mount's two re-shows are a recorded Divergence.

The quest mount is ported (`quest/src/manager.rs` `mount_api`, three new `BRIDGED` names, now
217; three `HorseOp` variants run in `horse_ride.rs`):
- `pc.mount(vnum, seconds)` (`G/questlua_pc.cpp:1392-1458`): nothing without a number first;
  the seconds default to 60 and a negative one is 60. The mount and its bonus go, and a summoned
  horse goes (`HorseSummon(false)`). Then `AFFECT_MOUNT` lays `POINT_MOUNT` for the vnum. The
  eighteen mount races of the three bands add 30, 40 or 50 movement speed as a second
  `AFFECT_MOUNT` row. That row is added with `IsCube`, so `add_pc_affect_keyed` finds the row it
  overrides by kind **and** point (`FindAffect(dwType, bApplyOn)`). `g_NoMountAtGuildWar`'s arm
  never runs: no war map is hosted.
- `pc.mount_bonus(apply, value, seconds)` (`:1461-1479`): with a mount only,
  `AFFECT_MOUNT_BONUS` (532, new in `loading_phase`) replaces the old one on
  `aApplyInfo[apply].bPointType` (`world::character::point_type`). An apply type at or above
  130 reads past the table in legacy (`:1475`), a Defect; the Rewrite refuses it.
- `pc.unmount` (`:1481-1489`) and `/unmount` (`G/cmd_general.cpp:2313-2368`): the mount and its
  bonus go and a horse ride stops. `/unmount`'s costume arm and `UnEquipSpecialRideUniqueItem`
  never act: every mount costume in the owner's data carries the first-use timer the item use
  refuses, so none is ever worn.

Scenario `a_quest_mounts_and_unmounts_and_a_login_takes_the_mount_off`:
- The quest mounts: its three adds are `(221, 109, 20201)`, `(221, 19, 30)` and `(532, 19, 10)`;
  the re-show carries 20201; the speed ends at 140 (100, the band's 30, the bonus's 10). The band's
  30 thus survives the mount's own recomputation.
- `pc.unmount` and `/unmount` each send the three removes, the mounts' first, and re-show the
  character unmounted.
- `/unmount` on a horse rider stops the ride and moves no affect.
- After a logout with the mount on, the three rows are saved. The next login's burst sends
  their adds and then their removes in `RemoveAffect` order, and the character is not mounted.

Unit tests:
- `a_computation_puts_the_held_affects_back` (world): a speed and a mount point survive
  `compute_points`, a point-0 row adds nothing, and a removed row does not come back.
- `the_mount_names_read_their_arguments` (quest): the non-number first argument, the numeric
  string, the default and negative seconds, the `DWORD` vnum and the apply byte's low 8 bits.

Ten mutants were applied to the pristine files and restored by checksum. All ten are semantic
kills:
- the refresh loop dropped;
- `affect_point_removed` and `affect_point_added` made no-ops;
- the `IsCube` key ignored;
- the bonus's mount gate flipped;
- the first band at 40;
- the `POINT_MOUNT` arm dropped;
- the load's mount arm made dead;
- `/unmount` keeping the bonus;
- `/unmount` keeping the ride. This one first survived and was killed once the horse-ride leg
  was added.

The load arm's first spelling was a compile-error mutant and is not counted. Dropping the quest
host's `affect_point_removed` is equivalent for the owner's data: the two kinds that path takes,
the book rows 512 and 513, carry no point, and no owner quest calls `affect.add*`. The scenario
passed 8 of 8 parallel runs.

## 400. The `/ride` toggle

`ACMD(do_ride)` (`G/cmd_general.cpp:3516-3642`) is ported as `GameState::run_ride_line`
(`prodomo/src/game_state/horse_ride.rs`). Its arms are in `ride_toggle`:
- the dead and the stunned (`is_down`) and the OX map (113) are silent;
- a morph hears "Nu poti folosi un mount atat timp cat esti transformat.";
- a horse rider stops riding;
- a mount rider dismounts through `do_unmount` (ledger 399's `unmount`);
- with a summoned horse the caller rides.

Otherwise the first inventory cell (0 to 179, in order) holding one of the following runs
through `UseItem`:
- a ride item (`CItem::IsRideItem`, now `pub` as `world::character::is_ride_item`);
- one of the quest seals 71114, 71116, 71118 and 71120;
- a mount seal 52001-52090.

With none, `[LS;501]` answers. The mount-costume arm and the ride item's three-cell condition
never act: every mount costume in the owner's data (52001-52090 and 71118 among them) carries
the first-use timer the item use refuses, so none is ever worn.

The line runs `/use_item`'s path: `Command::Ride` → `ride_line_step` (`main.rs`) →
`GameCommand::RideLine` → the kit-line dispatch. Its answer lands through `finish_use_line`,
split out of `use_item_line_step`, so a seal's quest climbs and guild stores are stored as a
used item's are. `GameState::nothing_used`, split out of `run_use_item_line`, answers the
empty step.

Scenario `ride_uses_a_seal_dismounts_and_toggles_the_horse`. A probe quest says `seal`, takes
71114 and mounts 20201 on its use, and says `late` and takes 71116 on that one's use. The
store seeds 71114 in cell 7 and 71116 in cell 20.
- A morph's `/ride` hears the refusal and uses nothing.
- `/ride` uses 71114 first: `seal`, then the mount's two adds and its re-show.
- `/ride` dismounts: the two removes and the unmounted re-show.
- `/ride` uses 71116: `late`.
- With nothing left, `/ride` answers `[LS;501]`.
- With a level-25 horse summoned, `/ride` rides (the re-show carries 20107) and the next
  `/ride` stops (the re-show unmounts).

Unit test `the_down_and_the_ox_map_ride_nothing`: the same caller hears `[LS;501]` standing,
and nothing while dead or on map 113.

Nine mutants were applied to the pristine files and restored by checksum.
- Eight are semantic kills: the morph arm dead, the mount arm dropped, the summoned arm dropped,
  the seal vnum, the `[LS;501]` line dropped, the scan order reversed, the down gate dropped,
  and the OX map at 114. The scan order first survived and was killed once the second seal
  was added.

## 401. The uncalled quest API

The owner chose, when asked on 2026-11-05, to mark the quest-api names no Lua file calls as
`unused` with evidence rather than port them. A client reaches a quest function only through a
script, so a name no script or library references is never reached. 366 of the 477 `missing`
quest-api rows are now `unused`, each with the same note. Owner question 37 lists them for
confirmation, grouped by namespace: `pc` 108, `d` 58, globals 38, `item` 25, `npc` 23, and so
on. A name a future quest needs is ported then.

What was swept: every file under `legacy/gamedata/locale/europe/quest` (scripts, libraries,
`object/` state files, `locale.lua`), except `quest_functions` (the `qc` name list), plus every
`locale/europe/*.lua`. That is 164 files and 1.6 MB, read as Latin-1 bytes. It includes files
legacy never loads (`questing.lua`, `questlib_extra.lua`, `BlueDragon.lua`,
`monkey_dungeon.lua`), so the sweep errs toward keeping a name. One tokenizer pass counts every
identifier as `ns.fn` (with optional spaces), `ns["fn"]` or `ns['fn']`, and a bare `fn` for
globals. So a call, a string or table call (`f "x"`, `f{}`), an assignment and a mention in a
string or comment all count as a reference.

Controls:
- Positive: `pc.setqf` 27, `pc.getqf` 40, `say` 896, `pc.get_level` 14, `d.setf` 5.
- Negative: the fabricated `pc.zz_never_defined` and `zz_never_global` count 0.
- `quest_functions` exclusion: `pc.unmount` appears in `quest_functions` and counts 0 elsewhere.

Indirect reaches checked:
- The `pc`, `npc` and `item` `__index` metatables (`questlib.lua:503-532`) resolve properties
  through `pc_index_table`, `npc_index_table` and `item_index_table`. Those tables name their
  getters literally (`pc.get_level`, `npc.getrace`, `item.get_vnum`, ...), so the tokenizer sees
  them.
- `rawget` there falls back to the raw table.
- `loadstring` occurs only in `questing.lua`, which legacy never loads.
- `_G[...]` in `dungeonInformationLibrary.lua:39` writes a global and calls nothing.
- No file aliases a namespace table: every bare `d`, `item`, `target`, `guild` or `q` is a local
  of the same spelling or a parameter.
- The C++ loads into the quest state are `settings.lua`, `questlib.lua` (with its `dofile`
  chain), `translate.lua`, `quest/locale.lua`, `object/state/*` and `oxquiz.lua`
  (`G/questlua.cpp:736-812`, `G/event_manager.cpp:1497`, `G/questlua_oxevent.cpp:70-74`). All
  of them are in the sweep.
- The one GM path that loads a Lua buffer, `do_priv_guild`'s `ADMIN_QUEST`
  (`G/cmd_gm.cpp:3191-3197`), formats the one-byte empty `msg`, so it runs nothing.

25 `partial` rows are also unreferenced (`setleftimage`, `getnpcid`, `pc.get_wear`, and others).
They stay `partial`: the owner's choice covered the `missing` rows.

Inventory: quest-api 139 ported, 82 partial, 111 missing, 367 unused (366 new, plus
`horse.set_stat0`). No code changed.

## 402. The global rank

`napierdalator`'s kill scores, the board mails, the season ends, and the prize claims.

What legacy does. Nine counters per player live in `stRankGlobal_player.count[9]`
(`C/tables.h:1855-1867`); the game's `rank_vec` is the snapshot the DB process mailed,
sorted per counter descending (`SortVec`, `G/RankGlobal.cpp:36-42`, `:147-175`). The
login ends with `RankGlobal_send_players` and `RankGlobal_send_items`
(`G/input_login.cpp:946-949`): the two `clear` lines, `GlobalRankData ref_season|<flag>`
off the `RankGlobalSeason` event flag, `GlobalRankData <type>|<name>|<count>|<lv>|<empire>`
for each counter's first ten places, `GlobalRankMyChar <type>|<name>|<pos>|...` for the
reader's own place (`:38-73`), then `GlobalRankDataItem` `clear_items` and one line per
prize (`:75-88`). `/open_global_rank` resends the board; `/rank_end_season` bumps the flag
and mails `HEADER_DG_RANKGLOBAL_LOAD_STATE` with `option = 1`
(`G/cmd_general.cpp:4118-4134`, `G/RankGlobal.cpp:90-104`), which the DB answers by
sorting, writing the winners for the listed (type, pos) prizes, and truncating
`rank_global` (`D/ClientManager.cpp:5382-5455`, `RankGlobal_state` `:5457-5471`). The DB
reads `rank_global` and `rank_global_reward` at boot (`:5249-5304`), takes
`HEADER_DG_RANKGLOBAL_ADD_POINT` per add (`:5473-5509`), and saves the counters every
`RANKGLOBAL_DB_SAVE_TIME` (`:5341-5380`). The chat quest
(`rank/rank_global_reward.lua`) claims by `pc.global_rank_get_reward`
(`G/questlua_pc.cpp:3680-3721`): each unclaimed prize is `AutoGiveItem`'d, then every
unclaimed row of the pid is marked `done`, and the answer is 1 if anything was won, 0
otherwise. `pc.global_rank_add_point` needs both arguments numbers and takes the counter
as `(BYTE)` (`G/questlua_pc.cpp:3723-3736`); a counter past the ninth is refused, game-side
(`G/RankGlobal.cpp:106-128`) and DB-side, with the same `sys_err`. The kill script
(`rank/rank_global.lua`, quest `napierdalator`) scores metin 0, dungeon boss 4, other
boss 1, plain monster 2, and PC 3 off `npc.is_metin`, `npc.is_boss`, `npc.is_pc`
(`G/questlua_npc.cpp:32-41`, `:400-428`, with `GetMobRank() >= MOB_RANK_BOSS` and the
PC default `MOB_RANK_KNIGHT`, `G/char.cpp:2640-2646`) and `pc.in_dungeon`
(`G/questlua_pc.cpp:318-323`). The killer's `kill` scripts run from `Reward`
(`G/char_battle.cpp:810-811`), the victim staged by `SetQuestNPCID`.

What the Rewrite ports. One migration, `0026_rank_global.sql`: `rank_global` (the pid, the generation, Name,
level, empire, nine counters), `rank_global_reward` (the Operator's prizes by counter and
place), `rank_global_winner` (each award with its `done`), and `rank_global_state` (the
season and the guard generation a season's end raises, so a save taken before it cannot
put an old row back after). `db/src/rank_global.rs` loads the boot, saves a row under its
generation, ends a season in one transaction, and claims with the items the claim gave.
`prodomo/src/game_state/rank_global.rs` holds the counters and the snapshot: the board is
installed before any client is accepted (a recorded Divergence — legacy's first snapshot
came 20 s after boot off the retired DB peer), a kill counts at once and shows at the
next 20-minute refresh, `rank_login` mails the board and the prizes at the end of
`Entergame`, and the season's end awards each counter's first ten listed places, empties
the counters and the snapshot, and raises the generation. The scenario
`a_kill_scores_the_killer_and_the_season_awards_and_empties` covers it end to end: Alpha
punches the dog dead, the logout writes `counts[3] = 1`, a reboot shows the board and the
prize lines, `/open_global_rank` lists them, `/rank_end_season` writes the winner and
empties the counters, and 20016's chat claims the Sword+9 once (`[LS;444;Sabie+9]`, the
item set, `done`), with a second visit hearing "there is no reward for you".

The quest side. Five names leave `missing` through `rank_api` in `quest/src/manager.rs`: `npc.is_pc`,
which answers whether the session's victim VID is a PC; `npc.is_metin` and `npc.is_boss`,
which read the stone flag and the rank off the victim and answer `nil` with no victim
(legacy pushes a 0 it never returns); `pc.global_rank_add_point`, which needs both
arguments numbers, takes the counter as `(BYTE)`, queues the point for the step's end,
and refuses past the ninth with legacy's line; and `pc.global_rank_get_reward`, which
gives each unclaimed prize by the session's `give_item` and answers 1 won, 0 none, with
the claim stored beside the items (`Giving::ItemsAndPrizes`). `pc.in_dungeon` goes
`partial` at always false: no dungeon is ported, so no character stands in one.
`sys.char.top_players` goes `partial`: the global rank is ported, the top-player effect
is not. The kill's quest run stages the victim by `set_quest_npc` before `kill`
(`quests.rs` `quest_kill`), as `Reward` stages `SetQuestNPCID`; the no-target scripts'
`kill` always runs, which is where `napierdalator`'s lives.

Corrections. `data.lua.unread` covered `BlueDragon.lua` on the claim that nothing loads it; the
claim was wrong. `locale/europe/settings.lua:174` dofiles `BlueDragon.lua`,
`CQuestManager::InitializeLua` loads `settings.lua` (`G/questlua.cpp:736-746`), and the
Rewrite already runs that chain (`quest/src/host.rs` `LIBRARIES` with `dofile` below the
locale directory), so `BlueDragonSetting` is set and the binder reads it in both. The row
now covers `monkey_dungeon.lua` alone, and the `spec.md` finding and owner question 5's
bullet are corrected the same way.

Quirks kept. Ties keep board order (legacy's `std::sort` leaves them unspecified); the snapshot
lags the counters until the 20-minute refresh; the season's end empties the snapshot, so
the board stays empty until the next one, as the DB's `option = 4` clear does. A boot at
season 0 leaves the `RankGlobalSeason` flag unset, as legacy only writes it at a season's
end, so `/geteventflag` does not list it.

## 403. The dungeon names

Thirteen quest-api rows are `ported`, all through one scenario:
`a_party_enters_the_forest_and_its_timer_sends_it_home`. A party of two forms on
channel 1, the leader clicks the forest guardian, and the dialog spends both members'
tickets (`pc.remove_item` on the blocked takes, stored under each owner's PID) before
`d.new_jump_party` creates the dungeon and jumps the party to its entry. Both reenter
on the private map index. A server timer's report then selects the dungeon by the
timer's argument (`d.select` by `get_server_timer_arg`) and notices back the index
(`d.get_map_index`), the stored leader (both `d.setf`/`d.getf` and
`d.getf_from_map_index`), and a `game.set_event_flag` write; a `d.spawn_mob` dog stands
at the party's feet. The first exit was cleared (`clear_server_timer`) and never
fires — both hear only the second — and `d.exit_all` sends both home to the warp
`d.set_warp_location` named. The rows: `lua.d.new_jump_party`, `lua.d.get_map_index`,
`lua.d.setf`, `lua.d.getf`, `lua.d.getf_from_map_index`, `lua.d.notice`,
`lua.d.set_warp_location`, `lua.d.exit_all`, `lua.d.spawn_mob`,
`lua.game.set_event_flag`, `lua.server_timer`, `lua.clear_server_timer`,
`lua.get_server_timer_arg`. `BRIDGED` grows 223 to 236.

The game side is a new `dungeons` module (`CDungeonManager`'s live dungeons and
`CQuestManager`'s `m_mapServerTimer`): the create names the first free private index,
the timers fire on the pulse tick (`rint(PASSES_PER_SEC(when))`), and the exits,
notices, flags, warp spots and spawns run against the staged indices a step's
`DungeonMoves` remaps (`GetDungeonForce`). The bridge's `dungeon_api` family holds
the nine `d.*` arms with the argument rules (three checked numbers, the map as
`(long)`, the vnum as `(DWORD)`, false for a map index of 0); the `ds.*` arms move
into a plain `ds_calls` helper, and the timers and `game.set_event_flag` into
`timer_api` and `game_api` families, so no function trips the line lint. `Session`
grows the staging vectors, `takes`, and the blocked takes' sides; `store_quest_items`
writes another character's take as its own exchange side, folding the reader's own
back in, and `db::rank_global::claim` takes the sides along so a claim and its takes
land in one transaction. A disconnect leaves its dungeon (`leave_dungeon`), and the
pulse runs the dungeon ticks.

Unit tests: `a_staged_server_timer_fires_in_its_seconds_pulses` pins the delay (149
quiet, 150 fires); the `grand_read` tail moves into `grand_outcome`, the smith's
protos into `smith_protos`, and the quest-info pair and records into their helpers,
as the `takes` field tips each fixture past the line lint. Two faults found while
gating: the probe's `quest` had been blanked to `Vec::new()` instead of `b"q"`,
failing every `pc.setqf` test through the shared manager, and `BRIDGED` listed the
`d.*` names out of `api::NAMES` order (`d.exit_all`, `d.spawn_mob` sort first).

and `sys_err` sit only in library code no quest calls. One probe calls them instead:

a party with the info line, 2 with a guilded character on the account, else 999; the
marriage arm never fires since no character of this build is engaged or married) so
the script's control flow sees the pushed value, queues the move, and the world judges
the same call again after the step for its records and the re-show. `main.rs` reads the
account's pids and change count into each quest step (`QuestAccount`) and stores a
landed move after the step: migration 0027 adds `change_empire`, and
`db::players::change_empire` moves the account row and counts the change in one

## 406. The quest item (`item.remove`, `item.get_name`, `item.get_size`, `item.get_refine_vnum`, `item.get_level`)

The readers sit only in `questlib.lua`'s `item_index_table`, which no quest indexes
through the metatable, and `item.remove`'s only callers are the battle-pass reset and
the ship-defense timber turn-in, both behind unported gates — so one probe calls all
five: `ITEM_PROBE` answers 31005's `use` (a vnum with no owner script, so the probe is
the only script that runs), reads the name, size, refined vnum and level, removes the
quest item, and reads the cleared pointer. The scenario
`a_use_reads_and_removes_its_quest_item` proves the notices, the clear between the
reads and the last notice, and the row's absence after the relog.

The `Game` trait gains `held_refine`, `held_refine_level` and `remove_quest_item`;
`BRIDGED` grows 248 to 253, and the new `item_remove_api` family holds the five arms so
`item_api` stays under the line lint. `held_refine` answers the locale name, the
proto's `bSize` and `dwRefinedVnum`; `refine_level` parses the number after the last
`+` in the proto's `szName` (`strtol`, saturating); `remove_quest_item` releases the
stack at its position, deletes its slots, clears its cell and destroys its row. The
removal lands in the call, like `set_socket` does, so its clear rides the step's own
records ahead of the last notice. The owner check is the held lookup itself: an item
the character holds nowhere answers `None` and takes nothing. Unit tests: the bridge
removal clearing the pointer, the `+` parser, and the single-stack removal.

Two scenario lessons: the probe's fourth `end` was one too many (no `if`), which `qc`
refused silently at load, and a global vnum swap briefly renamed the spiral scenario's

## 408. The guild-war bets and the watchers' warp

Five names, all behind the guild observer's two entries (`locale/europe/quest/guild_war_observer.lua`):
`lua.guild.get_reserve_war_table`, `lua.guild.war_bet`, `lua.guild.is_bet`,
`lua.guild.get_warp_war_list`, and `lua.pc.warp_to_guild_war_observer_position`.

`get_reserve_war_table` lists the battle reservations as (id, stronger, weaker, handicap),
ties to To (`G/guild_manager.cpp:876-910`, pushed in reverse order). `war_bet` runs the
`mapBet` rules (`G/guild_war.cpp:436-467`): the war's first bet raises its total and stores
the row, a second bet by the same login is quiet, and a backed guild outside the pair or a
non-number takes nothing; the login comes from a new `QuestAccount::login` field, filled at
the descriptor and threaded through the quest sessions to the shadow. `is_bet` is true for
an unknown war or a non-number (`G/guild_manager.cpp:912-920`), else whether the reader's
login bet that war. `get_warp_war_list` is the on-war non-field pairs. Reservations and
bets are stored (`guild_war_reserve`, `guild_war_bet`), loaded at boot, and installed with
the guilds; a reservation whose guild pair left drops, and a bet whose war left takes its
gold back.

`pc.warp_to_guild_war_observer_position` clears `IsObserved`, remembers the exit, and warps
to the war map's watchers' start (`G/questlua_pc.cpp:3926-3944`).

Bridge notes. The guild observer's bet entry calls `guild.get_reserve_war_table.00_say` —
`get_reserve_war_table` returns a table, on which `.00_say` is nil and legacy errors at
`_string_find` (`G/questlua.cpp:222`, `type 2` for `LUA_TTABLE`). No bet completes through
it, on legacy either; the script's failure is ported — a recorded owner question (38) asks
whether to fix the script. An earlier reading of the bridge also miswired `observer_start_x`
and `observer_start_y` (`pc_index_table` in `quest/questlib.lua`): they answer the watcher's
start cell of the *observer's* map, not the war map's observer coordinates — the script's
`game.get_observer_start_x` is the war map's, a different name. Both are recorded so the
next reader does not repeat them.

Three scenarios: the reserve table and legacy's error, the one bet and `is_bet`, and the
observers' warp.

The `QuestAccount` change (a `login: String` field, so `Clone` not `Copy`) moved the
quest/item/shop entry chain from by-value to by-reference accounts; the async game-handle
calls still move theirs into their messages.

Flakes. The stray-dog scenario failed once (byte `3e` past a swing, the known unrelated
load flake) and passed on rerun. `boot_hands_the_regens` failed once with `FIRST_NPC_VID +
2`: each vein draws its lifetime from 7-15 minutes (`G/char.cpp:2569`), so two short draws
in a row respawn twice inside the fixed 901-second loop; the draw is Parity, the test
window is the flake. Both reruns passed alone; the second full suite was green.

## 409. The 6th and 7th bonus (`CG_ATTR67_ADD`, the six `attr67add.*` names)

Seven entry points, one scenario (`an_attr67_regist_waits_and_collects`): `cg.game.attr67_add`,
the six `lua.attr67add.*` names, `quest.item_attr67add` (now `ported`), and `sys.custom.attr67`.

`CG_ATTR67_ADD` (169) runs `CInputMain::Attr67Add` (`G/input_main.cpp:3489-3507`) with no
observer gate: the open stands the window up, the close drops it, and the regist runs only
while it stands; an unknown sub-header is absorbed, a malformed record closes the connection.
`CHARACTER::Attr67Add` (`G/char_item.cpp:10478-10611`) runs its guards in legacy's order (no
trade, shop browse, safebox, or changelook window; the window empty; a regist item in the named
cell; a weapon or armor), the material count through legacy's actual precedence
(`!CountSpecifyItem(v) >= n` parses as `(!Count) >= n`, so any held stack passes and the spend
takes what is there), the level band's fragment (`CItemVnumHelper`, `C/VnumHelper.h:25-52`;
the pendant's 39079 arm sits behind `__PENDANT_SYSTEM__`, which this build lacks), and the
support percent (the named cell's proto `value3` / 5 × count). The success is
`number(1, 100) <= total`, stored with the wait (`get_global_time() + 86400`) and the rare-add
control (0); the regist item moves from its cell to the window, the client's old cell clears
and the window's fills, and the rows store as a move's do. Not ported: the sealed arm
(`__SOUL_BIND_SYSTEM__` is not in this build), the lock arm (only blend expiry locks, and no
blend item is a regist type), the logout destroy of a window legacy never saves (the Rewrite's
store owns the row, which the character keeps), and the item logs.

The bridge (`G/questlua_attr67add.cpp:28-137`) reads the window the script runs for (the
blocked PC's in a switched block, the reader's own otherwise): `holding`, `item_vnum`,
`window_type` (`ATTR67_ADD`), `window_cell` (0), `success` (false with no window item; else
whether the won flag stands, rolling the rare onto the window's item first when the control
is 0 or below), and `collect` (nothing with no window item; else the move to the first free
base cell and the three flags reset, or `Not enough inventory space.` with no room). The rare
roll is `CItem::AddRareAttribute` through the existing `add_rare_attribute` (the session now
carries the `item_attr_rare` rows); its cell updates and its row saves. `BRIDGED` grows 262
to 268. Unit tests: the material bands, the regist's spends/moves/flags and its silent
refusals, the bridge's window and flag rules, and the collect's move home.

The scenario stages Seon-Hae 20095 beside Alpha on map 1, Alpha a `HIGH_WIZARD` at `talk`
with sword 10 and 3 fragments: the empty-window click opens the client's dialog (the
`cmdchat` line, then `[DONE]` in skin 0), the regist with 255 fragments cannot fail, the

quest flags bank with the character's own save, so the scenario reads them at the disconnect.
Seon-Hae also runs the gaya entries, so the menu is golden with all four.

side, Alpha invites Yankee, the join walk drains, and the first Update's resend reaches

approximation, so the walk overshoots — the relay and the view's own records pass, the
resends drain until the wire holds nothing but heartbeats, and a click says `near 0`.

the count is 0 rather than 1.

## 411. The Okey card game

`do_cards` (`G/cmd_general.cpp:3812-3864`) is ported: a new
`prodomo/src/game_state/cards.rs` holds each character's hand (5 hand slots, 3
field slots, the cards left, the field and game points, the 24 drawn cards) and
the Okey table of ended games, behind `GameState::run_cards_line` on a new
`GameCommand::CardsLine`, with `Command::Cards` and `cards_line_step` wiring the
chat line through `finish_use_line` so the deck's spends and the end's box store
as a use does. The first word's first byte names the arm; the `o`, `d`, `a` and
`r` arms read the second word as a DWORD only when its first byte is a digit,
else they run nothing.

The open refuses with `Please close all windows first.` under a trade, a shop, a
safebox or the cube browse, and with `You don't have enough money` or `You don't
have any Okey Card Set(s)` when the deck is out and 30,000 gold or a card set
(79506) is missing; else it spends both, cleans both lists and refills 24. The
pullout refuses a full hand, an empty deck and five cards across hand and field
with their lines, else draws type 1-3 value 1-8, redrawing repeats. The end's
points buy the golden (71194), silver (71195) or bronze (71196) box through
`AutoGiveItem`, log the game to the Okey table, clean the lists, and send the
two info lines. The accept pays three of a kind 150, a suited run 100, three of
a value lowest*10+10, any run lowest*10, sends `cards reward` and resets the
field on a win, and restores the field to the hand on a loss. The destroy and
restore run nothing past their slots or on empty ones. Every arm sends the two
info lines (`cards info`, `cards finfo`) on the paths legacy does.

The Okey table lives in the world's memory, not the store: legacy reads
`log.okay_event` through the DB manager, which the Rewrite retired (ADR-0001),
and no scenario reboots across a rank read. Both ranks cut to the 4096-byte
buffer the way `snprintf` cuts them, NUL slot included.

One legacy Defect is not reproduced: `CardsRestore` and `RestoreField` write to
`cards_in_hand[GetEmptySpaceInHand()]` unchecked (`G/char_cards.cpp:193-205`,
`:301-312`), so a restore with a full hand writes past the hand. The Rewrite
runs nothing when no hand slot is free (STATUS defect bullet). The cube check
names the cube browse; the private shop and the cube-open flag are not ported,
so neither refuses here (module doc).

`pc.get_okay_global_rank` and `pc.get_okay_rund_rank`
(`G/questlua_pc.cpp:80-104`) are bridged: the quest snapshot carries both rank
texts read at the step's start, `BRIDGED` grows to 271, and the `pc_api` arm
reaches them through `pc_state`. `quest.cards_event` is ported with them: its
login icon, its card-set trade and its two rank chats all run, though no
scenario trades the set yet (inventory note).

One scenario: `a_cards_game_opens_pulls_ends_and_ranks`. Alpha holds one set and
100,000 gold at the teacher's point, with the Okey table (20417) staged one cell
east in map 1's `npc.txt`. `/cards open 1` spends 30,000 and the set (the gold
change's int-header low byte is 225) and hears the open and the empty info
lines; `/cards pullout` deals one card; `/cards destroy 0` clears the slot the
draw filled; `/cards end` with no points logs a zero game and hears the emptied
lines; and the table's menu offers the trade and both ranks, each rank naming
`1. Place - Alpha - 0 points.` Six unit tests cover the open's spends and
refusals, the pullout's five-card cap, a three-of-a-kind win with its bronze
box, the ranks' sums and order, and the `snprintf` cut. The Okey table is
staged, not probed: an early probe on the teacher proved the quest's 20417
chats were never the failure (a missing `pc_api` dispatch arm was: the bridges
sat in `pc_state` but no name reached them, so the click died silently).

Bridge notes. The revive tick (affect 215's remove and a character update) can
land between the click and its dialog, so the dialog reads
`read_script_past_ticks`. `GameState::new` tripped the line lint with the new
table, so the two card fields grouped into `CardTables`, the two offline-mail
fields into `whisper::OfflineMail`, and the dice seed split into `fresh_dice`.

The bridges were written in an earlier session and are covered now: `quiet_api`
snapshots the six notice slots (`(null)` for a missing one, more than six only
logs), `LC` answers the tongue, `command` runs a string, `initialize` prepares, and
`set_quest_state` moves the running quest at once and reserves other quests' moves.
The world judges after the step (`apply_quiet_calls`): `broadcast_notice` speaks
`SendLocaleNotice` (`G/cmd_gm.cpp:1252-1313`) to every online character in VID
order, each in its own language, each `[ENTER]` piece its own notice; `command`
runs `interpret` on the reader and dispatches the battle-pass usage gate
(`G/cmd_general.cpp:4184-4219`); `initialize` re-arms the temple.
`SendLocaleNotice`'s `%d`-to-`%s` rewrite and raw `vsnprintf` are kept
(`chat_line::notice_text` skips the locale-strings lookup, as the bare `vsnprintf`
does); the owner's quest texts hold only `%d`, `%s`, `%%` and bare-`%` literals, so
the ported conversions cover them.
New reader. `gamedata::quest_translate` loads each language's `locale_quest.txt`
through the tab-separated CSV reader, skips the header, inserts `atoi` of the first
column, and answers `NoName` on a miss and `en`'s table past the last language
(`G/locale.cpp:90-103,146-166`); `LOCALE_YMIR` loads the `en` file. The boot refuses
to start without the files (a Divergence, as for the locale strings). Two owner
files carry stray quotes, and legacy's reader fate is kept: the `pl` file's
unclosed dialog at line 8018 drops its rows from there on (its table ends at key
7258), and the `cz` file's stray quote at line 10842 never closes cleanly (line
11154 opens another), so its table ends at key 9825. `csv_table` refuses an
unterminated file, so the loader cuts the unfinished row's start and re-parses the
head; the `cz` merge-then-drop and the row counts per language are pinned against

from map 209's base, the drawn 1-based room, the guardian's and portal's VIDs, the
30 s activity arm with its 180 s idle and 600 s attacked moves, the 120 s portal

flood is fresh on every quest line; the world has no delayed-disconnect path), and
a click's dialog records beat the world's notices to the socket (the step's records

`oxevent.*` family 401 marked `unused` with no caller.

The bridge (`quiet_api`, `BRIDGED` 288): `(int)` of the first argument is the level (low byte), a
string-like second is the question (a number formats), the third slot's truth is the answer. Quiet
with no question: `AddQuiz` would fault on the NULL, and a crash the data can trigger is a Defect.
`strlcpy(Quiz, question, 256)` keeps 255 bytes and the NUL; the Vec grows one past the level, so a
level-3 quiz opens the gap at 0 and 2. `/show_quiz` (`G/cmd_oxevent.cpp:11-16`,
`G/OXEvent.cpp:189-204`) reads the list back through `GmLine::ShowQuiz`: the header, each level,
question and key (`[LS;858]`/`[LS;869]` passed through for the client to translate, as the Rewrite
holds no `LC_TEXT` table), the `[LS;880;%d]` count, and the footer.

`npc.get_guild` (`G/questlua_npc.cpp:60-70`) pushes the current NPC's guild ID, 0 with no NPC or no
guild. Only `CObject::RegenNPC` (`G/building.cpp:269-295`) sets one, from the land's owner, and no
building stands (`sys.world.objects` missing), so the answer is 0; the bridge (already in
`game_npc_api` and `BRIDGED`) is now scenario-proven, with a comment at the session's `npc_guild`.

`timer`, `party.show_cinematic` and `party.run_cinematic` are `unused`. The sweep over the 164 files
under `locale/europe/quest` (but `quest_functions`) and `locale/europe/*.lua`: `pc.setqf` counts 27
(positive control), a fabricated name counts 0 (negative control), `timer` has no call form (`(`,
string, `[[`, `{`) and its one bare token is the comment "Refrain from using these inside a timer."
(`dungeonFunctions.lua:50`), and the cinematics appear only in two commented lines
(`questlib.lua:35-36`). `timer` bridges `_timer`/`_set_named_timer`, already proven absent from the
manager in 403's sweep. Owner to confirm.

Scenario `a_quiz_lands_from_a_click_and_show_quiz_lists_it` (8/8 stable): a click lands a level-1
quiz and says `quiz:1 guild:0`; `/show_quiz` lists it. Units: the bridge's argument rules, the land
(truncation, gaps). Mutants killed: the answer forced true, the truncation at 200, the key forced

## 415. The Gaya market, the aura windows and the event pair

Seven quest names, all called by owner quests: `event_panel.quest` drives `start_event` /
`end_event` from its GM menu, `sistem_gaia.lua` opens the Gaya pair, and `aura_system.quest`
opens the aura trio (`BRIDGED` 295).

`game.open_gaya` chats `OpenGuiGaya`. `game.open_gaya_market` refreshes the market and chats
`OpenGuiGayaMarket`: a reader with no row gets nine rolls of `number(1, size - 1)` from the
21-row `gaya.txt` (a new `gamedata::gaya` reader, loaded at boot and shared like the other
tables) with the six slots locked and the 5-hour stamp in `system_gaya.gaya_time_world_4`,
then the markers (`GayaMarketClear`, the nine `GayaMarketItems`, `GayaMarketSlotsDesblock`,
`GayaMarketTime`) reach the client. The shelf lives on the world (a Divergence: legacy keeps
it in per-character `<Name>_gaya_system.txt` files, and `UpdateItemsGayaMarker0` faults on a
missing file). A one-row table rolls nothing: legacy's `number(1, 0)` has no range.

The aura trio shares `OpenAuraRefineWindow` (`G/char_aura.cpp:14-71`): an open window chats
`[LS;1014]`, an opener at `DISTANCE_APPROX` 1000 or more chats `[LS;459]`, else the new
`protocol::gc_aura` open (header 214, size 5, subheader 0, the window byte) goes out and the
window stands. `gc.aura` is `partial`: the item and refine subheaders wait for their systems.
GC coverage is now 118 of 134 (16 missing: 7 fixed, 9 dynamic).

`start_event` / `end_event` run `SetEventState` (`G/event_manager.cpp:719-779`): an unknown
index or an unchanged state is quiet, else the flag moves (the 14 `GetEventState` flags,
`:663-716`, pinned by a unit table) and the exp/loot arms grant their empire privs and speak
their notices. The priv runs a week (`RequestGiveEmpirePriv`'s maximum,
`G/priv_manager.cpp:47-66`), clamped 0-200, because the quest call carries no row times and a
week is what the scheduled path would grant at most. Every other arm waits for its system;
a zero exp/loot value moves the flag and grants nothing, as `SetExperienceEvent` refuses it.

Scenario `a_click_opens_windows_and_runs_the_exp_event` (8/8 stable): the dialog, the Gaya
window, the market markers, the absorb open, the priv notice and both exp notices, in order.
Units: the bridges' argument rules, the event flags/grants/notices, the flag table, the
market roll and markers, the aura gate. Mutants killed: the event index +1, a flag typo
(after a table test caught the class), the aura range at 10. Refactors for the lints:
`time_find_api` out of `api`, `QuietCalls`/`QuietOwned` bundles, `ReaderGains::take` and
`ReaderOrders::take`. No width was measured.

## 417. Meley's lobby

Nine quest names, all called by the owner's Meley quests: `meleylair.lua` chats the
registered pair, the requirements and the register's pair at 20419, then the enter's
pair; `meleylair_zone.lua` runs `Check()` at login and `Leave()` at the shelter
(`BRIDGED` 309).

`MeleyLair.GetRequirments` pushes (3, 600), `GetPartecipantsLimit` 16 and
`GetSubMapIndex` 62. The register judges mid-script from the shadow guilds: the (0, 0)
quiet for a guest or a non-master, (1, ch) when registered, (2, 0) on another
dungeon, (3, 3) and (4, 600) for the level and ladder gates, (7, seconds) on a live
cooldown, (5, 0) with no map to create, and (6, 300) on the pass, which moves the
shadow ladder and triple at once. The world re-judges the queued call after the step:
`CreatePrivateMap(212)` through the dungeon manager, the double ladder write (delta
and set, as `ChangeLadderPoint` + `SetLadderPoint`), the dungeon triple, the run, and
the `[LS;1001]` line to every online member that `SetLadderPoint` chats — dropped only
when the ladder is unchanged, as its `!=` guard is. The enter late-creates on a
registered-but-unhosted triple, refuses the wrong Channel and the full, finished and
non-guild arms, then rows the participant, saves the exit and orders the warp to the
recall spot on the run's index. `Check` outs a stranger, `Leave` drops the reader and
outs it; the login flow outs a shown stranger (`input_login.cpp:784-785`), the
disconnect drops a leaver from its run (`char.cpp:1757-1758`), a removed member is
warped out (`MemberRemoved`), and a disband ends its run (`GuildRemoved` ->
`EndDungeonWarp`). The enter's `GetRecallPositionByEmpire(212, 0)` is the town spawn,
already absolute: no owner quest registers a restart-city row, so the empire-0
`Town.txt` arm is the only one that fires. The fight engine (steps, spawns, rewards,
`CanGetReward`/`Reward`) waits; `sys.guild.dungeon` is `partial`.

Two fixes the lobby needed: the quest session now seeds the world's live runs, so an
enter after a register reads the registration, and click and dialog steps refresh the
mover's PK mode, alignment, guild, flags and dead bit from the world, as item steps
do — the descriptor's actor carries PEACE, which read every enter as non-guild.

Scenario `a_guild_registers_enters_and_leaves_meleys_lair` (8/8 stable): Alpha leads a
level-3 `MyGuild` with a 600 ladder beside 20419 on map 62; the register chats
`(6, 300)` and the `[LS;1001;0]` line, the row holds 0; in guild PK mode the enter
chats `(true, 0)` and warps to (320000, 1529000) on 2120000; coming back, the probe
login reads the map and the check keeps it. (`MeleyLair.Leave` runs the same
`order_meley_out` the unit leave pins; no NPC on the run's map can chat it over the
wire.) Units: the bridges' pairs, the shadow pairs, the register's gates, the
enter/check/leave warps. Mutants killed: the ladder cost -1, the submap name typo,
the shadow level +1. One incident: a mutation helper truncated the new untracked
`meley.rs` to 0 bytes; it was rewritten from the session transcript and verified
build-clean with every Meley test and the scenario green before the mutants reran.
No width was measured.
