## 418. The ship defence

The thirteen `ship_defense_mgr` names are bridged (`quest/src/host.rs` `BRIDGED`, now
`[&str; 322]`; the `ship_api` family in `quest/src/manager.rs`) and judged
(`prodomo/src/game_state/ship.rs`, new): the create's private map, cooldown fan, ready fan and
warp; the start's deck and wave-1 prepare; the join's party-gated warp; the leave's entry
recall; the land's port spot with the entry fallback; the shadow created/running pair; the
four `EInstance` constant flags; the heal's 1% paste, HP chat, 5-second stun and broadcast;
and `can_join`'s shadow read. The queens drain through `judge_ship_calls` from the dialog and
target steps. The run ticks on the pulse (`run_ship_ticks`): the wave regens from the owner's
`wave*.txt` tables (emitted as literals), the hydra and laser halves, the kill arm
(`ship_on_kill`, hooked from `fight.rs`'s non-player death before the reward halves), and the
jump-out land.

Three legacy readings pin the port. `SetAllianceHPPct`
(`G/ShipDefense.cpp:1701-1736`) ignores its argument: the mast heals
`WOOD_REPAIR_PCT` (1%) of its maximum past it, whatever the quest passed, so the judge reads
the queued `pct` and drops it. `Join` (`:1738-1772`) needs a party: a lone reader's join is
quiet. `GetLeaderPID` (`:1652-1673`) with no party answers the reader's own PID, so a lone
captain creates and starts.

`a_captain_boards_starts_and_lands_the_ship_defence`: Alpha stands beside 9009 on the cape
(135); its board chats the four true flags and the shadow pair around the create, and enters
warped to the recall spot (166700, 522300) on the run's index. Coming back, the deck's wheel
(20436) stands on the run; its start chats the running read, and the start's broadcast, the
wave's pair, the heal's notice, the stun's flag update and affect add, and the heal's
broadcast land in order. Its land ships out to the port spot (168500, 611200). The menus
carry the live quest's own chats beside the probes, since the loaded `ship_defense.lua`
arms on the same NPCs. `join` needs a party, which one client cannot form, so the wire pins
only its quiet; the unit join (`the_join_leave_and_land_order_their_warps`) pins its warp.
The unit create (`the_create_gates_the_member_and_warps_the_leader_in`) gates a member's
create, the start (`the_start_runs_the_deck`) flips the state and counts wave 1 from 60, and
the heal (`the_heal_pastes_chats_stuns_and_broadcasts`) pastes 1% past the maximum, chats the
HP, stuns and broadcasts. The shadow pair and the member-create queue are pinned in
`the_ship_shadow_stands_reads_and_starts`.

Quest-api is now 244 ported, 2 missing (`MeleyLair.CanGetReward`, `MeleyLair.Reward`), 370
unused and 83 partial; `quest.ship_defense` stays `partial` (its rankings arm is commented
out in the source). 8 parallel runs of the scenario pass.

## 419. Meley's fight

The fight engine behind the lobby (`prodomo/src/game_state/meley.rs`, from the
`CMgrMap` half of `G/MeleyLair.cpp:84-951`): the gate click starts the fight
(`meley_gate_click`, hooked before the shop's click), the statues flag at their
HP line and move the step on (`meley_statue_damage`), the spawn/effect/statue
ticks run on the pulse (`run_meley_ticks`), the kill hook counts stones and
step-3 bosses and strips the statue flags (`meley_on_npc_kill` from
`dead_npc`), seals break step-4 statues (`meley_gift` from `give_item`'s new
`MeleyStatue` arm), and the win stamps the chest's clock and stands the chest
(`meley_dungeon_result`). `Damage`'s Meley arms gate in `world` behind three
`Striker` flags (`meley_blocked`, `cannot_dead`, `meley_statue`), judged in
`fight.rs` and `pc_skill.rs` before each world damage call; the armada VIDs
live on the game thread (`meley_cannot_dead`).

The last two `MeleyLair` names are bridged (`quest/src/host.rs` `BRIDGED`, now
`[&str; 324]`; the `meley_api` arms in `quest/src/manager.rs`) and judged: the
shadow reads `CanGetReward` (step 4, participant, past the chest's clock, no
take yet), `Reward` queues its argument, and the world re-judges and gives
chest 1 for argument 1 else chest 2 (`meley_reward`, with `auto_give`). The
queued takes drain into the dialog, click and use-item steps' records and rows;
the event step drops them, as it drops the ladder store.

Three legacy readings pin the port. `GiveReward` (`:939-951`) never checks the
step or the clock — the quest does — so the judge re-checks what the shadow
read. `OnKill`'s step-2 strip (`:809-830`) only lifts `AFF_STATUE1`; a step-2
stone kill past all-`AFF_STATUE2` statues counts but strips nothing. The
statue's HP line (`CMgrMap::Damage`, `:729-783`) heals back to the line: the
flagged hit lands the line, not zero.

`a_guild_starts_meleys_fight_and_the_reward_refuses`: Alpha registers, enters
in guild PK mode, and clicks the gate on the run — over the wire the statues
have no proto on the owner's data (6118, 6112/6113/6115, 6116/6117 are absent
from `mob_proto.txt`), so a piece is missing and the three failed-start lines
chat with the `[LS;1001;600]` return; the shelter NPC's reward probe then reads
`may false` and the take gives nothing. The units pin what the wire cannot:
the real start and the statue flags (`the_gate_click_starts_the_fight_and_the_statues_flag_at_their_line`),
the kill strip (`the_stone_kills_strip_the_statues_at_the_limit`), and the
chest's one take past the clock (`the_reward_gives_one_chest_past_the_clock`).
8 parallel runs of the scenario pass.

Quest-api is now 246 ported, 0 missing, 370 unused and 83 partial;
`quest.meleylair_zone` stays `partial` (its gate-click arm is empty in the
source; the engine's failed start covers it). One suite run hit an unrelated
`Keyed` EAGAIN flake in `a_gm_aggregates_and_forgets_the_dogs_around`, green
alone and green on rerun.

## 425. The descriptor ticks

Three timed-event rows stood `missing` though each runs with a binary scenario against
the real server. No code changed; the slice marks all three `ported`.

`event.char.save_event` (`G/char.cpp:5064-5082`): every `save_event_second_cycle` the
character is queued and saved (`prodomo/src/main.rs::SaveEvent`). The shared delayed-save
queue is not reproduced (ADR-0002: one process, the descriptor writes the row itself);
what the client can see is that the row lands within one cycle and on disconnect.
`the_save_cycle_writes_the_row_while_the_character_is_still_connected` runs the binary
with a 1 s cycle and reads the moved point from the store while the descriptor is open.

`event.desc.ping_event` (`G/desc.cpp:163-204`): every `ping_event_second_cycle`, past the
admin bypass, a descriptor with no pong closes; else it sends `GC_PING`, clears its pong,
and sends the handshake (`prodomo/src/heartbeat.rs`).
`the_ping_cycle_closes_a_silent_client` runs the binary with a 1 s cycle.

`event.desc.disconnect_event` (`G/desc.cpp:812-828`): `DelayedDisconnect` closes the
descriptor when the delay runs out (`prodomo/src/chat.rs::ChatEffect::DelayedDisconnect`).
`a_tenth_whisper_in_a_run_closes_the_connection` runs the binary through the whisper
spam limit.

Three watchdog timers. `event.char.check_speedhack_event` never increments: both

once with the owner's `enable_hack_check` off (`G/battle.cpp:871`, `G/config.cpp:154`,
no key in `legacy/config/`), and the combo writer sits in `CheckComboHack` behind
the same switch (`G/input_main.cpp:1562,1747`); the port relays `FUNC_COMBO` with no
combo count, so the 1-minute clear/reset (`G/char.cpp:8566-8602`) has nothing to

no-descriptor arm (`G/party.cpp:326-335`), and the port hosts PC parties only (no

is the retired DB-peer's deferred load (`G/char_affect.cpp:508-558`): the port loads
affects synchronously at entry (`GameState::load_affects`), and its only other reach,
the `IsLoadedAffect` fixme in `CanUseItem` (`G/char_item.cpp:2777-2782`), is the
entry-race guard, dead with the race (owner question 48).

## 440. The jigsaw fish event

`sys.event.fish`, `cg.game.fish_event_send`, `gc.fish_event_info` and the two
`sub.FishEvent` arms are `ported`, with the scenario
`fish_boxes_fill_the_jigsaw_board_and_it_pays_and_clears`.

The records. `protocol/src/cg_fish_event.rs` decodes `HEADER_CG_FISH_EVENT_SEND`
(0xdb): a subheader byte, then the box's `ItemPos` or the board cell.
`protocol/src/gc_vid.rs` carries `GcFishEventInfo` (0xdf) with the subheader and
the two DWORDs, and the `gc_inventory` row is flipped, which moves the counts to
119 implemented and 15 missing. Both directions stay opaque above the subheader:
an unknown subheader, a cell past 23 and a non-inventory window end silently, as
`CInputMain::FishEvent` falls through them (`G/input_main.cpp:1326-1358`).

The board (`prodomo/src/game_state/fish_event.rs`). A normal box (25106) draws
`number(1, 6)` and a special box (25107) attaches shape 7
(`FishEventUseBox`, `G/char.cpp:10915-10959`), each spending one box and raising
the use count; anything else at the cell is told `You can not use this item
here`. `valid_position` and `place_shape` stenograph the head and offset tables
of `FishEventIsValidPosition` and `FishEventPlaceShape` (`:10961-11037`),
including the shape rows that repeat an offset and check a cell twice. A full
board pays `reward_for` (25113 at 10 boxes or fewer, 25112 at 24 or fewer, else
25111) through the item-step give, so the pickup line leads the item set exactly
as `AutoGiveItem`'s `ChatPacket`-before-`AddToCharacter` does
(`G/char_item.cpp:9181-9185`), then `PointChange(POINT_EXP, 30000)` and the
`REWARD` record, then the board and the count clear
(`FishEventCheckAndReward`, `:11039-11079`).

The report and the store. The login report is `FishEventGeneralInfo`
(`:10880-10913`): the `ENABLE` record with the `enable_fish_event` flag beside
the count, then one `SHAPE_ADD` per main cell, carried last in the burst where
`Entergame` sends it (`G/input_login.cpp:939`). A count of 0 clears the board
first. Migration 0031 holds the cells (`fish_event_slot`) and the count
(`fish_event_count`); the load installs them, the save writes them, and the
attached shape stays memory-only, so a relogin drops what was held. The leave
takes the cells before the board goes with the character, the way the affects
are taken before the event.

Defects not reproduced. `FishEventGeneralInfo`'s report guard compares the held
shape to the special box's vnum (`lastAttachedShape > ITEM_FISH_EVENT_BOX_SPECIAL`,
`:11086`), so every byte passes it; the Rewrite compares to shape 7, the highest
the tables name. Recorded in `docs/STATUS.md`.

The scenario plays five specials and a normal box with a paste: the refusal,
the attach, the landing, the misfit's resend and line, the relogin behind the
count-2 report, the completion with the pickup line, the set, the exp and the
reward record, then the normal box's draw 1-6 on the cleared board and the
relogin behind the count-1 report. The normal draw is ranged in the scenario
and pinned by the rigged-dice unit test, the way `/dice` splits its coverage.
Mutants: the shape-7 offsets, the reward vnum and bound, the exp, the shape max,
the kept filter, the load's cell, the use count and the draw range, all killed.
`apply_ground` lent its `NpcsOn` arm a helper to stay under the line limit.

## 441. The daily gift

`sys.custom.daily_gift`, `data.daily_gift`, `cg.game.daily_gift`,
`gc.daily_gift` and `cmd.daily_gift_event` are `ported`, with the scenario
`daily_gifts_collect_for_cash_and_a_ticket_and_the_week_renews`.

The records. `protocol/src/cg_daily_gift.rs` decodes `HEADER_CG_DAILY_GIFT`
(0xb4): an action byte and a slot. `GcDailyGift` (0xb4, 111 bytes) already had
its codec in `protocol/src/gc_nested.rs`; the `gc_inventory` row is flipped.
The flag gate, the silent slot past 6 and the silent unknown action are
`CInputMain::DailyGift` (`G/input_main.cpp:3512-3545`), which checks nothing
else: a collect slot at or above 7 indexes the week's gift vector unchecked
(`CDailyGiftItemGroup::GetVnum`, `G/item_manager.h:46-58`), a Defect the Rewrite
does not reproduce (recorded in `docs/STATUS.md`).

The week (`prodomo/src/game_state/daily_gift.rs`, `gamedata/src/daily_gift.rs`).
The owner runs four weeks (`locale/europe/daily_gift.txt`); the third is fully
covered by the item protos and the scenario plays it. The open is
`LoadDailyGiftWeek` (`G/char_daily_gifts.cpp:21-70`): renew first, the missing
group line, then the record, then the mission line for a character below 50.
The status is `GetDailyGiftStatus` (`:262-316`) with its early locks, its fresh
row with day 1 waiting, and its wait promotion that stores when the row
counted. The `[TEST]` print sits inside the status, so a collect's guard call
prints the day at the epoch before anything else, and a mission-less look
prints none; the scenario pins both. `ctime` is UTC (the Rewrite has no time
zone), with the trailing newline riding the line as legacy's `%s` carries it.

The collects are `CollectDailyGift` (`:132-260`): the locked day unlocks for
cash, or for the ticket whenever the ticket arm ran, even when the cash would
cover it (`!bUseTicket` gates the cash branch, `:166`); the waiting day collects
free and silent; the collected day is told it already was. Every gift runs
through the shared give with the pickup notice stripped, because legacy passes
`bMsg` false (`:170-174`). The line work the scenario pins: the usage with its
repeated `<renew>` block, the already-active refusal, the unlock line, the poor
day, the missing ticket, and the epoch guard line of each.

The line and the arm. `/daily_gift_event` (`G/cmd_gm.cpp:5061-5152`) starts the
event for a week or stops it; `isnhdigit` is a leading ASCII digit
(`libthecore/hangul.h:17`), and `str_to_byte` parses the words. The
`DailyGiftEvent` arm (`G/questmanager.cpp:1440-1451`) fires on the flag set, so
in the Rewrite it lands before the enable's notice; legacy's arm rides the
DB-peer's answer and lands later, an inherent timing of the retired roundtrip.
The command needed two claims the first scenario run found missing: the
`is_chat_line` row and the chat-flag gate, without which the game loop hit its
catch-all and the descriptor closed.

The store and the save. Migration 0032 holds the week (`daily_gift`) beside the
account's cash; the load installs the row, the cash and the renew time the
admission read from the flag. The cash loads once and spends from memory, where
legacy queries it on every open: an Operator grant mid-session shows at the
next login (a Divergence, recorded in `docs/STATUS.md`). The save writes the
row and the spent delta after the player row and advances the loaded baseline,
so a second save in the session finds no delta; the scenario shortens the save
cycle to a second and watches both saves land. The renew is
`CheckDailyGiftRenewTime` (`:89-129`): past its time the week steps to the next
with `order`, or to a random one, or the event stops.

Refactors for the line lint: `daily_collect` lent its locked arm
`daily_collect_locked`, the line lent its usage `daily_gift_event_usage`,
`apply_chat_flag` lent its stat arms `apply_stat_command`, `apply_delegated`
lends its pick list `is_pick_command`, `apply_ground` lends its event steps
`apply_event_step`, `mid_name` lends its flag rows `flag_name`, `select_character`
lends its burst `deliver_loading_burst` over a bundled `BurstDelivery`, and
`save_held` lends its stored rows `save_stored_rows` and its week
`save_daily_gift`.

Mutants, all killed: the unlock line, the mission level (by the unit test; the
scenario's 154 and 1 straddle no boundary), the quiet give, the cash spend, the
collect-time day base, the renew week step, the ticket branch, the fresh day-1
wait, the ctime weekday, the arm hook, the baseline advance (by the mid-save
watch), and the record's week. A flake-check run against a mutant binary is
worth a warning: the mutants build their binary and restore only the source, so
the next `ls -t` can pick a mutant binary; the 8/8 green check ran on a rebuilt
pristine binary.

## 442. The sash window

`CG_SASH` (`CInputMain::Sash`, `G/input_main.cpp:3395-3425`) with no observer gate (`:3862`):
close, add, remove and refine over the `OpenSash` windows (`G/char.cpp:9888-10560`), answered
as a move is. A waiting quest and an unknown sub-header are absorbed, as legacy's guard and
`default` do. The window is `sash_windows` (combination or absorption); its materials are item
ids in `sash_held`, so a held item stays held when it moves cells, as legacy's `LPITEM`
pointers survive the same moves. `OpenSash` ends in `ClearSashMaterials` (`:9933`), so the
fresh window holds nothing.

The add (`:10105-10213`) resolves `pos` 255 to the first free slot only when it is exactly
255 — legacy's report is `CUSTOM_INVENTORY_SLOT_END` (1370), which never fits a `BYTE`, so the
client always sends 255; the Rewrite matches the wire, not the report. Then the guards in
legacy's `else if` order: the item must exist (a worn cell, anything at or past 1370, belt
cells and dragon souls refuse), a combination takes costume and an absorption takes costume
in slot 0, a material held by another window chats `LOCKED_ITEMS`, slot 1 of a combination
takes the grade slot 0 holds (`SAME_GRADE`), a combination takes nothing at the grade-4
absorption cap (`MAX_AB`), slot 1 of an absorption takes a weapon or a body armour
(`ABSORB_WEAPON_ARMOR`), and slot 0 of an absorption refuses nothing already absorbed. The
last two arms are silent; `LC_TEXT` of an unknown key is the key itself, so the chat keys go
out raw. The landed add answers `ADDED` with the window flag, the grade price, the slot
(1370's low byte: `CheckEmptyMaterialSlot`'s `CUSTOM_INVENTORY_SLOT_END` truncates to 90 —
pinned as a Quirk), the named position, and `GetSashCombineResult` (`:10039-10103`): a
grade-4 pair keeps the vnum and widens by 5 up to 25; a lower pair steps the vnum up by one
when the proto table holds it and sets 5, 10, or 11..=19; an absorption shows slot 0's vnum
and absorption. Fewer than two materials zeroes every number.

The remove (`:10215-10255`) unlocks slot 1 alone, pricing what slot 0 still holds, while
slot 0 clears both; both answer `REMOVED` with a zeroed `{INVENTORY, 0}` position and vnum
0. The refine (`:10313-10511`) answers `REFINED` (value 4, despite the `CG_` name): a
combination sends `pos` 0 and `max_absorb` 100 on success, 0 on failure; an absorption sends
`pos` 255 and `max_absorb` 1. A combination at no gold chats `NOT_ENOUGH_YANG` and sends
nothing; a refine short of two materials is silent (`CanRefineSashMaterials` 0). A success
builds the result (`CopyAllAttrTo` through `refined_item`), rolls the absorption (`min` when
flat, else `number(min + 1, max)`), carries slot 0's absorbed socket, spends the gold,
destroys both materials, lands the new sash in slot 0's old cell, chats the rate (grade 4)
or `SUCCESS`, sends effect 25 around (which reaches the mover too, behind the answer), and
clears the window. A failure spends the gold, destroys slot 1 alone, keeps the window
standing, and unlocks slot 1. An absorption copies slot 1's attributes onto slot 0 (the
negative forced to 0, the refine element carried), stamps slot 1's vnum into socket 1,
destroys slot 1, chats `SUCCESS`, and clears the window. The money, item and sash logs are
`sys.log`'s, which owns no sink.

Death closes the window with its record (`Dead`, `:1620-1627`); the penalty's `CloseSash`
runs at `dead_event`, after `Dead` already closed it, so it sends nothing (`:330-336`). A
warp and a disconnect forget the window silently: no warp or disconnect path calls
`CloseSash`, and the client rebuilds its windows on the new view. The warp NPC judges
`CanHandleItem(false, true)` (`:7964`): the sash and the changelook refuse, the shop,
refine, cube, dragon soul, warp and aura arms are not ported.

A held material locks destroy, drop, move, give, sale, checkin and scroll-refine
(`CItem::isLocked`): the destroy, drop, move and sale refuse silently; the checkin chats
`[LS;667]` as for an unstorable item; the gift refuses silently. The move-destination arm
(legacy lets a move bury the held item) and the gift arm (`GiveItem` runs no `isLocked`
check) are Divergences, recorded in `docs/STATUS.md`.

The detachment scroll (`USE_DETACHMENT` with `VALUE0` 7, `CleanSashAttr`, `:10481-10500`)
rides use-on-item (`world::character::clean_sash_attr`): the absorbed socket to 0, every
attribute to 0, one scroll spent, silent on a refused target. Legacy's gate reads the
target's type `&&` subtype, so every costume that is no sash passes; the Rewrite keeps the
`&&` (a recorded Defect). The `ITEM_FLAG_REFINEABLE` check is skipped — the flag bit is not
ported — and is a Divergence. The owner's one detachment scroll (25100) has `VALUE0` 3, so
no wire scenario can carry the clean: it is unit-proved in `world`.

Scenario `sash_combines_and_absorbs` (ten helpers under the line lint): the reward pages to
the eight chats, "Combination" opens, slot 0 lands at the quirk, the bell lands silently
nowhere, slot 1 shows 85002 at 5..=5, a held destroy is silent, a one-material refine is
silent, the poor refine chats, slot 1 lifts priced by slot 0, slot 0 clears both, the close
answers and a second close sends nothing. With the gold stored the window refines at
80-in-100 until it succeeds (40 spare sashes, 40 draws: failing 38 in a row at 0.2 each is
1 in 3.6e27): each failure clears slot 1's cell, spends the gold, chats `FAILED` and
answers 0, and the retry proves slot 1 unlocked and slot 0 kept; the success clears both,
lands 85002 at absorption 5, spends 100,000 gold, chats `SUCCESS`, answers 0 and 100, and
the effect 25 follows. Then, as an IMPLEMENTOR (the mission's non-GM login gate keeps the
relog quiet), death closes the reopened window behind the dead and the three re-added
affects (540, 215, 540: the login's pair plus the penalty's own). The absorption chat
reopens it uncombined; the bell refuses slot 0 silently, the grade-2 sash lands priced
200,000, the bell lands as the weapon showing 85002 at 5..=5, and the refine updates the
sash (socket 1 stamped 5000), destroys the bell, chats `SUCCESS`, and answers 255 and 1.
The disconnect banks every row. Flake check 8/8.

## 443. The changelook window

`CG_CL` (`CInputMain::ChangeLook`, `G/input_main.cpp:3431-3459`) with no observer gate
(`:3857-3861`): close, add, remove and refine over the `pc.open_changelook` window
(`G/char.cpp:10504-10776`), answered as a move is. A waiting quest and an unknown
sub-header are absorbed, as legacy's guard and `default` do. The window is
`changelook_windows`; its materials are item ids in `changelook_held`, so a held item
stays held when it moves cells, as legacy's `LPITEM` pointers survive the same moves.
`ChangeLookWindow` ends in `ClearClWindowMaterials` (`:10535`), so the fresh window holds
nothing.

The add (`:10563-10672`) resolves a `pos` at or past 2 to the first free slot only when it
is exactly 255, then guards in legacy's `else if` order: the item must exist (`GetItem`
refuses a worn cell and anything at or past `INVENTORY_AND_EQUIP_SLOT_MAX`; a belt cell
refuses), a worn item chats the equipped line, anything but a weapon, armour or costume
chats the cannot line, an arrow or mount spear chats it, a non-body armour chats it, a
costume that is no body, hair, weapon or sash chats it (`ENABLE_WEAPON_COSTUME_SYSTEM` is
on), a held material chats the locked line, and an already-transmuted item chats the
transmuted line. `LC_TEXT` of an unknown key is the key itself, so the chat keys go out
raw. Slot 1 with slot 0 empty refuses silently, as does a filled slot; slot 1 of
mismatched type, subtype, original vnum (`GetOriginalVnum` is the vnum, `G/item.h:107`) or
antiflags (the sex pair either way, each job flag only when slot 1 names one slot 0 does
not; `GetAntiFlag` is the proto's, `G/item.h:78`) chats the cannot-submit line. The landed
add answers `ADD` with cost 0, the slot, and the named position.

The remove (`:10674-10708`) unlocks slot 1 alone while slot 0 clears both; both answer
`REMOVE` with a zeroed `{INVENTORY, 0}` position and cost 0, and a remove of an empty slot
sends nothing. The close answers with cost 0 only when the window stands; without one the
not-open line chats (the client close passes `bRequest = false`). The refine
(`:10710-10744`) sends nothing with slot 0 empty, chats the submit line with slot 1 empty,
and chats the gold line short of 50,000,000. Else it spends the gold (`ChangeGold`,
`ENABLE_REMOVE_LIMIT_GOLD`), destroys slot 1, stamps slot 1's vnum into slot 0's
transmutation (`SetTransmutation`, `G/item.cpp:352-356`: the `GC_ITEM_UPDATE` and the
save), clears the window, and answers `REFINE` with a zeroed position. The money and item
logs are `sys.log`'s, which owns no sink.

Death closes the window with its record (`Dead`, `G/char_battle.cpp:1642-1644`); the
penalty's `ChangeLookWindow(false, true)` runs at `dead_event`, after `Dead` already closed
it, so it sends nothing (`:334-339`). A warp and a disconnect forget the window silently:
no warp or disconnect path closes it, and the client rebuilds its windows on the new view.
The real-time expiry's locked-item clear (`G/item.cpp:2057-2062`) waits on the expiry
system, whose timers are `unused` (ledger 437). Improving an item drops its look because
the result is a fresh item (`CopyAllAttrTo` carries no transmutation), which
`world::character::refined_item` already builds that way.

A held material locks destroy, drop, move, give, sale and checkin (`CItem::isLocked`),
sharing the sash lock bit; the move-destination arm and the gift arm stay the Divergences
ledger 442 recorded. The attr67 regist, the trade and the personal shop run lock checks
the Rewrite never ported for the sash either, so the changelook adds none there.

The detachment scroll (`USE_DETACHMENT` with `VALUE0` 8 on a transmuted weapon, armour or
costume, `CleanTransmutation`, `:10746-10768`) rides use-on-item
(`world::character::clean_transmutation`): the transmutation to 0, the update record, the
`Transmuted` change, one scroll spent, silent on a refused target, and the locked line for
a held one. The `ITEM_FLAG_REFINEABLE` check is skipped — the flag bit is not ported — and
is the same Divergence the sash clean recorded. The owner's one detachment scroll (25100)
has `VALUE0` 3, so no wire scenario can carry the clean: it is unit-proved in `world`.

Scenario `a_transmutation_is_refused_stamped_and_banked` (eight helpers under the line
lint): past the reward pages to the eight chats, "Transmutation" opens the window with
the 50,000,000 cost. The head armour, the mount spear and the stone chat the cannot line;
the +0 sword lands in slot 0 echoing its position, the male-only armour chats the submit
line in slot 1, the fan chats it for its subtype (its job flags also disagree, so the
polearm proves the subtype arm alone: broad flags in slot 0, narrow ones in slot 1), the
held sword chats the locked line, the +1 sword lands in slot 1, and a held destroy is
silent. The male-only armour lands in slot 0 and the female-only one chats the submit
line (the sex flags disagree either way); slot 1 lifts alone with a zeroed position,
slot 0 clears both, an empty remove sends nothing, slot 2 removes nothing, the close
answers all four fields, and a second close chats the not-open line. A one-material
refine chats the submit line; the poor refine chats the gold line with no record. With
exactly the 50,000,000 stored the reopened window refines: the +0's row updates with the
+1's look, the +1 is destroyed, the gold empties, the refine answers, an add lands
nowhere and the close chats not-open (the refine cleared the window), and the disconnect
banks the stamp. Then, as an IMPLEMENTOR (the mission's non-GM login gate keeps the relog
quiet), death closes the reopened window behind the dead and the three re-added affects
(540, 215, 540) — after the stamped sword chats the already line and the polearm lands in
its place. Flake check 8/8.

Refactors for the line lint: `apply_ground` lent its window arms `apply_window_step`,
`use_item_to_item` lent its clean arm `clean_look_step`, and `write_change` lent its
holder trio `write_holder_change`.

Mutants, all killed: the close pos, the close guard, the ADD echo, the vnum arm, the job
arm, the sex arm, the type/subtype `||` (by the polearm — first `SURVIVED` twice, then
hardened), the weapon gate, the gold off-by-one, the poor gate (by the exact 50,000,000 —
first `SURVIVED`, then hardened), the remove bound (first `SURVIVED`, then hardened), the
empty remove, the slot-1 arm, the missing chat, the slot-1-empty guard, the filled-slot
guard, the add window guard, the belt guard, the already guard, the equipped guard, the
refine's window clear (first `SURVIVED`, then hardened), the `Transmuted` id, the death
close (by the death proof — first `SURVIVED`, then hardened), the locked guard, and the
clean stamp and guard (by hand, in `world`: the shared helper misreads multi-test runs).
One equivalent no-op mutant was replaced by the missing-chat drop. Two mutant binaries
were rebuilt pristine before the flake check.

row notes the cleaner. Sub-headers: the four `sub.ChangeLook.*` `ported` (49 `ported` /
64 `missing`). Quests: `quest.changelook` notes the window

## 444. The Gaya craft and market

`cg.game.gaya_system`, its three sub-headers, `cmd.w_gaya`, `data.gaya` and
`sys.custom.gaya` are `ported`, all behind `a_gaya_craft_spends_and_a_market_opens`.

The record's header byte 241 is the shadowed one: it frames as 67 bytes
(`TPacketCGClientVersion2`, first-wins in `CPacketInfoCG`) while the client sends 6
(`protocol::cg_gaya_system`, committed earlier). A phase-aware override frames the
byte at 6 in the game and dead phases (`try_decode_fixed_override`, routed in
`client_live.rs`); a 67-byte version-shaped frame on this byte never reaches the
handler. The step has no observer gate (`G/input_main.cpp:3881-3883`), and an unknown
sub-header is consumed and ignored, as legacy's `default`-less `switch` does.

The craft (`CraftGayaItems`, `G/char_gaya.cpp:275-309`) minerals the stone at
`{INVENTORY, pos}`: a missing cell sends nothing, a non-stone or one graded past
`GRADE_STONE` chats the error line, short of the `GLIMMERSTONE_COUNT` glimmerstones
the count line chats with the stone's locale name, and short of `COST_GAYA_YANG` the
Yang line chats. Else the roll runs and a win grants `GIVE_GAYA` with the grant and
success lines; either way the window refreshes (`GayaCheck`), the stones and the Yang
leave, and the cell loses one stone. `CreateItem` of the stone cannot fail here: the
proto is looked up, and a missing one sends nothing before the count line could name
it. The module doc records the unit the legacy keys keep (`GayaValues`).

The market (`MarketGayaItems`, `:311-344`) with no shelf chats the error line, as does
a slot past 8 (a negative slot is the shelf check's business first). Slots 0-2 buy at
once (`BuyItemsGayaMarket`, `:115-128`): short of the price the poor line chats, else
the Gaya leaves and the shelf's item is given through `AutoGiveItem`. Slots 3-8
unlock with `GAYA_EXPANSION_COUNT` expansion items when locked
(`UpdateSlotGayaMarket`, `:153-173`, re-sends the markers), and buy once open; a
locked slot short of the unlocks chats the count line with the unlock's locale name.
The refresh (`RefreshGayaItems`, `:346-367`) with no shelf chats the error line; short
of the `GAYA_REFRESH_COUNT` refreshers the count line chats, else they leave, the
shelf re-rolls with the slots kept, and the markers are re-sent.

The shelf and the slot unlocks live in memory per login: relogging reopens a fresh
shelf, but the scenario proves the unlocks survive the relog (the loaded count stands
behind the unlock, and the reopened line shows slot 3 open). Legacy keeps a
`<Name>_gaya_system.txt` file per character; the path is the character name
unsanitised, and a failed `fopen` NULL-derefs (`:175-273`). Recorded as a Divergence
in `docs/STATUS.md`.

`/w_gaya` (`do_gaya_system`, `G/cmd_general.cpp:4057-4091`) runs the same three lines:
an empty line, a bare word outside craft/market/refresh, and a craft or market with
no slot are all silent; the slot is `atoi`'s reading of the second word. It rides a
new `GmLine::GayaSystem` whose rows carry the move's gold, points and quickslots
(`GmRows` grows all three; `gm_line_step` stores the gold with the rows and holds the
rest, as `finish_item_step` does).

Two scenario findings, both asserted in the test. 55002 is missing from the owner
protos, so a row that holds it sells nothing (the price leaves, no pickup follows);
the four `ITEM_UNIQUE` rows likewise, since their make path is not ported
(`unported_drop`); the buy reads the first row the maker takes. And the landed count
is what `CreateItem` keeps: only a stackable row lands its count, a lone row lands
one (`G/item_manager.cpp:251`).

## 445. The biologist and the special-group tails

`cg.game.biologist`, `gc.biologist`, the four `sub.RecvBiologistPacket.*`, and
`sys.custom.biologist` are `ported`, all behind
`a_biologist_hands_over_materials_and_finishes_a_mission`, with
`a_biologist_refuses_the_wrong_state_level_and_done_missions` and
`a_biologist_last_pick_closes_the_finished_book` pinning the bounds. The special
item groups reach the world beside it: every creation stamps the `SIGVnum`, the
load recomputes it, a worn unique or ring appends its attr rows and answers its
effect path, and a stamped quest item runs its group's `sig_use`.

The biologist (`G/Biologist.cpp`, `__ENABLE_BIOLOGIST_RENEWAL_SYSTEM__`) runs its
ten missions through `GameCommand::Biologist`: the open guards (done, no mission,
level) and sends the 115-byte window; the take guards (wait, pick-wait, overflow,
no material), draws `number(1, 100)` against 60 or 100 with the elixir (71035),
spends the material either way, waits, and on the last take pays the reward item
and the lasting affect, rises the state and clears the taken — or lifts the wait
for the client's pick on missions 8 and 9; the pick pays below the last mission
and closes with the all-done line on it; the flower (30169, 30170) shortens the
wait. The three counters are `POINT_BIOLOGIST_*` fields banked by migration 0033
and loaded beside the row; the wait's end is the `biologist.timeout` quest flag
against `quest_now()`. Six Defects stay out (STATUS): the uninitialized `byIndex`,
the unchecked flower index, the 64-byte `memcpy`, the uninitialized close level,
mission 6's `POINT_RESIST_*` landing on `POINT_ATTBONUS_*`, and the callerless
`DropObjects` with its never-firing guard.

The `SIGVnum` scans (`G/item_manager.cpp:412-441`) stamp the last group key in
map order whose `quest` bag holds the vnum (`ITEM_QUEST`), or whose `special`
bag holds it (unique, mount costume, ring). The stamp lands in `make_drop_item`
and in the load's `item_from_row`; `Gear`, `Equipment`, `item_applies` and the
quest giver thread the groups through. A worn unique or ring appends its attr
rows (`sig_applies`, `G/item.cpp:1338-1374`) and answers its effect path as a new
`MoveRecord::SpecificEffect` (`G/char_item.cpp:8592-8604`), rendered as
`HEADER_GC_SPECIFIC_EFFECT` to the mover and the view. A used quest item with a
stamp runs `Manager::sig_use` instead of `use_item`. All three are dead on the
owner's data — its one group is type-less and no quest has a `sig_use` script —
so unit tests prove them: the stamping scan, the ring's appended rows and effect
path, the render, and the miss that runs nothing.

Mutants killed by their own tests: the stamping zeroed, the applies tail dropped,
the effect arm silenced, and `sig_use` answering the `use` event and true on a
miss. The protocol count tests now pin 120 implemented game-to-client rows and 14
missing. The save round-trip pins the three biologist columns with distinct
patterns. Clippy's line lint split `bio_provide`'s finish into `bio_finish`, folded
`session_head`'s alignment read into its literal, and gave the refuses scenario
`bio_enter` and `bio_banked`.

Client-packets: `cg.game.biologist` `ported` (84 `ported` / 12 `missing`).
Sub-headers: the four `sub.RecvBiologistPacket.*` `ported` (56 `ported` / 57
`missing`). Server-records: `gc.biologist` `ported` (82 `ported` / 12 `missing`).
Systems: `sys.custom.biologist` `ported`. Gamedata and `sys.item.proto` note the
tails; both stay `partial`: the bag is never drawn.

## 448. The cube

`sys.custom.cube`, `data.cube`, `cg.game.cube_renewal`, `gc.cube_renewal`, `cmd.cube`
and the two `sub.CubeRenewalSend.*` rows are `ported`, all behind
`a_cube_opens_crafts_and_closes`.

`gamedata::cube` reads the file (`Cube_load`, `G/cuberenewal.cpp:123-242`): `strtok`
on whitespace, the case-insensitive token, the two `str_to_number` words, `#` and
empty lines skipped. `section` opens, `end` validates (`FN_check_cube_data`: no zero
NPC, material or reward vnum or count) and files; a recipe with no NPC or not exactly
one reward is skipped, and the map keys the first NPC vnum
(`Cube_InformationInitialize`, `:257-315`). A token outside a section is skipped,
where legacy dereferences the stale pointer (Defect, STATUS). The boot stops without
the file (Divergence: legacy goes on).

`/cube open` (`do_cube`, `G/cmd_general.cpp:3256-3280`) stands the window on the quest
NPC the last click named (a new `Manager::npc_vid` getter); anything but `open` is
silent. `Cube_open` (`:317-359`) is silent without an NPC or on one no recipe names,
chats `Cannot open crafting window` with a trade, a shop, a safebox, a cube or an aura
window open (`OFFLINE_SHOP` is undefined, so the `GetPrivShopOwner` arm is compiled
out), and is silent at distance 1000 or past. The answer is the four sends
(`SendDateCubeRenewalPackets`, `:519-585`): the clear, one date per recipe in file
order, the loading, then the open. The date carries the reward, the stackable byte,
the first five materials, the gold, the percent and the category truncated to 100
bytes (Divergence: legacy's `memcpy` overflows); `npc_vnum` and `index` ride 0, as
legacy's unwritten words do (Defect kept).

`Cube_Make` (`:368-516`) chats without the window, is silent past the list, and chats
on short materials or gold with neither spent. The improve cell lends its whole stack
of 40 or fewer when the sum stays at or under 100, else what 100 leaves below it; the
lent count leaves before the rolls, even on a failure. Each craft draws
`number(1, 100)` against the percent plus the lend. The spends land before the grant,
as legacy's order does; no win chats `Failed`. A win grants
`CreateItem(reward, count * wins)` as `AutoGiveItemNew` does, and no room chats
`You don't have enough space in your inventory` with the spends kept. The close
forgets the window silently, as does a warp or a disconnect.

`/reload c` (`G/cmd_gm.cpp:2716-2719`) swaps the reread file in silently; a file the
descriptor could not read keeps the old recipes (Divergence, as the `t` and `m` arms).
`CommandEntry::mid_name`'s tail chain moved into `is_tail_line` for the line lint.

`cg.game.envanter_black` and `sys.item.extend_inventory` are `ported`, both behind

`CInputMain::InventoryExpansion` (`G/input_main.cpp:1069-1075`) is a 1-byte knock the
dispatch refuses to observers (`:3711-3714`); the codec (`CgEnvanterBlack`) already
existed. The world step is `GameState::extend_inven` (`prodomo/src/game_state/extend_inven.rs`),
reached through a `GameCommand::ExtendInven` kit entry and a `belongings_step` arm:
`CHARACTER::Update_Inven` (`G/char.cpp:11763-11788`) with its price list as
`unlock_price` (`INVENTORY_NEED_KEY_START + Inven_Point() / 3`, the triples made explicit),
the two key vnums counted together (72319 and 72320), the spend one at a time from
`INVENTORY_START_DELETE_VNUM`, the `ExInvenItemUseMsg` shortfall chat, and the full-row
silence. The key constants live in `common::item_slots` with `INVENTORY_LOCK_COVER_COUNT`
(18), written in legacy's own expression rather than the equal `INVENTORY_MAX_EXTENDED`.

`POINT_INVEN` leaves `NOT_PORTED`: its arm (`char.cpp:4356-4366`, beside `POINT_GAYA` in a
new `apply_kept`) refuses a total above the cover, keeps `m_points.envanter`, and sends
the change. The model's `Inven_Point` follows the points' after the rise and at the
admission, so the scans, the grants and the save read one number. The store gains
`player.envanter` (migration 0036, 0 to 18); the load seeds the points with it, the item
load searches with it, `hold_points` carries it, and `PointsPacket` sends it. The full
suite stays green.

`INT` (`STATUS.md`). No Defect: the spend loop cannot spin — the counted keys cover the
price, so a zero count on the current vnum always finds the other one.

## 450. `CG_REFINE_ELEMENT` + `GC_REFINE_ELEMENT`

`cg.game.refine_element` and `gc.window.refine_element` are `ported`: the scroll's
window, the draw, the downgrade and the change, and 255 closes. The `USE_ELEMENT_*`
scrolls (56002-56009) stand the window through `CG_ITEM_USE_TO_ITEM`; `CG_REFINE_ELEMENT`
runs it. The busy gates (trade, safebox, cube), the min-+7 and max-+3 gates, the
element-mismatch gate, the 3,000,000 / 10,000,000 fees and the `number(1,8)` /
`number(2,12)` raises are legacy's, as is the draw's 100% table (`REFINE_ELEMENT_*_PROBABILITY
= 100`), so the failed answer is unreachable but sent on the same path. The downgrade at
+1 clears the element to 0. The landed element is stored per row (`RowChange::Elemented`,
new `ItemChange::Elemented`), and the gold record rides last, after the landed answer.

Scenario `an_element_scroll_upgrades_and_a_hex_scroll_downgrades`: the lightning scroll
stands the upgrade window on the +7 sword, the answer lands lightning +1 with one scroll
left and the fee gone, the hex scroll stands the downgrade window and the downgrade clears
the element with its fee gone, the +6 sword is refused with the min-level line, 255 closes
silently, and the store holds the landed element and the final gold. Unit tests pin the
`%d%d%02d%02d%d%02d` packing and the scroll's `VALUE0` element. Mutants killed: both fees,
the downgrade clear, the +1 step, the landed kind, and the store column (the persist check
catches a write to the wrong column).

`world::character::MoveKind::Refined` answers it; `GameCommand::RefineElement` and
`GameState::apply_refine_step` carry it. `gamedata::item_kind` gains the three
`USE_ELEMENT_*` sub-types.

## 459. The monarch treasuries (`cmd.temp`, `cmd.check_mmoney`)

`/temp` moves one of the four monarch treasury cells (`TMonarchInfo.money`,
`C/tables.h:1574-1580`) and `/check_mmoney` names one, per `do_temp`
(`G/cmd_gm.cpp:4368-4388`) and `do_check_monarch_money` (`G/cmd_gm.cpp:4299-4313`)
with the DB server's guards (`D/Monarch.cpp:122-147`).

- The store: migration `0037_monarch_money.sql` holds the four rows (`empire`
  0 to 3, seeded at 0, `CHECK` behind the world's range), and `db::monarch`
  loads them (`load_all`, a missing row reading as legacy's zeroed struct
  does) and writes a moved cell (`store_money`). A boot call in `serve`
  (`install_monarch`, in the guilds/events/rank order) installs them on the
  world before the gate opens.
- The world (`game_state::monarch`): `/temp` answers nothing outside the
  test-server mode, answers `Usage: empire money` for a word missing, moves
  silently when the cell stays within 0 to 2000000000, and reports the slot
  with the landed cell for the store; `/check_mmoney` stays silent on an
  empty line and tells `____: %d __` (byte-exact from the frozen source)
  else, 0 for a slot past 3.
- One Defect is not reproduced: the game's send guard takes the empire as a
  `BYTE` but passes the full `int` on, and the DB server indexes the array
  with it unchecked (`G/monarch.cpp:118-132`, `D/Monarch.cpp:124`), so legacy
  writes out of bounds for an empire past 3. The Rewrite refuses it
  (recorded in `docs/STATUS.md`). Monarch identities, elections and the
  remaining monarch lines wait for `sys.event.castle_monarch`.

## 462. The reward window (`cmd.reward_system`, `sys.custom.reward`)

`do_reward_system` (`G/cmd_general.cpp:4299-4310`), `CHARACTER_MANAGER::SendRewardInfo`
and `DoReward` (`G/char_manager.cpp:1831-2043`), the kill call site
(`G/char_battle.cpp:1283-1292`), the level-up call site (`G/char.cpp:4051-4055`),
and the store (`reward_solo`/`reward_global`, `G/char.cpp:12991-13049`,
`G/char_manager.cpp:1831-1863`).

- The command name reaches `split_argument`'s word list as legacy passes the whole
  line: the handler's first word is `reward_system`, the second must be `update`.
  Fewer than two words, or any second word but `update`, stays silent. `update`
  stamps the caller's open and fans the open pair: the global full line
  (`RewardData 1 1 empty`, nothing claimed) then the solo full line (every count
  0). The two changes from the first green run: the wire initially stayed silent
  because `do_reward_system` had a `gm_tail_name` arm but no `mid_name` arm, so it
  fell to `NotPorted` — wired now.
- `SendRewardInfo` fans `RewardData <global 0/1> <clean 0/1> <body>`: the full fans
  (`mission` 255) for the opener, the singles behind the open gate. The P2P
  `isP2P` fan-out has no Rewrite equivalent (one process, ADR-0002); the global
  single fans to every opener on this server.
- `DoReward` claims unclaimed globals of `kind` whose `sub` passes (fanning the
  single, paying the `{31111, 1}` prize through `AutoGiveItem`), then adds `value`
  to the passing solo rows, clamps to the row's max, fans the single, and pays the
  prize exactly on reaching the max. The row tables are `m_mapRewardGlobal`
  (17 rows, 0-16; the source names 1 twice, so the second 1 is lost) and
  `m_mapRewardSolo` (18 rows). The prize rows ride back to the descriptor for
  storing, as the GM-line prizes do.
- The kill site pays `KILL_STONE`, `KILL_BOSS` at rank 4 and up, else
  `KILL_MONSTER`, at the race with the victim's level, unconditionally (outside the
  exp `no_reward`/war gates, as the `Dead` call site does). The level-up site pays
  `LEVEL_UP` at the new level after the quest `LevelUp` raise. The other eleven
  `DoReward` call sites (skills, item use, `FIRST_ITEM`, addon bonus, `pc.do_reward`,
  shops) port with their systems; `pc.do_reward` is `unused` (no Lua file calls it,
  ledger 401).
- The store is `0039_reward.sql` (`reward_solo` with the 0-17/0-100000 checks,
  `reward_global` with the 0-16 check), loaded at select and written on the next
  save, with the second global claim keeping the first name.
- The scenario's history matters: the first draft killed the dog expecting mission
  15 to mark, but the dog is `PAWN` rank 0, so the kill pays `KILL_MONSTER`/101,
  which no row carries — the kill fans nothing. A metin stone would pay
  `KILL_STONE`, but the smallest (8001, 14550 HP) needs dozens of swings, so the
  ship-side coverage splits: the scenario proves the open pair and the dog kill's
  silence (with the second `update` fanning the same pair and `reward_solo` empty
  on the store), and the unit test `do_reward_marks_counts_and_pays_the_prize_once_at_the_max`
  proves the positive arms (the mark, the single's bytes, the clamp, the once-only
  prize, the `sub` 0 catch-all, and the at-max silence).

(`G/constants.cpp:1340-1347`), and the `Damage` arm (`G/char_battle.cpp:2322-2336`).

- The six rows are compiled in (`DUNGEON_ROWS`, in the map's order): 1092
  (60-75, `SpiderDungeon`), 1093 (40-75, `deviltower_zone`), 2598 (75-90,
  `devilcatacomb_zone`), 2692, 6001 and 6418 (100-120, `meley`, `hydra`, `jotun`).
- Fewer than two words stays silent. `rank <mob> <rank>` parses by
  `str_to_number(DWORD)` and `str_to_number(BYTE)` (`C/utils.h:20-26`, `:52-58`;
  `unsigned_word` is now shared with `gm_lines`), stays silent past a parse miss, a

  descriptor reads it from the store and fans
  `dungeon_log_info <mob> <rank> <name|value|level#... or ->`. The rank's flag is
  `dungeon.<mob>_completed/fastest/damage`; rank 1 orders least first, the others
  most first; positive values only; the join drops flags whose player row is gone.

  full line; `update` fans the full line. Both gate on `ch->IsGM()`, which the
  always-on test-server mode always passes, so both always run. The full line lists
  every row the caller's level sits in as
  `<boss>|<cooldown-now>|<completed>|<fastest>|<damage>#`, or `-` with none; a boss
  argument fans that row's single line.
- The `Damage` arm runs in `fight.rs` before the damage record: a player attacker on
  one of the six whose hit tops the `dungeon.<race>_damage` flag raises the flag and
  fans the boss's single line. The comparison is strict (`<`), pinned by the unit
  test.

  store (a recorded Divergence). The ranks therefore see what the last save wrote,

  no `is_chat_line_tail` arm, so the ask never reached the world and the short rank
  closed the connection; and the cooldown line's first draft asserted literal
  `1093|0|...` cells, but an unset cooldown is `0 - now`, a large negative — the

## 464. The OX seat and its two lines

`do_oxevent_log` and `do_oxevent_get_attender` (`G/cmd_oxevent.cpp:18-40`) are `GmLine::LogOxevent`
and `GmLine::GetOxeventAtt`: the log char-logs every still-online attender `OXEVENT
LastManStanding` in pid order and answers `[LS;814]` (the `[LS;803]` arm never runs, because
`LogWinner` always answers true, `G/OXEvent.cpp:442-454`), and the count answers `[LS;825;%d]`
with the attender count.

The seat is `COXEventManager::Enter` (`G/OXEvent.cpp:91-115`, `G/input_login.cpp:853-874`), run at
the admit right after the show and before the revive-invisible add: on map 113 (instance maps
folded onto it) while the `oxevent_status` flag is not finished, the attender spot
(896500, 24600) joins the roster and the attenders past the multi-IP kick, and the audience spot
(896300, 28900) joins the roster only. A finished event and any other foot seats nobody, and a
refused player — but not a GM — is `WarpSet` to the empire start, ordered through the client
registry as a restart warp is. The kick is `CheckIpAddress` (`G/OXEvent.cpp:119-135`,
`ENABLE_KICK_MULTI_IP_OX`): a same-host attender on the same map that is a live online character
(the `FindByPID` and `GetDesc` arms) is hack-logged `MULTI_IP_OX` and sent home, and the seat does
not land. The leave drops the seat and the roster on a disconnect from map 113 only
(`RemoveFromAttenderList`, `G/char.cpp:1827-1830`); a warp keeps both. The login mount-strip is
`ENABLE_MOUNT_COSTUME_SYSTEM`-gated and belongs to the mount-costume gap of ledger 399's note.

The two world tests (`gm_lines.rs::the_spots_seat_and_the_lines_count_the_attender`,
`gm_lines.rs::a_finished_event_refuses_and_the_leave_drops_the_seat`) seat both spots with golden
values, kick a same-host second seat, refuse a finished event to a GM with no warp order, read
both lines, and prove the warp-keep/disconnect-drop leave pair. Mutants killed: the attender
spot +1, the finished status +1, the GM arm inverted, the audience roster dropped, the online-desc
arm inverted, and the leave map 113 to 114. The first attender-spot mutant survived because the
test reused the production constants; the test now spells the golden spots.

## 465. The three-way war's lines and death hook

`cmd.threeway_info` and `cmd.threeway_myinfo` are `ported`; `sys.event.threeway_war` and
`data.map.index` are `partial`.

The forked map index is now read whole: `gamedata::forked::ForkedMaps` keeps the SungZi indices
and the pass triples with `LoadSetting`'s `%d` scan (`G/threeway_war.cpp:137-197`), skipping each
pass group's coordinates and map name. The boot loads it beside the SungZi half and refuses an
unreadable file, as `G/main.cpp:658-665` does. The world holds `Initialize`'s state
(`G/threeway_war.cpp:80-87`): regen flag 0, scores 0, no revive tokens. No owner quest starts the
war, because every `forked.*` name is `unused` (ledger 401). The unset `threeway_war_*_idx` flags
therefore select entry 0 of each list: SungZi map 114 and the pass triple 118, 119, 120. A
negative or too-large flag reads map 0. Legacy indexes its vectors with the flag unchecked
(`:201-213`), a Defect recorded in `docs/STATUS.md`.

`/threeway_info` (`G/cmd_gm.cpp:4204-4226`) speaks:
- the header;
- the map line;
- `ThreewayPhase %d`;
- one `%s killscore %d usercount %d` line per empire. The `%s` is `EMPIRE_NAME`,
  `LC_TEXT(g_nation_name[e])`. The one-argument `locale_find` defaults to `LOCALE_YMIR`
  (`G/locale.hpp:10,31`), which answers the string as it is, so the line carries the raw CP949
  nation name (`G/start_position.cpp:5-11`). The country tables do translate those three keys,
  but this call never reaches them. The count is `FCountInMap`'s PCs of the empire on the event
  SungZi map, on the caller's Channel, the legacy process.

`/threeway_myinfo` (`:4228-4233`) speaks the header and `Deadcount %d`. That is 0 for a PID never
registered, because `GetReviveTokenForPlayer` default-inserts it. The two `LC_TEXT` formats match
no country table.

The death hook is `CThreeWayWar::onDead` (`G/threeway_war.cpp:290-330`). `Dead` computes
`isForked` for a PC on any SungZi or pass map (`G/char_battle.cpp:1325-1331`), and it then:
- skips `ItemDropPenalty` (`:1337`);
- leaves `INSTANT_FLAG_DEATH_PENALTY` as it was on a monster's kill (`:1374-1381`);
- runs the hook after the penalty (`:1359-1362`).

The hook:
1. stops for a GM unless the server is a test server;
2. stops once the regen flag is -1;
3. spends one revive token (`:128-134`, an unregistered PID reaching -1);
4. stops unless the map is any SungZi map (`IsSungZiMapIndex` walks the whole list, not the
   event's) and the killer is a PC of another empire;
5. adds `GetKillValue` (1/2/3 for the victim's level bands 30-39, 40-49, 50-99) to the killer's
   empire unless it is eliminated (-1);
6. notices a nonzero score to the event SungZi map. The notice goes out on every kill on a test
   server, else on every fifth point. It is the CP949 format cut to `szBuf`'s 64 bytes and
   re-used as each recipient's format, as `SendNoticeMap` does (`G/cmd_gm.cpp:1453-1484`), and
   only on the victim's Channel.

In the owner's deployment, Shared Channel 99 hosts the pass maps 118-120 and the SungZi maps 121
and 125, but not 114. A death there spends tokens and skips the penalty, and a cross-empire kill
on 121 or 125 scores. The notice to 114 reaches nobody, and the info line's user count reads 0.

Not ported: the elimination and victory arms (`G/threeway_war.cpp:332-552`). They cover the
empire warps, the map scripts, the broadcast, the `regen_mob_event` reload and the boss spawn.
They compare the scores with `threeway_war_kill_count`. No quest sets that flag, but a
`HIGH_WIZARD`'s `/eventflag` (ledger 291) does, so they are reachable. That corrects two
`unused` timer rows. `event.questlua_global.warp_all_to_map_my_empire_event` was marked
`unused` because ledger 429's sweep found no `event_create`; it missed the `quest::`-qualified
creates in `onDead` (`:356-385`, `:443-470`). `event.threeway_war.regen_mob_event` (ledger 439)
waited on the hook that now runs. Both are `missing` again, and owner question 57 withdraws them
from questions 43 and 55.

Tests:
- The scenario `a_gm_reads_the_threeway_progress_and_its_dead_count` runs both lines through the
  real binary. Its golden bytes cover the 114/118/119/120 map line, phase 0, the three raw CP949
  names and `Deadcount 0`.
- The world test `threeway::tests::the_lines_speak_the_progress_and_the_dead_count` covers the
  scores, phase -1, the token count, and a second-Channel PC the count must not include.
- `threeway::tests::a_forked_death_spends_a_token_and_scores_the_killer` covers the bands
  (45→2, 30→1, 50→3, 100→0), the same-empire and pass-map spend-only arms, any-SungZi scoring on
  121, the eliminated skip, the regen -1 gate before the spend, and the notice's golden bytes.
- `death::tests::a_monster_kill_on_a_forked_map_sets_no_penalty_and_spends_a_token` covers the
  `Dead` wiring.
- `item_penalty::tests::a_victim_on_a_spared_map_keeps_its_items` gains the forked map. It now
  seeds the dropping dice and asserts an ordinary-map control drops. Before this, the unseeded
  draw kept the item on every map, so its arena and castle arms proved nothing: the castle-gate
  mutant survived it.

Mutants killed:
- the nation name;
- the SungZi index +1;
- the pass slot -1;
- the myinfo default;
- the user count without the Channel filter;
- the regen gate removed;
- the event-map-only SungZi gate;
- the notice's test-server arm;
- the 64-byte cut;
- the eliminated `>= 0` to `> 0`;
- both band edges;
- the penalty's forked and castle gates;
- the `Dead` flag's forked arm;

Two survivors are equivalent:
- The SungZi gate rewritten as "a pass map returns" agrees on every forked map, the hook's only

- `ThreewayPhase %u` renders the same, because the Rewrite's `vsnprintf` prints `%u` from the

Two refactors keep the 100-line limit. `Dead`'s death-penalty flag moved to
`death::death_penalty_flag`. `run_ox_line` and `run_threeway_line` now return the

## 466. The three-way war's reach, corrected

Ledger 465 claimed too much. It said that in the owner's deployment a death on the pass maps
118-120 or the SungZi maps 121 and 125 runs the three-way hook, because Shared Channel 99's
`maps` list names them. It does not. The owner's `locale/europe/map/index` lists 59 maps and none
of the forked maps 114-128; maps 1 and 113 are listed, as positive controls, and
`gamedata::map_atlas::MapAtlas::load` builds every region from that index. No character can stand
on a forked map, so `Dead`'s `isForked` is never true and `CThreeWayWar::onDead` never runs on the
owner's Game data. Legacy's `SECTREE_MANAGER` builds from the same index, so this is parity, not
a gap.

The code of ledger 465 stands and is tested against the forked maps a test builds. It covers the
two GM lines, which answer the idle war, the hook up to the score notice, and the forked-map
penalty skip.

Inventory changes:
- `event.threeway_war.regen_mob_event` and `event.questlua_global.warp_all_to_map_my_empire_event`
  are `unused` again, with this evidence. Their only arming sites are `onDead`'s elimination and
  victory arms (`G/threeway_war.cpp:356-385`, `:410-418`, `:443-470`). Ledger 465 was still right
  that ledger 429's sweep missed the `quest::`-qualified creates.
- `sys.event.threeway_war` stays `partial`: the arms wait on the forked map folders.

- The `threeway.rs` docs no longer call the arms reachable through `/eventflag`.

  (`:136-158`).
- **`/duel <a> <b> [set] [minutes]`.** The arguments are parsed as `do_duel` parses them: the set
  clamps to at most 5, a negative set becomes 1, and the minutes default and clamp to 5. Then:
  - both characters lose their good and bad affects;
  - each leaves its party, deleting a party of two or quitting with the `<Party>` line;
  - `StartDuel` takes the first empty arena, records the PIDs and the set count, warps both to
    their start points, refills HP and SP, and arms both events (`:161-193`, `:466-505`).
  - The GM hears the success or the failure line.
- **`ready_to_start_event`** (`:207-383`):
  - state 0 binds the arena and tells the `arena_potion_limit_count` notice (or the "no potion
    limit" line past 10000) and the ten-second countdown;
  - state 1 tells the start line and sends each player `GC_DUEL_START` with the opponent's VID;
  - the return and restart states 2 and 3 are also ported;
  - a missing player ends the duel with the "opponent disappeared" line.
- **`duel_time_out`** (`:386-463`): the two notices, an empty `GC_DUEL_START`, then after ten
  seconds `EndDuel`.
- **`EndDuel`** (`:533-587`): it sets peace mode, restarts recovery, stands both players up,
  refills them, unbinds the arena, and warps each to its empire's arena return point
  (`G/start_position.cpp:34-40`).
- **The end commands.** `/end_duel <name>` (`:1028-1053`) and `/end_all_duel` (`:507-531`)
  answer with the legacy lines.
- **`OnDisconnect`** (`:951-968`) tells the other player and ends the duel.

The new codec `protocol::gc_duel_start` (header 40, a WORD size and up to eight VIDs) has golden
bytes. Its `gc_inventory` row is implemented.

The arena logic was written by a delegated agent and reviewed against `G/arena.cpp` here.

Defects not reproduced (`docs/STATUS.md`):
- `duel_time_out` sends its empty record twice to A and never to B (`:447-448`). The Rewrite
  clears both clients once each.
- A self-duel, and a character already in another arena, are refused with the start-failure
  line. Legacy accepts both (`G/cmd_gm.cpp:4013-4052`, `:466-495`), and two arenas then claim one
  player.

Divergences:
- **The duel crosses Channels.** The duel is held by player id across the one process, so a
  duelist warped to an arena map another Channel hosts keeps the duel. `EndDuel` sends each
  duelist back to the Channel it started on, or to Channel 1 for one that started on the Shared
  Channel, following the Shared-Channel row of the Divergence table. Legacy's arena manager is
  per core, so such a duel ends as "opponent disappeared" (`:224-245`).
  - In the owner's deployment, Channel 1 hosts map 112 and the duel stays on one Channel.
  - The scenario hosts 112 on the Shared Channel instead, so that it covers the crossing and the
    return.
- **Event order.** Arena events due on the same Pulse run in map and list order, the ready event
  before the time-out. Legacy runs them in its heap's order.
- **An early disconnect.** A disconnect ends a duel still in its first ten seconds. Legacy's hook
  needs `GetArena()`, which state 0 sets (`G/char.cpp:1737-1740`), so it would wait for the ready
  event's "opponent disappeared".

Gaps, in `sys.event.arena` (`partial`):
- `CanAttack` and `OnDead` (sets and score);
- the observers (the observer set stays empty, as legacy starts it);
- the login re-register;
- the `IsArenaMap` hooks in items, horse and login;
- the potion limit that state 0 announces, which the item hooks will enforce.

Inventory changes:
- `cmd.show_arena_list`, `cmd.duel`, `cmd.end_duel`, `cmd.end_all_duel`, `gc.duel_start` and
  `event.arena.ready_to_start_event` are `ported`, with scenario
  `a_gm_lists_starts_and_ends_an_arena_duel`.
- `event.arena.duel_time_out` is `ported` on the unit test
  `arena_timeout_clears_both_opponents_then_ends_after_ten_seconds`: a scenario would wait at
  least five minutes (spec, 2026-10-14).
- `sys.event.arena` is `partial`.
- Owner question 59 replaces the arena half of question 52.

Tests:
- unit tests in `arena.rs`, which pin:
  - table order and duplicates;
  - argument bounds;
  - the countdown's golden VIDs;
  - the time-out's clearing and delay;
  - the self and duplicate refusals;
  - the restart, end, disconnect and missing-player clearing;
- the `gc_duel_start` codec tests and the inventory wiring test;
- the scenario `a_gm_lists_starts_and_ends_an_arena_duel`, which passed 8 of 8 in a parallel
  flake check.

Mutants, each killed semantically and restored by checksum:
- `to_le_bytes`→`to_be_bytes` on the codec size;
- the time-out's empty list→opponent list.

## 468. The arena duel's combat

The arena's two combat hooks are ported in `prodomo/src/game_state/arena.rs`, `fight.rs` and
`death.rs`. The arena logic was written by the delegated agent of ledger 467 and reviewed here.

**`CanAttack`** (`G/arena.cpp:646-689`): two registered duelists of one arena, on one map, may
attack each other in either direction; a character never attacks itself, and the countdown state
does not restrict it.
- The override sits where `battle_is_attackable` places it (`G/battle.cpp:99-151`). The
  dead-victim, BANPK, ice-damage and downed-attacker gates come before it. The ordinary PK-mode
  policy and the grade-one horse refusal come after it, so it overrides them.
- The Rewrite also requires one Channel. Legacy's managers are per process, so two Channels'
  copies of map 112 never shared a duel there. This keeps that isolation inside ADR-0002's
  single process.

**`OnDead`** (`G/arena.cpp:692-864`): an arena death credits the killer's side. Then:
- either it tells the round-win line, the score notice in A-then-B order, and the ten-second
  next-round line, and re-arms the ready event's state 3;
- or, at the set count, it tells the match-win notice and the ten-second return line, and
  re-arms state 2.

The time-out event is kept. Every branch for a missing A, a missing B, both missing, a killer
outside the arena and a zero set count is ported.

**`Dead`** (`G/char_battle.cpp:1280-1309`) asks `OnDead` after the consent-duel bookkeeping and
before the quest and guild kill hooks. An arena death keeps the victim's items and exp and arms
no 180-second dead event (`:1333-1345`, `:1461-1470`, `:1553-1594`). It keeps the dead phase, the
fan, the affect handling, the target clearing, the `m_dwKillerPID = 0` reset and the window
closes.

**The round restart** (state 3, `G/arena.cpp:325-367`) shows both duelists at their start points
and sets the GAME phase. It stands them, restarts recovery, refills HP and SP, re-encodes the view
and sends the opponent records.
- Legacy calls `StartRecoveryEvent` before `SetPosition(POS_STANDING)`, so for the dead loser it
  returns early (`G/char.cpp:3292`). The Rewrite stands first.
- The difference is not observable. The restart refills HP and SP, the next hit restarts
  recovery in `Damage` (`G/char_battle.cpp:2421`), and `EndDuel`'s Warp restarts it at login
  (`G/input_login.cpp:657`).

Quirks kept:
- the duelists can attack each other during the countdown and the pause between rounds;
- `OnDead` does not check that the killer and the victim differ (`G/arena.cpp:717-719`).

Gaps, in `sys.event.arena` (`partial`):
- the observers;
- the login re-register;
- the `IsArenaMap` hooks in items, the horse, login and `/pvp`. The `cmd.pvp` note records that
  its arena gate (`G/cmd_general.cpp:850`) is now reachable;
- the potion limit (`:812-814`).

The ordinary same-empire killer-alignment penalty is not ported, so its arena exemption
(`G/char_battle.cpp:1412-1442`) needs no path yet.

Tests:
- unit tests pin:
  - the attackability truth table and the gate precedence;
  - both sides' scoring and match wins, with golden lines;
  - every missing-player branch, the zero set count and the outside killer;
  - the death lookup;
  - the item, exp and dead-event exemptions and the killer reset;
  - an outsider's death and the resumed recovery;
- the scenario `a_duelist_wins_an_arena_round` kills one duelist through real `CG_ATTACK` frames.
  Both read the winner, score and next-round lines, then the restart, the positions, the opponent
  records and the begin line. It passed 8 of 8 in a parallel flake check.

The scenario replaces `a_gm_lists_starts_and_ends_an_arena_duel` as
`event.arena.ready_to_start_event`'s scenario.

Mutants, each killed semantically and restored by SHA-256:
- the score threshold `<`→`<=`;
- the dead-event exemption negated;
- the arena attack override removed.

## 469. The arena's edges

The rest of `CArenaManager` is ported: the login arms, `/pvp`'s gate, the item, potion and
horse refusals, the potion limit, and the bound-duelist guards. The work was written by the
delegated agent of ledgers 467-468 and reviewed here; the review fixed the ejection's Channel
routing, two test fixtures, and the 468 scenario's burst order (below).

**Login** (`G/input_login.cpp:791-839`, `enter_arena`):
- a member entering its arena map is sent the empty `GC_DUEL_START`, is unhorsed, and leaves
  its party silently (a party of two is deleted);
- a GM_PLAYER nonmember is ejected to its empire start (`GoHome`);
- a GM stays. The observer arm is unreachable (below).

**`/pvp`** (`G/cmd_general.cpp:848-872`): a caller on an arena map, bound or not, hears
`[LS;403]`; a bound victim's owner hears `[LS;522]`.

**Items** (`G/arena.cpp:1131-1170`, `G/char_item.cpp:2764-2768,3441-3540,5579-5754`): on an
arena map, a listed potion vnum (50801-50826, 50020-50022, 71044, 71055) is refused with
`[LS;1205]`; general potions obey the `arena_potion_limit` flag (`[LS;403]`) and the
`arena_potion_limit_count` count. The count initializes per character from the flag at login
(`G/char.cpp:389`), resets at ready state 0 and after each scored round (`:272-273`, `:812-814`),
and decrements on each accepted potion use. Bound duelists also refuse quest seals
(`:2843-2850`). These gates read the map, not membership: a visitor is restricted too.

**Horse** (`G/char_horse.cpp:50-51`, `G/questlua_horse.cpp:52-80`): riding and the quest ride
and summon are silently refused on an arena map. The character-level `HorseSummon` has no
gate, and neither does the Rewrite's.

**Loaded affects** (`G/char_affect.cpp:638-641`): entering an arena map drops the loaded good
affects before the mounts are restored.

**Bound-duelist guards**: emotion consent (`G/cmd_emotion.cpp:114-118`), messenger and party
requests (`G/cmd_general.cpp:2274-2278,2430-2434`, `G/input_main.cpp:2478-2503,2580-2584`)
refuse with `[LS;403]` while bound.

**Observers: unreachable, by evidence.** The only external `AddObserver` caller is
`arena.add_observer` (`G/questlua_arena.cpp:86`), which no owner quest calls (zero references
outside the `quest_functions` name list; positive control `arena.add_map` has four at
`settings.lua:93-96`; a nonexistent probe has zero). `RegisterObserverPtr` requires a
pre-added PID (`G/arena.cpp:1089-1101`), so plain entry cannot manufacture an observer, and
both observer senders are commented out (`:981-1026`): observers would hear nothing anyway.
No roster is invented; `arena.add_observer` and `arena.is_in_arena` stay `unused`. Owner
question 60 confirms.

**The ejection names a Channel** (Divergence, `docs/STATUS.md`): legacy's `WarpSet` resolves
the empire start through the P2P map table. The Rewrite sends the ejected character on its
own Channel when that Channel serves the target, else on the lowest-numbered Channel that
does; a target no Channel hosts refuses as unserved. In the owner's deployment every Channel
hosts every empire start, so the ejection stays home. The first version used a plain
`order_warp`, which the Shared Channel cannot resolve (ledger 228's known gap); the scenario
caught it.

Review fixes, all in the scenario or the tests:
- The 468 scenario's geared entry now reads the member's empty duel-start record behind the
  team list.
- The visitor and the ejected character spawn on a movable cell: (862000, 15500) is blocked,
  and the entry search steps one cell over (`GetMovablePosition`).
- A granted name that never enters keeps every team list non-empty, since an empty team sends
  no record (`LoadList` early-returns).
- The scenario drains the duelists' leave with `quiet_allowing_farm`: their departures fan
  only the multi-farm burst to the visitor. Unread, it reset the visitor's close (RST) instead
  of logging it. The visitor stands outside the 5,500 view radius of both duelists, so it
  correctly reads no insert, no duel line and no removal.

systems are not ported (`G/char_item.cpp:3073-3089,3551-3556,3841-3861,5117-5161,5334-5350,
5862-5878,9922-9932`, `G/char.cpp:11117-11131`, `G/input_login.cpp:925-936`).

During mutant testing the reviewer's `git checkout --` wiped the agent's uncommitted

## 470. The weekly battle arena

`CBattleArena` (`G/BattleArena.h`, `G/BattleArena.cpp:12-333`) and `do_weeklyevent`
(`G/cmd_gm.cpp:4475-4501`) are ported, in the new `prodomo/src/game_state/battle_arena.rs`.
The logic was written by a delegated agent and reviewed here; the review found real breakage
(below).

Reachability: maps 190-192 are not in the owner's map index and no Channel hosts them, but
the event still runs degenerately — the notices, the `battle_arena` flag and the GM lines
fire, while every map operation finds no map or NPCs and no-ops. That degenerate behaviour is
the port, and the scenario proves it. Nothing gates on the maps existing: `Start` checks only
`STATUS_CLOSE` and the empire.

What the Rewrite does now:
- **`/weeklyevent [empire]`.** At rest the word's empire (1-3) starts, else a drawn 1-3
  starts, and the caller hears `Weekly Event Start`. While running the event force-ends and
  the caller hears `Weekly Event End`.
- **`Start`**: the CLOSE and 1-3 gates, the map table, the CP949 empire and ten-minute
  notices, the first arm (60 seconds on a test server, 300 otherwise), `STATUS_BATTLE`, and
  the `battle_arena` flag set to the map index. The nation name reuses the three-way war's
  raw CP949 table.
- **The eight states**, with every notice in golden CP949 bytes and every map op: the
  five-minute and one-minute warnings, the entry line with the flag cleared to 0 and the
  regen arm, the gather-or-stones state (five stones, then the falls line), the purge and
  return state, the home warp with `End`, the boss states (the last-boss lines, the felled
  or escapes lines, the purges). The `test_server` waits are kept.
- **`End`** (cancel, clear, flag 0) and **`ForceEnd`** (the `m_bForceEnd` latch, cancel,
  re-arm at state 3 after 5 seconds).
- **`SpawnRandomStone`** (the 7 vnums, the 3 regions, the `idx` latch) and **`SpawnLastBoss`**
  (vnum 8616, the 3 positions, the latch) on every Channel's copy of the map.
- **`FWarpToHome`**: every PC on the map warps to its empire start; a GM is skipped unless
  the server is a test server. The plain home order goes out, which resolves on the owner's
  topology (every Channel hosts every empire start).

`STATUS_END` stays unassigned, as legacy leaves it. No second map table: the port reuses the
existing 190-192 constants.

Divergence: at an equal Pulse the battle-arena state sorts after Santa's return. Legacy's
heap order at equal priority is heap-shape dependent, as the other arms note.

Gaps:
- `ba.start` stays `unused` (ledger 401): no quest names it.
- `battle_regen` does not run the empire's regen file: the game thread reads no regen files
  at runtime (they load at boot in `main.rs`). On the owner's data the files do not ship and
  no copy of the maps hosts anything, so the arm is empty either way; if the maps ever load,
  it needs the boot-time entries.
- `sys.event.arena` stays `partial` on the guards that wait for other systems (fish, potion,
  talisman items, the marriage ring, costume mounts, pet and mount login).

Review fixes (the agent's verification did not catch these):
- The agent's wiring replaced the `do_end_all_duel` dispatch arm with `do_weeklyevent` and
  dropped `do_threeway_war_myinfo` from the routing list, unporting both lines, and never
  added `do_weeklyevent` to the routing list, so the new line itself reached `NotPorted`.
  All three are restored; the weeklyevent scenario passes only with the routing.
- State 7 was ported as a redundant double-gated arm with a dead branch; it is now legacy's
  shape (increment, `>= 6` escapes, else spawn).
- `battle_notice`'s doc claimed a caller-Channel-only scope the code did not implement. The
  code is right: legacy walks its whole process's client set filtered by map only
  (`G/cmd_gm.cpp:1453-1489`).
- The new routing line pushed `mid_name` to 101/100 lines; the 43 GM-tail routes moved to
  `is_gm_tail_line`, beside the existing `is_tail_line` split.
- The scenario reads the whole `/geteventflag` list: the line ignores its word and lists
  every flag in name order.

Tests:
- 6 unit tests pin the Start gates, notices and flag, the empire draw, the first three
  states, the degenerate gather-and-boss path, the ForceEnd latch and `End`, and the spawn
  and warp latches.
- The scenario `a_gm_starts_and_force_ends_the_weekly_event`: a LOW_WIZARD starts empire 1,
  reads the CP949 start line, the ten-minute line and `Weekly Event Start`, reads
  `battle_arena 190` in the flag list, force-ends and reads `Weekly Event End`. It passed 8
  of 8 in a parallel flake check. The long waits are unit-proven (spec, 2026-10-14).

Mutants, each killed semantically and restored by checksum:
- state 2's flag clear dropped;
- the force-end re-arm moved to state 4.

Inventory: `cmd.weeklyevent` and `event.BattleArena.battle_arena_event` are `ported`;
`sys.event.arena` stays `partial` with the remaining list. Owner question 52's battle-arena
third is answered by the port.
