## 472. The world boss

`CWorldBoss` (`G/worldboss.h`, `G/worldboss.cpp:1-908`) and `do_worldboss`
(`G/cmd_gm.cpp:5204-5237`) are ported. A delegated agent wrote the first pass
(the table reader, the GC codec, the state machine, the wiring); the review
found real breakage and finished the slice (the CG dispatch, the hooks, the
boot load, the tests, the scenario).

What the Rewrite does now:
- **`/worldboss`**: the three-line usage for an empty word; case-insensitive
  `start`/`stop` through the `world_boss_event` flag bridge (which legacy runs
  in `SetEventFlag`, `G/questmanager.cpp:1344-1348`); `flush` parses and lands
  nowhere; any other word is silent.
- **`Enable`**: re-initialise, start the cooldown and speak (or speak the
  completion), then every connected PC hears its quest letter for
  `daily_world_boss` where the quest exists and its `worldboss %d` command line.
- **The three timers** on Pulse countdowns: the one-shot cooldown runs the run
  time; the every-second combat arm starts the cooldown past the duration and
  escapes a spawned boss at half; the one-shot spawn stands the boss. The
  owner's table reads cooldown 1, runtime 14400, min damage 250000, min level
  30, map 61, vnum 6418.
- **`Spawn`** on the channel-1 copy of the drawn map: the random map and vnum,
  the spawn and test-server-coordinates notices, the cleared temp ranking, and
  the state flag. **`Escape`** destroys the boss and speaks. **`Kill`** ranks
  the hunters on the boss's map past the level (`>=`) and damage (`>`) bars,
  clears every connected PC's `world_boss_reward` flag first, and speaks.
- **`Process`**: the info ask (state, both absolute seconds-left, the asker's
  total, the minimum) and the damage ask (the first hit speaks, then the total
  answers). **`GetRanking`** answers the temp ranking sorted by damage.
  **`Reward`**: the spawned-state wait line, the 3-second throttle (GMs skip),
  the killed-state, flag, level, damage and rank bars, the loot line, the
  group draw with the 7200-second mall-bonus affect, and the flag set.
- **The CG/GC 148 records** (`G/packet.h:3328-3361`): the 2-byte asks and the
  24-byte info, 8-byte damage, bare head and 43-byte ranking rows, with the
  analyzer gate and the harness framing opened for the byte.
- **The hooks**: a PC's hit on the boss answers its damage
  (`G/char_battle.cpp:2401-2406`, after the damage map fills), and the boss's
  death ranks (`:1672-1673`, before the Meley arm).
- **The boot table** (`world_boss.txt`): Config/Map/Boss/Ranking read at boot.

Legacy readings that shaped the port:
- The spawn wait is always 5 seconds: legacy builds `dist` and never samples
  it (`:596-599`, `random_time` stays 5).
- A refused file leaves legacy's table zeroed: the `EConfig` defaults die in
  the constructor's own `memset` (`:134-135`), and the loader zeroes before it
  reads (`:240`).
- The congrats lines speak before the give: a failed give still spoke them,
  and only the affect and the flag wait.
- The need count draws its own roll set (a BYTE sum, wrapping), as the give
  draws its own (`GetMultiIndex` runs twice).
- `GetRankingPointsByLootLevel` has no caller, so it has no port.

Divergences: the season bank is dropped (its only sink is the SQL season table,
which no game code reads back — the ranking answers come from the temp table —
so `/flush` is silent); a refused table stops the server (legacy logs on with
zeros, as for every other Game data file); equal-Pulse fires run
cooldown/combat/spawn, equal damage ranks by stable sort, and the kill walks
VIDs in order where legacy's orders are heap/pointer-dependent; channel 1
reads as hosted here. One Defect is not reproduced: the empty-draw give
returns an uninitialised `bSuccess` (`G/char_item.cpp:9586-9589`, `:9689`).

Gaps: the quest bridges stay `unused` (ledger 401); quest `event_sets` bypass
every flag arm (pre-existing, all arms alike); no quest sets
`world_boss_event`; keyword group rows land nothing, as `/letters_open`'s draw
does.

Review fixes: the spawn-wait draw (legacy never samples; now a plain 5), the
majority-Channel heuristic (now a hosted-channel-1 check), the `EConfig`
fallbacks (now zeros), the season double-bank (`/flush` banked again after the
kill; the bank is dropped), the kill's flag reset (all connected PCs, not just
ranked hunters) and dedup (legacy appends), the reward's order (congrats before
the give), need count (the drawn subset, not all rows) and rolls (one per row,
not one), the `IsGM` throttle (any GM level or the test server), the two
`#[allow(dead_code)]` (the dead enum member and function are gone), the missing
analyzer gate (148 closed the descriptor), and the harness framing for GC 148.

Tests:
- 9 unit tests pin the line parse and bridge, the cooldown-to-runtime chain
  with both notices, the escape and re-cooldown arms, the spawn refusal and
  stand on map 61, the kill ranking and flag clear, the first-hit speak and
  damage answers, the info record, the reward gates, and the player throttle
  on a live server.
- The scenario `a_gm_runs_the_world_boss_event`: an IMPLEMENTOR on a Channel 1
  hosting map 61 reads the usage, starts (the notice and `worldboss 1`), reads
  the coming-soon, 5-second and Mount Sohan spawn notices with the coordinates,
  asks info (state 2, minimum 250000) and the empty ranking, is refused the
  reward while the boss stands, stops (the completion and `worldboss 0`), and
  reads `world_boss_event 0` with `world_boss_state 2` in the flag list.

Mutants, each killed semantically and restored by checksum:
- the usage's first line shortened (scenario);
- start setting the flag to 0 (scenario);
- the spawn armed at 6 (the unit due pin; the scenario cannot time 5 from 6);
- the kill notice shortened (units).

Inventory: `cmd.worldboss`, `cg.game.world_boss`, `gc.world_boss`,
`sys.event.world_boss`, the three `event.worldboss.*` timers and
`data.world_boss` are `ported`. Five commands remain `missing`.

## 473. The battle pass

`CBattlePass` (`G/BattlePassManager.cpp:1-345`), `do_battle_pass` and
`do_battle_pass_admin` (`G/cmd_general.cpp:4176-4294`), the `CHARACTER` block
(`G/char.cpp:12762-12990`), and `HEADER_GC_BATTLE_PASS` (238,
`G/packet.h:3507-3527`) are ported. A delegated agent wrote the first pass (the JSON
read, the table, the lines, the buckets, the hooks, the store, the unit tests); it was
force-stopped, and the rest below is the finish: the clippy cleanups, the shipped-file
pin, the scenario with the 238 framing, the mutant kills, and every verification in
this entry, which was re-derived from the sources rather than taken from the residue.

The table boots from the owner's `locale/europe/battlepass.json` (158 missions, 30
free and 30 premium tiers, `endTime` 1704578399), through a hand-rolled reader
(`gamedata/src/battle_pass.rs`): no new dependency, since adding one needs the
owner's approval first. The reader follows legacy's rapidjson rules: numbers count
only as unsigned 32-bit plain digits (`IsUint`/`GetUint`), unknown `missionType` /
`missionSpecific` / `timeInfo` strings fall back to KILL / SPECIFIC / DAILY
(`:25-68`), a mission missing a field is skipped (`continue`), and a missing or
unusable `Settings` or `missions` refuses the file (boot-fatal here, where legacy
only logs and boots with an empty or half-cleared map: a Divergence). The mission id
is the array index (`missionMap[i] = mission`). Day math counts UTC midnights and
weeks (a Divergence: legacy's `localtime`/`mktime` counts the host zone). The id is
an array index that fits in 13 bits here, so the id's low word and the reward cells'
`u32` bit patterns match legacy's.

The lines run at their legacy levels (`G/cmd.cpp:522-523`: `battle_pass` GM_PLAYER,
`battle_pass_admin` GM_IMPLEMENTOR, already in the table since ledger 226).
`battle_pass` needs two words for the usage; `open` opens once (the parsed `value`
is unused) and sends the init record; `premium` runs the premium arm on ticket
30018, with the retro tiers guarded by the list length; overlong and unknown words
fall out of the `switch` silently. `battle_pass_admin` likewise needs two words
even for the list and the reset; `completemission` tops every held row of the
named id up (legacy's unsigned underflow when `progress > maxProgress` cannot
happen, since progress never passes the cap: checked, not a Divergence);
`getmissions` lists every held row; `resetMissions` clears and re-deals, weekly
before daily, then sends the init record (`ClearBattlePass`, `:12976-12987`).
`open` never re-deals: legacy deals only under `resetMissions` and at login
(`GetBattlePass`, `:12826-12850`, splitting the ten stored rows by nonzero end
time), so a stale bucket waits for the reset.

`BattlePassAction` (`:12852-12911`) is in legacy order: the pass-expiry gate, the
slot lookup (an unknown id answers the zeroed row and stays silent, as
`missionMap[mission]` default-constructs one), the filled check, the cap with
the points flag, the completion notice, the tier loop (one notice per crossed
tier, then the free tier and, when premium, the premium tier), and the update
record. The tier indexes are unbounded in legacy (`rewardsFree[i]` past the
list reads past it): a recorded Defect (see `docs/STATUS.md`), which the port
guards. The `test_server` info line stays silent (the build is never a test
server). The kill, use-item (non-`ITEM_BLEND`, with vnum 40004 ending the use
on the premium arm before the type switch, `:2822-2831`), sell (the clamped
count), craft and drop hooks run at their legacy order positions; the shop
hook reads the vnum and count before the sale moves them. Quest flags
(`battlepass.points`, `battlepass.isPremium`) ride the existing `quest_flag`
rows, and the ten stored rows ride the new `battle_pass` table (migration
0040), written only when both buckets hold at least five (`:1635-1650`).

Byte 238 was never registered in the client's decode table (134 headers in
`protocol/src/gc_inventory.rs`; near 238 only 231, 234 and 245; controls 0xe7
and 0xea present), so the record the port sends byte-exact (9-byte head,
11-byte rows, daily before weekly, `wSize` over the whole record) is
wire-only on a live client. No inventory row is invented.

Three mission types are never reached in legacy: DESTROY, FINISH_DUNGEON and
POLYMORPH have no `Register*` call site (the string map at `:27-35` names
them, but the ten call sites at `char.cpp:1524`, `char_battle.cpp:1272`,
`char_item.cpp:2825/3196/4302/7105`, `cuberenewal.cpp:459`,
`input_main.cpp:874`, `item_manager.cpp:1327` and `shop_manager.cpp:574` never
pass 2, 7 or 8), so the owner's 32 DESTROY and 2 POLYMORPH missions can only
be completed by the admin line. MESSAGES, CHEST_OPEN and PLAYTIME wait on
their paths: the shout fan-out lives in `main.rs` and never reaches the
world, no box-open flow is ported (the two `CHEST_OPEN` sites at
`char_item.cpp:3196/4302` wait with it), and no per-minute play tick exists
(the 60 s `Save` arm at `char.cpp:1518-1524` has no Rewrite path). The
`battle_pass.lua` quest's helpers are undefined: `quest_functions` names
`clear_old_battlepass` and `monthIndex`, but no Lua body and no C++ binding
defines them (a whole-`locale/europe` byte sweep finds only the quest's own
two call sites), so `quest.battle_pass` stays `partial`. The `ITEM_BLEND`
`USE_ITEM` site at `char_item.cpp:7105` sits inside the blend-use arm, which
is itself unported, so its count waits with that arm. `maxDailyMissions` and
`maxWeeklyMissions` are parsed and never read (legacy's draw always takes
five).

Tests: 9 `battle_pass` unit tests (the byte-exact wire goldens with
byte-asymmetric values, the open-once rule, kill progress and completion with
the exact notice count, wrong-race silence, pass expiry, row re-deal, and the
admin list/complete/reset), 13 `gamedata::battle_pass` tests (the minimal
file, the fallbacks, the skip and refuse rules, the escapes, and the owner's
158-mission file pinned), the quest `command("battle_pass ...")` usage test,
and the scenario `a_player_opens_the_battle_pass_and_the_admin_lists_it` (the
usage, `open` dealing the 119-byte init record, the silent second open, the
ten list lines, the admin usage, the reset re-deal). Mutants killed: `SUB_INIT
0->7`, header `238->239`, `MIN_LEVEL 30->31`, the KILL fallback `->SELL`, and
the reward-notice `!=->==` (the last first survived on a `>= 1` chat count
and is now pinned at exactly one). `select_character`'s tail split into
`hold_selected_points` keeps the line lint.

Inventory: `cmd.battle_pass`, `cmd.battle_pass_admin` and
`sys.custom.battle_pass` are `ported`; commands are 259 ported with 3
missing, systems 383 missing. `quest.battle_pass` stays `partial`.

Gates (2026-11-08): `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo build --workspace
--locked --offline`, `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --locked --offline
--no-fail-fast` (5080 passed, 0 failed in 46 targets, up 22 from 5058), `cargo
test --workspace --doc --locked --offline`, `cargo clippy --workspace
--all-targets --locked --offline -- -D warnings`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings"
cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --locked --offline`, the 238 scenario 8x, and

## 474. The guild's buildings

`/build` and `/clear_land` are `ported` (`cmd.build`, `cmd.clear_land`), leaving
`cmd.in_game_mall` the last missing command. The six `do_build` arms run on the first word's
lowercased byte behind the land gates (on a land, the master or a GM), and `do_clear_land`
wipes the land behind the table's `GM_HIGH_WIZARD`.

`prodomo/src/game_state/build_lines.rs` (new) holds the lines. `build_create` runs the proto
gates (unknown, group conflict, missing dependency), the spend gate (test-server mode or a
player caller: price cap, gold, materials in proto order) and `RequestCreateObject`'s bounds
and occupancy gates, then stands the object and spends. `build_delete` knocks by building
VID. `build_walls` stands the four single walls facing the direction word. `build_wall_blocks`
parses the set id as `int`, the size as `char` (the low byte, wrapping, then clamped 0..3)
and the doors west/north/east/south, and runs the four side runs. The `e`/`E` arms knock the
single walls and the set's blocks. `clear_build_land` knocks every object in id order, drops
the owner, halves the clear and stands the claim stone (20040) at the land center.

The parses match `common/utils.h`: `dword` is `strtoul`, which matters because NPC VIDs live
past `i32::MAX` (the first delete test's VID is 2^31+100) and the earlier `int_word` wrap
saturated them into a miss. The set id is `str_to_number(int)` and the size
`str_to_number(char)`, which matters because 1000 wraps to -24 and clamps to 0. Rotations are
compared as the integer degrees the lines parse, never as floats.

The halves drain through the new `GmRows.buildings` field and `store_quest_land_store`
(`prodomo/src/main.rs`), which stores the create, delete and clear halves beside the quest
steps' land halves. `db/src/guild_land.rs` gains the object-row write, delete and
land-clear.

Reachability, with ledger 466's lesson: the owner's 41 object protos name no single-wall
vnum (14201-14204) and no block vnum for any of the three sets, so on the owner's data the
wall arms parse and run but stand nothing — exactly as legacy would against the same table.
The create, delete and clear arms are live, and the scenario builds 14300 (no group gates)
for gold and materials.

Evidence: ten unit tests (the player-master create and spend, the stranger's silence, the
refusals, the delete, the four walls and their spots, the clear, the block stand and erase,
the char wrap, the door split, the west word's side) and the scenario
`a_master_builds_on_its_land_and_clears_it`, which builds, spends, knocks nothing by an
unknown VID and clears. Five mutants killed: the `dword` saturation, the size wrap, the door
order (which caught a missing test — the all-doors test could not see a swap), the spend
gate, and the group gate.

Gates (2026-11-08): `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo build --workspace --locked
--offline`, the full suite, `cargo test --workspace --doc --locked --offline`, `cargo clippy
--workspace --all-targets --locked --offline -- -D warnings`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings"
cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --locked --offline`, the 238 scenario 8x, and `legacy/` is
clean. `rustfmt` and `cargo-clippy` are the `/usr/bin` pair (1.85.1). No width was measured.
Afterwards no `prodomo\_%` database remained. No ADR changed.

## 475. The land list

`gc.land_list` is `ported`: the codec, the enter-game send, and the ownership-change fan.
`protocol/src/gc_land_list.rs` (new) carries the 24-byte elements (`dwID`, `x`, `y`,
`width`, `height`, `dwGuildID`) under the 3-byte header, with the count implicit in `size`;
the widths were measured by compiling the verbatim struct bodies for i386 next to the
8-byte two-`long` control (`.scratch/probe475/`; the link needs a 32-bit libc the machine
lacks, but the `static_assert`s are the measurement).

`GameState::land_list_lines` builds the enter-game lines: each land on the viewer's map
names its guild first (`SendGuildName`, deduped per viewer), then the one list carries
every land's element in id order, as legacy's `m_map_pkLand` walks. Nothing is sent on a
map with no land. The lines ride `Shown.land_lines` into the burst directly before the
time record, where the module doc already placed them. `GameState::fan_land_update` is
`CManager::UpdateLand`'s fan: the changed land's guild names itself, then the one-element
list reaches every body on the land's map. In legacy the DB answers the `RequestUpdate`
and the game fans; the Rewrite has no DB peer, so the two ownership-change sites fan at
once: `judge_land_sets` (the quest claim) and `clear_build_land` (the wipe, whose
`SetOwner(0)` is legacy `building.cpp:1031`).

The harness reads the lines centrally: `read_land_lines` consumes the burst's NAMEs and
list (or nothing) in all four burst readers, and `finish_enter_game` stashes them on
`Entered.lands` for the scenario.

Evidence: eight codec tests (golden bytes, the empty list, the ragged size, the
truncations, the wrong header, the overflow), two world tests (the enter names-then-lists
in id order with the dedup and the off-map silence; the claim fans NAME-then-list once and
a claimed land is quiet), and the extended `a_master_builds_on_its_land_and_clears_it`,
which reads map 1's 18-land list with land 1 owned and the clear's ownerless fan.

Known gap, found by this slice's scenario draft: stood buildings never show. Their ADD
and DEL fan through `packet_around` with an `EntityKey::Npc` no sectree holds (the object
VID is not a regen NPC), so both vanish — the scenario first asserted the clear's DEL and
read the land fan instead. Registering building entities in the view is follow-up work,
not this slice.

cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --locked --offline`, the scenario 8x, and `legacy/` is

## 476. The buildings show

Ledger 475 found that a stood building's ADD and DEL fan through a view key no sectree
holds, so both vanish. This slice registers the object entity in its sectree, as legacy
`CObject::Show` does (`G/building.cpp:150-187`): the stand shows, the knock hides, and
the viewers hear both.

`GameState::building_places` (new, `prodomo/src/game_state.rs`) is the reverse of
`building_objects`: the object entity's VID to its (Channel, map), mirroring
`CManager::m_map_pkObjByVID` (`:843-844`). `map_key_of` falls back to it for an NPC key
no regen NPC holds, and `deliver_insert` answers a building insert from it, so a late
entrant walking into view sees the standing objects too. `BuildingObject::add_record`
(new, `guild.rs`) is `CObject::EncodeInsertPacket` (`:92-128`), shared by the stand, the
swap and the enter-view path; the guild field stays 0, as legacy's commented-out write
does (`:121-124`).

The three stood paths change: `stand_build_object` shows the entity instead of fanning
around the NPC key, `install_building_objects` shows the booted objects (no client hears
yet), and the knock, the clear wipe and the quest swap remove instead. The swap keeps
legacy's delete-then-create order (`CObject::Reconstruct`, `:80-89`). The attribute
region `Show` sets (`:179-186`) is not ported: the Rewrite walks by server-attr cells,
which no object writes.

The build scenario asserts the ADD (header 1, type 5, vnum 14300) before the spend
records and the DEL (header 2, the entity's VID) behind the clear's notice. Four unit
tests move with the new records: the walls and the block walls count their ADDs, the
delete reads the knock's DEL, and the clear reads the wipe's DEL. No fixture proto
stands the claim stone (the mob table is empty), which the clear test now says.

## 478. The blend use

`sys.item.blend`, `data.item.blend` and `event.item.blend_use_expire_event` are `ported`.

The blend table (`locale/europe/blend.json`, `G/blend_item.cpp:48-178`) reads at boot into
`GameState::blend_table` (production wires it in `prodomo/src/main.rs`; every quest-giver
path and the drop path thread it through, replacing the default that made blends
unportable). Creation (`CBlendItem::SetItemValue`, `:180-207`) rolls the level into sockets
0-2 and 0 into socket 3; a 0 duration reads `INFINITE_AFFECT_DURATION`, and an unlisted
blend vnum still names the arm. The owner's table lists 24 vnums; the 25th `ITEM_BLEND`
proto, 71157, is not tabled, so its use is silent.

The use (`case ITEM_BLEND`, `G/char_item.cpp:7064-7118`) runs in
`prodomo/src/game_state/blend.rs`. An unlisted vnum ends the use as a step never run. A
plain vnum (the 508xx dews and 51002) refuses with `[LS;99]` past `AFFECT_BLEND` on the
point or the free-experience row on `POINT_RESIST_MAGIC`, then counts the battle-pass
mission, lays its `SetBlendAffect` marker and `AFFECT_BLEND` on the socketed point, and
spends one. An extended vnum (only the 20201-20217 range the `IsExtendedBlend` gate lets
in; the 508xx cases in `UseExtendedBlendAffect` are dead) refuses past `AFFECT_BLEND`, the
free-experience row or the mall row on the point, past the potion row for 20202 and the
speed row for 20201 and 20217, and past a held marker when this copy does not tick; else a
held marker toggles off, or the marker lays with the socketed point and value (`over`).
Socket 3 follows the lay, the client's cell updates, and the row saves.

The tick (`blend_use_expire_event`, `G/item.cpp:2090-2115`) runs once a second per ticking
character from `process_pulse`: socket 2 counts down with its cell updated, and one spends
at 0. A start past 8640000 or on a real-time item lays no tick. A stored socket 3 of 1
restarts at admission (`OnAfterCreatedItem`, `G/item.cpp:2759-2767`); the item load's doc
says so now.

Two things are not ported. The item lock (`Lock(true)` while a blend ticks) has no field:
a ticking blend can be moved, and the tick follows it by item id. And the GM `/item` grant
path builds a bare item with zero sockets, where legacy's `do_item` runs the full
`CreateItem` — the grant gap for every item, not only blends, so the scenario seeds its
blend through the store instead.

The unit tests lay, refuse, toggle and tick (the lists cover the owner's table whole), and
the scenario `a_blend_use_lays_its_marker_and_its_echo_takes_it_off` uses a stored 20210
over the wire twice: the marker lands and socket 3 runs, then the remove names it and the
socket stops. It passed 8 of 8 parallel runs.

The suite summed 5109 passed, 1 failed in 46 targets; the failure was the known
`a_gm_flags_a_stray_dog_aggressive_and_coward` load flake, green alone. The parity
re-run hit the other known flake (`a_gm_aggregates_and_forgets_the_dogs_around`, a read

## 479. The empire rates

`sys.gm.priv` was `missing`, and eight quest rows sat `unused` behind the ledger-401
token sweep (owner question 37): the three priv grants, the four priv getters, and the
guild id lookup. The GM `/priv_empire` line already ran — the scenario
`a_gm_grants_an_empire_rate_and_every_client_hears_it` exercises it — but `GetPriv`
read only its empire arm, and the quest calls had no bridge. This slice ports the
system whole: the world holds all three stores, the quest gives queue and land, and
the getters read the step's shadow. The rows move to `ported`: `sys.gm.priv` with the
scenario, the eight quest calls with world tests by path (no quest calls them, so no
binary scenario can reach them).

Legacy keeps the grants in the DB process (`D/PrivManager.cpp`) and fans them to every
game process; the one process holds them in the world (`GameState::guild_privs`,
`GameState::character_privs`, beside the existing empire rows). `GetPriv`
(`G/priv_manager.cpp:221-244`) reads whole now: the character row first — a negative
one wins unless the 70052 unique (`UNIQUE_ITEM_NO_BAD_LUCK_EFFECT`) is worn — else
the max of the positive character row, the all-empires row, the character's own row,
and its guild's row. Expired grants read 0 before the Pulse step clears them, as the
empire arm already did. The character and guild grants arrive only through the quest
calls; the GM `priv_guild` line still dead-ends in its empty Lua buffer, unported, as
before.

The bridge follows the quiet-call pattern. `quest::manager` routes the eight globals
through a new `priv_api` (`is_priv_name` keeps `api` under the line lint): the gives
stage into the `Fake` in tests and into the session queues live
(`give_guild_priv`, `give_character_priv`, `give_empire_priv_quest`, with the
reader behind the character call), and the getters push the shadow's answer, 0 for a
non-number pair. `apply_quiet_calls` lands the queued gives after the step
(`grant_guild_priv`, `grant_character_priv`, `grant_empire_priv_quest`), each with
its legacy clamp and notice: the guild grant's byte-exact format to every client when
the guild stands, silence when it does not; the empire grant's `[LS;724]` line; the
character grant's quiet 2-hour good or 1-hour bad lay, refusing a second grant while
one stands and a zero. The getters shadow the step's stores (`PrivShadow`: the empire
and guild snapshots and the Pulse), including the guild id lookup by byte-equal name
(`FindGuildByName`, `G/guild_manager.cpp:198-207`, now `Guilds::named_id`, which the
GM line also uses) and the two `name : value% (hours hours)` string builders, whose
hours helper (`priv_hours`) keeps the seconds-to-float conversion exact. The character
store is deliberately not shadowed: legacy has no quest getter for it
(`GetPrivByCharacter` serves only `GetPriv`).

Two refactors came with the threading. `arm_quest_session` passed the line lint, so
its head triple moved into `armed_head`, its context arm into `armed_context`, and
the 40-line destructure gave way to direct `self` paths. `quest::manager`'s `api`
and `quiet_api` each passed it too, so the priv arms live in `priv_api`.

The unit tests pin the new arms: the character loss wins over a 200 empire gain until
the unique is worn, the second and zero grants refuse, and the Pulse step clears; the
guild grant clamps 500 to 50, notices with the guild's name, joins the member's max,
and stays silent for no guild; the shadows read the stored value, the `None!` line,
and the named id. The quest bridge test stages the three gives and pushes the five
getters' answers. The existing scenario still passes, unchanged. The suite summed 5113 passed, 1 failed
in 46 targets; the failure was the inventory rule, which the first draft broke by
leaving the eight quest rows scenario-less — fixed by naming the world tests, and the
rule passes now.

## 480. The channel password login

`cg.login.login` was the last `missing` login row: the 49-byte password record on a
Channel (`CInputLogin::Login`, `G/input_login.cpp:101-151`). The live dispatch had no
arm for it, so the record fell through to the main input and died silent; the only
mention was the unwired router's `PasswordLoginUnsupported`. This slice routes it and
ports the row with the scenario
`a_channel_password_login_is_refused_version_or_waits_silent`.

The checks are `admit_password` in `channel_login.rs`: the test-server gate first
(`VERSION`), then the shared shutdown and user-limit pair (`SHUTDOWN`, `FULL`), in
legacy order, all answered under the handshake key through the existing
`refuse_channel_login`. `ChannelRefusal::Version` carries the new status. Past the
gate the record waits silent: its DB packet (`HEADER_GD_LOGIN = 1`) has no handler —
`ClientManager.cpp` dispatches only `HEADER_GD_LOGIN_BY_KEY`, and no DB file names
`TLoginPacket` or the header — so legacy sends nothing more and the descriptor waits.
The password itself is never read: authentication by password is the auth listener's
work (argon2id, ADR-0003), and the Channel answers only whether the gate stands.

The scenario's first half runs on `test_server = false`: the `VERSION` refusal arrives
sealed under the setup key, and a `LOGIN2` on the same wire then logs in, proving the
refusal leaves the connection open. The second half runs on the default config, where
`test_server` is on (legacy ships it on, `config.cpp:72`), and asserts the wire stays
quiet. The debugging detour is worth recording: the first draft ran the `VERSION` half
on the default config and read nothing for 9 seconds, because the default is a test
server and the gate stood open. The unit test pins the refusal order
(`VERSION` before `SHUTDOWN` before `FULL`).

`login_by_key` split into a send and `login_by_key_rest`, so the scenario can send the
`LOGIN2` after the `VERSION` read on the same `Keyed`. The suite summed 5116 passed,
0 failed in 46 targets.

## 481. The full server

`gc.login_failure` sat `partial` since ledger 185: every status was sent but `FULL`,
which "waits for an online count (`sys.login.enter`)". The count existed all along —
`context.clients.len()`, the registry of clients past the select, which the `len`
doc already ties to legacy's `GetUserCount` — and both login paths already refused
through `admit`. What was missing was the proof. This slice is the scenario
`a_full_server_refuses_login2_and_names_version_first`, and the row moves to `ported`.

With `user_limit = 1`, Alice enters the world and Bob's `LOGIN2` hears `FULL`. The
refusal arrives under the handshake key — the client key installs only after the
checks — so the scenario reads it through a new `Keyed::login_refusal`, which switches
the pair `send_login2` installed back to the setup key before the read. (The first
draft read on the pair and saw byte 220, which is the `FULL` record mis-decrypted, not
a server record at all.) The refused wire then sends a password `LOGIN` and hears
`VERSION`, proving both that the gate order holds on a live server and that a `FULL`
refusal leaves the connection open. `sys.login.by_key` stays `partial` but loses the
`FULL` item from its `Left`. The suite summed 5116 passed, 1 failed in 46 targets; the
failure was `boot_hands_the_regens_their_spawner_and_the_vids_it_left`, off by one VID
under load and green alone — a new flake, unrelated to this slice (no world code

## 486. The stacking skin

`sys.item.stack_attribute` was `missing` while the owner's file sat in the snapshot all
along: `locale/europe/item_stack_attribute.txt` holds one group, `Skin-Aquarian-Pumnal`
(40130), with a monster row (any race, apply 63, 25 per, ceiling 2500), a stone row
(apply 61, 20 per, ceiling 2000) and a boss row at vnum 591 (apply 63, 15 per, ceiling
1500). This slice ports it whole, and the real-time expiry it stands on.

`gamedata::stack_attribute` reads the table as `ReadItemStackAttrFile` does
(`G/item_stack_attribute.cpp:27-107`): groups of a `vnum` and up to three numbered rows
of five `str_to_number` ints, the first missing number ending the scan, no `vnum` refusing
the file, first group winning a repeat. Legacy reads it from a hardcoded
`locale/germany/` path (`:25`); the Rewrite reads it from the Locale folder. Boot holds
the table on the game thread (`main.rs`, `game_state.rs`).

`game_state::stack_attr` runs the feeds. The kill (`G/char_battle.cpp:1524-1549`) feeds
monster, stone or boss at the race when the killer is a PC near the victim's level,
after the boss-kill log and before `GC_DEAD`; the two `UseItem` tails
(`G/char_item.cpp:7375,7398`) feed the used vnum as an item feed after a `UseItemEx`
that returned true. Each worn costume weapon, then costume pet, is fed row by row
(`AddStackAttribute`, `:126-155`): a row whose feed vnum is 0 or the fed vnum runs
`SetStackAttributeIndex` (`:156-205`), which stamps the flood, then adds one to the
row's odd slot (1, 3, 5), recomputes the even slot (0, 2, 4) as the odd over the
progress with the row's apply, and `ApplyPoint`s the apply by 1 when the even slot
changed — while the odd slot sits below the ceiling. Each `SetForceAttribute` sends
its update and saves, in legacy's order. The flood gate (`G/char_item.cpp:7180-7185`)
refuses a use within a second of a feed with legacy's line; the stamp lives on the
body, as `m_dwUseItemStackAttrFlood` does (`G/char.h:2415`). The fish type has no call
site in the checked-in server, so no row of it ever feeds.

The skin is `LIMIT_REAL_TIME` 86400, so wearing it needed the expiry:
`game_state::real_time` runs `real_time_expire_event` (`G/item.cpp:2027-2087`) every
second from the game loop. A held, worn or stored real-time item whose socket 0 passed
is removed as `RemoveItem` with the owner on (`G/item_manager.cpp:566-595`): the
quickslot sync, the wear-cell points, the clear, the recompute, the destroy row. A
stored one takes the DEL record and a new `AccountRows` descriptor order; an unstamped
first-use item waits, as the load arm does (`G/item.cpp:2775-2780`). `world`'s use
stamps the first-use starts (`G/char_item.cpp:2804-2820`) after the checks, with the
live clock passed through `Gear`, so a later refusal lands as `Declined` with the
stamps leading. `worn_system_not_ported` and the load no longer refuse a plain
`LIMIT_REAL_TIME`: its clock runs from creation, not from the wear. An expiry while
the item is offered in a trade waits, because legacy's only caller is the character's
own event and a dying trade item would strand the trade window.

The scenario is `a_kill_feeds_the_worn_skin_and_the_flood_refuses_a_use`: Beta, lowered
to level 9, wears a dagger and the skin with its monster counter at 24, kills the stray
dog, and the feed's two updates land in legacy's order — (0, 25), then (63, 1) — with
the point move and the stored row; a drink at once is refused with the flood's line,
and a second later it lands. The skin is seeded with a day of clock ahead of it, as a
stored creation-stamped item is. The expiry's proof is the unit test
`a_passed_skin_leaves_and_a_live_one_stays` (and `a_passed_stored_skin_leaves`): a
passed skin leaves, a live one stays, an unstamped first-use item waits — a binary
scenario would wait on a live clock (owner decision, 2026-10-14).

## 488. The aura absorb window

`cg.game.aura`, `gc.aura` and `sys.custom.aura` are `ported`. The quest opener has stood
since ledger 415; this slice is the request it opens onto: `CInputMain::Aura`
(`G/input_main.cpp:5294-5340`) and the absorb arms of `CHARACTER::AuraRefineWindow*`
(`G/char_aura.cpp:64-871`).

`protocol::cg_aura` decodes the dead-word prefix and the three sub-records, and the
frame resolver sizes by sub-header past the dead word. `protocol::gc_aura` gains the
77-byte `SET_ITEM`: the two cells and the `TItemData` field order. The absorb guards run
in legacy's order, then the item locks, the `SET_ITEM` answers, and the result preview
copies the main with the sub's attributes and the sub's vnum in the drain socket when
both slots fill. The check-out answers `CLEAR_SLOT`, or `CLEAR_ALL` when the main leaves
with the sub filled; the accept moves the attributes, stamps the drain socket, updates
the main, destroys the sub, and clears. The cancel answers the close only when the window
stands. Growth and evolve run their shared guards and then nothing: their systems own
their arms, and `REFINE_INFO` waits for them. `CLEAR_RIGHT` has no send site, only the
enum.

Two legacy readings are worth recording. The preview's fullness check reads the main
slot twice (`m_pAuraRefineWindowItemSlot[AURA_SLOT_MAIN]` at `:374`, a Defect the Rewrite
does not reproduce: the sub read two lines down assumes both slots, so the Rewrite checks
both). `IsAuraRefineWindowCanRefine`'s `CanHandleItem` always fails while the window stands
(the aura's own `CanHandleItem` arm refuses it), so only the standing window and the
opener within 1000 count.

The locks ride with the sash and changelook: a held item refuses the move, destroy, gift,
shop, safebox and scroll-refine paths silently, and the open window refuses the destroy.
Death closes the window with its record (`G/char_battle.cpp:1629-1631`); a disconnect
forgets it silently — its `AuraRefineWindowClose` sends to a closing descriptor — and a
warp keeps nothing either, the client rebuilding its windows on the new view.

`an_aura_absorbs_a_shield_and_banks_the_drain`: the "Bonus absorption" chat opens the
absorb window, the shield refuses the main (`[LS;1472]`), the costume lands, the shield
lands as the sub with the preview (main's vnum, 13000 drained, attribute (7, 26)), a held
move stays silent, and the accept chats `[LS;1481]` first, updates the costume, destroys
the shield and clears; the disconnect banks the drained row. Three unit tests cover the
no-window lines, the check-out pair, the cancel, the growth guard, and the locks. The
accept's clippy split moved the chat ahead of the update, which is legacy's own order
(`:845` before `:851`).

## 489. The dragon soul refine window

`cg.game.dragon_soul_refine` is `ported` and `sys.custom.dragon_soul` is `partial`:
the window opens, closes and refines grade, step, strength and all
(`CInputMain::Analyze`, `G/input_main.cpp:3885-3919`, no observer gate; `DSManager`,
`G/DragonSoul.cpp:599-1155`).

The request reaches the world as `GameCommand::DragonSoulRefine` (new in
`game_loop_messages.rs`, through `apply_refine_step`), decoded by the existing
`CgDragonSoulRefine` codec in a new `ds_refine_step` handler in `main.rs`, which is
also named in `is_belongings_step` — without that the frame never reached the arm
and the scenario's connection died, which is how the missing gate was found. The
port itself is the new `prodomo/src/game_state/ds_refine.rs`:

- the open and close flip `ds_windows` and the open answers the `(0, NPOS)` record
  (`DragonSoul_RefineWindow_Open`, `G/char_dragonsoul.cpp:60-75`); a refine without
  the window chats nothing for step/strength/all and fails, while the grade run
  chats the system-error line first (`:688-704` vs `:824-840`);
- the gather skips worn cells and dedupes in grid order (legacy's `set<LPITEM>`);
  the grade and step runs check soul-kind, same-kind (type and grade, plus the step
  for the level run), the row's count (too few and too many fail differently), the
  fee and the gamble, in legacy's order, with legacy's chat lines;
- `Gamble` is the first probability whose running sum reaches `fnumber(0, range)`,
  with the pick split into `ds_pick` so the boundary is testable: a draw exactly
  on a sum picks that index;
- the spend takes whole stacks in grid order and decrements the last, with an exact
  stack leaving (`left >= stack`: `SetCount(0)` refuses, so `>` kept a ghost stone
  — the grade test caught it);
- the fee sets `moved.gold` to the delta (not the packed `None`, which never
  stored; the scenario caught it);
- the result is made with its drawn attributes (`DragonSoulItemInitialize`:
  basics scaled by the new weight, `number(add_min, add_max)` distinct additionals
  by weight, the duration socket) because `make_drop_item` refuses `ITEM_DS`;
  `auto_give_made` (new in `letters.rs`) places the already-made stone, and the
  result record names its cell;
- the strength run pairs one soul with one normal/blessed/holly material, refuses
  past the weights (`weight(strength + 1)` missing or under epsilon) with
  `FAIL_MAX_REFINE`, spends the fee before the draw, hardens one rung up on a win,
  gives nothing on a loss at 0, and softens one rung down above 0 — the copies
  carrying the old attributes through `RefreshItemAttributes` (basics rescaled,
  kept additionals re-looked-up and rescaled);
- the all run sweeps one grade box of one slot in 15-cell sweeps through the grade
  arm, stopping when a sweep writes nothing.

Six unit tests pin the grade success (Pcg32(0,0)'s 89.4 lands grade 1 with the
`111000` stone at inventory 0), the count fail, the gamble boundary, the strength
win (prob 100), loss (89.4 beats 80, softens to `110000`) and max-refine, and the
scenario `a_grade_refine_spends_the_stones_and_lands_a_new_one` opens the window
over the wire, runs the grade refine, and checks the result, the 30000 fee, the
emptied soul inventory and the landed stone. Mutation sweep: `>=` vs `>` on the
gamble and the spend, a dropped gold delta, swapped strength draws, and the
epsilon dropped from the max-refine gate — all killed (the first and third only
after the boundary test and the `moved.gold` assert were added).

The six `sub.DragonSoulRefine.*` rows port with it. The four `sub.Aura.*` rows
ledger 488 ported but never marked are marked here too.

## 490. The switchbot

`cg.game.switchbot`, `gc.switchbot` and `sys.custom.switchbot` port with the scenario
`a_switchbot_slot_registers_starts_and_runs`: Alpha carries a sword in the base inventory and a
stack of ten switchers, moves the sword onto switchbot slot 0 (the register answers the update),
starts the slot with a wish for apply 1 at 5 (the update answers again), and within 40 reads the
client sees either the finish whisper or an item copy behind the spend's update.

The wire: `protocol::cg_switchbot` decodes the 7-byte prefix (`size`, subheader, slot) and the
START's two 15-byte alternatives; `cg_variable` sizes START at 37 and STOP (or an unknown
sub-header, which falls through the switch) at 7 (`G/input_main.cpp:5411-5455`).
`protocol::gc_switchbot` encodes the head plus the update (191), the item copy (55) and the
attribute info. The GC inventory row flips implemented (124 done, 10 missing).

The system (`prodomo/src/game_state/switchbot.rs`, `ENABLE_SWITCHBOT`): a table per player id
holding items, actives, finishes and alternatives, with the START/STOP entry, the register and
unregister the slot moves call, the 2-pulse dice, the finish whisper
(`WHISPER_TYPE_SYSTEM` from `[Switchbot]`), the out-of-switchers stop, the move gates (a potion
cannot land on a slot, an active slot's sword cannot move), the warp stilling (`leave_world_by`
sets it, the login report clears it and re-arms a live dice), and the login report (the
attribute info for every character, then the table when it has one), which rides the enter-game
burst after the fish lines (`G/input_login.cpp:956`).

The dice spends first and changes second, and the copy rides unconditionally
(`refactorized_switchbot.cpp:355-377`): the first version returned early when
`ChangeAttribute` rolled nothing (an attribute-less sword), which spent in the world while the
client and the store never learned of it — eleven ticks in the log, no record on the wire. The
fix flushes the spend and the copy on every miss. A unit pins it through the character's inbox
(the spend's `ITEM_UPDATE` and the 55-byte copy arrive for an attribute-less sword), and the
mutant (the early return restored) fails on the missing update.

Also: `MoveFacts` folds its four prototype bools into `flags` (`MOVE_*` bits), because the new
`switchbot_item` bool tripped `struct_excessive_bools`; `leave_world_by` sheds its
departure-gated half into `leave_world_departure_gates` at the 100-line limit; the START bodies
parse defensively (a short `GameCommand` body leaves the defaults); the obsolete
"variable header without a resolver" test becomes `every_variable_header_has_a_resolver`, since
all twelve variable headers now resolve; and every enter-game burst reader in the parity
harness and `game_loop_thread` reads the new report.

## 491. The bundle build

`cg.game.myshop` is `ported`: `CInputMain::MyShop` (`G/input_main.cpp:3255-3314`) and
`CHARACTER::OpenMyShop` (`G/char.cpp:805-975`). The gates run in legacy order: at the yang cap
the line refuses with the plain text itself, stunned or dead is silent, and a trade, an open
safebox, a browsed shop, an open cube or an open aura window refuses with `[LS;1014]`. Then
`CanHandleItem` refuses with `[LS;841]` (an observer, an open own shop, a smith's window, a
cube, a dragon soul window, a sash, an aura window or a changelook window); a warp cannot run a
command, so its arm is vacuous. A running quest and an empty build are silent. A total at the
yang cap refuses with the Romanian line, an empty sign is silent, and a banned word refuses
with `[LS;812]` (the word check without the mob-name check, since a mob may name its sign).
Each table is then checked: a repeated cell is silent, an ungiveable or unsellable-in-a-shop
item refuses with `[LS;813]`, a worn one with `[LS;1060]`, and a window-locked one with
`[LS;1133]`. Without a silk bundle (71049) the build spends one paper bundle (50200), and
without either it is silent. Then the sign goes around, the window stands, the polymorph
affect goes, a summoned horse is dismissed (or else a mount is unlaid), and the seller shows
as the bundle mob, 30000.

The wire order is spend, sign, polymorph: the spend's records and the sign go out immediately
rather than riding the relay, because `set_polymorph` emits immediately too and a relayed sign
would reach a witness after the polymorph's view. A re-open refuses with `[LS;841]`:
`CanHandleItem` sees the open shop before `OpenMyShop` reaches its close-and-return, so the
legacy toggle is dead code and stays dead. `CloseMyShop` (`G/char.cpp:978-1007`) runs on
`/close_shop` (which this arms; its scenario moves from ledger 458's silence to the armed
path), on death and stun, and on leaving the world: the sign clears around and the seller shows
as its job again. `gc.shop_sign` is `ported` with it. The two Switchbot sub-header arms were
live since ledger 490 and are marked now. Buying from the window is next; the silk price list
is a DB packet with no client record.

Two bounds differ from legacy. A `bItemCount` past `SHOP_HOST_ITEM_MAX_NUM` (40) stands an
empty window, as `SetShopItems` returns after `Clear` but before the `resize`
(`G/shop.cpp:92-93`); kept. A `display_pos` of 40-44 passes the 45-cell grid check but writes
past the 40-entry window vector (`G/shop.cpp:139-161`): an honest client triggers it, so it is
a Defect (STATUS), and the Rewrite refuses the table, as the slot has no window cell.

Scenario `a_bundle_shop_opens_signs_and_closes`: Alpha carries a sword and a paper bundle,
opens under the sign `Swords` selling the sword for 500 yang in slot 3, the sign reaches
Yankee beside it, and `/close_shop` clears it on both wires, each polymorph reencode resending
the witness and map 1's NPCs in key order. Units cover the armed open, the dead toggle, the
silk keep, the silent cases, and the close. Five `myshop` units and one codec test join the
counts below.

## 492. The bundle buy

A click on a seller opens its bundle window, and a buy of a standing slot moves
the item by id, charges the full price, pays the seller net of the
`personal_shop` tax, and updates every guest. Both sides settle in one
transaction, as a trade's do.

Legacy (`G/shop.cpp:610-808`, the live arm: `OFFLINE_SHOP` is undefined
everywhere, so the `:200-438` overload never compiles). The order is the
slot's, then the item's (still the seller's, or sold out), then the buyer's
gold, then the buyer's cell (a dragon soul stone to its box, anything else to
the first free base cell), then the charge of the full price, then the tax
from the `personal_shop` flag, clamped to 100. The move clears the seller's
cell and fills the buyer's; the sold slot keeps its price and item id when
`pkItem` NULLs, so a rebuy finds the item gone from the seller and answers
sold out. The update carries vnum 0 with the kept price and count
(`BroadcastUpdateItem`, `:943-988`), and trails the move's item records; the
seller's gold lands after it, then `[LS;881;%d]` with the rate, then the
seller's empire takes the tax (`SendtoDBAddMoney`, `G/monarch.cpp:118-132`).
The dead check is the NPC arm's; the PC arm has none, because the window closes
at death. The click gates are `CHARACTER::OnClick`'s (`G/char.cpp:6236-6260`):
the seller's own click and another player's check different windows, and a
failed gate answers `[LS;841]`. NPC sales from a player's window are silent
(`G/shop_manager.cpp:477-478`).

The Rewrite (`prodomo/src/game_state/myshop.rs`, `buy_from_player` with its
`myshop_buy_ready` checks and `myshop_buy_move` packer). The buyer's and the
seller's update copies ride their settled sides, so the store write orders
them after the move's records; the other guests hear theirs at once. The
monarch cell rides `TradeSettled.monarch` and stores after the exchange. The
seller's empire reads from its body card. `ShopAnswer::Settled` carries both
sides through the shop dispatch to `finish_trade`; `ShopAnswer` compares
manually now, as the outbox cannot. The dragon soul cell helper is shared with
the give (`world::character::dragon_soul_buy_cell`). One Divergence (module
docs): `ChangeGold` refuses gold that would reach the cap after the buyer's
has been taken, losing the tax difference; the Rewrite refuses first, as the
sale does.

Scenario `a_bundle_shop_buy_settles_both_sides`: Alpha builds selling the
sword for 500 in slot 3, both click the window open, Yankee buys, and both
sides store before the records arrive; the seller hears its clear, its gold,
and the update with vnum 0 and the kept price and count; a rebuy answers sold
out with nothing stored. Units cover the untaxed settle, the 10% tax with the
treasury and the `[LS;881;10]` line, and the three refusal subheaders. Three
`myshop` units, one codec test and one scenario join the counts below.

## 493. The private build

A personal panel opens and closes, and a build stands the shop on the empire's
market map, stores the shop row and the wares in one transaction, and sends
`LOAD` to the owner and the stand's `ADD_ENTITY` around it.

Legacy (`CInputMain::PrivateShopBuild`, `G/input_main.cpp:4136-4185`,
`CHARACTER::BuildPrivateShop`, `G/char.cpp:11989-12127`, and
`CPrivateShopManager::BuildPrivateShop`, `G/private_shop_manager.cpp:80-184`).
The order is the logout cancel, the stun, the ten-second wait, the trade
windows (a trade, an open safebox, an open own bundle shop, a browsed shop, an
open cube, or a smith's window), the handle check, the open shop, the dungeon,
the empire's market map (1, 21, 41 by empire, anything else anywhere), the
trade cancel, the running quest, the empty build, the banword, the three-byte
title floor, and then each table: a repeated cell, a missing item or proto, and
a negative price are logged and silent, a bundle refuses with its line, an
item-shop item with its, a worn one with its, and a locked one with its. The
stand's polymorph clamps to the bundle row (30000-30008, else 30000), each page
grids 8-by-8 with each ware one wide and its size tall, and the store answers
before `SetPrivateShopTable` and `Show` send `LOAD` and `ADD_ENTITY`
(`G/char.cpp:12160-12178`, `G/private_shop.cpp:58-92`).

The Rewrite (`prodomo/src/game_state/private_shop.rs`, `protocol::cg_private_shop`,
`protocol::gc_private_shop`, `db::private_shop`, migration 41). The build stores
as one transaction — the shop row, the wares leaving `item`, the wares entering
`private_shop_item` — and the records go out after, through `ShopStep::PrivateBuild`
and `ShopAnswer::PrivateBuilt`. The stand's VID is the owner's (legacy allocates
a fresh VID per shop; the entity table is a later slice). Shop rows reference the
character, so a departure's cascade takes them; the stand's despawn is a later
slice with the close.

Ledger 492 filed the bundle buy under `sys.trade.private_shop`, whose scope the
inventory gives as the offline shops. That was the wrong row: the bundle is
`CShop`'s PC arm, so its note moved to `sys.npc.shop`, and this slice gives the
private row its own scope back.

in slot 3, hears `LOAD`, the shop and ware store with the ware gone from `item`,
and Yankee hears the stand. Units cover the panel, the stand, the short title,
the bundle and the repeated cell, and the wrong map. Five `private_shop` units,

## 495. The private close, withdraw and modify

The shop's state flips between open and modify, the stash empties into the
gold, and the close returns the wares to the owner's window, cleans the
viewers, and deletes the rows.

Legacy (`CInputMain::PrivateShopClose`, `PrivateShopWithdraw` and
`PrivateShopModify`, `G/input_main.cpp:4189-4220,4398-4480`, the DB close,
withdraw and flip, `D/ClientManagerPrivateShop.cpp:1205-1233,1289-1320,1435-1456,
1457-1515`, the game close with `TransferItems`, `G/private_shop_manager.cpp:
261-310` and `G/private_shop.cpp:174-496`, the game completion,
`G/char.cpp:12577-12596,12598-12671`, and the owner's close,
`G/char.cpp:12135-12158`). The close runs the logout cancel, the stun, the trade
windows, the owner with its panel open, the ten-second wait, the empty stash,
the same map, and the 3000 range; the wares move back biggest-first, the viewers
hear `END`, and the owner hears `CLOSE` with the closed line. The withdraw runs
the logout cancel, the stun, the owner with its panel open, the ten-second wait,
the gold cap under `GOLD_MAX_MAX` twice with two lines, and the stash; the gold
lands, the owner hears the withdrawn line and the bare `WITHDRAW`, and an empty
shop is destroyed with it. The modify runs the stun, the owner with its panel
open, and the one-second wait; the state flips and the owner hears `STATE_UPDATE`
as its own.

The Rewrite (`prodomo/src/game_state/private_shop.rs`, `db::private_shop`). The
shop keeps its stash and state in the world, and the build opens the panel the
three gates read. The close is one transaction — the wares leaving
`private_shop_item` for `item` at the placed cells, and the shop row gone — and
the records go out after. The cheque arms are compiled out, and the special
inventories with them (`ENABLE_PRIVATE_SHOP_SPECIAL_INV` is off), so a dragon
soul closes through its box and anything else through the base inventory.

Scenario `a_private_shop_flips_withdraws_and_closes`: the flip to modify answers
`STATE_UPDATE` and stores state 3, the withdraw on an empty stash is silent, and
the close answers `CLOSE` with the ware's set, the ware home in `item` with both

## 496. The private price, move, checkin and checkout

The four edits run on the modify state: the price reprices the ware, the move
re-slots it, the checkin shelves a held item, and the checkout unshelves it back
to the window.

Legacy (`CInputMain::PrivateShopItemPriceChange`, `PrivateShopItemMove`,
`PrivateShopItemCheckin` and `PrivateShopItemCheckout`,
`G/input_main.cpp:4481-4961`, the DB price, move, checkin and checkout,
`D/ClientManagerPrivateShop.cpp:1325-1434,1653-1955` with
`D/PrivateShop.cpp:339-418`, the game checkin and checkout,
`G/private_shop_manager.cpp:405-520`, and the owner- and shop-side syncs,
`G/char.cpp:12242-12373` with `G/private_shop.cpp:524-671`). The four share the
logout cancel, the trade windows with the modify line, the owner with its panel
open, the modify state, and the one-second wait, in that order — except the
checkout, which orders the trade windows before the logout cancel. The price runs
the stun, the ware, the cap with the old price out and the new one in, and the
silent negative. The move runs the stun, `CanHandleItem`, the ware, and the grid
with the ware lifted out; a move past the window or onto a taken cell tells the
cannot-move line. The checkin runs the stun, `CanHandleItem`, the cap, the silent
negative, the held item with its owner and proto, the item-shop, worn and locked
refusals, and the picked slot when it is free, else the first free one, else the
no-space line. The checkout runs `CanHandleItem` before the windows, the ware
with its proto, and the picked cell when it names a free one, else the first
free one, else the no-space line; a dragon soul stone lands in its box, anything
else in the base inventory. The cheque arms and the special-inventory cells are
compiled out, as before.

The Rewrite (`prodomo/src/game_state/private_shop.rs`, `protocol::cg_private_shop`,
`protocol::gc_private_shop`, `db::private_shop`, and the private dispatch). The
four hops settle as one: the price and the move update the row, the checkin moves
the ware from `item` to `private_shop_item` in one transaction, and the checkout
moves it back with the empty shop's row when no wares and no stash are left. The
price and the move go to the owner and the viewers around the stand; the checkin
sends `SET_ITEM` to the owner and `ADD_ITEM` to the viewers; the checkout sends
the viewers' clear on the game thread and the owner's clear with the set on the
move. `CanHandleItem` covers this build's windows; the observer, dragon-soul
refine and warp arms have no state here.

Scenario `a_private_shop_reprices_moves_checks_in_and_out`: the price reprices
slot 3 to 700, the move re-slots the ware to 5, the checkin shelves the second
sword from cell 1 at slot 7 with `SET_ITEM`, and the checkout unshelves it with
the clear and the set, with each store write checked. Units cover the
modify-state refusal, the two syncs to owner and viewers, and the shelve and
unshelve with the ware's window round-trip. Two `private_shop` units, two codec
tests and one scenario join the counts below.

## 497. The private rename and unlock

The stand gets its name changed and its locked slots opened
(`sub.PrivateShop.SUBHEADER_CG_PRIVATE_SHOP_TITLE_CHANGE` and
`SUBHEADER_CG_PRIVATE_SHOP_SLOT_UNLOCK_REQUEST`, `G/input_main.cpp:4033,4044`).

Legacy's rename (`CInputMain::PrivateShopTitleChange`, `:4961-5000`) refuses the stunned and the
dead silently, then the non-owner or closed panel, the non-modify state, the short title
(`TITLE_MIN_LEN` 3, `C/length.h:147`), and the one-second wait, each with its line, and forwards
the title to the DB peer. The DB completion (`D/ClientManagerPrivateShop.cpp`, the title arm)
writes the row and the game side answers `TITLE_CHANGE` to the owner and re-emits the stand's
`TITLE` to the neighbours. The Rewrite's `private_rename`
(`prodomo/src/game_state/private_shop.rs:2450`) keeps the gates in legacy order with the same
lines, stores through `db::private_shop::set_title`, and sends both records on the game thread;
`finish_private_rename` (`prodomo/src/main.rs:6424`) is the store-then-send.

Legacy's unlock (`CInputMain::PrivateShopSlotUnlockRequest`, `:5051-5123`) reads a bare `WORD`
cell, refuses the stunned, the dead and `CanHandleItem` silently, then the trade windows, the
logout cancel and the non-modify open panel with their lines, demands the Personal Shop Key
(vnum 72357, `C/length.h:138`) at the named cell, and refuses past the cap
(`PRIVATE_SHOP_LOCKED_SLOT_MAX_NUM` 64, `:137`). A standing shop forwards the key's value 0 to
the DB peer; without a stand the game side grows `POINT_PRIVATE_SHOP_UNLOCKED_SLOT` at once and
decrements the key. The DB completion grows the row's count and the game side spends the key
through `RemoveSpecifyItem` and tells the viewers `UNLOCKED_SLOTS_CHANGE`. The Rewrite's
`private_unlock` (`:2559`) keeps the gates and the lines, grows the stand's count or the point
(`private_unlocked_slots`, `:2689`), and spends the key through `remove_specify_item` either way
(`private_spend_key_and_grow`, `:2705`), whose `MovedItems` carries the spend's `ITEM_SET` clear
and the point record; `finish_private_unlock` (`:6449`) stores the count and the step. The point
rides the player row (`private_shop_unlocked_slot`, migration `0042`, loaded and saved with the
rest) so a stand-less unlock survives the session.

The scenario `a_private_shop_renames_and_unlocks_its_slots` builds the two-sword shop, browses
it from the second client, flips to modify, renames to `Swords` (owner's `TITLE_CHANGE`, both
wires' `TITLE`, the row), and unlocks with the key at cell 2 (the spend's clear, the viewers'
`UNLOCKED_SLOTS_CHANGE`, the key row gone, the count grown). Unit tests cover the unguarded
title's 32-byte truncation, the solo unlock's line, and the no-key and capped refusals.

The unlock's scenario failed five runs out of six with the connection closing and nothing on
the wire. The server log named it: `incorrect binary data format in bind parameter 2` on the
item step's destroy. The build's and checkin's `DELETE FROM item WHERE id = $1 AND owner_id =
$2` bound the owner as `i32` while `destroy_row` binds it as `i64` on the same text, and sqlx
caches the prepared statement per connection by its text: whichever connection ran the build
first described `$2` as `INT4`, and the unlock's 8-byte bind died in `exec_bind_message`. The
passing run had simply drawn a connection that never saw the build. Both sites now bind `i64`
(`db/src/private_shop.rs:105,335`), and a sweep of the other seven duplicated query texts found
their binds already consistent.

## 498. The private-shop warp

The owner walks away from its stand and warps back
(`sub.PrivateShop.SUBHEADER_CG_PRIVATE_SHOP_WARP_REQUEST`, `G/input_main.cpp:4039`, and
`event.char.private_shop_warp_event`, `G/char.cpp:12399`, replacing the ledger 436 note that
waited on the shop system).

Legacy's request (`CInputMain::PrivateShopWarpRequest`, `:5014-5036`) refuses without a
character or descriptor, the stunned and the dead silently, cancels a running timed event
with its line, and refuses a non-owner with `You do not have an open personal shop.` — the
panel is not asked. The DB peer (`CClientManager::PrivateShopWarpRequest`,
`D/ClientManagerPrivateShop.cpp:2008-2062`) looks the shop up and matches the channel, the
listen port and the map, answering the shop core's address and port or `NO_SHOP`. One process
holds the shop, so the lookup and the match collapse into the ownership and no `NO_SHOP` line
is reachable; that collapse is why the peer's three `sys_err` arms have no equivalent. The
answer runs `WarpToPrivateShop` (`G/char.cpp:12435-12474`): the owner check and timed cancel
again, the panel closed with its record, the shop time zeroed (the workaround for the close
the request just made), past `IsHack(false, true, 10)` with `You can not teleport to your
private shop right now.`, and the countdown at 10 seconds fighting, 3 else, with the
teleport line. Each fire tells `%u seconds until teleport.`; at 0 the event is gone and past
`CanWarp` the owner `WarpSet`s to the table's spot, else the bare cancel line tells. A shop
closed mid-countdown leaves the zeroed table, whose (0, 0) finds no map: the owner stays.

The Rewrite's `private_warp_request` (`prodomo/src/game_state/private_shop.rs`) keeps the
game gates and the warp leg in legacy order, packs the `CLOSE_PANEL` and the teleport line in
that order, and arms `TimedEvent::PrivateShopWarp` on the shared timed slot, so an exit line
cancels it with `[LS;511]` like any other countdown. The build now records the stand's
Channel beside its spot (`PrivateShop.channel`), which never moves. `fire_private_shop_warp`
counts down and at 0 orders the shared `ClientOrder::Warp` to the stand's spot, naming its
Channel only when it differs; the shop's `CanWarp` is `is_hack` plus the viewed-shop and
open-panel arms (`:8805-8811`), while the search arm has no state yet and never refuses. The
request takes no payload, so no codec was added: the framer's bare-prefix arm already covers
it. Unit tests pin the gates, the zeroed time, the calm 3, the fires and the order, and the
closed-shop stay.

The scenario `a_private_shop_warp_request_counts_down_and_returns_to_the_stand` builds the
one-sword shop, walks 700 east, and warps: the close, the teleport line, the 3-2-1, the
sectree leave, and `GC_WARP` naming the stand's spot, which the row stores and the
re-entered character stands on; the session answers `/move_channel 1` afterwards.

## 499. The private-shop search

The search window opens, searches and hears its wares change. Legacy's search is three
client records and one fan-out: `OpenShopSearch` sets the mode behind `USE_SPECIAL` 60004
and 60005 (`G/char_item.cpp:4391-4399`, `G/char.cpp:12669-12689`), `PrivateShopSearchClose`
drops it (`G/input_main.cpp:5132-5138`), `PrivateShopSearch` answers the matching wares
(`:5140-5176`, `G/private_shop_manager.cpp:940-1094`), and `SendShopSearchUpdate` tells
every searching character (`:713-749`). `PrivateShopSearchBuy` is the next slice.

The world keeps the searchers and their glass (`private_searching`, mode 1 looking or 2
trading) and the search throttle (`private_search_at`). Using a glass runs
`OpenShopSearch` in legacy order: the trade windows refuse with their line, else the mode
sets, the bare open answers (`SEARCH_OPEN_LOOK_MODE` 21 or `SEARCH_OPEN_TRADE_MODE` 22),
and the glass is kept, as the `USE_SPECIAL` arm consumes nothing. The close drops the
mode with no answer, as `CloseShopSearch` answers nothing. The search refuses stunned or
dead in silence and a search within two seconds of the last with the wait line, then
answers `SEARCH_RESULT`, or nothing when nothing matches, as legacy's empty answer sends
nothing (`:1080-1093`).

The scan follows `SearchItem`'s three arms: a named vnum rewrites the type and subtype
from its proto (an unknown vnum finds nothing), else a named owner scans that shop alone
(`strlen` on the field, `GetPrivateShopByOwnerName`), else a non-negative type scans
every shop. `FilterItem` runs under the flag: the vnum, the refine band on weapons and
armours, the alchemy band on dragon souls (grade and strength from the vnum's digits, as
`DSManager` decodes them), the job and gender against the antiflags, the stack, the
level band against `GetLevelLimit`, and the seven attributes on weapons and armours,
where each asked type needs a ware attribute of its own type at its value or better.
The sash absorption is read and never judged, as legacy reads it. The rows stop when the
next would overflow the 8192 safe bytes, and run in owner-VID and slot order; legacy's
`unordered_set` order is unobservable by an honest client. Legacy fans the search out to
every core over P2P and merges the answers; one process holds every Channel (ADR-0002),
so the scan already sees them all.

The updates ride the two `SetState` and `RemoveItem` call sites: a flip tells the whole
shop (`pos` -1) with its new state, and a buy and a checkout tell the gone ware with
`STATE_REMOVED`. The buy's update lands before the bought line, as `RemoveItem` runs
before the bought chat (`:628-643`). A close sends no update: legacy's delete path
removes the shop without telling the searchers (`:261-310`, `:76-87`). The mode closes on
death (`G/char_battle.cpp:1635`) and on departure, and refuses the shop warp
(`G/char.cpp:8809`).

The codecs are `CgPrivateShopSearch` (the 84-byte filter and the flag, 85 body bytes) and
`GcPrivateShopSearchData` (the 101-byte row: shop, owner, vnum, price, count, slot,
sockets, attrs, checkin, state), `GcPrivateShopSearchResult` and
`GcPrivateShopSearchUpdate`, with the two open-mode subheader consts. The framer's
`SEARCH => 85` arm already covered the frame.

The scenario `a_glass_opens_the_search_and_a_sale_tells_the_searchers` grants Yankee the
looking glass by seeding her row with a live expiry socket (a zero socket expires at the
first pulse, so the console grant and a bare seed both lose the glass before the use),
builds the one-sword shop, drinks the glass, searches vnum 19, browses and buys: the
open, the one-row result naming Alpha and the 500 price, and the update naming the shop,
slot 3 and the removal ahead of the bought line. Unit tests pin the blank search's
silence, the wait line, and the flip's whole-shop update.

Drive-by: `a_dungeon_info_rank_cooldown_and_update_fan_their_lines` compared the
`test_cooldown` and `update` lines byte for byte, but the `cooldown-now` cells tick on
the wall clock, so a straddling second failed the run (the suite's one failure at
first, and 1 of 4 alone). The compare is now cell by cell, with the two `left` cells
allowed a one-second tick; 6 of 6 since.

## 500. The search buy

The search's last record settles: the buyer picks wares off the search window and buys
them without browsing (`CInputMain::PrivateShopSearchBuy`, `G/input_main.cpp:5178-5246`,
with the DB checks, `D/ClientManagerPrivateShop.cpp:1520-1650`, the game transaction,
`G/private_shop_manager.cpp:517-655`, and the DB completion, `:2102-2186`).

The gates run in input order: the stun, the open search window, the buyer's own shop
among the picks (with the own-shop line, as the browse buy's missing ware answers
it), and the shared one-second buy wait. Then each pick runs the DB checks in order:
the shop's presence (the no-shop `tradus` line), the modify state, the ware's
presence, the shown price against the standing ware (a zero cheque on both sides, as
cheque is off), and the running gold balance, which falls by each passing price, as
legacy subtracts it on the request. The first failing pick stops the pass with its
line and settles nothing. Each passing pick settles through the shared settlement,
so the viewers hear `REMOVE_ITEM`, the owner hears `REMOVE_MY_ITEM`, `SET_SALE`, the
sold whisper and `BALANCE_UPDATE`, the searchers hear the update, and the buyer hears
its bought line. A pick with no room refuses with the space line at its check, as
`ItemTransaction` finds the cell before charging; the DB completion's marks and the
peer checks have no equivalent in one process (ADR-0002), where the world holds every
shop. The store writes each settlement in one transaction each, in pick order, and the
gold delta is the picks' sum.

The codec is `CgPrivateShopSearchPick::decode_search_buy`: the ten 18-byte tables
after the prefix (the shop id, the slot and the 12-byte price, 180 bytes), ending at
the first zero shop id, as legacy's loop breaks. The framer's `SEARCH_BUY => 180` arm
already covered the frame.

search, finds the sword's row, and buys it off the window: the gold, the ware's set,
the searchers' update and the bought line. The buyer hears no `REMOVE_ITEM`, as only
viewers do. The unit test pins the wrong price's refresh line settling nothing and
the shown price's settlement.

## 501. The market prices

The private-shop record set closes: the two market-price sub-headers are the last
missing rows in the sub-header table, which is now fully `ported`
(`SUBHEADER_CG_PRIVATE_SHOP_MARKET_ITEM_PRICE_DATA_REQUEST` and
`SUBHEADER_CG_PRIVATE_SHOP_MARKET_ITEM_PRICE_REQUEST`, `G/input_main.cpp:5247-5271`,
with the game sends, `G/private_shop_manager.cpp:1113-1206`, the DB average,
`D/ClientManagerPrivateShop.cpp:722-805`, and the hourly call,
`D/ClientManager.cpp:3192-3193`).

Every settling sale notes its price in the vnum's pending list, as `SetSale` does
(`D/PrivateShop.cpp:421-429`). The hourly tick folds each pending list with the
standing average into a new average and clears the lists, as `UpdateMarketItemPrice`
does; the sums run in `i128` and clamp to the wire widths, so a pathological price
cannot wrap the average. The game cores' fan-out has no equivalent in one process
(ADR-0002), where the world holds the prices the requests read. The data request
prices the held vnums — the inventory and worn cells, the dragon soul box, and the
standing shop's wares — in cell order, and the one-vnum request prices the named
vnum; both answer zero until a tick folds a sale in, so the client never asks again.
A zero price and the cheque side 0 ride because cheque is off. The pending lists and
the averages live only for the boot, as legacy's maps do. No sale's buyer or seller
needs to be online at the tick: the world holds the lists.

The codecs are `CgPrivateShopMarketPriceRequest` (the bare `DWORD` after the prefix)
and `GcPrivateShopMarketPrice` (the 16-byte `TMarketItemPrice` row, `tables.h:1974-1978`),
with the one-row result (26) and the data result (25) encoders. The framer's arms
already covered both frames.

glass at zero, settles the search buy, and prices again: the one-vnum request and
the two-row data request both still price zero, pinning that the sale alone moves
nothing and the tick moves the average. The unit test pins the sale's note, the
tick's average, and the priced data row.

## 505. The energy's share

The new set bonus row was `missing`, but half of it had been live since ledger 213: the
two hardcoded sets (`m_mapNewSetBonus`, `G/constants.cpp:205-276`) as
`set_bonus_applies`/`is_set_item`, with a set piece recomputing the points on wear and
take-off. All 16 piece vnums resolve on the owner's data. This slice ports the other
half's reachable pool: `CBuffOnAttributes` (`G/buff_on_attributes.cpp`) for `POINT_ENERGY`.

`POINT_ENERGY` leaves `NOT_PORTED` with its `PointChange` arm (`G/char.cpp:4717-4724`):
the amount adds, then the old and new totals run `BuffOnAttr_ValueChange` as bytes — a
fall to 0 switches off, a rise from 0 arms `On`, any other change rescales. `On` sums the
eight wear cells' counted attributes (the first five slots up to the first zero type,
`CItem::GetAttributeCount`) per type and lands each sum's energy percent through
`ApplyPoint`, the types ascending as `std::map` visits them; the wear and take-off run
`Add`/`Remove` in legacy's order (add before the recompute, remove before the wear
clears); the recompute clears the pool and its re-applied affects re-arm it. `On` needs
the worn attributes, which `PointChange` never sees, so the arm leaves a pending value
that the recompute (which holds the equipment) and `change_pc_point` drain; the drain
moves the energy record past the buff's, as legacy applies the buff before it writes the
energy packet. The scenario drinks the energy crystal (51002, sockets 80/10/1800) while
wearing the attributed armour: `AFFECT_ENERGY` lands, the maximum rises by 50 before the
energy's 10, and the take-off takes the worn 500 and the share back. The divisor mutant
(`/100` to `/10`) is killed by the unit test.

Not ported: the costume-attr pool — `POINT_COSTUME_ATTR_BONUS` stays refused, because no
owner proto, blend row or quest lays `APPLY_COSTUME_ATTR_BONUS` — and the attr-change
`Remove` sites, which wait on `sys.item.attr`. The item-load test's example unported
apply moves from `APPLY_ENERGY` to `APPLY_COSTUME_ATTR_BONUS` with it.

## 507. The web-shop line

`cmd.in_game_mall` was the last `missing` command. `do_in_game_mall`
(`G/cmd_general.cpp:3382-3456`) is descriptor-pure: past the Europe gate, which this
build's `europe` Locale passes (`LC_EUROPE` under `__MULTI_LANGUAGE_SYSTEM__`, so the
country code is `eu` and the test-server default arm never fires), the caller alone
hears one `CHAT_TYPE_COMMAND` record naming the web shop:
`mall https://{mall_url}/ishop?pid={pid}&c=eu&sid={sid}&sas={sas}`, where the
signature is the lowercase hex MD5 of `"{pid}{aid}GF9001"` as `%u%u%s` prints it. A
new `Command::InGameMall` routes through the notice dispatch to `in_game_mall_step`,
which reads the PIDs from the descriptor's character and account and the two keys
from `[game] mall_url` and `[game] server_id` (plumbed into the connection context,
documented in the shipped example); without a character or an account there is no
one to sign for, which legacy cannot reach, and the line is silent. The line rides
`%s` with the URL as its text argument rather than as the format, so a `%` in an
operator's URL prints literally where legacy's `ChatPacket(CHAT_TYPE_COMMAND, buf)`
would misread it.

The MD5 comes from the `md-5` crate, already at 0.10.6 in `Cargo.lock` through
`sqlx-mysql`; the lock gains exactly one edge (`prodomo -> md-5`), no new crate
enters the graph, no version changes, and no `cargo fetch` ran — everything
resolved offline. The golden signature is pinned against the system's `md5sum`, not
the crate. The scenario boots with a distinctive shop and server ID and reads the
whole signed line on Alice's wire for the 1/1 pair.

## 510. The guild bonuses

`sys.guild.bonuses` is `ported`: `CGuild::GuildUpdateAffect` and
`CGuild::GuildRemoveAffect` (`G/guild.cpp:1456-1549`), behind `__GUILD_BONUSES__`.

The table is four level windows with first-match overlap: 2-5 lands kind 801
(devil +5), 5-8 lands 802 (undead +5), 8-15 lands 803/804/805 (boss +8, metin +8,
monster +10), 15-20 lands 806/807/807 (skill damage +8, normal hit +8, human
+10). Level 5 takes the 801 row, level 8 the 802 row, level 15 the 803 row — the
windows' shared edges resolve to the earlier row, as legacy's loop breaks on its
first match. Two legacy shapes are kept: `AFFECT_GUILD_BONUS_8` is 807, the same
value as `AFFECT_GUILD_BONUS_7` (`G/affect.h:200-201`), so the top row lands two
rows of one kind; and the removal's `break` takes the first kind found and stops,
so a kicked member of a level-9 guild keeps 804 and 805. The keep survives more
than the session: bonus rows are not in the no-save list (`G/char_affect.cpp:43`),
so the save keeps them, and no later login clears them while the character stays
guildless, as no login runs then. That is legacy's shape, reproduced literally;
the owner may name it a Defect (remove the `break`) or a Quirk (keep it).

The six seams are legacy's call sites: the update runs at login after the saved
rows land (`LoginMember`, `G/guild.cpp:294`), at join through the same login
send, and once per level an offer gains (`GuildPointChange`, `:1618`); the
removal runs at logout (`:325`), at removal (`:241`), and at disband for each
member online (`:1019`). Three orderings needed care. The join's self packets
leave the descriptor after the commit returns, so the bonus collects its frames
— point moves included, self-only — and appends them to `own` behind the skills
(the outbox/direct split would otherwise invert them). The offer commit writes
the final level before its fan loop, while legacy's level-up loop climbs one
level per iteration, so each level's update takes the climbing level. And
legacy's loop nests each level's INFO with its bonus update, so the port
interleaves them the same way.

Proof is `a_guild_level_up_lands_its_bonus_and_a_kick_takes_the_first_kind`: a
join at level 1 with no bonus, four offers climbing to level 9 with every
level's INFO carrying its own update (including the level-8 non-crossing), a
kick whose wire carries the 803 take-back and then stays quiet, and Zulu's join
at level 9 walking the three pairs behind the skills. Unit tests pin the windows
and the removal order. Four existing tests moved with the new wire: the offer
helper reads each level's bonus, and the guilded-enter helper pulls the login's
pairs — one for the Meley lobby's level-3 guild, three for the land test's
level-10 guild.

Mutants (all semantic kills): row 1 ending at 4, the removal without its stop,
and the devil value at 6. Row 2's minimum is unconstrainable either way — the
overlap shadows it in 4-6, so both mutants were equivalent and the live boundary
(row 1's maximum) was tested instead.
