## 511. The refused addresses

`sys.net.ip_ban` is `ported`: the auth listener's `BANIP` ranges (`G/ip_ban.cpp`, gated
in `G/desc_manager.cpp:164`) and the Channel login's blocked-country ranges with their
login exceptions (`G/block_country.cpp:74-151`, gated in `G/input_login.cpp:164-170`).

Legacy loads both lists once at boot — the `BANIP` file when the auth process parses its
config, the `iptocountry` and `block_exception` tables when the DB process loads, fanned to
the game over the retired peer — so the Rewrite reads them once at startup from a new
`[access]` table (`ban_ip`, `block_country_ip`, `block_exception`), empty by default, as
the owner's deployment has no `BANIP` file and no rows in either table. A dotted address
that does not parse fails startup naming its key (`TopologyError::BadAccessIp`).

The match semantics are legacy's, quirks included. A `BANIP` line's mask is
`255 - (start ^ end)` per octet and the match is bitwise, not a span: `10.0.0.0`-`10.0.0.5`
bans `.0`, `.1`, `.4` and `.5` but not `.2`, `.3` or `.6`. The `mapBanIP` hash consults
only ranges whose start shares the candidate's first octet, so a cross-octet line
effectively bans its start address only. A country range compares first-octet-high
(`htonl`). The exception matches the lowercased login, as legacy compares after
`trim_and_lower` — including for a login the field otherwise refuses, which legacy still
checks. Two dead ends stay unported: the DB-side `IsBlockedCountryIp` has no caller, and
`RequestBlockException` is defined but never called. An IPv6 peer matches by its mapped
IPv4 address when it has one and matches nothing otherwise; legacy never saw IPv6.

The seams are legacy's gates: the accept loop refuses a banned peer on the auth listener
before the handshake (Channel listeners still shake it), and `channel_login` refuses a
blocked country right after the decode, before the shutdown gate, closing silently.
Proof is `a_banned_ip_is_refused_at_auth_and_a_blocked_country_at_login`: three servers,
a banned auth connect closing with no handshake beside a Channel control, a blocked
Channel login closing after a granted auth key, and the excepted login listing from the
same peer. Unit tests pin the mask (including the xor-not-or distinguisher), the hash,
the span ends, the exception, and the mapped peer; a config test pins the table and the
startup refusal.

Mutants (all semantic kills): the mask's or, the hash's wrong end, the inverted ban
match, the country range excluding its end, the exception falling through, and the
negated login gate (killed by the scenario).

## 514. The costume mount

`sys.char.mount` is `ported`: the follower a worn mount costume summons, its follow, and
the ride (`ENABLE_MOUNT_COSTUME_SYSTEM`, `G/MountSystem.cpp`, `G/char.cpp:11117-11237`).
New module `prodomo/src/game_state/mount.rs` holds the system; `GameState.mount_npcs`
is the actor map (rider, summon item, mob by follower VID).

The port, in legacy order:

- `MountSummon` (`G/char.cpp:11117-11163`): a morph hears the Romanian line, map 113
  and the arena maps stay silent, a horse ride stops and a summoned horse goes, and
  the `VALUE1` mob (or the transmutation target's, `__CHANGELOOK_SYSTEM__` being
  defined) stands within 100 of the rider, named `<rider> Mount`, of the rider's
  empire, facing the rider's heading turned half round. A mob the spawn refuses
  stands nothing, as legacy's null `SpawnMob` does past its `sys_err`.
- `MountUnsummon` (`:11165-11194`): a ridden mount of the same mob unmounts first,
  then the follower goes. A mob 0 never unmounts: legacy's `Unmount(0)` finds no
  actor and only logs.
- `CheckMount` (`:11196-11226`) is ungated; the login gates it on 113 and the arenas
  (`G/input_login.cpp:932-936`) and the restart-now arm calls it bare (`:515-517`).
  The plain here/town arms call nothing (only the unreachable threeway arm and the
  unhosted war-map arms do), so they are unchanged.
- The `/ride` mount arm (`G/cmd_general.cpp:3529-3570`) runs after the morph check and
  returns: ridden with none summoned unmounts, unridden with exactly one mounts. The
  ride item's three-cell condition always holds past it (no unique is ever worn).
- The `/unmount` mount arm (`:2315-2350`) runs the ridden arm and returns before the
  unique-item arm.
- The ride is `AFFECT_MOUNT` on `POINT_MOUNT` for socket 0 minus now in `DWORD` wrap
  (`INFINITE_AFFECT_DURATION` for a limitless mount), plus one appended
  `AFFECT_MOUNT_BONUS` per non-`NONE` proto apply. `Unmount` re-stands the follower
  while the costume is worn (wider view first, so the insert leads the removes),
  then clears the affects and the vnum, stops a horse
  ride, unsummons a summoned horse, and clears the vnum again.
- The mount tick runs every 12 Pulses (the 6-Pulse event with the 400 ms gate, which
  skips every other fire): a dead owner, a dead follower, a lost summon item or an
  item held by another unsummons; past 4500 the follower re-stands 200 behind the
  rider's heading on the rider's map (same-map `Show` or the cross-map move, whose
  insert and view rebuild are the move's own); past 300 it runs to 200 of the rider
  and stamps its last-attacked; nearer it waits. `m_dwLastActionTime`,
  `START_RUN_DISTANCE` and `m_originalMoveSpeed` are write-only and stay out, and so
  does the follower's `SetMount` flag (only `do_purge`'s `IsMount` reads the state,
  and the tick's map is what it reads here).
- The state machine skips followers (their actor's event does everything: no chat,
  guard, leader-follow or wander); `do_purge` spares them; `destroy_npc` drops their
  entry; the leave drops them with the character.

The equip hook is `run_item_step`'s tail: the mount cell's occupant is read before the
step, and after the answer is built the taken-off mount unsummons and the new occupant
summons, in legacy's unequip-first order. That covers the move, the use-to-wear (whose
first-use stamp lands before the wear checks, so a timed costume wears through the use
and refuses through the drag), the swap, and the expiry — whose destroyed item
unsummons by the follower's own entry, with the same ridden-first order. `world`'s
`WornSystem::Mount` is gone with it.

The quest horse gates needed nothing: ledger 393's `riding_mount` already reads the
wear cell and `AFFECT_MOUNT` with the 113/arena returns. The stale `Not ported` section
in `horse_summon.rs` (names, landed in 395, and `IsRidingMount`) is removed, and the
`cmd.ride` / `cmd.unmount` notes now name the mount arms.

Reachability: the owner's 52001-52090 are timed `COSTUME_MOUNT` protos with `VALUE1`
20201 and no applies, so the scenario's ride is `AFFECT_MOUNT` alone.

unsummons; the re-stand, the follow's Goto, the dead-owner unsummon; the login gate)

stands 20201 within 100 named `Alpha Mount`, `/ride` mounts, `/ride` unmounts and the

## 516. The bonus scrolls

`sys.item.attr` is `ported`: the four bonus scrolls of `UseItemEx`
(`G/char_item.cpp:6291-6688`) — `USE_CHANGE_ATTRIBUTE`, `USE_ADD_ATTRIBUTE`,
`USE_ADD_ATTRIBUTE2` and `USE_CHANGE_ATTRIBUTE2` — through a new `Arm::Bonus` and the
world's `change_target_attributes` (`world/src/character/use_to_item.rs`). The roll
rules were already ported (`change_attribute`, `add_rolled_attribute`,
`change_rare_attribute` in `world/src/character/drop_item.rs`, the GM's attribute lines,
the switchbot); what this slice ports is the scroll dispatch around them, with the
socket-scroll case's shared gates (`:6296-6321`): a target `use_target` refuses is
silent, and a costume or a glove chats `[LS;396]`.

In legacy's order: a change scroll chats `[LS;396]` without a set, `[LS;397]` without an
attribute, and the talisman line on a talisman; then the mortal cooldown (`GM_PLAYER`,
outside the test-server mode, with `g_dwItemBonusChangeTime` above 0) waits on the
`Item.LastChangeItemAttr` quest flag, chatting `[LS;398;%d;%d]` with the cycle and the
seconds left through a new `MoveRefused::AttrChangeWait` the move family delivers. The
GM level here is the character's own: the messenger's helper mutes it to implementor in
the test-server mode, which would free every mortal, and legacy's `GetGMLevel` knows no
such mode. Else the attributes redraw — 76014's on its golden table
(`change_attribute_on`, the dead inner-subtype table `[0, 0, 30, 40, 3]` named in the
doc but passed by no caller) — the shade scrolls only on a weapon or body armour whose
level limits are at most 40, the change counts itself in socket 3, `[LS;399]` chats,
and the scroll is spent unless `VRAJESTE_PERMANENT` holds. The rare change (behind
`__ATTR_6TH_7TH__`, which is defined) wants a rare attribute; 72351 runs on 10 in 100
and every other vnum always, a miss chats `Imbunatatirea a esuat.`, a redraw that adds
nothing back chats `Nu exista bonusuri de schimbat`, and the scroll is always spent.
The add wants fewer than four, keeps the shade gates, lands on the always-100
`aiItemAttributeAddPercent` (drawn, not assumed, against a later table edit) through
`add_rolled_attribute`, and spends unless `INTARIRE_PERMANENT` holds. The fifth scroll
wants four exactly (`[LS;404]` at five, `[LS;405]` below, and past five only logs,
drawing and spending nothing); on success the scroll's own count sets the adds
(`abs(2 - count)`), so a plain scroll runs `AddAttribute()` twice — a legacy Defect,
kept: the second lands nowhere while `[LS;400]` chats. The points the target gives are
not recomputed, as legacy does not, like the GM's lines.

Staying out: the dead `ENABLE_LEGENDARY_SWITCHERS` arms (the flag is nowhere defined)
and the dead inner `USE_CHANGE_ATTRIBUTE2`-subtype test of the change case, which the
`switch` already sorted away. The `item.*attr0` quest calls stay `unused` (ledger 401,
question 37). The three `[game]` keys (`item_bonus_change_time`, `vrajeste_permanent`,
`intarire_permanent`) were already configured; they are now wired into the world
(`with_bonus_scroll_rules`), with the owner's values unchanged (60, off, off).

Tests: four world tests (the change redraws, counts and cools down; the add lands and
a costume refuses; the fifth wants four; the rare change redraws) and the scenario
`a_bonus_scroll_adds_and_a_costume_refuses` (an add on a bonus-less bouquet chats
`[LS;400]`, updates the cell and spends the scroll, both rows stored; a second scroll
on a sash chats `[LS;396]` and stays).

The scenario hunts: a `[LS;400]`-to-`[LS;401]` notice mutant fails on the add line, and
it passed 8 parallel runs against the pristine build (7 flake slots plus the
post-restore rerun; the first flake slot's output file never appeared, so the rerun
took its place).

## 518. The weapon costume and the skin sweep

`sys.item.costume` is `ported` and `sys.item.skin` is `unused`. No code changed: the
cover switch, the hide mask and the take-off-first cascade were all live from earlier
ledgers — only the scenario and the sweep were missing.

The scenario is `a_costume_weapon_covers_and_a_hide_unhides`. Alpha, a shaman, holds
the fan 7000 at cell 0 and the fan-fit Halloween costume 40106 (`value3` 5, `WEAPON_FAN`)
at cell 1. Wearing the fan banks the weapon part; wearing the costume covers it
(`ITEM_WEAPON` banks nothing with a costume worn, `COSTUME_WEAPON` banks the look,
`G/item.cpp:1164-1320`); `/hide_costume 5` unhides past the 1.5 s move window
(`SetWeaponCostumeHidden 1`, then the fan's look, mask bit 4, `G/char.cpp:5409-5419`);
taking the weapon off first takes the costume off first (the costume lands at the
first free cell, the weapon at its target, `G/char_item.cpp:919-924`), and the part
falls to 0. The armour cover rides the same switch. Three scenario traps, each worth
its line: the costume needs a `value3`-matching worn weapon or the move refuses
silently; its `REAL_TIME` clock must be stamped (unstamped socket 0 is the epoch, and
the expiry tick clears it on the first second); and the enter waits out the revive
affect's five seconds, whose end pair otherwise lands in a move's window.

The skin row died on a sweep: `__SKIN_SYSTEM__` is defined in
`C/prodomodefines.h:198` but no game source names it — the sweep of `server/server`
finds only the define. The controls are `ENABLE_NEW_PASSIVE_SKILL` and
`__ENABLE_ADVANCE_SKILL_SELECT__`, which each hit game sources. Owner to confirm.

## 519. The renewal shop and the item-shop sweep

`sys.npc.shop` is `ported` and `sys.trade.item_shop` is `unused`.

The renewal `shopex` (`CShopEx`, `G/shopEx.cpp`) is live. The boot query's table
(`InitializeShopEXTable`, `D/ClientManagerBoot.cpp:384-466`) reads from the owner's
`player.sql` (`gamedata::npc_shop::renewal_shops_from_dump`): each `shopex` row with
every `shopex_item` row of its vnum, sorted by shop and item vnum, decoded with the
legacy policy. The one column the query transforms is handed over transformed:
`price_type+0` maps the enum to its 1-based index (`player.sql:1296`,
`enum('GOLD','SECONDCOIN','ITEM','EXP')`), which is the `SHOPEX_*` selector. Keeper
9001 — on-click 1, standing on map 1 at (469200, 951700) among others — opens
`START_EX` (10) with its one tab (`protocol::gc_shop::GcShopStartEx`, 2953 bytes a
tab: the 32 name bytes, the gold coin type, forty `packet_shop_item`s whose
`price_type` and `price_vnum` are now live fields). A buy numbers its slots across
the tabs and follows the selector: gold spends gold (tripled for a stranger, shown
and charged, unlike the base shop's deliberate Divergence), secondary coins and
items count the scanned cells and are taken before the bought item lands, and
experience is checked against the held pools and lost through `lose_exp`. A 0 price
refuses, and a selector past `SHOPEX_EXP` (4) answers nothing and changes nothing,
as legacy's fall-through does. The bought item carries the row's sockets and
attributes. A sale runs the base sale path, because legacy routes every sale through
`CShopManager::Sell`, which knows no tab.

Coverage: the owner's one row (shop 1, `test`, item 50011 for 0 gold) proves the
window, the 0-price refusal and the invalid second tab in the scenario
`a_click_on_a_renewal_keeper_opens_its_tab_and_a_buy_follows_the_selector`; the
three reachable price arms and the silent fifth selector are unit-tested in world
and in the state's shop tests. The secondary-coin spend is unreachable on the
owner's data — no proto has type 32 — but shares the item spend's stack-by-stack
take, tested through it.

The item shop died on a sweep: `ENABLE_ITEMSHOP` and `ENABLE_ITEMSHOP_TO_INVENTORY`
are defined (`C/prodomodefines.h:153-154`) but no game source names them, no game
source names `coins`, no client or GC record carries the shop, and no quest or
locale file reaches it. The shop lives in the retired DB server only
(`D/ClientManager.cpp`). The account's `coins` stay an Operator currency. The
secondary-coin `shopex` arm above is not it: it spends items of type 32, and the
owner's data has none. Owner to confirm.

`sys.skill.buff_npc` is `ported`.

The toggle 69700 flips its socket-3 bit (`OnUseToggleItem`, `G/ItemUtils.cpp:177-196`):

`ActivateToggleItem` (`:58-102`), and a stack past 1 unstacks first — the count drops

no-room line when there is none (`:61-76`). The group check reads value 5 and no

group 0 there, not 1 — value 0's 1 is the wear flag). The world's
`use_toggle_item` answers the flip with the socket write, the unstack, and the store
changes; the state flips the summon, then runs `CheckMaximumPoints` and
`UpdatePacket` (`:99-101`, `:129-131`).

The summon stands mob 20114 within 100 of the owner (`CShamanActor::Summon`,
`G/ShamanSystem.cpp:93-141`), of the owner's empire with the name `Buff`, facing the
owner's heading turned half round, wearing armour 11899 with weapon 5109
(`UpdateEquipment`, `:143-150`) — the parts the additional record names. The follow
runs every 3 Pulses (the `shamansystem_update_event`, `:50-68`): a moved or dropped
summon item unsummons, then a live owner is buffed (`CShamanActor::Update`,
`:161-172`) and the follower walks — running past 750 — to 250 of the owner,
re-standing 200 behind past 4500 (`UpdateFollowAI`, `:447-487`).

`UseSkills` (`:392-416`) casts the first missing buff of the five, in index order,
one per tick past a 3-second stamp: 94 (`AFF_HOSIN`, `POINT_RESIST_NORMAL_DAMAGE`,
1.3x level), 95 (`AFF_BOHO`, `POINT_MAX_HP`, 100x level), 96 (`AFF_GICHEON`,
`POINT_CRITICAL_PCT`, 1.3x level), 111 (`AFF_JEUNGRYEOK`, `POINT_ATT_GRADE`, 8.75x
level, premium), 110 (`AFF_KWAESOK`, `POINT_NORMAL_HIT_DAMAGE_BONUS`, 0.3x level,
premium, plus a same-flag `POINT_CASTING_SPEED` row of the bare level). Each lands

level-30 stone line, the 65% read counts past the level's books until the level
climbs, the report follows, and the fresh buff casts at once. The quest arms

socket write, both report lines, the 94 cast with its level-20 record, and the

## 522. The siege and kingdom wars

`sys.event.manager` carries its war arms (13-14); `gc.event_kw_score` is `ported`;
`event.event_manager.warp_all_to_village_event` is `partial`.

Both wars run on map 103 (`metin2_map_t1`, in the owner's index, hosted by every
Channel). The siege start stands the three kingdom stones (8020-8022) at the base
plus offsets on every Channel hosting 103, clears the defeat count and the three
score flags, chats the start and raises `siege_war_event`
(`SetSiegeWarEvent(true)`, `G/event_manager.cpp:1531-1565`). A stone a PC kills on
103 chats its empire's line, counts the defeat, queues that empire's 3 s home
warp, and on the second defeat writes its score flag at once, then ends the war
(`OnDead`'s stone arms, `:833-923`). The end pays each empire 25, 50 or 100 exp
(the winner's 3 also 50 loot) for 48 hours by rank — an undefeated empire takes
the `m_bSiegeScore + 1` fallback — clears the flags, chats the end, queues the
60 s home warp, kills the monsters, stones and veins on 103 (`FKillSectree`,
`:191-203`), and chats the map the teleport line (`:1566-1658`). The kingdom
start zeroes the four score rows and chats the start; a player a PC of another
empire kills on 103 counts one for the killer's empire and fans the score
record to every PC on 103; the end pays by the sorted rows' positions
(all-empires holds 0 and sorts first, so the kingdoms take 1-3), clears the
rows, chats the end, queues the 60 s warp and chats the teleport line

## 523. The OX quiz engine

The panel index 11 starts the OX event (`CEventManager::SetOXEvent`,
`G/event_manager.cpp:1482-1525`): the start refuses while `oxevent_status` holds
or the process runs, clears the quiz list, loads `oxquiz.lua` beside the quests,
chats the start, arms the open process with five registration minutes and three
rounds, and opens the status. The end chats, finishes the flag and the status,
warps the roster home and disarms. The process (`ox_event_process`, `:1376-1478`)
counts the open minutes down with their lines, closes the entries and spends a
round, quizzes while more than five attenders stand, pays the 50109 reward and
chats the teleport line at five or fewer, and turns the round or ends the event.
A quiz draws one level-1 question, chats the header, the text and the footer,
arms the timer with the answer, quizzes the status and leaves the list; the
timer (`oxevent_timer`, `G/OXEvent.cpp:226-272`) waits, checks, and warps the
misses to the audience before closing. The check fails the wrong foot with
`SE_FAIL` into the miss list, passes the right foot with `[LS;980]`, a cheer and
`SE_SUCCESS`, and drops the offline from the attenders, the roster and the
misses. The 113 entry strips the ride first, in legacy's order.

Reachability first, as ledger 466 taught: the attender seat, the audience seat,
both answer halves and all four miss spots sit inside map 113's 8x8 `server_attr`
on cells holding attribute 4 (no-fight), so the whole engine runs on the owner's
data. The loader (`quest::ox_quiz`) runs the file on a Lua state of its own that
knows only `add_ox_quiz`: the start is judged after the quest step that queues
it, when the step's session is gone, and running the file during the step would
land quizzes even when the world then refuses the start. On the owner's data the
file is 567 pure level-1 calls and the answers are what the live state would
collect; anything else fails the load, as a failed `lua_dofile` fails the start.

Coverage: `a_click_starts_the_ox_event_and_the_herald_seats_the_entrant` starts
the event over the wire (the dialog, then the start line — the quiet queue runs
the dialog first) and runs Uriel's herald behind it: the menu, the first page,
the entry page with its `Enter`/`Cancel` select, the farewell page, the removal
and the warp to the attender seat on Channel 1, with the contest's letter riding
Bob's login behind the flag. The minutes, the draw, the feet, the misses, the
reward's vnum bytes, the round turn and the end are unit-tested in the state: no
scenario waits out the 5-minute registration.

Three traps, each worth its line: the attender seat (896500) stands in the gap
between the O half (to 896300) and the X half (from 896600), so the feet must
walk before the check; in test-time `last_pulse` never steps, so the quiz's
timer is already due when the quiz fires and step 0 runs inside the same call;
and the reward test first asserted only a non-empty inbox, which the enter burst
and the notices fill with no give at all — the mutant that swapped the vnum
survived until the test pinned the `ITEM_SET` bytes with item ids installed.

A fourth trap surfaced in review after the suite went green: the reward's first
cut dropped `packed.changes`, so the giftbox vanished on relog — the game
thread owns no store handle, and inventory rows persist only through command
answers or a descriptor order. The reward now orders its rows to the winner's
descriptor, as the direct pick-up orders its given rows, and the pin covers the
`Created` 50109 row behind a joined lease. The battle-pass tier grant had the
same drop — a tier earned off a kill hook has no descriptor in the step — so
`pass_give` orders its rows the same way, with the free 27005 row pinned
behind a quest runtime that answers the points flag. Both order mutants
(empty rows) kill their tests.

## 525. The guild GM chats

The guild man's two GM entries (`guild_manage.lua:3-66`) run over the wire, and
`pc.select` learns what `GetPC` always did. Ten API rows and the quest turn `ported`.

**Legacy** (`G/questlua_pc.cpp:1814-1836`, `:1180-1197`, `G/questmanager.cpp:1087-1099`,
`G/questpc.cpp:42-45`, `G/questlua_global.cpp:80-87,743-757`,
`server/server/liblua/lvm.c:258-268`):

- `pc.select(vid)` calls `GetPC(pid)`, which switches `m_pCurrentPC` and
  `m_pCurrentCharacter` — the whole current character, not just the game fields.
  `getqf`/`setqf`/`delqf` then read `GetCurrentPC()->GetCurrentQuestName()` as their
  prefix: the *target's* last-run quest, not the running script's. No stack: naming
  the old VID back restores by direct set.
- The re-entry tool reads `u_disbandTime` at line 31, which nothing assigns — line 17
  assigns `u_withdrawTime` twice (positive control: the double assignment; negative:
  no `u_disbandXyzTime` anywhere). `nil > 0` errors in Lua 5.0 (`luaV_lessthan` ->
  `luaG_ordererror`) and 5.1 alike, so the retry math, `get_time` and
  `is_test_server` never run, on legacy too. The error ends the script through
  `GotoEndState`: the buffered page plus `[DONE]`.
- The `_50` format string (`"Abgezogene Zeit Tag"`) holds no `%s`, so the computed
  `time_to_str` text is discarded — the bridge still runs.
- `questlib.lua:456-530` resolves `pc.*`/`npc.*` field reads through metatables onto
  the bridged getters, so the info chat's `pc.has_guild()`, `pc.isguildmaster()`,
  `pc.empire` and `npc.empire` need no new bridge.

**Rewrite** (`quest/src/manager.rs`, `prodomo/tests/parity.rs`):

- The `pc.select` arm now switches `cx.current` to `pid_of(vid)` when the select
  switched (old VID nonzero), mirroring the block's switch without its stack.
- `getqf`/`setqf`/`delqf` prefix with `flag_quest()`: the current PC's last-run
  quest, snapshotted per-PC in `operate` and refreshed for the root by `execute`
  (which already wrote `pc.current`; without the refresh the login tests read
  empty prefixes — the first red run).
- The scenario `a_gm_reads_the_guild_info_and_the_re_entry_tool` founds `MyGuild`,
  joins Yankee and parts it (the stamp lands, Yankee's quest rests at
  `guild_building`), then reads twice: before the relog the stamp says the withdraw
  line; after the relog the login scripts moved Yankee's quest and the line stays
  out — the prefix-follows-target pin. The unknown name says the missing-user page;
  the info chat sends the triad and empires over `CHAT_TYPE_TALKING`. Both mutant
  halves (no map switch, running-quest prefix) kill the scenario, and the unit test
  `quest::manager::a_select_switches_the_flag_map` pins the switch with 11 last
  running `other`.
- Two traps, each worth its line: Yankee's enter needs the GM `TEAM_LIST` drain
  (`enter_world_on_with_team`), since Alpha's grant names someone else; and the
  info chat's end sends `[DONE]` in skin 0, because the client picked a menu entry.

Parity rows: `lua.pc.is_gm`, `lua.chat`, `lua.pc.has_guild`, `lua.pc.isguildmaster`,
`lua.pc.is_guild_master`, `lua.pc.getempire`, `lua.pc.get_empire`,
`lua.npc.get_empire`, `lua.find_pc_by_name` and `lua.time_to_str` are `ported`;
`quest.guild_manage` is `ported` (all five arms scenario-covered: founding in 269,
part and disband in 273, the GM pair here). `lua.pc.select` notes the switch.
`lua.get_time` and `lua.is_test_server` stay `partial`: the defect kills the only
caller before them. The `u_disbandTime` defect joins STATUS.

## 530. The war's edges

The event manager started and ended its wars in silence. Legacy's `UpdateGameFlag`
(`G/event_manager.cpp:788-800`) notifies every connected character on each flag change —
`SendEventBeginNotification`/`SendEventEndNotification` (`G/cmd_gm.cpp:1584-1596`) run the
no-target `event_begin`/`event_end` scripts on each — and the Rewrite's `start_game_event`/
`end_game_event` never did. So no war ever lettered, and `quest.kingdom_war_event` sat
`partial`.

`Manager::event_begin`/`event_end` (`quest/src/manager.rs:1483`) mirror `levelup` over
`QUEST_NO_NPC`'s scripts: an unknown character misses, as legacy's `GetPC` returns NULL.
`GameState::fire_event_edge` (`prodomo/src/game_state/quest_quiet.rs:467`) fans out in VID
order, each PC hearing its own records; it sits inside the start/end arms (beside the flag
write, where `UpdateGameFlag` sits), including the siege, kingdom and OX early returns.
The quest `set_event_flag` path stays quiet, as `RequestSetEventFlag` never notifies.

`quest.kingdom_war_event` is `ported`: `a_kingdom_war_letters_joins_and_clears` starts the
war on the probe's chat, reads the start notice, the quest-16 letter and its title, ends
the war (the scoreless pays, the loot, the end line, then the twelve `q.done` clears in
quest order, skipping the panel), restarts it, re-reads the letter, presses the button —
No refuses with the 130 line, Yes closes the dialog and warps to the war map's corner
(0, 25600) — and hears nothing after. `send_letter` is `questlib.lua:142`,
`clear_letter` is `q.done` (`questlib.lua:143`), and the dialog's options are
`translate.locale.yes`/`no` ("Yes "/"No ", `translate.lua:9141-9142`); the `_120_sayReward`
suffix is only a key name, and `say_reward` plays no part. One mutant died: the kingdom
arm firing the end edge answers no letter. The login arm is a manager test
(`an_event_begin_letters_and_its_end_clears`), since the login letter pass already covers
the `login` trigger. The 522 and exp scenarios now read the same traffic: the stacked
begins re-letter the siege (both `with` guards hold), and the siege end clears eleven,
quest 16 keeping its letter while its flag holds. The OX, siege-unfought and kingdom-kill
scenarios now read their start letters and end clears too, each watcher hearing its own.

## 542. The flag at once

The last API partial was `set_state`'s nuance: legacy writes the `__status` flag at once
(`SetCurrentQuestStateName`, `G/questpc.cpp:115-119`) while the `leave`/`enter`/`letter`
scripts wait for the script's end, but the Rewrite held the old flag until the end. Now the
bridge resolves the named state's number and writes the flag into the live map when the call
runs, deleting it for state 0 as `SetFlag` does, while `pending_state` still carries the
scripts to `end_running`.

Two things made it a port rather than a line: the bridge needed the host's state numbers
(a new `Cx.quests` borrow), and the step's writeback merged `execute`'s stale `__status`
over the script's newer write — it now fills only what the script did not write, as legacy's
order does. The stale unit assert (`Some(0)` while waiting) now expects the new state.

`a_click_sees_the_new_state_at_once` pins the wire: the flag probe reads 0 before the call
(`start` is state 0) and non-zero right after it. A skipped write says `deferred` and dies
there. The probe cannot name `away`'s number: `qc` refuses a literal it would print as
`1.50368e+09`, so the exact CRC stays pinned by the unit test. The quest-API table has no
partial left: 337 ported, 362 unused.

## 547. Three more dead server bytes

Twelve `codec` rows stood after ledger 546, and three more of them are bytes the
checked-in server never sends.

`gc.main_character` (15): the enumerator is `HEADER_GC_MAIN_CHARACTER_OLD`
(`G/packet.h:115`), and no `TPacketGCMainCharacterOld` or `MainCharacterOld` line exists in
`server/` or `legacy/` in any case, with no send writing a literal 15. The live main
character is byte 113, sent from `char.cpp:2018`, which is the control. (`spec §47` calls
byte 15 a dead generation; the sweep now pins it.)

`gc.login_key` (118): the enumerator (`packet.h:191`) and `TPacketGCLoginKey`
(`packet.h:491-495`) have no sender, and no send writes a literal 118. Every other
`login_key` hit is the DB-peer key (`C/tables.h` `GD_LOGIN_KEY`), the session key
(`desc`/`desc_manager` `CLoginKey`), or the auth-success field
(`TPacketGCAuthSuccess.dwLoginKey`, `packet.h:844`) — none of them this record. The
positive control is the live auth send: `HEADER_GC_AUTH_SUCCESS` from `input_db.cpp:1715`.
The `legacy/` hits are a MySQL index name, not a send.

`gc.bindudp` (254): `UDPGrant` fills the record (`desc.cpp:551-561`), but its only caller is
`CInputUDP::Handshake` (`input_udp.cpp:65`), and both arms of `CInputUDP::Analyze` are
commented out (`input_udp.cpp:102-120`), as is the whole of `CInputUDP::Process`
(`:124` onwards). `CInputUDP` is never instantiated — the only `CInputUDP` lines are the
class, its constructor and its member definitions — the UDP bind, watch and close sit
behind `__UDP_BLOCK__` (`main.cpp:678,692,740`, defined at `prodomodefines.h:195`), and
`io_loop` checks only the TCP and P2P sockets (`main.cpp:852-860`). So even legacy, with
the owner's defines, could not send byte 254 on any path.

All three rows move to `unused`, pending the owner's confirmation (question 66). No code
changed.

## 549. The gated pickup and the effect without a file

Four `codec` rows stood after ledger 548. Two stay: `gc.skill_level` (72) is the old
generation beside the live byte 76, and `gc.event_reload` (156) is the live event-manager
send the Rewrite must port. The other two are unreachable.

`gc.pickup_item_sc` (64): every send and the enumerator itself sit behind
`ENABLE_SPECIAL_DROP_CHAT_RENEWAL` — the enumerator (`packet.h:153`), the struct
(`packet.h:3313`), the `SendPickupItemPacket` definition (`char.cpp:11790`), its declaration
(`char.h:728`), and all five call sites (`char_item.cpp:8045,8077,8141,9122,9178`). No
`server/` file defines that switch, so the compiled server takes the `#else` arm every
time: the `[LS;444;%s]` chat line. The positive control is a switch that is defined:
`__SASH_SYSTEM__` at `prodomodefines.h:15`. Define the switch and the rows revive; on the
owner's defines the byte never leaves the server.

`gc.specific_effect` (208): `SpecificEffectPacket` (`char.cpp:7544`) has exactly two
callers in `server/`. The wear arm (`char_item.cpp:8592-8603`) needs a UNIQUE or RING item
whose SIGVnum names a SPECIAL group (`item_manager.cpp:426,436`) with an attr group
carrying an `effect` filename (`item_manager_read_tables.cpp:204-207`,
`item_manager.h:206-208`). The owner's `special_item_group.txt` is one group
(`Cufar_Lumina_Lunii`, 50011) with no `type` line at all — type NORMAL — and no `effect`
line anywhere in the file, so `GetSpecialAttrGroup` can only ever return nothing on the

## 558. The automatic potions

The twelve automatic-potion vnums toggle their rows now (`G/char_item.cpp:5334-5510`),
and the affect tick tops their recovery up (`AutoRecoveryItemProcess`, `:9892-10020`).

`world/src/item.rs` gains `Item.locked` (`m_isLocked`, `G/item.h:412`), memory-only with
no row column, and `world/src/character/items.rs` its `set_locked`. The item half is
`world::character::potion::toggle_auto_potion`: a swap stands the old item down first (a
missing old item is silently fine, as legacy's `NULL` check is), a stack splits one
single off into the first free base cell carrying socket 1 only, and the single toggles
socket 0 and the lock on — or off. Seven unit tests pin the fresh single, the split (with
its `Count`/`Created`/`Sockets` changes), the toggle-off, the swap, the missing old item,
the roomless split and the roomless swap (which leaves the old item lit).

`prodomo/src/game_state/auto_potion.rs` holds the rest. `auto_at` dispatches the twelve
vnums by vnum alone (72723-72730, 76004/76005, 76021/76022); `use_auto_item` runs the
arena gate (`[LS;403]`), the flagged-duel gate (`[LS;1205]`, read live from the
`no_potions_on_pvp` event flag `questlib_extra.lua` sets at load, with legacy's allowed
list plus the SP X) and the one-second throttle (`@0949WAIT_BUFF` — `WAIT_BUFF` is in no
locale file: the main table and all 12 country files were swept, so europe's lookup
answers `@0949` plus the key, `G/locale.cpp:244-255`), then the step, the row
(`AddAffect(type, bonus, 4, id, INF, 0)`, the X laying `POINT_MAX_HP/SP_PCT`) and the
immediate process. A stack with nowhere to split hears `[LS;1130]`. The tick runs the
process HP then SP after the drain: the dead, stunned and stun-marked are skipped, a
missing or stood-down item removes the row, an arena map or flagged duel strips it (the
strip's step sends and orders its rows, as the fishing timeout does), else the missing
pool pays into the recovery with `SE_AUTO_HPUP`/`SE_AUTO_SPUP`. The restore re-locks the
named item (`LoadAffect`, `G/char_affect.cpp:600-608`); `pvp_is_fighting` (`G/pvp.cpp:244-260`)
is new in `duel.rs`. Thirteen GameState tests and one restore test cover the use, the
toggle-off, the split, the swap, the X pair, the full pools, the roomless stack, the
arena gate and strip, the tick's top-up, the allowed list and the strip's end rule.

Two orders are the architecture's, not legacy's: the step's Update precedes the add frame
(the store commits before the records go), and on toggle-off the answer's Update precedes
the remove frame (a command's direct frames land behind its answer, as the blend's do).
Legacy toggles the socket after the add and removes before the unlock; the final states
match. The PvP gate's live-duel composition (flag up plus a fighting pair) is
review-only: no unit harness holds both a quest manager and a consent pair, and its three
reads are one line each, shared with the tested strip. The throttle's adjacent-second
boundary is review-only too: it mirrors legacy's `< 1` byte-for-byte, and straddling it
in a scenario would be timing-flaky by nature.

Review caught two order bugs before the gates ran: the swap stood the old item down
before the split, so a roomless swap left the old item dark in memory while the store kept
it lit (legacy splits first, `:5419-5440` against `:5442`), and the tick ran the process
before the drain's records went out while `again` was computed before the process, so a
strip of the last row lingered an extra tick and the Points rode inverted. Both are fixed
(the split precedes the stand-down, with a regression test; the drain sends, then the
process runs, then `again` is recomputed), and the end rule has its own test.

Scenario `an_auto_potion_lays_its_row_pays_each_tick_and_toggles_off`: the use lays the
row with the item's id, lights socket 0, pays the 920 missing and shows effect 19; two
ticks spend 99 each while the heals keep the pool past the maximum, so the process stays
silent (the top-up itself is the unit test's, where no heals run); the second use darkens
the socket and removes the row; and past a quiet second a double-use toggles once and
hears the wait line once. The store follows the socket both ways. 8/8 parallel runs green.

Mutation sweep, each applied to the pristine file and restored by checksum: pay-at-zero
(`>` to `>=`, killed by the full-pools test), the wrong SP X (killed by the new SP-X test —
the first run survived, which is why the test exists), the throttle off (`< 1` to `< 0`,
killed by the scenario), the flipped toggle branch (killed) and the AND-strip (killed).

## 559. The ownership record

The ledger-229p note on `gc.item_ownership` said no scenario reaches the record, because no
hosted kill drops an item. That was true when written, and it is still true of kills; but
the mining dig has been laying owned ore since ledger 556's neighbours, and two scenarios
already pin the record on the wire. The row's blocker was a kill-drop system that never
arrived, not the record itself, so this slice re-reads the send paths and flips the row.

The wire matches legacy exactly: header 0x1f, the ground VID, the 25-byte name
(`TPacketGCItemOwnership`, `G/packet.h:1495-1500`, `CHARACTER_NAME_MAX_LEN` 24), encoded by
`view_encode::ground_ownership` through `GcNamed` with `GC_NAME_FIELD_SIZE` 25. All four
send paths exist: the named set in `set_ground_ownership` (with the `<= 10` seconds-become-30
rule, `G/item.cpp:1733-1775`), the empty-name clear (`SetOwnership(NULL)`, `:1735-1749`),
the empty-name expiry in `release_expired_ownership` (`ownership_event`, `:1704-1728`), and
the insert's ownership while the event runs (`EncodeInsertPacket`, `:192-199`; the insert
flow at `view_encode.rs:382-386` sends it after the ground add). Scenario
`a_vein_dug_with_a_pick_drops_its_ore_or_fails_and_trains_the_pick` pins the named set on
the digger's wire, and `a_dug_ore_loses_its_diggers_name_fifteen_seconds_on` pins the
empty-name lapse; both were re-run green.

The kill path needed care before the flip. The distribution is ported:
`reward_drops` lays one item for the killer and several round-robin over `drop_owner_list`
(the 10% damage qualifiers, ties by lower VID where legacy ties by pointer — a recorded
Defect), and `set_drop_owner` stores each owner's store id and 25-byte name; the owner
list has its unit test, and no live scenario can pin a kill's dice (the same reason
`sys.combat.drop` is ported but unit-tested, ledger 230ab). The gold piles looked wrong at
first — `lay_monster_gold` lays them with `owner: None` — but legacy's `RewardGold`
(`G/char_battle.cpp:558-750`) never calls `SetOwnership` either: it only creates and adds
to ground. The port matches.

scenario; one `partial` server record remains (`gc.walk_mode`, V3).

## 560. The dungeon's returns

`sys.dungeon.core` was `missing`; it is `partial` now. The slice ports the two arms
that fire when a party comes apart inside a dungeon: the leader's disconnect sends
the near members home (`FExitDungeon`, `G/party.cpp:655-661`), and a body that lands
on a living dungeon's map rejoins its present set (the login's `SetDungeon` stamp,
`G/input_login.cpp:788`).

The exit arm (`exit_dungeon_nears`, `party.rs:634`) runs in `unlink_party` between
the bonus zeroes and the near clear, while the flags still read, as legacy orders
it. It fires only when the leader stands on a living dungeon's map; every other
linked near member with a saved exit is ordered home in PID order and leaves the
present set, and members with no exit stay, as `d.exit_all` leaves them. The
re-stamp (`join_dungeon`, `dungeons.rs`, called from `place_body` in `motion.rs`)
cancels the dead event through the member-entered path, as the login's stamp does
through `IncMember`.

The scenario first tried to prove the re-stamp with a relog back inside, and the
relog refused to go there: the row names the dungeon, so the login re-seeds the
pending warp from the exit columns. That is `SetPlayerProto`
(`G/char.cpp:2289-2294`), unconditional in legacy too — a relog whose row names a
private map always comes home. Legacy shows the character on the dungeon map first
and warps it after; the Rewrite lands it home directly. The end states match, so
the re-stamp is a safety net for jump-landings and future warp-onto-private paths,
and the scenario pins the homecoming instead:
`a_leader_disconnect_sends_the_near_home_and_the_relog_comes_home`. A party of two
jumps into the forest and both hear the landing `back`; past one party tick the
leader disconnects and Yankee warps to its saved exit while its row goes home;
Alpha's relog lands home too, Yankee quits to disband the pair, and the quiets
prove no `back` reaches the outsiders.

Two races surfaced while writing it. Alpha's own removal may or may not reach
Yankee before the warp-leave drops Yankee's pending outbox, so the scenario
accepts it but does not require it (the same-map disconnect fan is proven
elsewhere). And the 3 s party Update fans the relink's own headers, so Yankee's
re-enter runs in a tick-free window (a blind 3.5 s sleep while both stand offline)
through a new `enter_game_view_partied` helper, modelled on the guilded enter,
which pulls the link's walk — own ADD, every member's ADD, every online LINK,
every member's UPDATE, own UPDATE, PARAMETER — and pushes the burst back.

The slice also asked how the forest middle runs on the legacy server at all: no
jump stamps its members (`d.new_jump` and `d.new_jump_party` only `Create` and
warp, and `FWarpToDungeon`'s `IncPartyMember` is commented out), so every
member's `m_pkDungeon` is NULL and `pc.in_dungeon()` is false until someone
relogs — owner question 70. If the middle is dead there, the Rewrite's running
middle (membership derived live from the map) is a recorded Divergence. The
same stamp question holds the invite and leave gates (`PERR_DUNGEON`/`[LS;822]`,
`[LS;673]`, `[LS;531]`): legacy reads the stamp, so they may be dead there too,
and they stay open until the owner answers. Two related arms are dead on the
data regardless: `CParty::Link`'s dungeon stamp (`G/party.cpp:586-589`) needs
`d.join`, which no quest calls (`lua.d.join` is `unused` since ledger 401), and
`IsPartyInDungeon(351)` needs a dungeon of base 351, which no quest jumps to
(the sweep finds 65, 66, 209 and 210; the index lists those four and no 351).

Unit tests: a re-enter rejoins the present and cancels the dead event, and a
leader unlink in a dungeon sends only the near with exits home (the far member
holds an exit and the near fourth holds none, so each gate is pinned alone).
Mutants: dropping the near filter, the exit gate, the unpresent call, the join
and the motion re-stamp all fail their test. Dropping the dungeon-alive gate is
equivalent (the dungeon lookup behind it gates the same map), and the PID exit
order is unobservable (per-session warps race in legacy too), so neither is
mutated. The scenario is 8/8 green.

## 561. The dragon's scaled blows

`BlueDragon_Damage` (`G/BlueDragon.cpp:139-196`) is ported: the three stone arms that scale a
rated hit after the death-blow multiple and before the flag (`G/char_battle.cpp:2298`).

The host snapshots `BlueDragonSetting.DragonStone[1..4]` once after the libraries load
(`quest/src/host.rs`, mirroring `BlueDragon_GetIndexFactor`'s miss arms:
`G/BlueDragon_Binder.cpp:166-213` — a missing table, row or number reads 0), the snapshot rides
`GameData.settings` into `GameState.dragon_stones`, and the pure `blue_dragon_damage`
(`world/src/character/combat/dragon.rs`, fed by the shared row in `common/src/dragon.rs`) runs
the arms: the monster 2493's hit grows by the first `ATK_BONUS` row's percent times its live
stones on the attacker's map, a hit on it shrinks by the first `DEF_BONUS` row's percent times
its live stones on the victim's map (at least 1), and a hit on a stone by a rider whose mount is
the row's feared `enemy` multiplies by `enemy_val`. The counts are the caller's
(`GameState::dragon_counts`, `fight.rs`): live stones only, as `FCountSpecifiedMonster` requires
`IsStone` and the dead leave the sectree (`G/sectree_manager.cpp:1595-1617`). Every melee mirror
(`damage_normal`, `damage_special`, `damage_melee` with its `damage_range`/`damage_magic`
delegates, `damage_normal_range`) hooks it through `dragon_scaled`, and every mob mirror
(`strike_pc`, `skill_damage_pc`, `shoot_pc` through `finish_shot`) through `mob_scaled`; legacy
counts once per side and combat never crosses maps, so each path counts on the map the arms that
can fire share. The guard path (`strike_npc_by_npc`) stuns with no Damage body, so its arms never
run. `skill_damage_pc`, `magic_damage` and `finish_shot` now take the `MobStriker` they already
had a caller for.

The scenario stands map 1 with only the two stones and the dragon on the dog's proven cell and
pins both count arms: the punch rates 172 and lands 129 past one live 8031, the dragon's first
swing rates 1244 and lands 1555 past one live 8032 (`the_dragon_stones_scale_the_dragons_blows_
both_ways`, 8/8 green). Two things make the numbers pin although the dice seed is random per
boot: the file swap (the map's `npc.txt` holds only the three lines, `regen`/`stone`/`boss` are
empty, so nothing else idles) and the patched proto (the dragon's damage flattened to 200, its
defence to 0 so the punch rates past the `battle_damage_floor` draw, its critical and penetrate
enchants to 0). The mount arm is unit-pinned (a feared 20110 triples a hit on 8031; any other
mount is the identity), as are the floor-at-1 and the default-snapshot identity. Both hook
mutants are killed with the exact unscaled values (172, 1244).

Reachability, by the ledger-466 rule: 2493 and 8031-8034 never spawn on the owner's data. No map
regen names them (sweep of `locale/europe/map/`), no quest names 2493 and only `BlueDragon.lua`
itself names 8031 (positive control: 6408 is found in `enchanted_forest_zone.lua`), the boss
event's regen names 2493 but its map 230 is not in the owner's index, and nothing in `server/`
names the `templul_dragonului` regen files. `sys.dungeon.dragon_lair` is `partial`:
`UseBlueDragonSkill`, `BlueDragon_StateBattle`, the skill/range binders and `DragonLair.cpp` are
next.

## 562. The quest that never loads

Ledger 227 kept `quest.change_empire` `missing` while it waited for the owner to fix the
source. The wait is over: the row is `unused`, and the fix it waited for is withdrawn.

The file's `move_pc` (`change_empire.lua:57-140`) is unbalanced even textually. The `:133`
`elseif` comes after the `:117` `else`, so `:137` and `:138` close the `if` and the function
while `:139` (`return false`) is still ahead: the function-body loop breaks at `:138` and
`:139` lands in `WhenListOrFunction`, which refuses it with `expecting 'when' or 'function'`.
Both `qc`s run the identical loop (`while nested >= 3`, the same `Do`/`If`/`Function`-up and
`End`-down count, the break at 2 — `server/server/quest/qc.cpp:765ff` against
`quest/src/qc.rs:648ff`), so legacy refuses the file exactly as the Rewrite does: the quest
never loads on either side. The controls compile (`cards_event.lua`, `changelook.lua`, the
alphabetical neighbours). Nothing references the quest: the only other `change_empire`
spellings are the `quest_functions` API names and stale `translate.lua` strings no quest
reads. The `pc.change_empire` machinery underneath stays ported (ledgers 405, 477); only the
dialog is dead. Owner question 71 asks the owner to confirm the boot-time refusal on their
server.

(a GM skips the sash's letters through its `not pc.is_gm()` gate; `/eventflag` answers at

`InvalidServerLog` have no callers in `game/`, `db/` or `common/` (the positive control is
the same sweep finding the other 20, e.g. `ItemLog` in 21 files, `CharLog` in 18). The 20
live ones span per-drop spam (`ItemLog`, `MoneyLog` on every drop) and security rows
(`HackLog`, `GMCommandLog`, `SpeedHackLog`): tracing all of them is dozens of sites, so the
owner picks the kept set before the calls are added. What exists today stays: `CHAR_LOG`,
one `ITEM_LOG`, one `HACK_LOG` and one `MONEY_LOG` site.

## 569. The stamina in StateMove

V3 is closed. `StateMove`'s stamina arm (`G/char_state.cpp:812-851`) runs on every step
(`step_stamina`, called from `step_motion`): a run within twenty seconds of a fight spends
a point a step (every other step with the half-stamina unique 70040 worn, on the Pulse's
odd half), and a walk past five seconds restores the pool to its maximum, below the
maximum only (`:814` — on a full pool legacy sends nothing). `PointChange`'s
switch (`G/char.cpp:4286-4296`) lives in `change_pc_point`: an emptied pool walks the flag
at once, a pool that climbs off 0 restores the mode line's point, and the dead and the
locked run no switch. The switch fans before the point record, as legacy's `SetNowWalking`
runs before the packet is written. The walk stamp is `Option<u32>` (`Body::walk_start_ms`):
the mode lines stamp it on a walk, and the first walking step stamps it when no line did.

The consume gauge (`StartStaminaConsume`/`StopStaminaConsume`, `G/char.cpp:7383-7402`) runs
with it: the first spend sends a zero-change record and the start line with the drain rate
(25 a second, 12 with the unique worn) and the pool, each once. The stop runs its
zero-change record and line on the emptying step, on a step past the fight window, on
arrival (`:897-904`), and on a non-`MOVE` function (`G/input_main.cpp:1872-1876`), each
guarded by the flag. The drain calls `StartAffectEvent` (`:826`), whose refill covers the
pool three idle seconds on; the walk arm's own five-second restore covers chained moves,
whose accepts keep the idle count short. The emptying step sends, in order: the walk fan,
the spend's zero, the start's zero and line, the stop's zero and line.

The refill is rerouted through the switch: `run_affect_event` computes the recovery
records as before, runs the potions, then refills through `change_pc_point` (legacy's
order, `:213-222`), and the `again` gate reads the pool after it. A refill that climbs
off 0 now restores the mode line's point with its fan, as legacy's `PointChange` does.

A Defect, recorded in `docs/STATUS.md`: the constructor never initializes
`m_dwWalkStartTime` (`G/char.cpp:280-312` sets every neighbour but it), while the walk
arm reads it whenever a body walks (`G/char_state.cpp:813-820`), so a body walking on an
empty pool — `IsWalking` through `GetStamina() <= 0` with the line never flipped —
restores from a garbage clock on its first steps. The Rewrite stamps the first walking
step. Pre-existing and untouched: the refill moves a dead player's pool, where legacy's
arm returns on `IsDead` (`:4279`); the 229d refill never gated it, steps never run for
the dead, and no revive path spends stamina there, so the arm cannot observe it.

Scenario `a_run_after_a_swing_spends_stamina_then_walks_and_restores`: Alpha stores
stamina 3, swings, and runs 1600 south while Yankee watches. The collected stream pins
the start's zero and `StartStaminaConsume 25 2`, the walk fan before the spend's zero,
and the stop's zero and `StopStaminaConsume 0`; Yankee's watching stream (no inserts)
pins the walk fan and, mid-walk, the refill's climb and the run fan, and Alpha's own
stream pins the 890 restore. Unit pins: the five-second boundary (5000 holds, 5001
restores), the full-pool silence past five seconds, the first-step stamp, the window
end (a step at 20001 past the fight stops the gauge and spends nothing), the arrival
stop, the half-stamina skip, the gauge's once each, and the climb off 0 for both line

## 570. The deck strikes the mast

The ship's defence fights now. `SetWave` runs `FindAllyCharacter`
(`G/ShipDefense.cpp:635-660`): every monster on the run's map takes the standing
mast as its NPC victim, so the wave walks the mast instead of idling, while the
wheel — no monster — holds nothing. The NPC victim rides the mind's `victim_npc`
slot through the state machine: Idle starts the fight on a held mast at its first
tick and drops a dead or gone one with the 1-second wait, the walk's arrival asks
for Battle past it, and Battle's head guards run first (stones and NPC strikers
never fight; `CanMove` holds; the stun returns with the duration as it was).

The swing is `CHARACTER::Attack` on an NPC victim (`G/char_battle.cpp:220-328`):
the chat before the reach, the SPECIAL blank, the RANGE/MAGIC shoot past the same
reach, the claim, the victim's `BeginFight` past `CanBeginFight` — which the mast's
NPC type never passes, so the strike stands there — and the swing stamp. Its melee
body is `strike_npc_by_monster`: `battle_hit` (`G/battle.cpp:760-817`) into
`Damage`'s NORMAL path (`G/char_battle.cpp:1744-2436`), down to the damage shown —
the NPC-arm `CalcMeleeDamage`, the affect draws, the block, critical and penetrate
chances, the NPC-vs-NPC steals, the bonuses, the BANPK refusal, the chat draw, the
stun and dead checks, the user rate (an identity off a monster), the stoneskin, the
death blow, the dragon, and the `+0.5`. The shared tail (`npc_damage_tail`) serves
the mast's reflect too: the victim's `POINT_REFLECT_MELEE` share of the pre-bonus
base, thirded when the striker is immune, back as `DAMAGE_TYPE_SPECIAL` off the
NPC's empire (`:1979-1988`), filling the striker's damage map SPECIAL with no
party share. A hit on the mast broadcasts its HP (`:2277-2282`), and the run's
stored HP follows the NPC's. The splash learned the NPC arm (`splash_hit_npc`):
PCs run before NPCs, the recompute mirrors the PC's, and the CRUSH slide refuses
the NOMOVE mast.

Two corrections ride along. Base 358 is no ship map: `IsDungeon` runs
`358*10000..359*10000` (`:1955-1958`), and no live run's index is ever the base —
the earlier `map == MAP` arm was wrong, and `base_358_is_no_ship_map` pins the
range. And the already-running gate is the quest bind's, not `Start`'s: the bind
refuses past `IsRunning` (`ship_defense_mgr_start`,
`G/questlua_shipdefense_mgr.cpp:41-61`, into `IsRunning`'s `STATE_START` read,
`:1636-1648`), while `Start` keeps its own two gates (the leader holds the call,
and holds a run) — a second start restarts nothing and prepares no second wave
(`the_second_start_is_quiet`).

starts, and watches wave 1 land on the mast — the start burst, the countdown chats
at 60 and under 10, a `GC_TARGET` naming the mast below its 5,000,000, and the
fake-hydra clear destroying the intimidation's head 3 s on. Unit pins: the mast
swing and the fake's refusal (`a_monster_swings_on_the_mast_and_not_on_a_fake_hydra`),
the retarget's hold with the dead and gone mast refusals, the mast-hit broadcast,
the held-NPC-victim Idle and walk arms, and the reflect's pre-bonus base and

## 573. The killer mark

`sys.char.pk` runs the killer mode. `pk_actor` used to feed the policy a peaceful
fiction — every mode but protect read as peace, alignment 0, no killer, no party, no
guild. It now reads the card's mode (all five, `SetPKMode`'s range behind it), the
stored alignment, the killer flag, the party leader and the guild, with the duel
stamping the consensual fight as before. `attack_player` reads the policy's answer
instead of its shape: a same-empire hit on a blameless player marks the attacker
before the swing lands (`SetKillerMode`, `G/char_battle.cpp:3568-3581`), and the flag
`g_protectNormalPlayer` (`[game] protect_normal_player`, default off both sides)
keeps a negative attacker off a blameless target in peace.

The mark lives on the body (`AddState::killer`, beside the spawn bit it shares the
`m_bAddChrState` byte with), rides the insert and the update (`character_add`,
`character_update`), clears on death (`Dead`, `:1469`) and 30 seconds after the set
(`UpdateKillerMode` from the recovery event, `G/char.cpp:3252`, in Pulses). A repeat
set stamps nothing, as legacy's early return stamps nothing.

Scenario `a_free_hit_on_a_player_of_his_own_empire_marks_the_killer`: Dave of empire 1
goes free, hits Alpha of empire 1, and the swing lands (140, Dave's own attack
against Alpha's defence) with the killer bit raised on Dave's update for both.
Unit pins: the set's bit, the repeat's silence, the clear, and the 749/750 decay
boundary; the policy's peace refusal, free mark, killer fair game, revenge and
guild alignments, and the party/duel/protect gates. Mutants (free never marks, a
31-second decay) both killed. Inventory: `sys.char.pk` stays `partial`; the
alignment's revenge and the item drop penalty wait.

Refactors (Clippy, no behaviour): `GameState`'s shop and emotion bools fold into
`ShopToggles`, the body's add-state bits into `AddState`, and the warp NPC's hack
check reads `own_mover` instead of building its own.

## 577. The hidden alignment

`sys.char.pk` closes ledger 234's named gap: the hide-alignment unique's second value is
ported. Legacy keeps `m_iAlignment` and `m_iRealAlignment` as two values
(`G/char_battle.cpp:3452-3475`); the Rewrite kept one. Now the card holds the real one
and the body the shown one (`Body::shown_alignment`, seeded equal at entry per
`SetPlayerProto`, `G/char.cpp:2244-2245`). `UpdateAlignment`'s `bShow` arm
(`:3479-3481`) moves the shown and sends the update only when the two agree; while the
cloak holds the shown at 0, kills and quest changes move the real in silence. The wear
and take-off run `ShowAlignment` (`:3457-3475`, `G/char_item.cpp:8287-8288,8556-8557`),
and `pc.get_alignment` reads the shown while `pc.get_real_alignment` reads the real
(`G/questlua_pc.cpp:1081-1091`).

Three findings shaped the slice. First, the cloak 70048 is `WEAR_SHIELD` in its proto,
but the file cell reads as `WEARABLE_UNIQUE` (the reader's name table crosses the two
pins, `ProtoReader.cpp:426`), so `FindEquipCell` puts it on the first unique cell —
and the port's `wears_vnum` check reads every worn cell, so it lands wherever the
proto puts it. Second, the wear's own look carries the old shown (its `Mover` is built
before the step), so the hide's update joins the step's own records behind it, fanned
to the view with the look; a direct send would race the store-first ordering the
descriptor keeps. Third, the take-off answers `Moved`, not `Unequipped` (the worn cell
clears, then the grid path sets the destination), so the sync runs on every kind but
the refusal and lets `ShowAlignment`'s equality silence the rest.

The cloak is the one unique that wears: `worn_system_not_ported` and the `CanEquipNow`
`WEARABLE_UNIQUE` arm except it, and every other unique still refuses
(`world::character::equip::the_hide_alignment_cloak_wears_while_other_uniques_refuse`).
The unique expiry event with its `Start/StopUniqueExpireEvent` arms is still unported,
so the cloak never expires — a named wait, not a silent drop. `CG_ITEM_USE` knows no
unique arm (`USED_BY_WEARING` has no `ITEM_UNIQUE`), so the wear goes through the move
path; legacy's `UseItem` routes the same way through `EquipItem`.

Proved by `a_worn_cloak_hides_the_shown_alignment_and_its_takeoff_restores_it`: Alpha
stored at 4321 wears the cloak onto cell 187 — the sets, the recompute, the step's
look at 432 and the hide's look at 0 — takes it off — the step's look at 0 and the
show's look at 432 — and the stored row still says 4321. The unit pins are
`show_alignment_hides_restores_and_silences_the_crossing` (hide, re-hide silent,
hidden crossing silent, show, re-show silent), `the_cloaks_wear_and_takeoff_hide_and_show`
(the sync joins and fans exactly one update each way), and the quest `Game`
`shown_alignment` reads (probe, session, and the seeded `Session` field). Three
mutants killed: the sync skipping `Moved` (scenario fails), the inverted `show` arm
(unit fails), and the world gate un-narrowed (world test fails).

## 578. The bank's alignment

`sys.char.save`'s last `Not ported` was the alignment a bank's minutes earn
(`G/char.cpp:1529-1539`): outside a `BANPK` cell each banked minute earns 5, or 60
(120 with `UNIQUE_ITEM_FASTER_ALIGNMENT_UP_BY_TIME`, 70050) while the real
alignment is negative. It runs inside `CreatePlayerProto`, before `tab.playtime`
and `tab.lAlignment` are read (`:1545-1546`), so the saved row holds the earned
value.

`GameState::answer_kept` is the bank: it already set the points' playtime before
reading the kept alignment, so `earn_alignment_for_playtime` runs there, between
the two. The minutes are only the fresh ones — the banked minus the points'
last — because a logout re-banks the session's whole minutes (ledger 261) and a
re-bank must earn nothing twice. The `BANPK` read is the body's own cell through
`is_banpk`; the unique read is `wears_unique`'s two unique cells, as
`IsEquipUniqueItem` reads them (`G/char_item.cpp:9519-9540`). Zero or negative
minutes earn nothing, and the move goes through `update_alignment`, so the shown
follows, the /10 update goes out, and the band affects move with it.

Tests: `the_banks_minutes_earn_five_each`, `a_negative_bank_earns_sixty_or_one_twenty_but_never_twice`
(the 60, the 120, the no-twice silence, and the zero bank at a band edge that
kills the `<=`/`<` mutant), `a_bank_on_a_banpk_cell_earns_nothing`, and
`a_kept_save_banks_the_playtime_then_earns_its_minutes` (the kept row reads the
earned alignment, the re-bank earns nothing). A body with a place but no spot
earns nothing, as legacy's null-sectree arm skips (`GetSectree()` null).
`read_war_end_past_pings` pumps past a stray `GC_CHARACTER_UPDATE`: the war
outlasts a bank, and the bank's /10 crossing sends the `UpdatePacket` legacy
sends too. Scenario
`a_save_past_a_minute_of_play_writes_the_alignment_the_minute_earned`: Alpha's
row holds 300 minutes and alignment 0, and the logout writes 301 and 5. Mutants:

## 579. The unique's hour

`sys.char.pk`'s tail was the unique expiry event: ledger 577 wore the cloak
without its timer, and every other unique refused at equip and at load. The
event is ported now, on `Due::Unique`, one due entry per worn unique.

`sync_unique_expire` runs after every equip and use step, beside the cloak's
`sync_hide_alignment`: every worn unique with no due entry is started, every due
entry whose item is no longer worn is stopped. The start reads the saved socket
4 seconds (capped at 60, 60 when 0), clears the socket, and arms the fire; the
stop banks the seconds left back into socket 4 — unless value 2 is set, which
keeps ticking unworn, as legacy's stop refuses those (`G/item.cpp:2227-2243`).
The fire runs the countdown arm (remove at remain 1 or less, else tick down and
re-arm 60 s) and the value-2 absolute arm (remove when passed, else re-arm the
seconds left capped at 600). The removal is `RemoveItem` with the owner logged
on: the quickslot delete, the worn points, the release, the clear, the destroy
row, and the cloak's `ShowAlignment(true)`. A missing item, proto or wearer ends
the event silently. Real-time uniques still refuse (their expiry is the
real-time event), and so do special-grouped ones (the owner's only group sits
above the 30000 gate, so `m_ItemToSpecialGroup` never fills one); the
premium-shop arm stays out (no shop window holds a unique here).

The wear gates opened with it: `worn_system_not_ported` and the `CanEquipNow`
`WEARABLE_UNIQUE` arm now refuse only the real-time and the grouped uniques.
The load follows through the same gate.

Tests: `a_worn_cloak_arms_and_its_fire_removes_it` (60 s arm, removal, the
re-shown alignment), `a_remain_above_one_ticks_down_and_rearms`,
`a_takeoff_banks_the_seconds_left_and_a_rewear_spends_them` (bank 60, re-arm
from the bank, clear on start), `a_remain_of_one_removes_at_the_fire`, and the
re-aimed `world`/`prodomo` gate tests (`a_real_time_or_grouped_unique_is_refused_as_not_ported`,
the cloak's wear, the load's real-time unique). Scenario
`a_worn_cloaks_saved_seconds_fire_and_remove_it`: the cloak banked at 2 s arms
2 s on, and the fire clears wear cell 187, re-shows 432, and deletes the row.
The stop's bank and the start's clear ride the step that owns them: their update
record and their `Sockets` row change are folded into the wear's or take-off's own
`MovedItems`, behind the wear cell's records, so one transaction stores them with the
step and one burst sends them (the suite caught the first cut, which wrote the
record straight to the socket and stored nothing). The cloak's hide scenario gained
the take-off's `Count(0, 1)` and the banked-socket store check. Mutants: the first
gap, the remain bound, the tick, the re-arm and the value-2 split all fail.

Gates (2026-11-11): `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo build --workspace --locked --offline`, the full suite (5418 passed, 0 failed in 46 targets), the doc suite (1 passed, 0 failed in 9 targets), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked --offline -- -D warnings`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --locked --offline`, and the store/legacy checks. The first suite run found the take-off bank's unsent store row (5417 passed, 1 failed; the fix folded the stop into the step).

## 587. The premium shop

The 507 arm `UseItemEx` runs before the renewal loop (`G/char_item.cpp:6835-6843`):
`SetPremiumPrivateShopBonus(value(3))` (`G/char.cpp:12695-12742`), and true consumes
one of the stack. The setter adds the duration to the held 507 row's, clamped to the
week (`PRIVATE_SHOP_MAX_PREMIUM_TIME`, 604800); within 60 s of the max it refuses
with the verbatim recently-reached line (trailing space) and the item is kept. Else
the 507 row lands `over` on `POINT_NONE`, the held expiry becomes `duration + now`,
the increased line tells (no trailing space), and at exactly the max the reached-max
line tells too (trailing space) — all three `LC_TEXT` verbatim, since `locale_find`
with `LOCALE_YMIR` returns its input (`G/locale.cpp:71-89`). The account expiry is
the new `account.private_shop_premium_expire` column (migration 43, a unix time like
`private_shop.premium_time`): the descriptor stores it before the item rows, with the
account's shops' rows retimed in the same transaction (legacy retimes only cached
shops, a store detail; the Rewrite retimes rows, which is what it has). The world
holds the expiry per online `Vid`, seeded at admission (a `Character` names no
account, so the map keys on `Vid` like `affect_events`) and cleared on leave. The
two readers port: the build writes the held expiry verbatim as `premium_time`
(`remain + now` is the expiry, `G/private_shop_manager.cpp:171`), and the affect
tick syncs the 507 row to `remain + 1` or removes it past expiry
(`G/char_affect.cpp:343-363`), before the guild strip. Out of scope, recorded: the
other six premium indices (no stored expiry, no ported reader), the respawn and
despawn sweeps the Rewrite has no seat for (the value is stored but unread), the
index-9 off-by-one (a Defect: the `0..=` loop reads past the array), and the affect
row itself on relog (no-save 500-509, already filtered). Scenario
`a_shop_premium_use_lands_507_stores_the_expiry_and_refuses_the_second`: the 507 add
on point 0 with 604800 s, the spend, the increased line, the account row a week out,
the queued max line, and the second use's recent line with the row kept at 1.

port's `compute_affect` (`affect.rs`): below 120 each held top row (321-323)
goes, uncomputed through `RemoveAffect` with its remove packet sent, the flags

strip nests once through the remove's own `ComputeAffect`, which finds no row
and stops — the port calls the point arm directly and skips the empty second
pass. Every `compute_affect` caller keeps its behavior: the nine remove-path
callers outside `affect.rs` and the seven inside ignore the strip's answer
(their own strips run through the same gate), and the add path folds the one
nested strip in. `/level` and `/advance` run the strip on a move off 120 and
carry the fallen IDs in `LevelHeld::fell_top`; `level_step` deletes them

now. The `ClearAffect` line's kept-top row now falls through the first

`TopPlayerAffLog` row is `sys.log`'s, still waiting on the owner's answer
(question 73). Scenario
`a_level_to_120_grants_the_top_row_and_a_move_off_fells_it`: `/level 120`

## 594. The disband's land-clear

`RequestDisband`'s other half (`ClearLandByGuildID`, `G/guild.cpp:1045`) runs with
the destroy: the owned land clears before the guild goes. `first_owned_land`
(`FindLandByGuild`, `G/building.cpp:799-812`) finds it — the first in id order, as
legacy's `std::map` scan does — then each hosted place holding its map clears its
objects through the `/clear_land` wipe (`clear_build_land`, now shared) in place
order, once the owner is dropped the land fans, and the claim stone stands. The
fan lands before `by_id` drops the guild, so a viewer that never heard the guild
still gets its NAME (the scenario's master already knows its own, so no NAME
rides there). The judged stores carry the disband first, then each place's
`Clear`; the `/deleteguild` drain (`store_deleteguild_store`) stores each half in
order — the disband's delete cascades the owner row first, so the clear's drop is
a no-op and its object delete does the work. The quest destroy's halves drain
through the same shared land path. The land answers come with the finder: the
walk INFO's `has_land` bit (`HasLand`, `G/guild.cpp:1990-1993`, the one stale "not
ported" the row's note named), `guild.has_land0` in the world and the shadow
(they answered false since 230s), and the symbol upload's land gate
(`G/input_login.cpp:1016-1021`, held unless owned except on a test server) —
refuse where legacy closes, as the unknown-guild arm already did. Scenario
`a_master_builds_on_its_land_and_clears_it` grows a tail: the guild reclaims the
land into the store, the master relogs onto it (the rows install at boot), and
`/deleteguild` fans REMOVE, the object's removal, the ownerless list and the
claim stone with its summary, and the store empties. The walk INFO's bit is
pinned at the first enter (`guild_walk_info`, captured by the guilded-enter
helper for every guilded scenario). Unit seats: `a_disband_clears_its_land` (the
disband first, then the clear, in one judgement), `a_landless_disband_queues_no_clear`,
and `a_landless_upload_stops_off_test_but_passes_on_it` (the gate, both readers,
the INFO bit).

## 596. The spam block

`SpamBlockCheck` (`G/input_main.cpp:192-234`) is the one chat gate still missing
from `sys.char.chat` after ledger 255: the level-gated, per-IP score that blocks
a spammer's address for fifteen minutes. It is live now, on both arms that run
it — the talking line (`:836-839`, past the silence, before the type switch) and
the whisper (`:540-552`, past the blocks, before the copy) — and
`event.input_main.block_chat_by_ip_event` is `ported` with it. The row's only
remainder is the prism check, which is dead in legacy (`ProcessTextTag` returns
0) and stays a note.

The words come from `spam_db` as `LoadSpamDB` reads them:
`SELECT word, score FROM spam_db WHERE type='SPAM'`, once at boot
(`G/db.cpp:760-779`; the refresh behind `ENABLE_SPAMDB_REFRESH` is dead —
`event.db.reload_spam_event` stays `unused`). `gamedata::spam` is the new rule:
`build_spam_table` keeps the `(word, score)` pairs in row order with both caps
checked before anything is allocated, and `spam_words_from_dump` reads them from
the Game data `common.sql`. The score is `atoi` at the `Insert` call (`:798`),
so a stored negative converts to `unsigned int` — `atoi_score` keeps that wrap
(`wrapping_neg`, so `-1` is `0xffff_ffff`), and a dump without the table is the
owner's shape (`command grep -c spam_db` on their `common.sql` prints 0): no
words, not an error. The `[game]` tunables (`spam_block_score` 100,
`spam_block_duration` 900 s, `spam_block_max_level` 10) predate this slice with
the compiled-in defaults (`G/config.cpp:129-135`); the score keeps legacy's
`MAX(1, …)` (`:1365`).

The gate itself is `GameState::spam_block_check` (`prodomo/src/game_state/whisper.rs`),
in legacy's order: at or past the level it passes; otherwise the IP's entry is
found or made, an armed block answers its remaining seconds, else the line's
score adds to the entry and a total at or past the bar blocks the IP and answers
the full duration. The score is `GetSpamScore` (`G/spam.h:16-36`) — spaces
stripped, every word summed, the last match logged — over `WildCaseCmp`
(`G/utils.cpp:290-328`): `*` swallows a run, `?` one byte, the rest
case-insensitive. The per-IP map is keyed on the sender's address, the Rewrite's
`GetHostName()`, as the legacy's is keyed on the hostname
(`spam_score_of_ip`, `:166-167`; divergence of representation, not of behaviour:
both key one watch per connecting address). The clear event (`:169-189`) has no
port: the block is an expiry Pulse on the game thread, and reading a lifted
block zeroes the score first, which is what the event did. `SPAM_SCORE` and `SPAM_IP` stay tracing logs (`info!`). The
`CharLog(ch, 0, "SPAM", word)` has no port: quest `char_log` is the only
`CHAR_LOG` trace, and ledger 566's question (which game logs the operator
keeps) is still open, so no new log kind is added here.

On the chat arm the descriptor asks the world once per plain line
(`spam_answer`, `prodomo/src/main.rs`): a slash line goes to the interpreter
before the question (`:802`), and the judge runs the verdict in legacy's place —
counter, then the silence, then the spam verdict, then the type switch (`:807-839`).
On the whisper arm the game thread runs the check itself, past the blocks
(`deliver_whisper`); a blocked whisperer hears the silence ladder, not
`[LS;652]`, because the check already sent it. The dispatch gains a fifth
quarter (`apply_block_chat_line`) so `apply_chat_line` stays under the line
lint.

Proved by `a_spammy_line_blocks_its_ip_and_a_high_level_speaks_through`: the
server boots on a `common.sql` with one seeded `SPAM` row (`*gold*`, 100) via
the new `Server::start_with_tables_configured` (`parity/src/server.rs`), which
seeds a `game_tables` dump the way `start_with_files_configured` seeds Game
data. Yankee (level 1) speaks a clean line the map hears, then a spammy line
that is consumed with `[LS;1030;15;0]`; a second line hears the countdown again
(the kept instant, not a timer task); its whisper is refused with the ladder too;
and the same line from Alpha (level 154) reaches the map. The score-99 mutant
(the seeded row under the bar) kills the scenario. Unit seats:
`the_wildcard_matches_stars_questions_and_folds_case`,
`the_spam_score_strips_spaces_and_sums_every_hit`,
`a_blocked_verdict_answers_the_ladder_and_pass_continues` (`prodomo/src/chat.rs`),
`a_spammy_whisper_blocks_its_ip_and_a_second_line_hears_the_countdown` and
`a_high_level_whisper_speaks_past_the_words` (`whisper.rs`), and the
`gamedata::spam` row tests including the owner's empty table.

## 597. The polymorph ball and book

Ledger 364 morphed through the GM line; this slice ports the two consumables that
morph through the timed affect: the ball five (70104-70107, 71093) and the 50322
practice book (`ItemProcess_Polymorph`, `G/char_item.cpp:9749-9814`, with
`CPolymorphUtils::PolymorphCharacter`, `G/polymorph.cpp:36-115`, and the practice
tail, `:117-129`). `sys.char.polymorph` stays `partial`; its note names the two new
scenarios.

The ball's use runs in three seats. The guards (`ball_use_allowed`, in
`use_item_guards`) refuse with legacy's line and the ball kept: morphed `[LS;458]`,
riding `[LS;1053]` (`IsRiding` is the horse or the mount vnum, `G/char.cpp:8783-8786`),
a zero or unknown socket-0 vnum `[LS;460]`, and a mob at or past the caller's level
plus `MAX(0, 20 - level * 3 / 10)` `[LS;461]`. The world step (`MoveKind::Morphed`,
`world/src/character/equip.rs`) consumes one of the stack. The land
(`land_polymorph_ball`) takes the ball, socket and skill captured before the step —
the step already spent the ball — and lays the timed `AFFECT_POLYMORPH` pair: 5
minutes unskilled, else `5 + (5 + skill / 40 * 25)` minutes (`:9800`),
`POINT_POLYMORPH` with the socket-0 vnum (override `true`) and `POINT_ATT_BONUS`
with `(2 + skill / 40) * 100` (override `false`, `:9807`, so the second row does
not retire the first), strips the two blade auras (skills 4 and 63, `:9809-9812`),
and tells `USE_POLYMORPH_BALL` to the log.

`POINT_POLYMORPH` leaves `NOT_PORTED` for the plain arm, and `change_pc_point`
runs the `SetPolymorph` arm (`G/char.cpp:4705-4709`) after the point record, as the
mount arm does — so the affect's compute morphs through the point change, and its
expiry unmorphs the same way. The remove path needed no new code: `compute_affect`
with `add = false` runs the negative change, whose total 0 clears the race.

The book's use is a `MoveKind::Booked` world step that changes nothing — its count
never falls — and the land runs the chance: the master's duration (10/15/20/25
ticks from the skill ladder, anything else silent), the hit when the chance (the
caller's level minus the mob's plus socket 2 plus 29 plus the skill) beats 0 and
the `number(1, 100)` draw, the morph row (override) and, for the dog or 1901 (the
two `m_mapSPDType` rows; the attack and defence tables stay empty), the
move-speed bonus row of skill plus socket 2 (`duration - 1`, no override), then
socket 1's stamp down — or the spent line when it already reads 0. The two
`LC_TEXT` lines are in no locale file (the main table and all 12 country files
were swept), so the lookup answers the key itself. `GiveBook` and `BookUpgrade`
stay unported behind their two `unused` quest names. The stamp's update and store
change join the step's, as `SetSocket` sends and stores.

Proved by `a_used_ball_morphs_through_the_timed_affect_and_spends_itself` (the
grant, the granted cell read off the wire, the log line, the witness's race-101
spawn reencode, the spent row gone) and
`a_blank_book_keeps_itself_and_morphs_nothing` (a blank socket 0 keeps the book
and morphs nothing). Unit seats: the land's morph and spend, the four gate lines
with the ball kept, and the book's hit (seed 0) and miss (seed 1) with the stamp
and the failed line. Along the way `use_item`'s early arms and the land's captures
moved into their own seats (`use_item_early`, `UseLand`), and the world's use
classification into its own tuple, so the line and argument lints hold.
